# AD3D feature specification

**Status:** 2026-10-20. Assembled from the *Hello LuBan* manual (Aug 19, 2025), the LuBan blog (150 posts), the channel transcripts and frames, and `docs/research/`. Every entry is a specification only: no app code implements it yet.

## Purpose

This document lists every feature AD3D will (or deliberately will not) build, one entry per feature. AD3D is a personal, clean-room desktop take on LuBan (luban3d.com): a Tauri 2 app with a React/TypeScript UI and a Rust geometry core that turns photos and 3D models into parts for 3D printing, laser cutting and CNC milling. It runs only on the owner's machines and is never distributed (CLAUDE.md). Each entry records what LuBan does, with a source for every fact, and what AD3D will do instead, so that a generator can be built and tested from its entry alone.

### How to read an entry

Every entry uses the same template:

- **Heading:** `### <ID> — <AD3D name> (LuBan: <LuBan name>)`. In parts 2, 3 and 5, whose entries sit inside chapter subsections, the heading is one level lower (`####`). The ID is stable and is what code, tests and the build order refer to. A heading `<ID> — merged into <canonical>` is a stub left by the duplicate merge. Non-entry notes sit under a `Part N notes` heading at the end of each part.
- **LuBan path:** where the feature lives in LuBan's menus.
- **What it makes**, **Fabrication** (printer, laser or router) and **Inputs**.
- **Parameters table:** `| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |`. One row per setting; rows whose LuBan label is "— (AD3D only)", "— (ours)" or similar are our additions.
- **Outputs**, then **Behaviour and rules** (what LuBan does, with sources).
- **How we will do it better:** concrete improvements, each tied to a LuBan limitation or to PLAN §4.
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** how AD3D will build it (crates, libraries, papers).
- **Milestone:** where it falls in the build order (part 9).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:** everything the sources do not settle, and the next source to check.

Parts 1 to 6 follow the manual's chapters (part 6 adds the post-manual Projection family, Thermal, Mold and File → Create objects). Parts 7 and 8 hold features known only from the blog or only from channel videos. Part 9 is the recommended build order. The appendices map every manual subsection, blog post and channel video to the entries.

## Legend and conventions

- **UNCONFIRMED** marks anything no source states. Parameter defaults and ranges are UNCONFIRMED unless a source (usually a screenshot) shows them.
- **"(suggest: …)"** marks our proposed value or design, never a LuBan fact. "Our reading" marks our interpretation of a source.
- **Citation formats:**
  - `§x.y (PDF p.N)`: the manual, *Hello LuBan.pdf* (123 pages). PDF page numbers are the file's pages; the page numbers printed in `docs/reference/hello-luban-toc.txt` are not PDF pages (in most ranges PDF page = printed page + 1). `Fig. N` is a manual figure.
  - `blog: <slug>`: a post in `docs/research/luban-blog/posts-all.txt`.
  - `video <id> @mm:ss`: a transcript in `docs/research/channel/subs/` or a Squama frame (`f_NNN`, `docs/research/squama-video/frames/`); `video <id> (title)`: only the title in `docs/research/channel/videos_dated.txt` is known, and its date is approximate.
  - `research NN §x`: `docs/research/NN-*.md`; `PLAN §n`: `docs/PLAN.md`; `START_HERE`: `docs/START_HERE.md`.
  - `luban-docs notes §n`, "CN Get started p.N", "zh GS p.N": LuBan's official Chinese decks (2018–2019), via `docs/wip/spec-sections/00-luban-docs-notes.md`.
- **LuBan labels** are verbatim, typos included. Where no screenshot exists, the label is the manual's wording and its on-screen spelling is UNCONFIRMED.
- **AD3D keys** are `snake_case`. Some parts suffix units (`_mm`, `_deg`) and some do not; the key style is to be unified when the code lands. Settings shared across entries already use one key: `x_layers` / `z_layers` for Hash and Wireframe layers, `sphere_angle_deg` for sphere angles, `min_part_volume_mm3` (owned by APP-VALIDATE) for the smallest part kept, and `label_height_2d` (owned by FORM-SHEETS) for the size of labels on cut sheets.
- **Units:** millimetres everywhere. Angles are degrees in the UI and radians in code.
- **Milestones:** M0 (spike) to M12, "Later / maybe never" and "Not building", as defined in part 9. Each entry's Milestone line gives its part 9 milestone and its position in that milestone's row; "Gated" means it is scheduled but not started until its video is transcribed.
- **Part tags:** the appendices tag each entry ID with the part that holds it, as a bare number in parentheses: "CUT-CONIC (4)" means part 4. In the body, the same reference is written "(part 4)". Parts 1–6 follow the manual's chapters plus post-manual features, part 7 holds blog-only features and part 8 video-only features.
- **Clean room:** built only from the manual, the blog, public videos (transcripts and frames) and the research notes in this repo. No LuBan binary is downloaded, run, decompiled or inspected, and the binary-derived listings in research 02 §2–3 are not used as sources. AD3D uses its own names, file formats and UI (CLAUDE.md).
- **Owner's machines** (START_HERE): 3D printer Creality CR-6 SE, 235 × 235 × 250 mm, bed-slinger (bed moves in Y); laser: a "3015" machine (3000 × 1500 mm class; fiber vs CO2 is UNCONFIRMED); CNC: a "1325" router (1300 × 2500 mm class). All three are in use, so laser and CNC features have real value.
- **Generators** are pure functions in the core crate: `(params, inputs)` → mesh or 2D paths, off the UI thread, cancellable, and watertight with consistent winding under randomised-parameter tests (CLAUDE.md).

## 1. App shell and cross-cutting

This section specifies the app shell AD3D wraps around its generators: workspace and views, schema-driven parameter panels with live preview, viewport and light, parts, projects, import and export, image and mesh utilities, machine profiles, nesting, labels, estimates, batch/CLI, settings and help. Manual ch. 1 itself covers only download, install, licence, update, language, settings, the 2D/3D window frames and the Enter-to-update rule (install, licence and update are recorded here but not built: personal use, CLAUDE.md); LuBan's other app-wide behaviour is scattered across later chapters, the blog, the channel videos and the two 2019 Chinese decks, and is collected here so that feature sections can point to it. Source keys: "GS p.N" and "Intro p.N" are pages of "LuBan Get started 快速入门.pdf" and "LuBan Introduction 简介.pdf" in `docs/reference/luban-docs/` (both PDFs were created in Jan/Mar 2019, but the Get-started screenshots show a build from about August 2018: its file dialogs list folders dated Aug 2018, GS p.7, p.10; "2019" below means that deck-era build; Chinese labels kept verbatim, English glosses are ours; `docs/wip/spec-sections/00-luban-docs-notes.md` summarises both decks), "f_NNN" is a frame of the Squama video Wd26qsSIRY8 taken at (NNN−1)×4 s, and transcript times for VA67Jm3ijHg, t2-1zMjWUAw, F20FZvL0r9g and DzvYxTm8pbo are one-minute chunks written @mm:00. Throughout the manual the PDF page is the printed page + 1 (printed p.7 = PDF p.8; checked for ch. 1 and spot-checked up to PDF p.122). Underscores in file names are taken from the PDF pages, because the pdftotext copy drops them ("MU License.dat" is MU_License.dat in the PDF). A value read off a screenshot is recorded as "shown"; it counts as a default only where a source says so, because LuBan restores last-used settings (§1.6; DzvYxTm8pbo @08:00) and figures can differ from stated defaults (Fig. 10, PDF p.17, shows Resolution 0.12 while §2.21.2, PDF p.41, says the default is 0.1 mm/pixel for every lithophane shape except tattoo). Facts that research 02 derived from LuBan binaries are deliberately not used here (clean room; research 07 §f, research 00 §6).

### APP-LAUNCH — Start screen and generator launcher (LuBan: File → Create, Mesh → Cut / Mesh → LuBan, startup "Tip")

- **LuBan path:** startup "Tip" dialog; File → Create → {3D shape, Bamboo-copter, Bottle, Dice, Eyeglasses, Glider, Lithophane, Projection, Photo magic}; File → Open a model, then Mesh → Cut or Mesh → LuBan (manual §1 intro, PDF p.8; video Wd26qsSIRY8 f_052 @03:24, f_054 @03:32).
- **What it makes:** The entry point to every generator. LuBan groups its most-used functions into four clusters: Lithophane and Photo magic under File → Create, plus Mesh → Cut and Mesh → LuBan for an opened 3D model (§1 intro, PDF p.8). The forms it generates are listed as "lithophane, cookie cutter, extrusion, stack, hash, plate, relief, module, and wireframe" (§1 intro, PDF p.8).
- **Fabrication:** App-wide. LuBan's outputs are for 3D printing, laser cutting and CNC milling (§1 intro, PDF p.8).
- **Inputs:** None (navigation). The mesh launchers need an opened model first (f_052; GS p.3).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tip: "Click Yes to show, or No to hide, the tip in future." | `show_start_screen` | Show the start screen at launch | Shown until "No" is clicked | Yes, No | f_052 @03:24 |
| File → Create (submenu) | `generator_id` | Photo/parametric generator to open | — | 3D shape, Bamboo-copter, Bottle, Dice, Eyeglasses, Glider, Lithophane, Projection, Photo magic | f_054 @03:32 |
| Mesh → Cut / Mesh → LuBan | `generator_id` (mesh group) | Mesh generators applied to the opened model | — | Methods of ch. 4 and ch. 5 | §4 intro (PDF p.84); §5 intro (PDF p.96) |
| 网格 → 鲁班 L ("Mesh → LuBan", 2019 UI) | `generator_id` | Same launcher in the 2019 build | — | — | GS p.3 |
| — (AD3D) | `recent_projects` | Recent projects listed on the start screen | — (AD3D; suggest: 10) | 0–50 | PLAN §4 (recent files) |

- **Outputs:** None.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - The Tip lists five routes, verbatim: "Make an eyeglass frame File -> Create -> Eyeglasses"; "Make a lithophane File -> Create -> Lithophane"; "Convert a photo to a 3D model File -> Create -> Photo magic"; "Cut a model File -> Open the model, then Mesh -> Cut"; "Convert a model to various forms File -> Open the model, then Mesh -> LuBan" (f_052).
  - Inside a launcher a drop-down picks the variant: "Shape" for Lithophane (Fig. 10, PDF p.17), "Method" for Photo magic, Mesh → Cut and Mesh → LuBan (Fig. 8, PDF p.15; Fig. 149, PDF p.84; Fig. 172, PDF p.96), "Mode" for Projection (Fence, Squama; f_059 @03:52, f_060 @03:56). Squama is therefore File → Create → Projection → Mode = Squama: "the squamama is under the projection menu. It is a projection method" (Wd26qsSIRY8 @03:44–03:50; research 01 §2); Fence is also "under file create projection" (t2-1zMjWUAw @00:00).
  - "3D shape" is listed in the menu (f_054) but not described in any source; the manual text never mentions it.
  - The File menu has no recent-files list: its items are New, Open, Assemble, Set password, Save, Close, Invoke 2D window, Data receiver, Create ▸, Import ▸, Export ▸, Multi-view sequence, Exit, Exit all (f_054; research 01 §3).
  - The Tip appeared at start in the 2026 video (f_052); whether it is shown by default or because of a saved setting is UNCONFIRMED (§1.6 stores settings).
  - Background, not a feature: the 2019 Introduction deck calls LuBan "new-generation, generative CAD/CAM software" whose concept came from MIT and whose R&D was done at SUTD (Intro p.2), and lists 2-D nesting and 3-D nesting among its core technologies (Intro p.3).
  - Related overview videos (titles only): "What can I do with LuBan" (UiDXdb4nAHM), "Magic of LuBan" (s_43eCcNUM8).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - A start screen with recent projects and a generator gallery grouped by input (photo, mesh, text) and by process (print, laser, CNC); dropping a file on it suggests the generators that accept that file (PLAN §4: drag-and-drop, recent files; LuBan's File menu has no recent-files list, f_054).
  - A command palette (⌘K) opens any generator by name, with LuBan's names ("Squama", "Hash", "Stack") as search aliases so the manual maps onto AD3D (PLAN §4: command palette).
  - Every generator is a first-class launcher entry; none hides as a "Mode" inside another generator (LuBan nests Squama under Projection, research 01 §2).
  - Tips live in a dismissible side panel instead of a modal dialog at launch (f_052).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Generator registry exported from the `ad3d-core` schemas; one React route per generator (PLAN §1).
- **Milestone:** M1 (part 9, after PROJ-SQUAMA-TILE; Squama only), then one entry per generator as each milestone lands.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - What "3D shape" generates.
  - The complete current Mesh menu; only items named in the manual, blog and GS p.3 are known (see APP-MESH-TOOLS).

### APP-WINDOWS — Workspace: 3D view and 2D view in one window (LuBan: 2D and 3D window frames)

- **LuBan path:** "File → Invoke 2/3D window" (§1.7, PDF p.15); in the 3D window the menu item reads "Invoke 2D window" with accelerator U (f_054 @03:32), and from the 2D window the manual goes back with "File → Invoke 3D window" (§3.6.7, PDF p.73); "Exit" (Alt+F4) and "Exit all" (Shift+Alt+F4) (f_054); 2019 UI: 切换到 2D 窗口 U, 关闭窗口 Alt+F4, 关闭所有窗口 Shift+Alt+F4 (GS p.2).
- **What it makes:** LuBan has a 2D window frame focused on image processing and a 3D window frame focused on mesh processing, "with completely different menu items"; the 3D window is shown at start (§1.7, PDF p.15; Fig. 7).
- **Fabrication:** n/a.
- **Inputs:** n/a.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (window shown at start) | `start_view` | View shown at launch | 3D window | 3D, 2D | §1.7 (PDF p.15) |
| File → Invoke 2/3D window (U) | `show_2d_view` | Show the 2D sheet/image view | — | on, off | §1.7; f_054 |
| Exit / Exit all | — | Close one window / close every window | — | — | f_054 |
| — (AD3D) | `split_ratio` | Share of the window given to the 3D view when both views are shown | — (AD3D; suggest: 0.6) | 0.2–0.8 | PLAN §1 (2D sheet view) |

- **Outputs:** n/a.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - 2D window menus: File, Batch, View, Tool, 3D, Draw, Help. 3D window menus: File, Batch, Edit, View, Mesh, Object, Draw, Help (Fig. 7, PDF p.15). The early 3D window had File, Batch, Edit, View, Mesh, Draw, Help with no Object menu (GS p.2; also the older English UI on Intro p.6); 物体 O (Object) appears later in the same deck (GS p.22).
  - The manual's text says "When LuBan starts, the 3D window will be show by default" (verbatim, §1.7, PDF p.15); the startup frames agree (f_052; GS p.2).
  - The window title is the open model's or image's name, e.g. "duck" (GS p.3), "Sagat" (Fig. 149, PDF p.84), "Moon map" (Fig. 23, PDF p.24), "Sheet_1.shp" (GS p.8).
  - Several windows can be open ("Exit" vs "Exit all", f_054); some 2D tools put their result in a new image window ("A new labeling image will be generated, which can be closed", §2.20.4, PDF p.39).
  - Workflows hop between frames: prepare a photo in the 2D window, export it, return to the 3D window and load it (§2.13.1, PDF p.23–24; §2.20.4, PDF p.39; §3.6.7, PDF p.71–73); copy the 3D view and paste it into the 2D window as an image (§3.2.9, PDF p.57).
  - After a Stack model is saved, its contours are nested on cut sheets and shown in a 2D window (§5.3.3, PDF p.102–103).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - One window with the 3D viewport and the 2D sheet/image view docked side by side, both updating live, instead of two frames with different menus (§1.7) and sheets that appear only after Save (§5.3.3) (PLAN §1: 2D sheet view).
  - Photo preparation happens inside each generator's input slot (APP-IMAGE), so there is no frame switching and no export/re-import loop (fixes §2.13.1, §2.20.4, §3.6.7).
  - Tabs for several open projects instead of many top-level windows (ours); native macOS menu bar, full-screen and window restore (CLAUDE.md: macOS first).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Tauri 2 window; React layout with resizable panes; react-three-fiber canvas plus an SVG sheet view (PLAN §1).
- **Milestone:** M0 slice, finished in M1 (part 9, after APP-LAUNCH). Spike: shell with the 3D view; the 2D sheet view is its M4 slice (part 9, thin-slices table).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Contents of the 2D window's "3D" menu and of both "Draw" menus beyond Draw → Create → Image (APP-2D).
  - Whether a 2D window and a 3D window can be visible side by side in LuBan.

### APP-PANEL — Parameter panel (LuBan: control panel)

- **LuBan path:** The GUI of every major function: a control panel on the left and a 3D display on the right (§1.8, PDF p.15, Fig. 8); restated in §2 intro (PDF p.17), §4 intro (PDF p.84) and §5 intro (PDF p.96).
- **What it makes:** The panel that holds a generator's variant selector, input pickers, parameters, read-only measures and action buttons.
- **Fabrication:** n/a.
- **Inputs:** File pickers: "Select photo" + "Browse" (§2 intro, PDF p.17; Fig. 8, PDF p.15), "Shadow" + "Browse" (Squama, f_060 @03:56); mesh generators use the opened model (§4 intro; §5 intro).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Method / Shape / Mode (drop-down at the top) | `variant` | Picks the method inside a group | UNCONFIRMED. Shown: Lithophane "Flat" (Fig. 10); Mesh → Cut "Planar cut" (Fig. 149); Mesh → LuBan "Hash" (Fig. 172) and 无 "None" when first opened in 2019 (GS p.5); Projection "Fence" when first opened in the video (f_058–f_059 @03:48–03:52). LuBan restores last-used settings (§1.6), so these may not be defaults | Per group | Fig. 8, 10 (PDF p.15, 17); Fig. 149 (PDF p.84); Fig. 172 (PDF p.96); GS p.5 |
| Select photo — Browse | `input_image` | Input photo(s); several can be selected in one go where a shape takes several | None | See APP-IMPORT | §2 intro (PDF p.17); §2.16 (PDF p.28) |
| Input / Output / measure section; 输入 / 输出 / 度量 (2019) | — | Panel sections of Mesh → LuBan: "Input" (Method, Unit, Model size X/Y/Z), "Output" (method settings) and a measure section at the bottom. Mesh → Cut instead shows "Input" and "Cutting Plane" ("Plane: Ax + By + Cz = D", A/B/C/D boxes with sliders). Photo magic, Lithophane and Projection panels show only a title ("Photo magic", "Lithophane", "Projection") | — | — | Fig. 172 (PDF p.96); §5 intro (PDF p.96); GS p.5–6; Fig. 149 (PDF p.84); Fig. 8, 10; f_060 |
| Save model (button) | `export` (action) | Writes the result to an export folder | Disabled until an input is loaded | — | §2.12 (PDF p.22); §5 intro; video Wd26qsSIRY8 f_060 @03:56 vs f_066 @04:20 |
| Close (button); 关闭 (C) in 2019 | `close_generator` (action) | Leaves the generator | — | — | f_060 @03:56; GS p.5 |
| 导出部件 E ("Export parts", 2019) | `export` (action) | 2019 name of the export button in Mesh → LuBan | Greyed while Method = 无 (GS p.5) | — | GS p.5–7 |
| Cut (button, Mesh → Cut) | `apply_cut` (action) | Performs the cut; each part is saved as an STL file in a selected folder | — | — | §4.2 (PDF p.85) |
| 压印 ("Imprint", 2019 Wireframe) | `export` (action) | Generates the 2D vector drawing | — | — | GS p.26–27 |
| File size (read-only) | `estimated_file_size` | Predicted file size (see APP-ESTIMATES) | — | — | §2.6 (PDF p.20) |

- **Outputs:** n/a.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Layout is the same for every major function: "The left area is a control panel and the right area shows a 3D display of a generated model" (§1.8, PDF p.15); for lithophanes, "Control parameters are laid out on the left panel and live display is rendered on the right" (§2 intro, PDF p.17).
  - Control types: drop-down lists, radio buttons, check boxes, spin buttons and text boxes (§1.8, PDF p.15), plus sliders (GS p.6, 12, 18, 26; §2.16 "several sliders", PDF p.28; §4.2 "text boxes or sliders", PDF p.85).
  - "Some settings are shared among several methods" (§5 intro, PDF p.96).
  - Long panels scroll (scroll bars in Fig. 8, 10, 149, 172; GS p.12, 18).
  - In the 2019 build, slider labels show their current value, e.g. "环片宽度: 29" (ring width) and "转角: 8 度" (turn angle, degrees) (GS p.6, p.12).
  - Some numeric boxes have spin buttons: Elevation angle and Clearance (Fig. 8), Slant (deg) (Fig. 10), Light angle and Surface angle (f_060), Number of fence (f_059), Quantity (Fig. 161, PDF p.90).
  - Fields appear or disappear with other choices, e.g. a border-thickness box appears only when a dark border is selected (§2.7, PDF p.20).
  - Numbers are parsed leniently: "Cell size" accepted "4j" as 4 (research 01 §3; visible in f_102 @06:44 and f_165 @10:56).
  - Example panel, Fig. 8 (PDF p.15), title "Photo magic": Method "Extrusion"; Select photo [Browse]; Positive (selected) / Negative; Photo / Text (selected); [Font] "Arial"; Text "LuBan"; Model size X 100; Model size Y 26.4; Extrusion 1; Elevation 0; Elevation angle 50 (spin button); Expansion 1; Clearance 1 (spin button); Support "Convex Arc"; Base shape "Rectangle"; Base thickness 5; Keychain hole 0; File size 5 MB (read-only). No units are printed. These values are specified in the Extrusion entry (§3.5); here they show the panel's anatomy.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Panels are generated from each generator's schema (label, unit, default, min/max/step, help text, visibility rules), so every field has a documented unit, range and tooltip (PLAN §1: panels generated from each generator's schema).
  - Every numeric field gets a slider and a typed box with strict parsing; invalid input such as "4j" is flagged instead of truncated (research 01 §3).
  - Auto-adjusted values are explained inline, e.g. "198 mm = 33 cells × 6 mm", instead of changing silently (research 01 §2: 200 → 198).
  - Per-field reset, a "changed from default" marker, and presets per panel (APP-SETTINGS).
  - Export is enabled as soon as a valid result exists and always writes the previewed design at full resolution (APP-LIVE).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Rust parameter structs → JSON Schema (e.g. `schemars`) → generated TypeScript form; zustand store (PLAN §1).
- **Milestone:** M1 (part 9, after APP-WINDOWS).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Whether LuBan sliders regenerate while being dragged (see APP-LIVE).
  - The full set of action buttons per LuBan generator.

### APP-LIVE — Live preview (LuBan: "Hit the Enter key to update display")

- **LuBan path:** Every generator panel (§1.8, PDF p.15–16, Fig. 9).
- **What it makes:** The rule that links parameter edits to the displayed result.
- **Fabrication:** n/a.
- **Inputs:** Parameter edits.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (text box) + Enter / Return | `commit_on_enter` | Typed values apply only after Enter, which acts as LuBan's "Apply" | Required for text boxes | — | §1.8 (PDF p.16); GS p.6 |
| (drop-down, radio button, check box, spin button) | — | A change applies at once | Immediate | — | §1.8 (PDF p.15–16) |
| (Enter on an unchanged value) | `seed` | Puzzle: hitting Enter in a text box without changing it (e.g. Model size X) regenerates with "a random process", giving a different puzzle pattern from the same parameters | New random pattern on every Enter (Puzzle; other randomised generators UNCONFIRMED) | — (AD3D: integer seed plus a "Re-roll" button) | §3.10.7, Fig. 146 (PDF p.82) |
| — (AD3D) | `preview_mode` | Live while dragging/typing, or manual | — (AD3D; suggest: live) | live, manual | CLAUDE.md (Speed); PLAN §1 |
| — (AD3D) | `preview_latency_ms` | Latency target for drag previews | — (AD3D: ≤ 50 ms at typical sizes, CLAUDE.md) | — | CLAUDE.md |
| — (AD3D) | `preview_resolution_scale` | Resolution factor used while dragging | — (AD3D; suggest: chosen automatically from the last job time) | 0.1–1 | PLAN §1 |

- **Outputs:** A preview mesh or 2D paths while editing; the full-quality result on release.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Changing a selection updates the display automatically; text boxes are the exception: press Enter (or Return), which "carries the same purpose as an 'Apply' button"; LuBan has no Apply button by design (§1.8, PDF p.15–16).
  - The rule recurs through the manual (e.g. §2.5–2.7, PDF p.20; §2.13.1, PDF p.23; §4.1, PDF p.85; §5 intro, PDF p.96), in GS p.6 ("改变文字输入框的数字后要按回车键以更新模型": after changing a number in a text box, press Enter to update the model) and in the videos ("Hit the enter key to update the display", Wd26qsSIRY8 @05:11).
  - Enter can rewrite the typed value: Squama sizes snap to whole cells (200 → 198 and 202 → 204 at cell 6, Wd26qsSIRY8 @05:16–05:54), and aspect-locked sizes recompute the other axes (§2.13.1; §4.1). See APP-SIZE.
  - The preview is not always the saved result: the 2D wireframe preview omits the boundary line and base socket and the 3D wireframe preview omits wire thickness, because they are "time consuming to calculate ... for real time display"; the model must be saved to see them (§5.10.1, PDF p.122). Modular-cut modules are generated only after "Export parts" is clicked (GS p.22–23).
  - Coarse-then-fine is left to the user: for tattoo lithophanes the manual recommends "a large resolution value ... when adjusting a photo's position and scale on a 3D model; then a small resolution value ... for the final generation", because small values "can take a long time to generate" (§2.21.2, PDF p.42).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - No Enter key: every control previews while dragging or typing (low-res within 50 ms, full-res on release) on a latest-wins queue that cancels stale jobs (CLAUDE.md Speed; PLAN §1, §4). This automates the manual's coarse-while-adjusting, fine-for-final advice (§2.21.2).
  - Enter still commits immediately and Esc reverts a field, for keyboard users.
  - What you see is what you export: the preview runs the same generator at a lower resolution, including boundaries, sockets and wire thickness (fixes §5.10.1 and GS p.22); only display decimation is allowed (PLAN §1).
  - Deterministic randomness: an explicit `seed` with a Re-roll button, so the same parameters always give the same output, results cache by parameter hash and undo is exact (PLAN §1; fixes §3.10.7, where Enter silently re-rolls).
  - Strict numeric input with optional unit suffixes (e.g. "1 in" → 25.4 mm) and inline errors (fixes "4j", research 01 §3).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Job runner with cooperative cancellation; preview vs final quality flag; `tauri::ipc::Channel` for progress and `tauri::ipc::Response` for binary mesh transfer (PLAN §1); LRU cache keyed by a hash of generator id, version and parameters.
- **Milestone:** M0 slice, finished in M1 (part 9, after APP-PANEL). Spike criterion 5: slider on a 50×63 plate at ≥ 30 fps (PLAN §2).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Whether LuBan's sliders and spin buttons regenerate continuously or only on release.
  - Whether a value typed into a spin button's box (e.g. Light angle, f_102) needs Enter like a text box; §1.8 lists spin buttons among the controls that update automatically but does not separate clicking the arrows from typing.
  - Whether LuBan shows any progress indicator during regeneration.

### APP-JOBS — Background jobs and job log (LuBan: multi-threaded Modular cut; View → Program output)

- **LuBan path:** No job UI is documented; View → Program output (f_167 @11:04); blog: multi-thread-modular-cut.
- **What it makes:** The execution model for generators, mesh tools and exports: off the UI thread, multi-core, cancellable, with progress and a log.
- **Fabrication:** n/a.
- **Inputs:** Jobs submitted by panels, tools and exports.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| View → Program output | `show_job_log` | UNCONFIRMED in LuBan (not described; f_167 shows no tick beside it). AD3D maps it to a job-log panel (ours) | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED (AD3D: on, off) | f_167 @11:04 |
| — (AD3D) | `worker_threads` | Threads used by the rayon pool | — (AD3D; suggest: all logical cores) | 1–N | PLAN §1 (rayon) |
| — (AD3D) | (Cancel button) | Cancel the running job | — | — | PLAN §1, §4 |

- **Outputs:** Progress events, log lines, warnings.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Blog multi-thread-modular-cut (2023-11-15): Mesh → Cut, Modular cut became "significantly" faster through multi-threading; the gain was best on Windows, then macOS 11 or 12, then macOS 10, and least on Linux Ubuntu, and is most obvious for files larger than 20 MB.
  - Slow cases named in the manual: tattoo lithophanes of dense models, and small resolution values that "can take a long time to generate" (§2.21.2, PDF p.42); mesh simplification, "time consuming" (§2.5, PDF p.20); the native Cocoon shape, which "requires much longer processing time than the rest" (§5.1.1, PDF p.97); wireframe previews that skip expensive geometry (§5.10.1, PDF p.122).
  - No source describes a progress bar or a way to cancel a running operation.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Every generator and tool runs off the UI thread on all cores, with the same behaviour on macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon) and Windows; LuBan's speed-up differed by OS (blog multi-thread-modular-cut) (PLAN §4; CLAUDE.md Speed).
  - A progress bar and Cancel for any job longer than about 300 ms (suggest); superseded previews are cancelled automatically (PLAN §1).
  - A job log panel takes the place of "Program output": timings plus warnings such as validation failures, repairs applied and parts larger than the bed (ours).
  - Large exports stream to disk; hot paths have criterion benchmarks (CLAUDE.md; PLAN §5).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** rayon; cancellation token checked in inner loops; Tauri channel events (PLAN §1).
- **Milestone:** M0 slice, finished in M1 (part 9, after APP-LIVE).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - What LuBan's "Program output" shows.
  - Whether a running LuBan operation can be interrupted.

### APP-VALIDATE — Print-readiness checks (LuBan: none documented)

- **LuBan path:** None. No validation or print-readiness UI appears in the manual, blog or videos.
- **What it makes:** Automatic checks on every generated mesh and 2D output, shown as a status badge with a report, and enforced before export.
- **Fabrication:** 3D print (watertight, wall thickness, fits the bed); laser/CNC (closed cut paths, fits the sheet).
- **Inputs:** Generator outputs.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — (AD3D) | `validate_mesh` | Edge-manifold, watertight, consistent winding, no degenerate triangles | — (AD3D: always on in debug builds, tests and export) | — | PLAN §1; CLAUDE.md |
| — (AD3D) | `min_wall_mm` | Flag walls thinner than this | — (AD3D; suggest: 0.8, i.e. 2 × a 0.4 mm nozzle) | ≥ 0 | research 04 §B-1 ("thin spots below the nozzle width") |
| — (AD3D) | `min_part_volume_mm3` | Flag tiny parts instead of exporting them silently. This entry owns the key; CUT-REPAIR, CUT-GRID, CUT-MODULAR and TOOL-SEPARATE use the same value | — (AD3D; suggest: 50) | ≥ 0 | §4.5.2 (PDF p.90) |
| — (AD3D) | `check_bed_fit` | Warn when a part exceeds the printer or the sheet | — (AD3D; suggest: on) | on, off | PLAN §4; research 08 §2.4 |

- **Outputs:** A validation report per part.
- **Behaviour and rules:** LuBan evidence that checks are needed:
  - Export folders can contain parts named "Tiny_1, Tiny_2, etc.", very small parts "often caused by defects in the original model or residual errors produced in the cutting process" (§4.5.2, PDF p.90).
  - Low vertex density can make Spin produce defects "such as self-intersections" (§5.7, PDF p.112).
  - Printability limits are given as advice, not checks, e.g. the Squama author caps Surface angle at 20 "for now" and warns that larger values cause printing issues and need support when the light is at the top or bottom (Wd26qsSIRY8 @09:23–10:07).
  - Some constraints are stated, but whether LuBan enforces them is UNCONFIRMED, e.g. a dark border's thickness "must be larger than the Max thickness by 5%" (§2.7, PDF p.20).
  - LuBan's own checks and silent fallbacks: Modular cut asks you to print the model in one body when it is not bigger than the build volume (§4.5, PDF p.89); a Stack dowel size "roughly bigger then 1/3 of the smallest dimension of a contour" silently prevents dowel holes (§5.3.1, PDF p.102); a failed natural cut "will roll back to the pure planar cut" (§4.2.3, PDF p.86); some Hash contours "do not interlock with the others" and "cannot be assembled" (§5.4.3, PDF p.105).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Watertight-by-construction generators, each backed by a property test over random parameters (CLAUDE.md; PLAN §5), with `validate()` run on every output (PLAN §1).
  - A visible badge (OK / warnings / errors) with click-to-highlight of problem areas; tiny parts are listed and excluded by default instead of appearing as files.
  - Export is blocked on errors; warnings need an explicit "export anyway" (ours).
  - Fallbacks and dropped features are reported instead of happening silently: natural cut falling back to planar, dowel holes not generated, contours that interlock with nothing (fixes §4.2.3, §5.3.1, §5.4.3) (ours).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Half-edge manifold check after vertex welding; manifold used only as an independent validator (research 08 §2.2); proptest (PLAN §5).
- **Milestone:** M0 slice, finished in M1 (part 9, after APP-JOBS). Spike criterion 3 (PLAN §2).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - None about LuBan (it has no such feature); the thresholds above are suggestions to tune after test prints.

### APP-SETTINGS — Settings, last-used values and presets (LuBan: MU_Setting.txt)

- **LuBan path:** `MU_Setting.txt` in the folder that contains the LuBan application (§1.6, PDF p.14–15).
- **What it makes:** Persistent app settings plus remembered parameter values for each function.
- **Fabrication:** n/a.
- **Inputs:** n/a.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MU_Setting.txt | `settings_file` | Where settings are stored | Same folder as the LuBan application | — | §1.6 (PDF p.14) |
| background color | `background_color` | Viewport background (see APP-VIEWPORT) | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED | §1.6 (PDF p.14) |
| parameters in many functions | `last_used_params` | Remembered values per function | Loaded at start; LuBan "will be able to remember the last used settings" | — | §1.6; DzvYxTm8pbo @08:00 |
| (no setting file found) | — | Default settings are applied | Defaults | — | §1.6 (PDF p.14) |
| Run as administrator (Windows, setup.msi install) | — | Needed at least once: the manual says it lets LuBan "read the setting file located in the system folder "C:\Program Files (x86)\LuBan"", the video says it lets LuBan "save setting files in the folder" | — | — | §1.6 (Fig. 6, PDF p.14–15); DzvYxTm8pbo @08:00 |
| MU_Setting.txt copy in an export folder | — | Copy it next to the application and restart to roll back to an old project's settings | — | — | §2.12 (PDF p.23) |
| — (AD3D) | `presets` | Named parameter sets per generator, printer, laser and material | — (AD3D; suggest: one "Default" preset per generator) | — | PLAN §4 (presets per printer, laser and material) |

- **Outputs:** The settings file.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Settings load when LuBan starts; without a settings file LuBan applies its defaults (§1.6, PDF p.14).
  - The first administrator run "will generate a setting file" that "contains all kind of settings that LuBan used"; later runs remember the last used settings (DzvYxTm8pbo @08:00).
  - Uninstalling (Control Panel → Programs and Features) leaves the LuBan3D folder with the settings behind; the narrator first says "except the license", then corrects himself to "the setting", so whether the licence file also stays is unclear (DzvYxTm8pbo @15:00–16:00).
  - The 2026 Squama video still opens on the start-up Tip and on Projection with Mode "Fence" (f_052, f_058–f_059); whether these come from the settings file is UNCONFIRMED.
  - Each lithophane export folder holds "<photo>_Setting.txt", e.g. "family_Setting.txt" ("Human readable settings used to generate the lithophane"), and a copy of "MU_Setting.txt" (§2.12, PDF p.23).
  - "There should be a default setting file in that folder, which can be overwritten by the file from the old project. Then, restart LuBan; all settings will be rolled back" (§2.12, PDF p.23).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Settings live in the per-user app-config folder as versioned JSON with migrations; no administrator rights are ever needed (fixes §1.6; Tauri path API).
  - Last-used values per generator plus named presets per printer, laser and material (PLAN §4).
  - Projects carry their own parameters, so returning to an old design means opening its project, not swapping a global settings file and restarting (fixes §2.12).
  - "Reset to defaults" per generator and globally; settings export/import to copy the setup to the owner's second machine (ours; CLAUDE.md: 1–2 machines).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** serde + JSON with a schema-version field; Tauri `app_config_dir`.
- **Milestone:** M1 (part 9, after APP-FILES).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - The full list of what MU_Setting.txt stores.
  - LuBan's default background colour (see APP-VIEWPORT).
  - Where the settings file lives on Mac and Linux: §1.6 only says "the same folder as the LuBan application", and on Mac the application sits inside a package (§1.3.3, PDF p.11–12).
  - Whether the administrator step is Windows-only: the manual ties it to a setup.msi install (§1.6), and the install video seems to say "this is only [on Windows]" (garbled caption "this is only a wing see", DzvYxTm8pbo @08:00).

### APP-SHORTCUTS — Keyboard shortcuts and command palette (LuBan: menu accelerators)

- **LuBan path:** Accelerators printed in the menus (f_054 @03:32; f_167 @11:04; f_091 @06:00) plus keys named in the manual and the videos.
- **What it makes:** Keyboard access to commands. In the table, "Default" is LuBan's binding and "Range / options" is the AD3D binding we suggest for macOS.
- **Fabrication:** n/a.
- **Inputs:** Keyboard.
- **Parameters:**

- **How we will do it better:**
  - macOS-native bindings (⌘ instead of Ctrl; F1 and F5 need fn on Mac laptops) and a command palette, with shortcut hints in menus and tooltips (PLAN §4: keyboard shortcuts, command palette).
  - Keep LuBan's single-letter viewport keys where they do not clash, so the manual's instructions still work (ours).
  - Rebindable shortcuts later (suggest).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Tauri menu accelerators plus a React hotkey layer.
- **Milestone:** M1 (part 9, after APP-ESTIMATES; core set) → Later (palette polish, rebinding).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**

### APP-HELP — Help, About and in-app guidance (LuBan: Help menu, Help → About, Tip)

- **LuBan path:** Help → About (§1.3, PDF p.9; Fig. 2, PDF p.10); Help → Language (§1.5, PDF p.14); startup Tip (f_052 @03:24).
- **What it makes:** Build information and access to documentation.
- **Fabrication:** n/a.
- **Inputs:** n/a.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| About: Website | — | Product site link | www.luban3d.com | — | Fig. 2 (PDF p.10) |
| About: Email | — | Support email | luban3d@gmail.com | — | Fig. 2 |
| About: Built on | `build_info` | Build date and time of the executable | Example "Dec 11 2020 22:52:50" | — | Fig. 2; DzvYxTm8pbo @10:00 |
| About: License ID / Expiration date | — | Licence fields (not building; APP-LICENSE) | Examples "{AA050064000000900004} Win 64-bit" and "01-Jul-2079 (permanent license)" | — | Fig. 2 |
| — (AD3D) | `help_drawer` | Per-generator help generated from docs/spec/FEATURES.md | — (AD3D) | — | PLAN §4 (per-feature help drawn from our spec) |

- **Outputs:** n/a.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - LuBan shows no version number; the About box's build date identifies a release (Fig. 2; "help about is generated on February 6", DzvYxTm8pbo @10:00).
  - Support channels: the Facebook LuBan group, the MeWe LuBan group and email (§1 intro, PDF p.8).
  - Documentation ships in the download folder's "Doc" folder, which "contains the documentation", alongside "brief documentation on how you get started" (Fig. 1, PDF p.9; DzvYxTm8pbo @01:00). There is no in-app help beyond the Tip; the manual sends users to the website, a Facebook group, a MeWe group and email (§1 intro, PDF p.8).
  - The About box (Fig. 2, PDF p.10) holds exactly: the LB logo and "LuBan", an "Ok" button, Website, Email, Built on, License ID and Expiration date. The licence ID is meant to be copied from it as text, "with the brackets and the OS information" (§1.3.2, PDF p.10).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - About shows version, git commit, build date and the running architecture slice (x86_64 or arm64) (ours; CLAUDE.md universal build).
  - A help drawer per generator generated from this spec, including that generator's print/cut checklist (PLAN §4; CLAUDE.md physical-testing handover).
  - Every field tooltip shows meaning, unit and range from the schema (APP-PANEL).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Build script embeds `git describe` and the target triple; Markdown rendering of the spec section.
- **Milestone:** M1 (part 9, after APP-SHORTCUTS; About, tooltips) → M2 (help drawer).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Other items in LuBan's Help menu.

### APP-LANGUAGE — UI language (LuBan: Help → Language)

- **LuBan path:** Help → Language (§1.5, PDF p.13–14).
- **What it makes:** Selects the language of the user interface.
- **Fabrication:** n/a.
- **Inputs:** n/a.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Help → Language | `ui_language` | UI language | UNCONFIRMED (English is built in and needs no folder; the initial selection is not stated) | Chinese (Simplified) zh_CN, Chinese (Traditional) zh_TW, English, French fr_FR, German de_DE, Greek el_GR, Italian it_IT, Lithuanian lt_LT, Malay ms_MY, Polish pl_PL, Portuguese (Brazilian) pt_BR, Russian ru_RU, Slovak sk_SK, Slovenian sl_SI, Spanish es_ES, Thai th_TH | §1.5 (PDF p.13–14); Fig. 5 (PDF p.13) |

- **Outputs:** n/a.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Every language except English is a folder, named exactly as listed, holding an MU.mo file and placed next to the application (§1.5, PDF p.14; Fig. 5).
  - The folders are installed automatically on Mac and by setup.msi on Windows; users of the bare LuBan.exe must download, unzip and place them by hand (§1.5, PDF p.14). Fig. 5 (PDF p.13) shows them next to LuBan.exe in the Win 64 download folder; the install video lists them in the install folder (DzvYxTm8pbo @06:00–07:00).
  - A language folder "is often downloaded as a zip file"; after unzipping, its name must be "exactly same as shown in the above list" (§1.5, PDF p.14).
  - On Linux only English is available (§1.5, PDF p.13).
  - Selecting a language: run LuBan, then "Help → Language" and "Select the language that you hope to display" (§1.5, PDF p.14). Whether a restart is needed is not stated.
  - The install video recommends setup.msi over the bare LuBan.exe for a first install, "especially if you want to use Luban in a non English environment" (DzvYxTm8pbo @02:00).
  - 16 languages in total: English plus 15 folders (§1.5, PDF p.13–14).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - English only for now (personal use, CLAUDE.md); all UI strings in one catalogue so a translation can be added later without loose folders or exact-name rules (fixes §1.5) (ours).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** i18next-style message catalogue (suggest).
- **Milestone:** Later / maybe never (part 9).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - None that affect AD3D.

  - The status bar shows "&Viewing angle: az, el, 0" continuously (Fig. 7, 8, 10, 149, 172); menu and toolbar labels are echoed there with the "&" left in (research 01 §3; f_093, f_102, f_165).
  - Turning edges on makes imprinted part numbers readable (§4.5.2, Fig. 162, PDF p.90) and shows a model's vertex density (§2.21.2, PDF p.42).
  - In the Squama video the plate is selected first and then edges are enabled to show the cell grid (Wd26qsSIRY8 @06:01–06:13).
  - View → Copy plus View → Paste moves the 3D view into the 2D window as an image; the manual uses this to extract a template (§3.2.9, PDF p.57).
  - Toolbar (Fig. 7, PDF p.15; f_060): Open, Save, an antenna-like icon, then display buttons (Show/Hide Edge is the wire-cone icon and Show/Hide Surface the solid-cone icon, identified via the status bar in f_090, f_093 and f_102), axis buttons X, Y, Z, then mouse-mode buttons (Rotate highlighted; Move light is the last one, tooltip "&Move light", f_165 @10:56), then the slider. A light-bulb icon is greyed in an empty scene (Fig. 7; f_060) and lit once a model is loaded (Fig. 8; f_066); the 2019 notes read it as lighting (luban-docs notes §2.6). Its function and the other icons are unidentified.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Trackpad/mouse navigation that never needs a mode switch: orbit, pan and zoom by gesture or modifier; modes only for tools (LuBan makes Float/Shift/Rotate/Clip/Move light exclusive menu modes, f_167) (ours).
  - A view cube with explicit ± axis views (fixes "after one click, the letters may turn their back toward you; click again", §3.2.9).
  - Display toggles: shaded, edges, wireframe, x-ray, colour by height, by part or by overhang; a section (clip) plane.
  - Build-volume or sheet outline drawn from the active machine profile (APP-MACHINES; research 07 §a).
  - Screenshot to PNG at a chosen resolution or to the clipboard, for documentation and for preview screenshots handed to the owner (ours; CLAUDE.md handover).
  - Live dimensions in the status bar (replaces the Mesh → Statistics pop-up, APP-MESH-TOOLS); in-viewport handles for generator controls (light, crop, cut planes), as LuBan began doing for cut planes (blog mouse-movable-cutting-plane).
  - Large meshes are decimated for display only (PLAN §1); dark and light themes (PLAN §4).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** react-three-fiber + three-mesh-bvh (PLAN §1); orbit controls and a view-cube gizmo (e.g. drei, suggest); meshoptimizer decimation for display (research 07 §b).
- **Milestone:** M0 slice, finished in M1 (part 9, after APP-VALIDATE). Spike criterion 1 (PLAN §2).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - What the Float, Shift and Clip mouse modes do.
  - The View → Viewport submenu, the Window size dialog and Reset object coordinates.
  - The meaning of the third number in "&Viewing angle".
  - Whether the second number really is an elevation: the 2019 decks show "13, 139, 0" with the duck (GS p.3) and "26, 119, 0" in the old English UI (Intro p.6), outside the −90…90 range an elevation would have; the azimuth/elevation reading (research 01 §3, by analogy with MATLAB) is therefore UNCONFIRMED.
  - The slider's behaviour outside Select mode: in f_092 @06:04, with the slider at its left end, the background turns white and the label "Squama" appears; research 01 §3 guesses it controls transparency (UNCONFIRMED).

### APP-LIGHT — Viewport lighting and physical-light preview (LuBan: View → Lighting angle, View → Move light, Backlight)

- **LuBan path:** View → Lighting angle (dialog) and View → Move light (mouse mode) (f_167 @11:04; f_168 @11:08; Wd26qsSIRY8 @10:56–12:06); Lithophane → Backlight (§2.11, PDF p.22).
- **What it makes:** Controls the render light used to judge shading-based results (Squama facets, Fence shadows) and the backlit look of lithophanes.
- **Fabrication:** The preview should mirror the physical setup: a single low-angle light in a dark room for Squama (PLAN §6; research 08 §2.3), a single point light for Projection (VA67Jm3ijHg @07:00–09:00), a backlight for lithophanes (§2.11).
- **Inputs:** Scene; generator light parameters.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lighting angle: "X angle is between [0, 180]." | `light_x_angle_deg` | Light angle about the X axis ("the angle about the x axis") | Shown: the dialog opened pre-filled "90 0" (f_168, zoomed); whether that is the default or the current light is UNCONFIRMED | 0–180 | f_168 @11:08; Wd26qsSIRY8 @11:12 |
| Lighting angle: "Y angle is between [-180, 180]." | `light_y_angle_deg` | Light angle about the vertical axis ("the angle about the y axis ... this is referring to the vertical axis") | Shown: 0 (same caveat) | −180–180 | f_168 @11:08; Wd26qsSIRY8 @11:12–11:20 |
| "Example 1: 30 (X angle: 30, Y angle: 0) Example 2: 30 20 (X angle: 30, Y angle: 20)" | — | Input format: one number sets X with Y = 0; two numbers set X and Y | — | — | f_168 @11:08 |
| View → Move light | `mouse_mode` = `move_light` | Drag horizontally: the light revolves about the vertical axis; drag vertically: it moves about the X axis | — | — | Wd26qsSIRY8 @11:20–11:53 |
| Backlight | `backlight_preview` | Simulates a lithophane under backlight; light colour, filament colour and light intensity are configurable | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED | §2.11 (PDF p.22); blog lithophane-3rd-release |
| — (AD3D) | `ambient_level` | Room (ambient) light added to the preview | — (AD3D; suggest: 0.1) | 0–1 | PLAN §4 (ambient-light slider); research 08 §2.3 |
| — (AD3D) | `cast_shadows` | Shadow maps on/off | — (AD3D; suggest: on for Squama and Fence) | on, off | PLAN §1, §4 |
| — (AD3D) | `light_follows_generator` | Render light follows the generator's light parameters | — (AD3D; suggest: on) | on, off | Wd26qsSIRY8 @11:54–12:06 (LuBan does not do this) |

- **Outputs:** n/a.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - The author calls changing the lighting angle "not an often used function in LuBan" (Wd26qsSIRY8 @11:01).
  - The dialog is titled "&Lighting angle", asks "Enter lighting angle (degree).", takes both angles in one text box and has OK and Cancel buttons (f_168).
  - Squama's "Light source" parameter only marks where the light is (magenta spheres) and "doesn't actually simulate the lighting direction"; the user must move the render light by hand to see the image (Wd26qsSIRY8 @04:28, @11:54–12:06).
  - Backlight: the colour of the light and of the filament can be configured and the light intensity adjusted (§2.11, PDF p.22; blog lithophane-3rd-release: "Lamp color and intensity, filament color").
- **How we will do it better:**
  - A physically motivated preview: directional or point light with real shadow maps and an ambient slider that shows how room light washes the image out (PLAN §4: realistic preview).
  - The preview light is bound to the generator's light parameters by default (Squama side and angle, Fence light position), with a "free light" toggle; no separate dialog with a different angle convention (fixes Wd26qsSIRY8 @11:54–12:06).
  - A draggable light gizmo in the viewport, with numeric fields in the generator's own convention (degrees of elevation above the plate) (ours).
  - Transmission mode for lithophanes: light through the plate, thickness → brightness, filament colour presets (PLAN §4).
  - A split "lit vs room light only" compare view for checking Squama's hide-and-reveal effect (ours).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** three.js directional/spot lights with shadow maps; custom shader for lithophane transmission (Beer–Lambert attenuation with thickness, suggest); Lambert shading model as in research 00 §2 / research 01 §2.
- **Milestone:** M0 slice, finished in M1 (part 9, after APP-VIEWPORT). Spike criterion 1: movable directional light casting shadows (PLAN §2); Squama shadows in M1, lithophane backlight in M2.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - LuBan's default lighting angle.
  - LuBan's backlight parameter names, defaults and ranges (lithophane section).
  - Whether LuBan renders cast shadows at all; no source shows any.

### APP-OBJECTS — Parts list: select, explode, restore, delete (LuBan: Object menu, toolbar slider)

- **LuBan path:** Object → Select (J), Delete, Explode (E), Restore (R) (f_091 @06:00; VA67Jm3ijHg @01:00; GS p.24); blog: exploded-view.
- **What it makes:** Inspection of multi-part results: highlight one part, show an exploded view, restore it, delete parts.
- **Fabrication:** Used to check assembly relationships before printing or cutting (§4.3, §4.5.3).
- **Inputs:** Multi-part results (cut parts, assemblies, nested boxes, hash contours, generator components).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Object → Select (J) | `selected_part_index` | Highlights one part; the others are drawn translucent (Fig. 156 right; GS p.24) | — | 1…N | §4.3, Fig. 156 (PDF p.87–88); GS p.24; VA67Jm3ijHg @01:00 ("object select or keyboard shortcut J key") |
| toolbar slider | `selected_part_index` (slider) | Navigate all parts one by one in Select mode | — | 1…N | §3.2.5 (PDF p.51); §4.3 (PDF p.88); §4.5.3 (PDF p.90) |
| "选择J" dialog: part name "Part_01", 删除 ("Delete") button, slider | `delete_part` | The 2019 Select dialog: shows the highlighted part's name and can delete it | — | — | GS p.24 |
| Object → Explode (E) | `exploded` | Shows all parts pulled apart | Off (inferred: results open assembled) | on, off | §4.3, Fig. 156 (PDF p.87); f_091; F20FZvL0r9g @05:00 |
| Object → Restore (R) | `exploded` = off | Back to the assembled view | — | — | §4.3 (PDF p.87); f_091 |
| Object → Delete | `delete_part` | Delete the selected object | — | — | f_091 |
| — (AD3D) | `explode_factor` | Explode distance as a continuous slider | — (AD3D; suggest: 0–2 × assembly size) | 0–2 | ours |
| — (AD3D) | `part_visible` (per part) | Show/hide/isolate parts | — (AD3D; suggest: all visible) | on, off | ours |

- **Outputs:** n/a (view state only; Delete affects exported parts).
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Results can include visualization-only components, e.g. Projection's "beam" and "projected image", "for visualization only. You do not have to print these two" (VA67Jm3ijHg @01:00); Squama's magenta spheres only mark the light side (Wd26qsSIRY8 @04:28).
  - The manual uses Select/Explode for: poly-face assemblies (Fig. 31 caption, "To enable the exploded view, use 'Object → Select'", §2.15.3, PDF p.28), nested boxes (§3.2.5, PDF p.51), cut parts (§4.3, Fig. 156, PDF p.87–88), assembly order (§4.5.3, PDF p.90), hash contours (§5.4.4, PDF p.105). The videos use E for Projection (VA67Jm3ijHg @01:00) and Thermal (F20FZvL0r9g @05:00).
  - Blog exploded-view (2019-04-03): "Show multiple objects in a window in an exploded view. 'Object -> Explode' and 'Object -> Restore'."
  - Browsing parts with Select and the slider works for modular cut only "if the number of parts is relatively small, e.g. fewer than 20"; beyond that the manual points to the assembly sequence file (§4.5.3, PDF p.90–91).
  - With a Squama result on screen, the Object menu shows Delete and Restore greyed and Explode, Transform and Align enabled; Select's state is unclear in the frame (f_091 @06:00).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - An outliner listing every part with name, size, process (print/cut), visibility and an export checkbox; visualization-only helpers (beams, light markers) are flagged and never exported (LuBan relies on the user knowing not to print them, VA67Jm3ijHg @01:00) (ours).
  - Click-to-select in the viewport, isolate, and a continuous explode slider with animation (ours).
  - An assembly-step scrubber that animates parts in assembly order (ties to APP-ASSEMBLE and the sequence output).
  - Delete/hide is an undoable parameter change, not a destructive edit of the result (PLAN §4: undo/redo).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** three-mesh-bvh raycasting (PLAN §1); explode offset = (part centroid − assembly centroid) × factor.
- **Milestone:** M1 (part 9, after APP-MACHINES). Slices: a basic parts list for Squama tiles in M1; cut parts in M3.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - What Object → Select does when the scene has a single object (f_091 shows Delete greyed for a Squama plate with its light markers).
  - Exactly what Object → Delete removes.
  - The highlight colour: in f_090 @05:56 one light marker is green a few seconds before the author says "If you select these are the lights" (Wd26qsSIRY8 @06:01–06:06), which suggests a green selection highlight; in Fig. 156 the highlighted part keeps its own colour.

### APP-TRANSFORM — Transform, align and place objects (LuBan: Object → Transform, Object → Align, Mesh rotate/scale/move)

- **LuBan path:** Object → Transform (§3.2.9, PDF p.57–58, Fig. 87; §5.2.2, PDF p.99; §5.6.1, PDF p.108); Object → Align (f_091 @06:00); 2019 Mesh menu: 改变比例 R ("Change scale"), 绕 X / Y / Z 轴旋转 ("Rotate about the X / Y / Z axis"), 刚体移动 T ("Rigid-body move"), Z 基面置零 ("Set Z base to zero") (GS p.3).
- **What it makes:** Re-orients and resizes a model before a generator runs. Contour and Relief offer fixed directions only; any other direction needs the model pre-rotated with Object → Transform (§5.2.2, PDF p.99; §5.6.1, PDF p.108).
- **Fabrication:** Print orientation (see also APP-EXPORT).
- **Inputs:** An opened or generated model.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (fields above "Scale or Size"; "Y 0", "Z 0" visible) | `translate_mm` or `rotate_deg` | UNCONFIRMED which: only the bottom of this group is visible | 0 | UNCONFIRMED | Fig. 87 (PDF p.58) |
| Scale or Size: Scale / Size | `transform_mode` | Scale by factor, or set an absolute size | UNCONFIRMED; Fig. 87 shows Size, which the text tells the user to pick ("The size option should be selected as opposed to the scale option") | scale, size | Fig. 87; §3.2.9 (PDF p.58) |
| Fixed / Flexible | `lock_aspect` | Fixed keeps proportions; Flexible sets X, Y, Z independently (our reading of the labels and the worked example) | UNCONFIRMED; Fig. 87 shows Flexible, which the text tells the user to pick | fixed, flexible | Fig. 87; §3.2.9 (PDF p.58) |
| X / Y / Z | `size_mm` (x, y, z) or `scale` (x, y, z) | Target size or scale per axis | Example 197, 6.32, 110 before resizing X and Z to 194.6 and 107.2 | — | Fig. 87 (PDF p.58) |
| Mirror | `mirror` | Mirror the model | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED (only the heading is visible) | Fig. 87 |
| Object → Align | `align` | UNCONFIRMED (not described) | — | — | f_091 |
| 改变比例 R | `scale` | Change scale (2019 Mesh menu) | — | — | GS p.3 |
| 绕 X / Y / Z 轴旋转 | `rotate_deg` (x, y, z) | Rotate about an axis (2019 Mesh menu) | — | — | GS p.3 |
| 刚体移动 T | `translate_mm` | Rigid-body move (2019 Mesh menu) | — | — | GS p.3 |
| Z 基面置零 | `drop_to_bed` | Move the model so its lowest point is at Z = 0 (gloss of the label) | — | — | GS p.3 |

- **Outputs:** The transformed model (LuBan then uses File → Export → STL to save it, §3.2.9).
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Worked example: Mesh → Statistics gives the lid's bounding box; Object → Transform with "Size" and "Flexible" sets the lithophane's X and Z to match; File → Export → STL saves it (§3.2.9, PDF p.57–58).
  - Axis conventions differ between generators: "They are X and Z, not X and Y, due to different orientation of the two models" (§3.2.9, PDF p.58).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Move/rotate/scale gizmos in the viewport plus numeric fields, with snapping (15°, 1 mm) (ours).
  - "Lay face on bed" and an auto-orient-for-print helper (minimise height or overhang) (ours).
  - Transforms are non-destructive project parameters applied before the generator, so they are undoable and re-editable (PLAN §4: projects, undo/redo).
  - One axis convention across all generators (Z up), with the print orientation shown explicitly rather than applied silently at save time (LuBan rotates a slanted flat lithophane to vertical when saving, §2.13.2, PDF p.24).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** glam affine transforms (PLAN §1); bounding boxes from `ad3d-core`.
- **Milestone:** M3 (part 9, after CUT-WORKSPACE; mesh input).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - The fields above "Scale or Size" in the Transform panel, the Mirror options and what Object → Align does.

### APP-SIZE — Model size, aspect lock and snapping (LuBan: Model size X / Y / Z)

- **LuBan path:** "Model size X / Y / Z" fields in nearly every panel (Fig. 8, PDF p.15; Fig. 10, PDF p.17; Fig. 149, PDF p.84; Fig. 172, PDF p.96).
- **What it makes:** The shared rules for setting a model's overall size.
- **Fabrication:** Size decides whether a part fits the printer or the sheet (APP-MACHINES).
- **Inputs:** Photo aspect ratio or mesh bounding box.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Model size X / Y / Z | `size_x_mm`, `size_y_mm`, `size_z_mm` | Overall size; for Mesh → LuBan it is the size of the original model, not of the generated one | Per generator, shown not stated: 50 × 50 for a flat lithophane (Fig. 10); 300 × 300 for Squama before a photo is loaded (f_060). For an opened mesh the fields start at the model's bounding box in the chosen unit (duck 98.5 × 76.7 × 70.2 mm, GS p.5–6; inferred) | UNCONFIRMED | §2.13.1 (PDF p.23); §4.1 (PDF p.85); §5 intro (PDF p.96) |
| (aspect lock, photo input) | `lock_aspect` | Flat lithophane: X and Z follow the photo's aspect ratio; the arc lithophane shares this, with Model size X replaced by the arc angle. Poly-face lithophanes instead "automatically crop from the center of a photo", and a rectangle lithophane's X, Y and Z "can be independently set" | Locked (flat, arc) | Locked for flat/arc (and Squama, f_066); cropped, not locked, for poly-face | §2.13.1 (PDF p.23); §2.14 (PDF p.25); §2.15 (PDF p.26) |
| (aspect lock, mesh input) | `lock_aspect` | X : Y : Z fixed to the original model | Locked | Locked only in LuBan | §4.1 (PDF p.85); §5 intro (PDF p.96) |
| (snap to whole cells, Squama) | `snap_to_cells` | Size rounded to an integer multiple of the cell size | On (200 → 198 and 202 → 204 at cell 6) | — | Wd26qsSIRY8 @05:16–05:54; research 01 §2 |

- **Outputs:** n/a.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Changing one size and pressing Enter changes the others to keep the ratio (§2.13.1, PDF p.23; §4.1, PDF p.85; §5 intro, PDF p.96).
  - To get a given lithophane aspect ratio the photo itself must be cropped first, in another program or in the 2D window (§2.13.1, PDF p.23–24).
  - Squama's Model size Z follows the photo after loading (300 → 378, research 01 §2).
  - An imported model with very small coordinates "produces something nasty" until the model size is set to a reasonable value (F20FZvL0r9g @11:00).
  - Changing a poly-face lithophane's model size "may change the region of the photo to include" (§2.15, PDF p.26; Fig. 28, PDF p.27).
  - Modular cut assumes the model is bigger than the build volume; "If not, you will be asked to print the model in one body and no cutting will be done" (§4.5, PDF p.89).
  - In the 2019 build, Wireframe imprint greys out the size fields (GS p.26).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - A lock/unlock toggle where the generator allows it, with "fit to bed" and "fit to sheet" buttons driven by the machine profile (APP-MACHINES; PLAN §4: machine profiles).
  - Snapping explained inline ("198 mm = 33 cells × 6 mm"), with the option to keep the size and adjust the cell size instead (ours; fixes the silent change in research 01 §2).
  - A warning when the result exceeds the printer or sheet, with an offer to tile (PLAN §3 M1: tiling; research 08 §2.4: Squama's plate at its default 300 mm width, 300 × 378 for the 4:5 Mona Lisa (f_060 → f_066), printed upright exceeds most printers).
  - Crop-to-aspect inside the input slot instead of a 2D-window detour (APP-IMAGE).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Size solver in the generator schema (locked ratios, snapping rules); bounding boxes from `ad3d-core`.
- **Milestone:** M1 (part 9, after APP-EXPORT).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - LuBan's minimum and maximum model sizes.

### APP-UNITS — Units and import scale (LuBan: "Select unit" dialog, Unit drop-down)

- **LuBan path:** Entering Mesh → LuBan opens a 选择单位 ("Select unit") dialog (GS p.3–4), still present in 2026: "Go to mesh, LuBan ... and then select the unit millimeter" (F20FZvL0r9g @03:00). Mesh → Cut and Mesh → LuBan panels have a "Unit" drop-down in the Input section (Fig. 149, PDF p.84; Fig. 172, PDF p.96; 单位, GS p.6); whether Mesh → Cut also opens the dialog is UNCONFIRMED.
- **What it makes:** Tells LuBan what unit an imported mesh's coordinates are in.
- **Fabrication:** Wrong units give wrongly sized parts.
- **Inputs:** Imported mesh.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 选择单位 / Unit | `input_unit` | Unit of the imported mesh's coordinates | Shown: 毫米 (mm) highlighted in GS p.4; "mm" in Fig. 149 and 172 (default vs last-used UNCONFIRMED) | 米 m, 分米 dm, 厘米 cm, 毫米 mm, 英寸 inch (the list has a scroll bar, so more units may exist: UNCONFIRMED) | GS p.4; Fig. 149, 172 |
| "按撤销键即为使用上一次的单位." | `input_unit` (remembered) | Pressing Cancel uses the last unit | Last used | — | GS p.4 |
| Resolution (millimeter per pixel) | `resolution_mm_per_px` | Example of a unit-bearing parameter (lithophane) | Per generator | — | §2.5 (PDF p.20) |
| "Slant (deg)", "转角: 8 度", "Enter lighting angle (degree)." | — | Angles are shown in degrees | — | — | Fig. 10 (PDF p.17); GS p.12; f_168 |

- **Outputs:** n/a.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Lengths are millimetres wherever a source names a unit, although most panels print none: "you will have 0.2 mm gap" (VA67Jm3ijHg @05:00); Resolution in "millimeter per pixel" (§2.5, PDF p.20); a slot "expanded by 0.3 mm on both sides" (§2.15.3, PDF p.28); Puzzle tolerance "-0.2 mm" (§3.10.6, PDF p.82); "Color_105_86.jpg" means 105 by 86 mm (§2.22, PDF p.42).
  - Model size fields refer to the original model, not the generated one (§5 intro, PDF p.96); the 2019 deck shows them in the chosen unit (GS p.5–6; inferred).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Millimetres everywhere internally and in the UI; angles in degrees in the UI and radians in code (CLAUDE.md: Units).
  - On import, guess the unit from the bounding box, show the resulting size, and offer one-click ×10, ×25.4 and ×1000 alternatives; remember the choice per file in the project (fixes F20FZvL0r9g @11:00, the "very small" horse) (ours).
  - Every panel shows its unit next to the field (APP-PANEL); 3MF exports declare `unit="millimeter"` so slicers never mis-scale (PLAN §4: 3MF with units).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Scale on import; 3MF `unit` attribute.
- **Milestone:** M1 (part 9, after APP-SIZE; mm everywhere, unit-aware 3MF) → M3 (import unit chooser).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Whether LuBan writes exports in the chosen unit or always in millimetres.

### APP-FILES — Documents and project files (LuBan: File → New / Open / Save / Close, FGS/FGD scene files)

- **LuBan path:** File → New (Ctrl+N), Open (Ctrl+O), Save (Ctrl+S), Close (Ctrl+F4) (f_054 @03:32; GS p.2); FGD/FGS scene files (§2.12, PDF p.23; §5 intro, PDF p.96); "File → Close, then open a new model" (文件 → 关闭, 再打开一个新模型, GS p.17); "close the project" (F20FZvL0r9g @10:00).
- **What it makes:** Opening, saving and closing work. LuBan saves a scene as a pair of files; AD3D saves a project.
- **Fabrication:** n/a.
- **Inputs:** Meshes, images and FGS scenes (APP-IMPORT).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| File → Save, "LuBan format": XXX.fgs + XXX.fgd | `save_project` (action) | FGD stores the model data blocks; FGS stores the 3D scene settings such as viewing angle and lighting | — | — | §2.12 (PDF p.23); §5 intro (PDF p.96); blog password-protected-3d-file |
| Open an .fgs file | `open_project` (action) | Opens the scene and automatically loads the matching .fgd | — | — | §5 intro (PDF p.96) |
| "<photo>_Setting.txt" (e.g. "family_Setting.txt") | (inside the project) | "Human readable settings used to generate the lithophane" | Written on Save model (lithophane) | — | §2.12 (PDF p.23) |
| — (AD3D) | `autosave_interval_s` | Autosave interval | — (AD3D; suggest: 60, plus on every export) | 0 (off) – 600 | ours |
| — (AD3D) | `recent_files` | Recent projects | — (AD3D; suggest: 10) | 0–50 | PLAN §4 |
| — (AD3D) | `undo_depth` | Undo history length | — (AD3D; suggest: 200 steps) | — | PLAN §4 |

- **Outputs:** LuBan: `.fgs` + `.fgd`. AD3D: one `.ad3d` file (zip: JSON parameters + input assets + optional cached preview) (PLAN §1; research 07 §a).
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Save, Close and Set password are greyed until a document is open (f_054).
  - Opening the FGS file shows the model "in exact the same 3D environment when it was saved" (§2.12, PDF p.23).
  - Scene files written by generators use fixed or derived names: "LuBan_Model.fgd and LuBan_Model.fgs" in a lithophane export folder (§2.12, PDF p.23); "<model>_Asm3D.fgd/.fgs" in a Mesh → LuBan export folder (GS p.10).
  - To return to an old project's settings, LuBan's advice is to copy that project's MU_Setting.txt next to the application and restart (§2.12, PDF p.23); global settings double as project state.
  - No source describes undo or redo. The curved-arrow icons in the 2D toolbar (Fig. 7, PDF p.15; GS p.8) are unidentified (undo/redo or image rotation: UNCONFIRMED).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - The `.ad3d` project stores generator id and version, all parameters, transforms, input assets (embedded, or referenced with a content hash) and the machine profile; reopening regenerates exactly, because generators are pure and deterministic (PLAN §1). No global settings file to swap (fixes §2.12).
  - Undo/redo for every parameter and transform change; undo simply restores parameters (PLAN §1, §4).
  - Recent files, autosave and crash recovery (PLAN §4; ours).
  - Only our own formats plus open exchange formats: AD3D does not read or write FGS/FGD/SHP (CLAUDE.md: our own file formats; research 07 §f).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** serde JSON + `zip` crate (PLAN §1: io); content hashing for assets (e.g. blake3, suggest).
- **Milestone:** M1 (part 9, after APP-UNITS; save/load a Squama project, undo/redo).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - What LuBan's File → Save writes for a generated result versus an imported mesh (only the password workflow describes it).
  - Whether LuBan has undo at all.

### APP-IMPORT — Import: meshes, images and vectors (LuBan: File → Open, File → Import, "Browse")

- **LuBan path:** File → Open (Ctrl+O) and File → Import ▸ (f_054 @03:32); "Select photo" → "Browse" (§2 intro, PDF p.17); the "Select image" file dialog (research 01 §2 step 4; f_065 @04:16).
- **What it makes:** Loads the inputs that generators work on.
- **Fabrication:** n/a.
- **Inputs:**
  - Meshes: OBJ, PLY or STL ("打开一个 OBJ, PLY, 或 STL 文件格式的三维模型", GS p.2); LuBan scenes via .fgs (§5 intro, PDF p.96).
  - Images: the photo dialog's filter reads "All supported format (*.bmp;*.j…" (research 01 §2 step 4); BMP, JPG and PNG are used throughout the manual (§2.13.1, PDF p.24); FLT, LuBan's float image format (§3.10.8, PDF p.83).
  - Vectors: stencil and box lithophanes accept a vector template in DXF or SHP (blog vector-image-template); SHP, SVG and DXF outputs open in the 2D window (§3.10.7, PDF p.82; VA67Jm3ijHg @06:00).
  - Related video (title only): "LuBan Importing and rendering 3D voxel images" (eXA3n6sIaes).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| File → Open | `open_file` (action) | Open a mesh, image or scene | — | OBJ, PLY, STL (GS p.2); .fgs (§5 intro) | GS p.2; f_054 |
| File → Import ▸ | `import_file` (action) | Import into the current document | — | UNCONFIRMED (submenu never opened) | f_054 |
| Select photo — Browse | `input_image` | Photo input; several photos can be chosen at once for multi-photo shapes | — | "All supported format (*.bmp;*.j…" | §2 intro (PDF p.17); §2.16 (PDF p.28); research 01 §2 |
| (colour/grey to black-and-white) | `image_mode` | Some generators assume a black-and-white input and convert colour or grey photos automatically | Automatic (Projection) | — | VA67Jm3ijHg @00:00 |
| (photo order) | `input_images` (ordered) | LuBan orders multiple photos by file name | By file name | — | §2.15.1 (PDF p.26); §2.20 (PDF p.36) |
| Unit dialog | `input_unit` | See APP-UNITS | — | — | GS p.4 |

- **Outputs:** Loaded inputs.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - To change the order of photos on a poly-face lithophane, the user must rename the files (e.g. swap p2.jpg and p3.jpg) and select them again (§2.15.1, PDF p.26).
  - Mesh generators need the model opened first (f_052).
  - Dense models make some generators slow (§2.21.2, PDF p.42).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Drag-and-drop onto the window or onto a specific input slot (PLAN §4: drag-and-drop).
  - Images: PNG, JPEG, BMP, TIFF, GIF and WebP through the `image` crate; HEIC (iPhone photos) through macOS ImageIO in the Tauri host (suggest); EXIF orientation honoured (ours).
  - Meshes: STL (binary and ASCII), OBJ, PLY and 3MF (research 00 §4); vectors: SVG and DXF; depth maps as 16-bit PNG/TIFF or a float format of our own (replaces FLT).
  - Every imported mesh goes through the mesh doctor with a report (APP-MESH-DOCTOR; PLAN §4).
  - Multi-image slots show the order explicitly and allow drag-reordering (fixes §2.15.1 renaming).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** `image` + `fast_image_resize` (PLAN §1); `stl_io` or our own STL reader (PLAN §1); OBJ/PLY readers (e.g. `tobj`, `ply-rs`, suggest); 3MF via `zip` + an XML parser; SVG via `usvg` and DXF via a DXF crate (suggest).
- **Milestone:** M1 (part 9, after APP-IMAGE). Slices: images M1; meshes M3; vector templates M4–M5.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - The contents of LuBan's File → Import submenu and its full list of image formats.

- **Inputs:** The current result.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| "Color_W_H.jpg" (e.g. "Color_46_46.jpg", "Color_105_86.jpg") | `write_color_filter` | Colour-filter photo whose file name carries its size in mm | Written for all lithophane shapes except balloon and tattoo | — | §2.12 (PDF p.23); §2.22 (PDF p.42) |

- **Outputs:** As listed. Examples: Projection writes an "all in one" record plus film.stl and socket.stl, plus SHP and SVG (seen in the 2D window) and DXF (VA67Jm3ijHg @05:00–07:00); Layering saves each layer as DXF + SVG + STL (§3.6, PDF p.68); an assembly-type poly-face lithophane saves each face as its own STL (§2.15.3, PDF p.28); a lithophane save writes "Color_46_46.jpg", "family_LP_Model.stl", "LuBan_Model.fgd" and "LuBan_Model.fgs", "family_Setting.txt" and "MU_Setting.txt" (§2.12, PDF p.23); a 2019 Stack export wrote DXF, SHP and STL subfolders, an "_Asm3D" scene and a readme (GS p.10), although GS p.8 also promises SVG, which the p.10 listing does not show (discrepancy, UNCONFIRMED).
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Each save creates a new time-stamped folder (§2.12; GS p.9).
  - After a Stack save, LuBan nests the contours on cut sheets and shows them in a 2D window (§5.3.3, PDF p.102–103); Modular-cut modules are generated only on export (GS p.22–23).
  - An unregistered LuBan saves only files of 1 MB or less (§1.3, PDF p.9) — not applicable to AD3D.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - 3MF with millimetre units and several named parts (and colours where relevant) as the default print format; binary STL streamed to disk; OBJ only where colour matters (PLAN §4: better exports; CLAUDE.md: stream large exports).
  - SVG/DXF with separate cut, engrave and score layers (layer name plus colour); kerf offset applied to cut paths only (research 08 §2.6; PLAN §4).
  - An export dialog that previews exactly which files and parts will be written, with sizes (ours).
  - Readable, stable naming: `<project>/<generator>/<part>.3mf|stl|svg|dxf` plus a `manifest.json` (generator version, parameters, seed, units, part list, bed/sheet assignment) and a PDF assembly guide where relevant (PLAN §4: PDF assembly guides).
  - Every exported mesh passes `validate()` first (APP-VALIDATE; CLAUDE.md).
  - A `CHECKLIST.md` (print orientation, material, light setup) written next to the files for the owner's physical test (CLAUDE.md: physical testing handover).
  - Print orientation is shown in the preview before export, not applied silently (fixes §2.13.2).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Our own streamed binary STL writer; 3MF via `zip` + XML; SVG writer; DXF writer (ASCII R12/R2000, suggest); PDF via a Rust PDF crate (suggest) (PLAN §1: io).
- **Milestone:** M1 (part 9, after APP-IMPORT). Slices: STL/3MF M1; PDF assembly guides M3; SVG/DXF M4.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Squama's actual export files: Save model is never clicked in the video (research 01 §2).
  - The DXF version and units LuBan writes; G-code export (see APP-GCODE).

### APP-ASSEMBLE — Multi-object scenes and assembly (LuBan: File → Assemble)

  - SHP "is the default LuBan format. No other software can open" it (VA67Jm3ijHg @06:00); "The SHP format is defined by LuBan and can be opened in a LuBan 2D window" (§3.10.7, PDF p.82; §5 intro, PDF p.96).
  - Nested sheets show grey parts with red outlines and engraved labels such as "1.1", "2.1" (GS p.8).
  - After a Stack save the nested sheets open in a 2D window (§5.3.3, PDF p.102–103).

- **How we will do it better:**

  - Drag parts between sheets, lock positions, re-nest the rest (APP-NEST) (ours).
  - Exports go straight to SVG/DXF; no proprietary SHP (clean room, CLAUDE.md).
  - Rulers and a measuring tool in millimetres (ours).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** SVG rendering in React; Clipper2 or `i_overlay` for offsets (PLAN §1).
- **Milestone:** M4 (part 9, after FORM-SHEETS).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - The 2D window's "3D" menu and the rest of its Draw menu.
  - Whether SHP stores whole sheets with labels or single shapes.
