- **Outputs:** Images (in AD3D: an in-memory image passed to the generator, stored non-destructively in the project).
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Each LuBan workflow leaves the generator: switch to the 2D window, run several tools, export an image, switch back and load it (§2.13.1 crop to an aspect ratio; §2.20.4 crop to a template's rectangle; §3.2.8 outline image; §3.6.7, a ten-step recipe).
  - Distance-map units: "the length of a pixel corresponds to 100", so "-1000 0" keeps a 10-pixel outline (§3.2.8, PDF p.55).
  - Related 2D functions are specified in their own feature sections (placement in LuBan's menus UNCONFIRMED): halftone for laser engraving (blog halftone) and halftone lines ("Base line intensity, line width, gap between lines, and line angle can be adjusted", blog halftone-line), collage (File → Create → Collage, §2.17.1; blog collage), ID photo (blog id-photo), string art (blog string-art).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - A non-destructive image stack inside each generator's input slot: crop (with the target aspect ratio pre-applied), rotate, gamma/contrast/levels, channel, threshold, invert, blur/denoise and an outline band, all previewed live, with no window switching or re-import (PLAN §4: image controls; fixes §2.13.1 and §3.6.7).
  - Crop handles drawn on the image in the viewport (ours).
  - Images are kept as 32-bit floats internally and exported as 16-bit where precision matters (replaces FLT) (ours).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** `image`, `imageproc` (threshold, distance transform, connected components), `fast_image_resize` (PLAN §1).
- **Milestone:** M1 (part 9, after APP-LIGHT; crop, gamma, contrast for Squama) → M5 (threshold, outline, mask, arithmetic for Photo Magic).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Other items in LuBan's Tool menu and the default thresholds.

### APP-MESH-DOCTOR — Mesh doctor: diagnose and repair imports (LuBan: Mesh → Repair)

- **LuBan path:** 网格 → 修复 R ("Mesh → Repair") and 反转 R ("Reverse", gloss) in the 2019 Mesh menu (GS p.3); related video (title only): "LuBan Mesh Repair" (ce6XCcfx2DA).
- **What it makes:** Checks imported meshes and repairs them so that slicing, capping and Booleans work.
- **Fabrication:** All mesh-based features (M3+) depend on it.
- **Inputs:** STL, OBJ, PLY, 3MF meshes.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 修复 R (Repair) | `repair_mesh` (action) | Repair the mesh | — | UNCONFIRMED | GS p.3 |
| 反转 R (Reverse) | `flip_orientation` (action) | UNCONFIRMED (probably flips face orientation) | — | — | GS p.3 |
| — (AD3D) | `weld_tolerance_mm` | Merge coincident vertices | — (AD3D; suggest: 1e-4 × bounding-box diagonal) | > 0 | research 00 §6 |
| — (AD3D) | `fill_holes` | Close open boundaries | — (AD3D; suggest: on) | on, off | research 00 §3 |
| — (AD3D) | `voxel_fallback_mm` | Voxel size for the last-resort remesh | — (AD3D; suggest: automatic from model size) | > 0 | PLAN §6 |

- **Outputs:** A repaired, manifold mesh plus a report.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - LuBan's own symptoms of bad input: "Tiny" part files caused by defects in the original model (§4.5.2, PDF p.90); self-intersections from deformation of low-density models (§5.7, PDF p.112).
  - No diagnostic report is described in any source.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - A report of holes, non-manifold edges, flipped faces, self-intersections, separate shells and volume, with problem areas highlighted in the viewport and a one-click fix (PLAN §4: mesh doctor).
  - Runs automatically on every import, because import repair is on the critical path of every mesh feature (research 08 §2.11; PLAN §6).
  - Voxel remesh as the last resort (PLAN §6).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** manifold (validation, Booleans); a generalised winding-number inside/outside test (libigl, MPL-2.0, research 08 §2.10); voxel remesh (e.g. OpenVDB, licence UNCONFIRMED per research 07 §e); test corpus of 30–100 CC0 meshes including broken ones (PLAN §5).
- **Milestone:** M3 (part 9, after CUT-REPAIR).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - What LuBan's Repair and Reverse actually do.

- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**

### APP-MACHINES — Machine and material profiles (LuBan: printer setting, sheet size and tolerance per method)

- **LuBan path:** Mesh → Cut, Modular cut → printer settings (§4.5.1, PDF p.89); Mesh → LuBan Output section: sheet width/height/thickness, tolerance (Fig. 172, PDF p.96; GS p.6, 12, 18); 2019 3D-module printer base 矩形 / 圆形 (rectangle / circle) (GS p.22–23); blogs printer-bed-shape, multi-printer-modular-cut.
- **What it makes:** Reusable definitions of the owner's printer(s), laser, CNC router and materials, referenced by every generator instead of being retyped in each panel.
- **Fabrication:** 3D print (bed shape and build volume), laser (sheet size, kerf, measured thickness), CNC (tool diameter → dogbones).
- **Inputs:** n/a.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 打印机基面 (printer base): 矩形 / 圆形 | `printer_bed_shape` | Bed shape | 矩形 (rectangle) in the example | rectangle, circle | GS p.22–23; §4.5.1 (PDF p.89); blog printer-bed-shape |
| 打印空间 X / Y / Z 尺寸 (build volume) | `printer_build_x_mm`, `printer_build_y_mm`, `printer_build_z_mm` | Build volume | Example 200 / 150 / 140 | UNCONFIRMED | GS p.22; §4.5.1 |
| 基面直径 (base diameter) | `printer_bed_diameter_mm` | Diameter of a circular bed | Example 340 | UNCONFIRMED | GS p.23 |
| Relative speed; Quantity (multi-printer mode) | `printer_relative_speed`, `printer_count` | Used to give printers parts that finish at about the same time | UNCONFIRMED. Shown: 1 and 1 in the entry fields; the example table holds speeds 1, 2, 1 and quantities 1, 1, 3 (Fig. 161) | UNCONFIRMED; Quantity has a spin button (Fig. 161) | §4.5.1, Fig. 161 (PDF p.89–90); blog multi-printer-modular-cut |
| Sheet width / Sheet height (板材宽度 / 板材长度) | `sheet_width_mm`, `sheet_height_mm` | Sheet size | 600 × 450 (GS p.6, 12, 18); 800 × 400 (Fig. 172) | UNCONFIRMED | GS p.6; Fig. 172 (PDF p.96) |
| Sheet thickness (板材厚度) | `sheet_thickness_mm` (measured) | Sheet thickness (in Contour it is the gap between sheets, §5.2.1) | 5 (GS p.6, 12); 3.2 (GS p.18; Fig. 172) | UNCONFIRMED | GS p.6; Fig. 172; §5.2.1 (PDF p.99) |
| Tolerance (公差) | `fit_tolerance_mm` | Positive compensates material lost to laser cutting; negative compensates edge thickening in 3D printing | 0 (GS p.12; Fig. 172); −0.2 (3D module, GS p.22); −0.3 (poly-face slots, §2.15.3) | Signed mm | GS p.12; §2.15.3 (PDF p.28); VA67Jm3ijHg @05:00 |
| — (AD3D) | `laser_kerf_mm` | Beam width; cut paths are offset by kerf/2 | — (AD3D; suggest: 0.15) | ≥ 0 | research 08 §2.6; PLAN §4 |
| — (AD3D) | `cnc_tool_diameter_mm` | Router bit diameter; drives dogbones and tool compensation | — (AD3D; suggest: 3.175) | > 0 | research 08 §2.7; PLAN §4 |
| — (AD3D) | `bed_margin_mm` | Margin kept free for brim/skirt when fitting parts to the bed | — (AD3D; suggest: 5) | ≥ 0 | research 08 §2.11 |

- **Outputs:** Profiles stored in settings and referenced from projects.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - LuBan repeats sheet size, thickness and tolerance in each Mesh → LuBan method (GS p.6, 12, 18; Fig. 172).
  - In multi-printer mode LuBan tries to have all printers finish "roughly around the same time", while warning that set-up time, filament changes and failures cannot be modelled (§4.5.1, PDF p.89).
  - A part may count as fitting a printer only after a 90° rotation about Z (§4.5.2, PDF p.89–90).
  - Tolerance advice from the videos: negative for printed fits ("you will have 0.2 mm gap"), positive for laser-cut parts if zero is loose (VA67Jm3ijHg @05:00).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Named profiles, chosen once per project and used by every generator: printer (bed shape, build volume, nozzle), laser (bed, kerf), CNC (bed, tool diameter), material (measured thickness, fit allowance) (PLAN §4: machine profiles).
  - Kerf compensation that offsets every cut path by kerf/2 (outer contours outward, holes and slots inward) and leaves engraving untouched, plus slot width = measured thickness − kerf + fit allowance (research 08 §2.6); LuBan has one tolerance knob.
  - Automatic dogbone/T-bone reliefs on inside corners from the tool diameter (research 08 §2.7; PLAN §4).
  - Calibration coupons (fit and kerf test pieces) generated from the profile, so the owner measures instead of guessing (research 07 §e.4).
  - The active printer's build volume or sheet is drawn in the viewport (APP-VIEWPORT).
  - Sheet size comes from the active laser or CNC profile (e.g. up to 3000 × 1500 mm for the owner's 3015, or a stock-sheet size within it) instead of a per-method value that differs between builds (600 × 450 in GS p.6; 800 × 400 in Fig. 172) (START_HERE; ours).
  - Bed-slinger awareness: the printer profile records which axis moves, so tall parts printed standing (Squama plates, lithophanes) are oriented with their face parallel to Y on the CR-6 SE (START_HERE).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Clipper2 / `i_overlay` for offsets and dogbones (research 03 §13; PLAN §1).
- **Milestone:** M1 (part 9, after APP-SETTINGS). Slices: printer profile M1 (Squama tiling to the bed, PLAN §3); laser and CNC profiles M4.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - LuBan's printer defaults when none are shown in an example.
  - The owner's machines are now recorded (docs/START_HERE.md): a Creality CR-6 SE printer, 235 × 235 × 250 mm, a bed-slinger (bed moves in Y); a "3015" laser (3000 × 1500 mm class); a "1325" CNC router (1300 × 2500 mm class). (suggest: ship these three as the initial profiles.) Still open: whether the laser is fiber or CO2, which sets kerf and material defaults (START_HERE open question 1), and the router's tooling, which sets `cnc_tool_diameter_mm`.

### APP-NEST — Nesting engine for sheets and print beds (LuBan: Nesting compact / ordered / balanced, Layout, batch nesting)

- **LuBan path:** Contour → Nesting (§5.2.5, PDF p.101); Stack → 布局 (Layout) 紧凑 (compact) (GS p.6); 网格 → 布局 N (Mesh → Layout) (GS p.3); Stack contours are nested on cut sheets on save (§5.3.3, PDF p.102); blog batch-slicing ("optionally nest the models"); Intro p.3 lists 平面套料 (2D nesting) and 立体套料 (3D nesting) among the core technologies; video (title only) "LuBan 2D Nesting" (Lx5tmdVsGdk).
- **What it makes:** Arranges 2D parts on cut sheets and 3D parts on print beds.
- **Fabrication:** Laser/CNC sheets; print beds.
- **Inputs:** Parts (2D outlines or 3D meshes) and a machine profile.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Nesting: compact / ordered / balanced; 布局: 紧凑 | `nest_mode` | compact packs as tightly as possible regardless of order; ordered keeps consecutive numbers on each sheet; balanced is a compromise | 紧凑 (compact) in the Stack example | compact, ordered, balanced | §5.2.5 (PDF p.101); GS p.6 |
| — (AD3D) | `nest_spacing_mm` | Gap between parts (at least the kerf) | — (AD3D; suggest: max(kerf, 2)) | ≥ 0 | research 08 §2.6 |
| — (AD3D) | `nest_rotations` | Allowed rotations | — (AD3D; suggest: 0/90/180/270 on sheets; free about Z on beds) | — | research 04 §14 |
| — (AD3D) | `nest_lock_grain` | Keep the wood-grain direction | — (AD3D; suggest: off) | on, off | research 04 §14 |
| — (AD3D) | `nest_sheet_margin_mm` | Unused border around each sheet | — (AD3D; suggest: 5) | ≥ 0 | research 04 §14 |
| — (AD3D) | `nest_time_limit_s` | Solver time budget | — (AD3D; suggest: 5 for preview, 30 for final) | > 0 | research 07 §e.6 |

- **Outputs:** Part placements per sheet/bed; SVG/DXF sheets or a multi-part 3MF plate.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - The nesting choice decides how contour frames are laid out on cut sheets (§5.2.5, PDF p.101).
  - The original method sorts parts largest first and places them first-fit (Sass 2025 via research 04 §14).
  - Observed on the 2019 Stack sheet "Sheet_1.shp" (GS p.8; observations, UNCONFIRMED as rules): parts packed in a strip along one sheet edge with outlines touching or nearly touching (no visible spacing), and a small part placed inside the hole of ring part 1.1 (hole nesting). The lattice-cube strips are nested in rows on one sheet (Intro p.16).
  - The 2019 Introduction lists 3-D nesting [立体套料] as a core technology feeding 3D printing (Intro p.3); 网格 → 布局 N (Mesh → Layout, GS p.3) may be that tool (UNCONFIRMED).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - True-shape nesting that uses holes for small parts, across several fixed-size sheets, with a time limit and a greedy fallback (research 04 §14; research 08 §2.9).
  - Runs live in the 2D view, and manual drag adjustments survive re-nesting (APP-2D) (ours).
  - A minimum part spacing of at least the kerf is enforced and hole nesting is an explicit option, instead of parts that touch on the sheet (GS p.8) and so share or burn a cut edge (research 08 §2.6).
  - 3D bed packing for printed parts, as LuBan's "3D nesting" claims (Intro p.3) (ours).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** No-fit-polygon search as in SVGnest (MIT); packingsolver (MIT); sparrow/jagua-rs (Rust; strip packing only, research 08 §2.9); skyline/shelf fallback; Clipper2/`i_overlay` offsets (research 03 §12).
- **Milestone:** M4 (part 9, after FORM-ETCHED; sheets); 3D bed packing Later.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - LuBan's spacing between nested parts, its rotation rules and its 3D-nesting UI.

### APP-LABELS — Part labels and naming (LuBan: labels, text size, part number, prefix)

- **LuBan path:** Stack labels and Text size (§5.3.3, PDF p.102–103); 字体大小 (font size) slider in Hash and Plate (GS p.12, 18); Modular-cut part number, start number and prefix (§4.5.2, PDF p.89–90).
- **What it makes:** Labels that identify parts on screen, on the parts themselves (engraved or imprinted) and in file names.
- **Fabrication:** Laser engraving of labels on cut parts (§5.3.3); part numbers imprinted on printed parts (§4.5.2).
- **Inputs:** Parts.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Text size (3D label); 字体大小 | `label_size_mm` | Size of the labels displayed in 3D | 16 in the 2019 examples (unit UNCONFIRMED) | UNCONFIRMED | §5.3.3 (PDF p.102); GS p.12, 18 |
| (2D label size) | `label_height_2d` | Size of labels on the cut sheets | Fixed in LuBan ("That text size cannot be changed.") | — (AD3D: adjustable) | §5.3.3 (PDF p.103) |
| Part number (Yes/No) | `imprint_part_numbers` | Imprint the part number on the part's surface | UNCONFIRMED | Yes, No | §4.5.2 (PDF p.90) |
| Start number | `part_start_number` | First part number (optional) | UNCONFIRMED (file names start at "Part_1") | Integer | §4.5.2 (PDF p.89–90) |
| Prefix | `part_name_prefix` | Replaces "Part_" in part file names (prefix "er" gives er1, er2…) (optional) | "Part_" | Text | §4.5.2 (PDF p.90) |
| (label scheme) | `label_scheme` | layer.contour[.segment], e.g. "2.1" or "10.3.4" (Stack); "P1_Part_1" with several printers | — | — | §5.3.3 (PDF p.102); §4.5.2 (PDF p.89) |

- **Outputs:** Engraved/imprinted text; names used in files and in the parts list.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Labels are meant to be engraved so the parts can be found during assembly (§5.3.3, PDF p.103).
  - An imprinted part number "may not be clearly seen by default"; turning on edges helps (§4.5.2, Fig. 162, PDF p.90).
  - On the 2019 nested sheet the engraved labels look larger on large parts and tiny on small ones (GS p.8; an observation, UNCONFIRMED as a rule; it does not contradict §5.3.3's "cannot be changed", which is about the user).
  - Numbering order in the original method: bottom-front first, increasing with elevation, then left to right (Sass 2025 via research 04 §13).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - One label engine for 3D view, sheets and file names, so names always match (ours).
  - Single-stroke engraving font for lasers; embossed or debossed text with a depth parameter for prints; auto-fit inside the part (pole of inaccessibility) while avoiding slots and holes (research 04 §13).
  - Adjustable 2D label size with a fit check (fixes §5.3.3).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Single-stroke (Hershey-style) font data, keeping its attribution notice (research 08 §2.13); polylabel placement; manifold for 3D text (research 00 §3).
- **Milestone:** M3 (part 9, after CUT-LABEL; part numbers) → M4 (engraved sheet labels).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - LuBan's label defaults and units.

### APP-ESTIMATES — Measures and estimates (LuBan: Measure section, File size)

- **LuBan path:** 度量 / Measure section at the bottom of Mesh → LuBan panels (§5 intro, PDF p.96; GS p.6, 12, 18, 24); "File size" read-out (§2.6, PDF p.20; Fig. 8, PDF p.15; Fig. 10, PDF p.17).
- **What it makes:** Read-only figures about the result.
- **Fabrication:** Planning print/cut time and material.
- **Inputs:** The current result.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 部件 (Parts) | `part_count` | Number of parts of an assembly (Contour, Stack, Hash, Plate) | — (examples 16, 21, 30, 5) | — | §5 intro (PDF p.96); GS p.6, 12, 18, 24 |
| 加工用时 (Machining time) | `machine_time_min` | Estimated machine time | — (examples 6 min, 20 min, 16 min, 16 h) | — | GS p.6, 12, 18, 24 |
| 组装用时 (Assembly time) | `assembly_time_min` | Estimated assembly time | — (examples 16 min, 24 min, 41 min, 3 min) | — | GS p.6, 12, 18, 24 |
| 总用时 (Total time) | `total_time_min` | Machine plus assembly time | — (examples 22 min, 57 min, 16 h) | — | GS p.6, 18, 24 |
| (model size) | `result_size_mm` | Size of the generated model (Cocoon, Relief, Spin, Spring, Wave) | — | — | §5 intro (PDF p.96) |
| File size | `estimated_file_size` | Predicted size of the model file on disk (read-only) | — (examples 13 KB, 5 MB) | — | §2.6 (PDF p.20); Fig. 10; Fig. 8 |

- **Outputs:** n/a.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - File size is "readable only" and is reduced most effectively by increasing Resolution (§2.6, PDF p.20); at 10, 1 and 0.2 mm/pixel a tattoo lithophane is 1 MB, 8 MB and 190 MB (Fig. 58, §2.21.2, PDF p.42).
  - LuBan's prominence of file size ties in with its 1 MB save limit for unregistered users (§1.3, PDF p.9).
  - Times are shown in minutes [分钟] or hours [小时] (GS p.6, p.24); the decks never explain the time model.
  - With an empty method (方法 = 无) the Output and Measure sections are blank (GS p.5); for 3-D modules (today's Modular cut) the measures stay blank until Export parts is pressed, and wireframe imprint never fills them (GS p.22, p.24, p.26–27).
  - Related video (title only): "How to get accurate estimate of material and time of a big 3D printing project" (R0YZ624Z6KU).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Live triangle count, STL and 3MF size, bounding box and volume for every result; for print parts a rough filament mass and time from the printer profile; for laser parts total cut length, engrave length, sheet count and utilisation (ours; PLAN §4: machine profiles).
  - Per-part figures in the parts list (APP-OBJECTS); a warning before writing very large files with the option to stream or lower resolution (research 00 §6: about 6 M triangles, ~300 MB STL at 0.1 mm/px) (CLAUDE.md: stream large exports).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Counts and volumes from `ad3d-core`; time models parameterised by the machine profile (suggest).
- **Milestone:** M1 (part 9, after APP-OBJECTS; triangles, file size, dimensions) → M4 (laser metrics).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - How LuBan computes machining and assembly time.

## 2. Lithophane

### Lithophane: shared concepts and parameters (2.1–2.12)

A lithophane is a translucent part whose thickness follows the darkness of a photo, so the photo appears when light shines through it; LuBan says it can be 3D printed or CNC-machined in any material that lets light through (§2 intro, PDF p.17). Every LuBan lithophane shape is made under File → Create → Lithophane, in one control panel. §2.1–2.12 describe its shared settings: shape list, photo picker, positive/negative, exterior/interior, model size, min/max thickness, resolution, predicted file size, border, base and socket, hanger, support, backlight simulation and Save model (§2 intro, §2.1–2.12, Fig. 10, PDF p.17–23). Not every shape has every setting: exterior/interior is stated only for Arc and Sphere (§2.14, §2.17), and base/socket, hanger and support exist on "several" shapes only (§2.8–2.10). The function launched on 2019-04-25 as "Turn any 2D photo into a 3D printed photo with a frame" (blog: lithophane-1st-release). This section specifies that shared core once (LITH-COMMON) and gives each shared mechanism that needs its own geometry or UI its own entry (LITH-BASE-SOCKET, LITH-HANGER, LITH-EDGE-SUPPORT, LITH-BACKLIGHT-PREVIEW, LITH-EXPORT); the shape entries from §2.13 onward point to these entries for the shared settings and specify their own surface mapping and shape-specific options. Conventions: lengths in mm, angles in degrees in the UI, AD3D keys in snake_case, axes as in LuBan's viewport (X width, Z height, Y depth; Fig. 10).

---

#### LITH-COMMON — Lithophane core: shared settings and photo-to-thickness pipeline (LuBan: Lithophane control panel, shared settings)

- **LuBan path:** File → Create → Lithophane. Control parameters sit in the left panel and a live 3D display on the right; the shape is picked from the "Shape" drop-down list and the photo with "Select photo" → "Browse" (manual §2 intro, Fig. 10, PDF p.17). Shared settings: §2.1–2.12 (PDF p.17–23).
- **What it makes:** A closed, two-sided shell with one smooth surface and one rough (relief) surface; the thickness between them follows the photo's intensity, so the photo shows when the part is lit from behind (§2 intro; §2.2, Fig. 12, PDF p.18). This entry defines the controls and the photo → thickness → mesh pipeline that every shape reuses. LuBan reuses the same min/max thickness and resolution semantics in Photo magic → Puzzle (§3.10.2, §3.10.4, PDF p.81), and the cover of the Pandora light box "can be a customized lithophane" (blog: pandora).
- **Fabrication:**
  - 3D printing or CNC machining, "as long as light can penetrate the material in use" (§2 intro). The chapter's practical advice is all about printing (§2.23). Laser: not mentioned by the sources.
  - Orientation: print flat lithophanes standing up. A printer's X/Y resolution beats its layer height, so a vertical print carries richer thickness variation (§2.23, PDF p.44). LuBan rotates a slanted Flat lithophane back to vertical when saving (§2.13.2, PDF p.24). The Squama video gives the same advice, "just as with a lithophane" (research 01 §2).
  - Slicer support "can be disabled", because removing it may damage the rough surface. Where it must be used (e.g. a sphere), orient the part so support touches only the smooth surface. A small sphere may print without support, letting the printer close the upper gap (§2.23, PDF p.45; §2.17, PDF p.31).
  - Print settings from the manual (§2.23, PDF p.44–45):
    - speed 30–50 mm/s rather than 80–100 mm/s, because high speed makes the printer vibrate and leaves line strips;
    - a properly tightened belt, since a loose one causes vibration;
    - an extruder flushed regularly by running filament through it at a high feed rate; dust can clog it, extrude unevenly and leave regions lacking material;
    - layer height usually half the nozzle diameter, e.g. 0.1 mm with a 0.2 mm nozzle; a smaller nozzle gives a higher-resolution lithophane but a longer print.
  - Thickness trade-off: a thick lithophane is strong but needs a strong light; more depth variation gives more contrast but makes support more likely (§2.4, PDF p.19).
  - Material: Eryone silk silver filament produced a sharp interior lithophane with min/max thickness 0.6/2.4 mm (Fig. 14, PDF p.18).
  - CNC: details finer than the machine's resolution cannot be made (§2.5, PDF p.20).
- **Inputs:**
  - Photo via "Select photo" → "Browse" (§2 intro, Fig. 10).
    - BMP, JPG and PNG are implied: the §2.13.1 workflow exports one of these from LuBan's 2D window and loads it (PDF p.24).
    - LuBan's image picker in Projection → Squama shows the filter "All supported format (*.bmp;*.j…", which is cut off (research 01 §2).
    - The full format list is UNCONFIRMED.
  - Colour photos are accepted (inference). LuBan writes a colour-filter image for every shape except Balloon and Tattoo, and Fig. 62 shows the colour original beside it (§2.12; §2.22, PDF p.42, p.45; blog: lithophane-9th-release).
  - Photo count depends on the shape: one or several for poly-face (§2.15.1) and cylinder/cone/vase (§2.16), up to two for balloon (§2.20), and one for sphere (§2.17.1).
    - Poly-face and balloon order the photos by file name (§2.15.1, §2.20).
    - The order for cylinder/cone/vase is UNCONFIRMED.
    - The shape entries own those rules.
  - Template image (Stencil, Balloon) or 3D model (Tattoo): see those shape entries (§2.19–2.21).

- **Outputs:** One closed lithophane mesh per shape. Since 2020 the base, lamp socket and lithophane are one body (blog: lithophane-update). Save model writes it as `<photo>_LP_Model.stl` together with the other files listed in LITH-EXPORT (§2.12, PDF p.23). The poly-face "Assembly" option instead saves each face as a separate STL, held together by a base and a cap (§2.15.3; see LITH-POLY-ASSEMBLY).
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Changes in a text box apply only when Enter (Return) is pressed. Drop-downs, radio buttons, check boxes and spin buttons update the display at once. There is no Apply button (§1.8, Fig. 9, PDF p.15–16; §2.3, Fig. 15, PDF p.19).
    - The Squama video shows the same behaviour (video Wd26qsSIRY8 @05:11), and so does a 2018 Mesh → LuBan walkthrough (luban-docs Get started p.6, per docs/wip/spec-sections/00-luban-docs-notes.md §4.1).
  - Fig. 10's panel is scrolled to the top: the Border row is cut off and everything below it is out of view. That is why the labels of the base, socket, hanger, support, backlight and Save model controls are UNCONFIRMED (Fig. 10, PDF p.17).
  - Positive resembles the photo's intensity distribution; Negative inverts it (§2.1, Fig. 11).
  - Exterior: rough surface toward the viewer, smooth surface toward the light. Interior: the reverse (§2.2).
    - Exterior prints generally look sharper, because of how light scatters in the material (§2.2, Fig. 13). Some filaments make interior prints sharp too (Fig. 14).
    - Interior surprises viewers: without backlight they see only a smooth surface (§2.2, PDF p.19).
    - LuBan's renderer makes interior look better than exterior; the manual calls this "only a rendering issue" (§2.2). "Some LuBan users" therefore tune settings on the interior display and switch to exterior just before saving (§2.14, PDF p.26).
    - On an Arc the convex surface is the exterior (§2.14). On a Sphere, switching flips the print orientation so slicer support touches only the smooth side (§2.17, PDF p.31).
    - The manual adds Exterior/Interior to the Arc "in addition" to the Flat settings (§2.14), so Flat appears not to offer it (inference).
    - The interior option arrived in the 4th release, 2019-06-01: "Lithophane on the interior surface" (blog: lithophane-4th-release).
  - Model size X, Y and Z are text boxes (§2.3).
    - Flat and Arc lock the aspect ratio to the photo: changing X (then Enter) changes Z, and vice versa (§2.13.1; §2.15: they "adjust the model size to include an entire photo"). A 100 × 50 mm Flat needs a 2:1 photo. It is cropped beforehand in any image editor, or in LuBan's 2D window with Tool → Body → Crop and typed coordinates (§2.13.1, PDF p.23–24, Fig. 23).
    - A Rectangle sets X, Y and Z independently; other poly-face shapes derive Y from X and the face count and crop the photo from its centre (§2.15, PDF p.26).
  - Resolution is in mm per pixel, so a smaller value means finer detail and a larger file (§2.5, Fig. 17).
    - Photo pixels needed across X = Model size X / Resolution; e.g. 50 mm / 0.1 = 500 px (§2.5).
    - Going finer than the photo's own resolution, or than the printer's or CNC machine's resolution, gains nothing (§2.5).
    - The manual advises against shrinking files with Mesh → Simplify (non-uniform resolution, slow); raise Resolution instead (§2.5, §2.6, PDF p.20).
  - File size is read-only and predicts the model's size on disk (§2.6). Fig. 10 shows "13 KB" while the preview shows a blank plate, i.e. before a photo is loaded (reading of Fig. 10).
  - Border size 0 means no border. A positive Border size with Dark selected shows a Border thickness box, which "must be larger than the Max thickness by 5%" (§2.7). Fig. 18's values fit the rule: 4 ≥ 1.05 × 3.2 = 3.36, taking Fig. 10's Max thickness (our arithmetic).
    - Reading of Fig. 18 (PDF p.21): without a border the plate's edges follow the relief and look ragged; Bright gives a thin light frame; Dark gives a thick frame standing proud of the image.
  - Base/socket, hanger and support exist only on some shapes (§2.8–2.10): see LITH-BASE-SOCKET, LITH-HANGER and LITH-EDGE-SUPPORT.
  - Settings persist between sessions in `MU_Setting.txt` next to the program. It is loaded at start-up, and defaults are applied if it is missing (§1.6, PDF p.14).
    - On Windows, after installing from setup.msi, LuBan should be run once as administrator. The manual says this lets it read the settings file in "C:\Program Files (x86)\LuBan" (§1.6, PDF p.14–15).
    - The install video says it lets LuBan save the settings file, after which it remembers the last-used settings (video DzvYxTm8pbo @00:08–00:09).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - **Live preview while dragging** any slider, instead of type-then-Enter (§1.8, §2.3, §2.5–2.7). During a drag the pixel size is coarsened automatically so each update stays within 50 ms; full resolution follows on release (CLAUDE.md speed rule; PLAN §1 latest-wins queue). Thickness-only changes (min, max, polarity, tone) can update the GPU preview without remeshing (suggest).
  - **"Pixel size (mm)" instead of "Resolution"**, which reads backwards (§2.5 has to explain that smaller means finer). The panel shows what the value implies: the photo pixels needed (§2.5 formula), the photo's own pixel pitch, and the printer's limit from the machine profile. It warns when the pixel size is finer than either limit (§2.5 reasons 1–2; nozzle/2 rule of thumb in §3.3.6 and §2.23).
  - **Exact output size per format before export:** triangle count, binary STL bytes (84-byte header + 50 bytes per triangle) and 3MF, instead of one predicted figure (§2.6). A warning appears above a size threshold, and the export streams to disk (CLAUDE.md).
  - **Smaller files without LuBan's simplification trade-off** (§2.5): the rough side stays on a uniform grid, while the smooth side, walls, frame and base are triangulated from their boundaries only. That is lossless for the image and roughly halves the triangle count against a naive matching back grid (our estimate).
  - **Validated, interdependent inputs at the moment of change:** max > min > 0; frame thickness ≥ 1.05 × max (§2.7); socket diameter < opening (§2.17.3); strict number parsing (LuBan's Squama panel accepted "4j" as 4; research 01 §3).
  - **Built-in photo controls:**
    - a crop box locked to the model's aspect ratio (`size_mode` = `crop_to_size`), replacing the 2D-window crop with typed coordinates (§2.13.1, Fig. 23);
    - gamma and contrast (PLAN §4 lists gamma, contrast and crop as Squama image controls), plus rotate/flip and levels (ours);
    - drag-and-drop, plus a reorderable photo list with empty-face slots for multi-photo shapes. LuBan orders photos by file name, so swapping two means renaming files, and an empty face needs a white image with a black border (§2.15.1, Fig. 29; §2.20).
  - **Measured tone curve** (ours): intensity is mapped to thickness through a transmission curve fitted to a photo of a printed step wedge, per filament, stored in the material profile. The sources show no tone control in LuBan beyond Positive/Negative and Min/Max thickness (§2.1, §2.4; Fig. 10). This is the same idea as the Squama calibration tile (PLAN §4).
  - **Interior on every shape, Flat included** (ours), with automatic mirroring so the photo always reads correctly from the viewer's side. LuBan states the option only for Arc and Sphere (§2.14, §2.17).
  - **Printability checks:**
    - maximum relief slope (overhang) in the chosen print orientation, with a warning or an optional slope limiter (`max_overhang`), because deeper relief makes support more likely (§2.4);
    - min thickness against the nozzle line width ("thin spots below the nozzle width", research 04 §B.1).
  - **Bed-fit check of the whole part** (photo, frame, base, hanger, stabilisers) in the print orientation, against the printer profile (PLAN §4 machine profiles; research 07 §(a) build-volume outline). Optional tiling with alignment keys reuses Squama's tiler (PLAN §3 M1), as an alternative to LuBan's spiral-and-hot-water route for long lithophanes (§2.18).
  - **CNC tool preview** (ours): show what a ball-nose cutter of the profile's diameter can actually reach (§2.5 machine resolution; PLAN §4 CNC tool diameter).
  - **Honest exterior/interior preview** through LITH-BACKLIGHT-PREVIEW, so the tune-on-interior-then-switch workaround is unnecessary (§2.2, §2.14).
  - **Projects, presets, undo/redo** (PLAN §4), instead of one global `MU_Setting.txt` that needs admin rights on Windows (§1.6) and a copy-and-restart to roll back (§2.12).
  - **Multi-core, cancellable generation** with rayon (PLAN §1, §4), and CLI/batch, e.g. "a lithophane for every photo in a folder" (PLAN §4).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  1. Decode the photo (`image` crate), apply crop/rotation, convert to luminance (suggest: linearise sRGB, Rec. 709 weights), then area-resample to nx = round(size_x / pixel_size) + 1 columns (and likewise rows) with `fast_image_resize` (PLAN §1; §2.5).
  2. Tone and polarity: I′ = curve(levels(I)). Positive: t = t_min + (1 − I′)(t_max − t_min); Negative uses I′ in place of (1 − I′) (research 04 §B.1; research 00 §3). LuBan's own curve is UNCONFIRMED.
  3. Shell: map (u,v) to the shape's surface S(u,v) (shape entries). Smooth surface = S; rough surface = S offset along the normal by t, on the viewer side (`viewer`) or the light side (`light`). Join the two along the boundary with wall strips, sharing boundary vertices exactly so every edge has two faces. That makes the shell watertight with consistent winding by construction, with no booleans (research 04 §B.1). A regular grid with shared indices avoids the T-junctions and saddle pinches that broke the Squama prototypes (PLAN §6).
  4. Frame: extra grid rings at constant thickness inside the same grid (ours).
  5. Attachments (LITH-BASE-SOCKET, LITH-HANGER, LITH-EDGE-SUPPORT) are joined locally, through shared boundary loops or a manifold union of only the small attachment region (manifold through its C API, PLAN §1).
  6. `validate()` (edge-manifold, watertight, consistent winding, no degenerate triangles), property tests with randomised parameters, and criterion benchmarks at preview and full resolution (PLAN §5; CLAUDE.md).
  7. Scale: 200 × 150 mm at 0.1 mm/px is 3M samples, about 6M triangles and about 300 MB of binary STL (our arithmetic; matches research 00 §6). LuBan's own example: a tattoo lithophane at 0.2 mm/px came to 190 MB (Fig. 58, PDF p.42). So: row-parallel rayon meshing, a decimated display mesh, and a streamed STL (PLAN §1). Research 00 §6 suggests a 0.2 mm/px default.
  8. Reference implementations (research 03 §3): s1lentCommit/stl-ready-image (MIT), yomboprime/lithofun (MIT), colbrydi/Lithophane (MIT), furti/FreeCAD-Lithophane (MIT), and muldjord/lithomaker (GPL-3.0; may be read or ported for personal use, CLAUDE.md).
- **Milestone:** M2 (part 9, first in its row; PLAN §3: Flat, Arc, Cylinder/Cone/Vase and Sphere first; backlight preview; base/socket/hanger).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Defaults taken from screenshots (Fig. 10, Fig. 15, Fig. 18) may be last-used values rather than factory defaults, because LuBan keeps settings between sessions in `MU_Setting.txt` and "will be able to remember the last used" settings (§1.6; video DzvYxTm8pbo @00:08–00:09).
  - The intensity → thickness curve (research 04 assumes linear) and the grayscale conversion are not stated.
  - The default pixel size: §2.21.2 says 0.1 mm/px for every non-tattoo shape, but Fig. 10 shows 0.12. It may be photo-dependent or an older default.
  - Ranges and limits for size, thickness and pixel size, and whether LuBan rejects max ≤ min or min = 0.
  - The Exterior/Interior default, and which shapes offer it beyond Arc and Sphere. Fig. 13 and Fig. 14 show cylinder- and vase-like interior prints.
  - Whether Model size includes the frame (this changes the final dimensions and the bed fit). Suggest: Model size = overall outer size.
  - The thickness of a Bright border (it looks thin in Fig. 18; suggest: Min thickness), and whether a Dark frame stands proud on the rough side, the smooth side or both (Fig. 18 suggests the rough side).
  - What LuBan does when Border thickness ≤ 1.05 × Max thickness: clamp, warn or nothing.
  - How X and Z react when a photo with a different aspect ratio is loaded. In Squama, X stays and Z follows the image (research 01 §2).
  - Photo format and size limits, and EXIF orientation handling.
  - Which file format the File size prediction assumes, and how accurate it is.
  - Channel videos with no transcript in the repo may show panel defaults: fKl1rsrthcg "LuBan Lithophane" (0:45), ba6xj2IISNU "LuBan Lithophane 2" (13:05), lIWNKgNKYsU "Relief on Lithophane", SyBoLFeHbV4 "Add text to Lithophane", 9scNC9aa5D0 "Easter egg lithophane" (channel videos_dated.txt, titles only). "Add text to Lithophane" hints at a text workflow; its content is UNCONFIRMED, but a caption tool in our photo controls would cover it.
  - LuBan's menu bar has a Batch menu (Fig. 10). The only batch feature in the blog is slicing ("Slice a batch of models and optionally nest the models", blog: batch-slicing), so whether it batches lithophanes is UNCONFIRMED.
  - The labels and positions of the controls below Border, which Fig. 10 cuts off.

#### LITH-BASE-SOCKET — Stand and lamp fitting (LuBan: Base and Socket)

- **LuBan path:** File → Create → Lithophane, then the base/socket fields of the chosen shape (§2.8, PDF p.21):
  - Flat and Arc: base length, base thickness, socket diameter, O-shape/U-shape, socket height (§2.13.3, PDF p.25; §2.14).
  - Rectangle, Hexagon, Octagon, Dodecagon: base thickness (blog: lithophane-update).
  - Cylinder, Cone, Vase: solid/hollow base, socket diameter, socket height (§2.16.2, PDF p.30).
  - Sphere: socket diameter, base thickness, socket height (§2.17.3, PDF p.34).
- **What it makes:** The part that lets a lithophane stand on its own or sit on a light source: a stand behind a flat or arc photo, a floor or ring at the bottom of a revolved shade, or a funnel narrowing from a sphere's opening into a socket tube (reading of Fig. 41), optionally with a socket sized to a lamp (§2.8, §2.13.3, §2.16.2, §2.17.3).
- **Fabrication:** Printed as part of the lithophane (one body since 2020, blog: lithophane-update). A slanted Flat printed upright needs some support under its base (§2.13.2, PDF p.24). A solid base makes a watertight vessel that can hold water and a waterproof LED (§2.16.2).
- **Inputs:** The lithophane shell from LITH-COMMON and the shape entry, plus the lamp's measured size. For the Sphere the manual says the socket diameter is the socket's inner diameter (§2.17.3); other shapes do not say.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base length (Flat, Arc; panel label UNCONFIRMED) | `base_length` | Length of the stand extending toward the back; 0 hides the base | UNCONFIRMED (30 mm in Fig. 25) | ≥ 0; upper limit UNCONFIRMED | §2.13.3; Fig. 25 (PDF p.25); §2.14 |
| base thickness (Flat, Arc, Rectangle, Hexagon, Octagon, Dodecagon, Sphere) | `base_thickness` | Thickness of the stand or base plate, mm (Fig. 25). On the Sphere, Fig. 41 suggests it sets the wall thickness of the socket tube: from 4 to 10 the tube gets fatter while its bore stays the same (our reading) | UNCONFIRMED (Fig. 25: 4 and 8 mm; Fig. 41: 4 and 10) | UNCONFIRMED | §2.13.3; Fig. 25; blog: lithophane-update; §2.17.3; Fig. 41 (PDF p.34) |
| solid / hollow (Cylinder, Cone, Vase) | `base_fill` | Solid floor (watertight) or open base that can take a socket | UNCONFIRMED | `solid`, `hollow` | §2.16.2; Fig. 36 (PDF p.30); blog: lithophane-update |
| socket diameter | `socket_diameter` | Diameter of the lamp socket, mm; 0 = no socket. Inner diameter on the Sphere (§2.17.3); elsewhere UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED (Fig. 41: 50 and 30) | > 0 enables the socket. Flat/Arc: also needs base length ≠ 0. Cylinder/Cone/Vase: needs a hollow base. Sphere: "should be less than the opening diameter", otherwise a warning on Enter | §2.13.3; §2.16.2; §2.17.3 |
| O-shape / U-shape (Flat, Arc) | `socket_style` | Closed ring (tube) or open U slot at the end of the stand | UNCONFIRMED | `ring` (O-shape), `slot` (U-shape) | §2.13.3; Fig. 26 (PDF p.25); blog: lithophane-update |
| socket height | `socket_height` | Height of the socket tube, mm; on Flat/Arc only for O-shape | UNCONFIRMED (Fig. 26: 10 and 20 mm; Fig. 41: 10 and 30) | UNCONFIRMED | §2.13.3; §2.16.2; §2.17.3; Fig. 26; Fig. 41 |
| Opening diameter (Sphere; read-only) | `opening_diameter` (derived) | Opening computed from sphere angle and diameter; upper limit for the socket | — (Fig. 40 shows 53.7 with "Sphere angle (deg)" 290 and "Model diameter" 100) | read-only | §2.17.2 (PDF p.33); Fig. 40 (PDF p.34) |
| — (AD3D only) | `socket_clearance` | Fit allowance added to the measured lamp diameter, mm (sign convention to match the global tolerance convention) | n/a in LuBan (suggest: 0.3, the size of LuBan's example poly-face slot tolerance of −0.3, §2.15.3) | 0–1 (suggest) | AD3D proposal |
| — (AD3D only) | `fitting_preset` | Saved lamp-fitting dimensions, measured by the owner | n/a in LuBan (suggest: none) | user list | AD3D proposal; PLAN §4 presets |
| — (AD3D only) | `socket_as_separate_part` | Export base/socket as its own 3MF object instead of fusing it | n/a in LuBan (suggest: off, i.e. one body like LuBan since 2020) | on/off | AD3D proposal; PLAN §4 multi-part 3MF |

- **Outputs:** Part of the lithophane body. LuBan has written base, lamp socket and lithophane as one body since 2020-03-01; before that they were disconnected components (blog: lithophane-update).
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Several shapes offer a base, which may integrate a light socket; details are per shape (§2.8).
  - **Flat and Arc:**
    - The base is a stand that extends toward the back; base length 0 hides it. With a non-zero length, the base thickness and a socket can be set (§2.13.3, Fig. 25).
    - A socket appears only when both base length and socket diameter are non-zero. It is O-shaped (with a socket height) or U-shaped (Fig. 26). Arc shares all Flat settings (§2.14).
    - The 2020-03-01 update lists O and U socket types for Flat and Arc (blog: lithophane-update).
    - Reading of Fig. 26: the O socket is a tube standing near the back end of the stand; the U socket is a notch open to the stand's back edge.
  - **Rectangle, Hexagon, Octagon, Dodecagon:** base thickness control (blog: lithophane-update). Poly-face "Assembly" holds separate faces in slots in a base and a cap, with optional light-blocking pillars and a slot tolerance that "is defaulted to a negative value, e.g. -0.3", meaning each slot is widened by 0.3 mm on both sides (§2.15.3, PDF p.28; see LITH-POLY-ASSEMBLY).
  - **Cylinder, Cone, Vase:**
    - A solid base gives a watertight lithophane (§2.16.2).
    - A hollow base can take a socket (non-zero socket diameter) with its own socket height, for a standing lamp shade (§2.16.2, Fig. 36).
    - Reading of Fig. 36 (right): the socket is a central ring held inside the bottom ring by three radial spokes. Spoke count and width are owned by LITH-REVOLVE.
    - For a hanging shade the manual points to the Inverted option (§2.16.2 → §2.15.2).
  - **Sphere** (socket added 2020-03-19, blog: sphere-lithophane-base):
    - The socket is enabled by a non-zero socket diameter. That is the inner diameter, and it "should be less than the opening diameter"; otherwise LuBan warns when Enter is pressed (§2.17.3).
    - Base thickness and socket height shape the socket (Fig. 41: sphere angle 300°, diameter 100, base thickness 4, socket diameter 50, socket height 10; then variants with socket diameter 30, socket height 30, base thickness 10).
    - Reading of Fig. 41: below a dark ring line the sphere narrows like a funnel into the socket tube. A smaller socket diameter makes the funnel steeper, a larger socket height makes the tube longer, and a larger base thickness makes the tube wall thicker.
  - **Balloon:** no socket option. The manual suggests intersecting the exported balloon with a cylindrical tube in MeshMixer (§2.20, PDF p.36; video tjD-cq9AjkQ "Use MeshMixer to create a light socket for LuBan balloon lithophane", title only). The Extra space setting makes room for a socket (§2.20.2).
  - **Tattoo:** a light socket "may be inserted using other software, such as MeshMixer"; the manual describes no socket option for Tattoo (§2.21, PDF p.40–41).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - A lamp fitting on every closed shape, Balloon and Tattoo included, inside AD3D. LuBan sends users to MeshMixer (§2.20, §2.21; video tjD-cq9AjkQ).
  - Fit clearance and owner-measured fitting presets. The manual describes no fit tolerance for sockets (§2.13.3, §2.16.2, §2.17.3), although it gives the poly-face slots one (§2.15.3). A small printable socket test ring checks the fit before a long print (ours, in the spirit of PLAN §4 calibration tiles).
  - Live constraint feedback while dragging (socket < opening; a socket needs base length > 0 or a hollow base), instead of a warning after Enter (§2.17.3, §2.13.3).
  - One watertight body, guaranteed and validated, plus an option to export the base/socket as a separate 3MF object for a different material or colour (PLAN §4 multi-part 3MF; LuBan has generated them as one body since 2020, blog: lithophane-update).
  - A light-through preview with the lamp at the socket position, to show hot spots before printing (see LITH-BACKLIGHT-PREVIEW).
  - Bed-fit check including the stand's footprint in the print orientation (PLAN §4 machine profiles).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - Primitives (stand plate, ring tube, U slot, revolved floor or ring) are generated directly as watertight low-poly meshes from 2D outlines (Clipper2 or i_overlay, PLAN §1) that are extruded or revolved.
  - They are joined to the shell along a shared loop where possible (the bottom rim of revolved shapes, the bottom edge band of a flat). Otherwise a manifold union runs on the small overlap region only, avoiding a global boolean on a multi-million-triangle shell (PLAN §1 manifold C API; the boolean timings in research 08 §1.4 show why).
  - `validate()` after the join, plus property tests over base and socket parameters (PLAN §5).
- **Milestone:** M2 (part 9, after LITH-FLAT; PLAN §3: base/socket/hanger).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Panel labels, defaults and ranges of every field above.
  - Whether the socket diameter is the inner diameter on every shape (stated only for Sphere, §2.17.3).
  - The socket wall thickness: on the Sphere, base thickness appears to set it (Fig. 41, our reading); for the other shapes no parameter is given. Also the ring width of a hollow base.
  - Whether polygon shapes can have a socket (the blog mentions base thickness only).
  - Where the socket sits on a Flat stand (Fig. 26 shows it near the back end) and the U-slot geometry.
  - Whether the Sphere socket must fit the inner or the outer opening. Fig. 40's numbers fit the inner surface if the sphere's Max thickness is 3.2 mm: 2 × (100/2 − 3.2) × sin((360° − 290°)/2) = 53.7. The outer surface would give 57.4 (our arithmetic; the sphere's Max thickness in Fig. 40 is not shown).
  - Whether the hollow-base spoke count is fixed at the three shown in Fig. 36.
  - Idea, not in the sources: a cable notch for solid bases.

#### LITH-HANGER — Hanging tab and key-chain hole (LuBan: Hanger)

- **LuBan path:** File → Create → Lithophane, then the hanger option of shapes that have one, e.g. Flat and Hexagon (§2.9, Fig. 19, PDF p.21). A Flat lithophane "has an option to generate a slanted photo with a base and a hanger" (§2.13, PDF p.23).
- **What it makes:** A tab with a hole, so the lithophane can hang as a photo or as a lamp shade, or carry a key ring (§2.9, Fig. 19, Fig. 20).
- **Fabrication:** 3D printed with the lithophane. Fig. 20 (PDF p.22) shows small printed lithophanes on key rings.
- **Inputs:** The lithophane shell (and frame, if any) from LITH-COMMON.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| hanger option (panel label UNCONFIRMED) | `hanger_enabled` | Add hanging tab(s) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: off) | on/off | §2.9 (PDF p.21) |
| hanger hole size (manual wording; panel label UNCONFIRMED) | `hanger_hole_diameter` | Size of the round hole; treated as a diameter (ours). Units UNCONFIRMED (suggest: mm) | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED. Fig. 19 shows a small and a large hole, the larger on a larger tab | §2.9; Fig. 19 |
| — (AD3D only) | `hanger_position` | Where tabs go | n/a in LuBan (suggest: `top_center`, as on the Flat in Fig. 19) | `top_center`, `top_corners`, `per_face` (polygons), `corner_hole` (key chain, inside the frame) | AD3D proposal |
| — (AD3D only) | `hanger_count` | Number of tabs on polygon and revolved shapes | n/a in LuBan (suggest: on alternate faces, as the Hexagon in Fig. 19 appears to have) | 1 to the number of faces | AD3D proposal; Fig. 19 |
| — (AD3D only) | `hanger_thickness` | Tab thickness, mm | n/a in LuBan (suggest: frame thickness if framed, else `thickness_max`) | ≥ `thickness_min` | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** Part of the lithophane body.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Several shapes offer a hanger, for a hanging photo or a hanging lamp shade. The hole size is customisable, and the hanger doubles as a key-chain hole (§2.9, Fig. 19, Fig. 20).
  - Reading of Fig. 19:
    - On the Flat lithophane the hanger is a rounded triangular tab centred on the top edge, with the hole near its apex; a larger hole comes with a larger tab.
    - On the Hexagon, tabs stand on the top rim (three visible).
    - The tab looks thinner than the dark frame.
  - Reading of Fig. 20: on the small square key chains, a small rounded tab with a hole sits on one edge; on the long panoramic plate it sits at one short end.
  - The sources show two routes to a hanging lamp shade:
    - hanger tabs on the top rim with the photos upright (Fig. 19, Hexagon);
    - the Inverted photo option, for a shade "hung upside down" so the inverted photos read upright again (§2.15.2, Fig. 30), which §2.16.2 recommends for hanging Cylinder/Cone/Vase shades.
    - How an inverted shade is hung (by tabs, or by its base and lamp fitting) is UNCONFIRMED.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Position and count options (top centre, corners, per face, key-chain corner hole). The manual names only the hole size as customisable (§2.9).
  - A strength check: the ligament of material around the hole must be at least two nozzle line widths, taken from the machine profile (ours; PLAN §4 machine profiles).
  - Tabs lie in the plate's plane, so an upright print needs no slicer support. That matters because §2.23 says support damages the rough surface (ours).
  - On polygon and revolved shades, tabs go automatically on whichever rim is on top for the chosen photo orientation, Upright or Inverted (§2.15.2) (ours).
  - Live preview while dragging the hole size (PLAN §4).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** The 2D profile is the convex hull of a circle (hole radius + ligament) and the attachment segment on the top edge, minus the hole (Clipper2 or i_overlay, PLAN §1). It is extruded to `hanger_thickness` and attached to the frame or top rim along a shared edge band, or by a manifold union of that small region only. Then `validate()` (PLAN §5).
- **Milestone:** M2 (part 9, after LITH-BASE-SOCKET; PLAN §3: base/socket/hanger).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - The panel label, default, range and tab thickness.
  - Which shapes have a hanger beyond Flat and Hexagon.
  - Tab count and placement on polygon shapes.
  - Whether a border is required for a Flat hanger.
  - The rule that places the key-chain tab in Fig. 20 (an edge, or a short end), and whether it is the same control as the hanger.

#### LITH-EDGE-SUPPORT — Upright print stabilisers (LuBan: Support)

- **LuBan path:** File → Create → Lithophane, Shape = Flat or Arc, Support option (§2.10, PDF p.21–22; blog: flat-lithophane-support).
- **What it makes:** Detachable side supports that hold a tall Flat or Arc lithophane steady while it prints, then come off (Fig. 21 shows them "attached and detached"). The blog calls it "edge support" that reduces "the out-of-plane movement during 3D printing" (§2.10, Fig. 21, PDF p.22; blog: flat-lithophane-support).
- **Fabrication:**
  - Printer vibration and extruder movement can shake a large lithophane, leaving artifacts; the support reduces this (§2.10).
  - "A tall flat lithophane is particularly sensitive to nozzle movement" (blog: flat-lithophane-support, 2019-09-02, updated 2019-09-22).
  - Fig. 21 shows the printed part with the supports attached, then detached.
  - This is LuBan-generated geometry, not slicer support. For lithophanes the manual says slicer support "can be disabled" (§2.23).
- **Inputs:** The Flat or Arc lithophane shell (and frame) from LITH-COMMON.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Support (section title; panel label and control type UNCONFIRMED) | `print_stabilisers` | Add detachable edge supports for printing upright | UNCONFIRMED | on/off (suggest); the sources name only Flat and Arc | §2.10; Fig. 21; blog: flat-lithophane-support |
| — (AD3D only) | `stabiliser_auto` | Recommend stabilisers automatically from the part's slenderness and the printer profile | n/a in LuBan (suggest: on) | on/off | AD3D proposal |
| — (AD3D only) | `stabiliser_tab_pitch` | Spacing of the breakaway tabs, mm | n/a in LuBan (suggest: 15) | 5–50 (suggest) | AD3D proposal |
| — (AD3D only) | `stabiliser_tab_neck` | Thickness of each tab's neck, mm | n/a in LuBan (suggest: 0.6) | 0.3–1.5 (suggest) | AD3D proposal |
| — (AD3D only) | `stabiliser_foot_length` | Length of each rail's foot on the bed, mm | n/a in LuBan (suggest: 25 % of part height) | 10–50 % of part height (suggest) | AD3D proposal; Fig. 21 shows feet |

- **Outputs:** Printed connected to the lithophane (Fig. 21), so it is part of the exported body. Whether LuBan writes it into the same STL is UNCONFIRMED.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Recommended for large Flat or Arc lithophanes (§2.10). Edge support for Flat and Arc was added in 2019-09 (blog: flat-lithophane-support).
  - Reading of Fig. 21:
    - Two upright rails stand one beside each vertical edge. Each tapers upward and flares into a foot on the bed.
    - A row of small tabs, about five per side counting a hook at the rail's top end, joins each rail to the lithophane's side edge.
    - In the detached photo the tab stubs stay on the rails.
    - The printed lithophane has a light frame.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Named "print stabilisers", so it is not confused with slicer support. LuBan uses the word "support" for both (§2.10 vs §2.23).
  - Automatic recommendation from height-to-thickness ratio and the printer profile. LuBan leaves the choice to the user ("useful when printing a large Flat or Arc lithophane", §2.10).
  - Adjustable tab pitch and neck for clean removal, and tabs placed only on the frame band, never on image pixels (ours).
  - Export as a separate 3MF object or fused (PLAN §4 multi-part 3MF).
  - The same generator stabilises upright Squama plates (PLAN §4 "a stand"; research 08 §2.4 notes that a 3 mm plate standing 250 mm tall wobbles).
  - The print orientation is previewed with the bed outline (research 07 §(a); PLAN §4 machine profiles).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Rails are extruded rectangle profiles running alongside the side edges (following the arc ends on an Arc). Feet are boxes on the bed plane. Tabs are small boxes bridging the gap between rail and frame, fused to both so that one connected body prints, as Fig. 21 shows. All are low-poly and built directly or by a manifold union of only the tab regions (PLAN §1). Then `validate()` (PLAN §5).
- **Milestone:** M2 (part 9, after LITH-HANGER; with Flat and Arc, PLAN §3).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - LuBan's control label and parameters (rail size, tab count and size, gap).
  - The size threshold for "large".
  - Arc geometry.
  - Whether the supports are written into the same STL as the lithophane.

#### LITH-BACKLIGHT-PREVIEW — Light-through preview (LuBan: Backlight)

- **LuBan path:** File → Create → Lithophane, Backlight settings in the control panel (§2.11, PDF p.22). The exact controls are not shown in any screenshot.
- **What it makes:** An on-screen simulation of how the lithophane looks when lit from behind. The light colour, filament colour and light intensity are configurable (§2.11, Fig. 22).
- **Fabrication:** None; this is a preview only. It informs physical choices:
  - a thick lithophane needs a strong light (§2.4);
  - filament choice changes sharpness (Fig. 14);
  - colour lithophanes add a colour filter, ideally printed on transparent paper; plain white paper "may also work if a light source is strong" (§2.22, PDF p.42).
- **Inputs:** The thickness field and surface from LITH-COMMON and the shape entry; lamp settings; filament colour. AD3D adds a material profile and, for enclosed shapes, a lamp position.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Backlight (section title; control type UNCONFIRMED) | `backlight_on` | Show the transmitted-light simulation | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: on once a photo is loaded) | on/off | §2.11 (PDF p.22) |
| colour of the light (manual); "Lamp color" (blog) | `light_color` | Lamp colour | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: warm white) | colour picker | §2.11; blog: lithophane-3rd-release |
| light intensity (manual); "Lamp … intensity" (blog) | `light_intensity` | Lamp brightness | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0–200 %) | §2.11; blog: lithophane-3rd-release |
| colour of the filament (manual); "filament color" (blog) | `filament_color` | Material colour/tint | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: white) | colour picker | §2.11; blog: lithophane-3rd-release; Fig. 54 caption (PDF p.40) |
| — (AD3D only) | `ambient_light` | Room light on the viewer side, to show how it washes the image out | n/a in LuBan (suggest: 10 %) | 0–100 % | PLAN §4 ambient-light slider |
| — (AD3D only) | `material_profile` | Measured attenuation per mm (per RGB channel) of the filament | n/a in LuBan (suggest: generic white PLA, uncalibrated) | profile list | AD3D proposal |
| — (AD3D only) | `lamp_position` | Lamp position for enclosed shapes (cylinder, sphere, box) | n/a in LuBan (suggest: at the socket, or the shape's centre) | draggable in the viewport | AD3D proposal |
| — (AD3D only) | `compare_unlit` | Split view: lit vs unlit, as in Fig. 22's photos of a real print | n/a in LuBan (suggest: off) | on/off | AD3D proposal; Fig. 22 |

- **Outputs:** Rendering only. AD3D adds an optional PNG snapshot for the physical test log (PLAN §5).
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Simulates the lithophane under backlight; light and filament colour are configurable and intensity adjustable (§2.11). The controls arrived with the 3rd release, 2019-05-27: "Lamp color and intensity, filament color" (blog: lithophane-3rd-release).
  - Fig. 22 (PDF p.22) sets LuBan's simulation beside a real print with and without backlight.
    - Reading of Fig. 22: the simulation is a front view of a warm, amber-lit image, close to the lit print.
    - Its view carries axis rulers (0–100 across, 0–90 up; units not shown, presumably mm), and the border is drawn grey.
  - "Changing the filament color can produce vivid rendering effects" (Fig. 54 caption, PDF p.40). Fig. 54 shows the same balloon in grey and two shades of pink.
  - The manual admits that computer rendering "cannot fully simulate the actual physical process": interior renders look better than exterior although exterior prints are sharper (§2.2; §2.14).
  - Generic viewport lighting also exists: View → Move light and View → Lighting angle ("X angle is between [0,180]. Y angle is between [-180,180]") in the Squama video (research 01 §2). The saved scene file keeps the viewing angle and lighting (§2.12).
  - Fig. 10's toolbar has a light-bulb icon and an unlabelled slider; their functions are UNCONFIRMED (research 01 §3 guesses the slider sets transparency). The 2018 builds show the same bulb, also unexplained (luban-docs Get started p.2, p.22, per docs/wip/spec-sections/00-luban-docs-notes.md §2.6).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Transmission computed from the real thickness map: exponential attenuation with thickness, tinted per channel by the filament (ours).
    - LuBan's simulation method is undocumented.
    - The manual admits its rendering "cannot fully simulate the actual physical process" and shows interior better than exterior, the reverse of real prints (§2.2, §2.14).
    - In ours the exterior/interior difference comes from the physics, so the preview no longer misleads.
  - A scattering blur that grows with the material light crosses after the relief (more for interior), predicting §2.2's "exterior looks sharper" (ours).
  - An ambient-light slider (PLAN §4) and a lit/unlit split view (Fig. 22 shows both states only for a real print).
  - Calibration per filament (ours, mirroring the Squama calibration tile, PLAN §4): print a thickness step wedge, photograph it on the lamp, and fit the attenuation, stored in the material profile and shared with LITH-COMMON's `tone_curve`.
  - Lamp position and hot-spot preview for lamp shades with sockets (cylinder, sphere), so over-exposed areas show before printing (ours).
  - Live while dragging any lithophane slider. Lamp and filament changes are GPU-only, and thickness changes re-upload one texture, so updates stay within 50 ms (PLAN §4 live preview; CLAUDE.md).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - The thickness field t(u,v) that the mesher uses is uploaded as a float texture and drawn with a custom ShaderMaterial in the react-three-fiber viewport (PLAN §1 "backlight preview for lithophanes"; research 04 §B.1 lists a backlight preview).
  - Per fragment (suggest): T_c = exp(−μ_c · t) for c ∈ {R, G, B}, with μ_c from the material profile or derived from the filament colour. Radiance = I_lamp · C_lamp,c · T_c · g(lamp geometry) + ambient · albedo_c · surface shading.
  - Blur (suggest): pick a mip level or Gaussian radius from `relief_faces` and the local thickness.
  - Enclosed shapes (suggest): point lamp at `lamp_position` with inverse-square and cosine falloff.
- **Milestone:** M2 (part 9, after LITH-EDGE-SUPPORT; PLAN §3: backlight preview).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - LuBan's control labels, defaults and ranges.
  - Whether LuBan models a lamp inside enclosed shapes, and whether it previews the colour-filter image (§2.22).
  - What the toolbar bulb and slider do.
  - Our attenuation and blur constants need physical measurement (calibration wedge) before the preview can be trusted.
  - CMYK lithophanes use custom filament colours too (blog: cmyk-lithophane-filament-color; video wxtrrqEZDRc, title only). That shape entry should reuse `filament_color`.

#### LITH-EXPORT — Export and project save (LuBan: Save model)

- **LuBan path:** File → Create → Lithophane, "Save model" button at the bottom of the control panel (§2.12, PDF p.22–23).
- **What it makes:** An export folder holding the printable model, a colour-filter image, LuBan's scene files and settings files (§2.12).
- **Fabrication:**
  - A slanted Flat lithophane is rotated to vertical on save for better print quality (§2.13.2, PDF p.24).
  - The colour-filter image is printed (ideally on transparent paper) at the size in its file name. It is then cut along the edges of its irregular pattern and attached behind the lithophane. For a full sphere the user must generate two half-spheres, attach the filter, and glue the halves together (§2.22, PDF p.42–43).
- **Inputs:** The generated model(s), the parameters, the photo(s) and the viewport state: view angle and lighting (§2.12). The status bar shows the view angle, e.g. "&Viewing angle: 23, -32, 0" (Fig. 10).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Save model (button) | `export` (action) | Write the output folder | — | — | §2.12 (PDF p.22) |
| export folder (how it is chosen for lithophanes is UNCONFIRMED) | `export_dir` | Parent folder for the export | UNCONFIRMED for lithophanes. Elsewhere Save model asks the user to select an export folder (§3.2.9, §5 intro), and a 2018 build's "Export parts" button opened a folder picker with a "Select folder" button (luban-docs Get started p.7). (suggest: ask, starting at the last used folder) | path | §2.12; §3.2.9 (PDF p.57); §5 intro (PDF p.96); docs/wip/spec-sections/00-luban-docs-notes.md §4.1 |
| automatic folder name | `export_folder_name` | LuBan: `<photo>_LP_<Shape>_<hh-mm-ss>`, e.g. `family_LP_Arc_10-25-29` (10:25 AM, 29 s). Mesh → LuBan uses the same pattern, `<model>_<Method>_<HH-MM-SS>`, e.g. `duck_Stack_13-42-02` (luban-docs Get started p.9) | automatic | whether it can be edited is UNCONFIRMED | §2.12 (PDF p.23); docs/wip/spec-sections/00-luban-docs-notes.md §5 |
| — (AD3D only) | `export_formats` | Files to write | n/a in LuBan (suggest: 3MF + STL + settings) | `3mf`, `stl`, `color_filter_pdf`, `color_filter_png`, `heightmap_png16` (CNC), `project` | AD3D proposal; PLAN §4 better exports |
| — (AD3D only) | `print_orientation` | Orientation of the exported part | n/a in LuBan (suggest: `upright`, per §2.23) | `upright`, `flat`, `as_modelled` | AD3D proposal; §2.13.2; §2.23 |
| — (AD3D only) | `split_parts` | One body, or separate objects (lithophane, stand/socket, stabilisers) | n/a in LuBan (suggest: one body) | on/off | AD3D proposal; PLAN §4 multi-part 3MF |
| — (AD3D only) | `write_checklist` | Write a print-and-light checklist next to the files | n/a in LuBan (suggest: on) | on/off | AD3D proposal; CLAUDE.md handover rule |

- **Outputs:**
  - **LuBan** (§2.12, PDF p.23), a folder `<photo>_LP_<Shape>_<hh-mm-ss>/` containing:
    - `Color_<W>_<H>.jpg` (e.g. `Color_46_46.jpg`): the colour-filter image, with its physical size in mm in the name; `Color_105_86.jpg` means 105 × 86 mm (§2.22, PDF p.42).
      - Made for every shape except Balloon and Tattoo (§2.22).
      - Its intensity component is "removed as much as possible", so it looks washed out next to the original (§2.22, Fig. 62, PDF p.45).
      - Added in the 9th release, 2020-09-16 (blog: lithophane-9th-release).
    - `<photo>_LP_Model.stl`: the lithophane model.
    - `LuBan_Model.fgd` and `LuBan_Model.fgs`: LuBan's model data and setting files. They record the model and the 3D space settings, such as viewing angle and lighting, and opening the FGS file shows the model in the same 3D environment.
      - §5 adds that the FGD stores data blocks and the FGS the scene settings, and that opening the FGS loads the matching FGD automatically (§5 intro, PDF p.96).
      - The same .fgs + .fgd pair is LuBan's own saved-model format (blog: password-protected-3d-file).
    - `<photo>_Setting.txt`: the human-readable settings used.
    - `MU_Setting.txt`: LuBan's settings file. To roll back to an old project's settings, copy it into the LuBan program folder over the default and restart LuBan (§2.12; §1.6).
  - **AD3D** (names ours, suggest), a folder `<photo>_<shape>_<YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS>/` containing:
    - `<photo>_<shape>.3mf`: unit = millimetre, named objects;
    - `<photo>_<shape>.stl`: binary, streamed;
    - `<photo>_color_filter_<W>x<H>mm.pdf` and `.png`: 1:1 scale, with the cut outline;
    - `<photo>_<shape>.ad3d`: the project (parameters, photos, view and light);
    - `settings.json`;
    - `PRINT-CHECKLIST.txt`.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - The folder name comes from the photo's file name, "LP" (lithophane), the shape and the time of the click (§2.12).
  - In Projection → Squama, Save model becomes active only once an image is loaded (research 01 §2). Whether the lithophane button behaves the same is UNCONFIRMED.
  - A slanted Flat is rotated vertical on save (§2.13.2).
  - Poly-face "Assembly" saves each face as its own STL (§2.15.3).
  - The colour image may not be rectangular (Fig. 61 shows cone, vase and sphere layouts); the size in its name is the bounding rectangle. Users resize it, e.g. in MS Word, and the aspect ratio in pixels may differ from that in mm, so the resize may not keep the aspect (§2.22, Fig. 61, PDF p.42–44).
  - Settings roll-back means copying `MU_Setting.txt` into the program folder and restarting (§2.12). On Windows, a setup.msi install should be run once as administrator so LuBan can use the settings file in "C:\Program Files (x86)\LuBan" (§1.6; video DzvYxTm8pbo @00:08–00:09).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - 3MF with millimetre units and named, multiple parts (PLAN §4: "3MF with units and multiple parts (LuBan has none)"); LuBan's printable lithophane output is STL only (§2.12).
  - Streamed binary STL for models of hundreds of MB (research 00 §6; CLAUDE.md "Stream large exports to disk"), run as a cancellable background job with progress (PLAN §1).
  - Collision-free folder names that include the date. LuBan's time-only stamp repeats every day (§2.12 example). Never overwrite silently.
  - One project file restores editable parameters, photos, view and lights; open it and carry on (PLAN §4 projects). In LuBan the FGS file restores the scene, but rolling back settings means copying `MU_Setting.txt` and restarting (§2.12).
  - A colour filter at true scale (PDF, plus PNG with DPI) with its cut outline, so no MS Word resizing step and no pixel-vs-mm aspect error (§2.22).
  - A `PRINT-CHECKLIST.txt` in every export: upright orientation, slicer support off, 30–50 mm/s, layer height ½ nozzle, light and colour-filter notes (§2.23; CLAUDE.md handover rule).
  - An explicit print orientation with preview and bed check. LuBan rotates silently (§2.13.2).
  - CLI: `ad3d-cli lithophane --preset <file> --photos <dir> --out <dir>` (command syntax ours; PLAN §4 batch/CLI).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - Binary STL streaming writer: rows → triangles → buffered writer (PLAN §1, `stl_io` or hand-rolled).
  - 3MF: `zip` crate + XML with `unit="millimeter"` (PLAN §1).
  - PDF writer: crate choice UNCONFIRMED; an SVG with mm units is the fallback.
  - Project `.ad3d`: JSON + assets (PLAN §1).
  - Generators are deterministic, so export is a full-resolution re-run keyed by the parameter hash (PLAN §1).
- **Milestone:** M2 (part 9, after LITH-BACKLIGHT-PREVIEW), for the lithophane-specific outputs. The STL/3MF/project infrastructure lands in M1 with Squama (PLAN §3, §4).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Whether the user picks the parent folder for lithophanes. Elsewhere the manual says Save model lets you select an export folder (Photo magic → Box, §3.2.9, PDF p.57; Mesh → LuBan intro, §5, PDF p.96); the lithophane chapter does not say.
  - Whether the time stamp is 12- or 24-hour. The Mesh → LuBan folder `duck_Stack_13-42-02`, created at 1:42 PM, suggests 24-hour (luban-docs Get started p.9–10, per docs/wip/spec-sections/00-luban-docs-notes.md §0, §5); the lithophane example (10:25 AM) cannot tell.
  - Whether the STL is binary or ASCII.
  - Whether `<photo>_Setting.txt` can be loaded back, and whether the FGS restores editable parameters or only the scene.
  - How multi-photo shapes name the folder.

### Lithophane shapes: Flat, Arc, Poly-face, Cylinder/Cone/Vase, Sphere (2.13–2.17)

These LuBan lithophane shapes (manual §2.13–2.17, PDF pp.23–34) become one generator family in AD3D: a photo-driven thickness field is mapped onto a parametric surface (plane, cylinder segment, prism faces, surface of revolution, sphere cap) and closed, together with its base, socket and hanger, into one watertight shell. Shared settings (polarity, rough side, min/max thickness, resolution, file size, border, base/socket, hanger, support, backlight, save) are specified in LITH-COMMON and its companion entries LITH-BASE-SOCKET, LITH-HANGER, LITH-EDGE-SUPPORT, LITH-BACKLIGHT-PREVIEW and LITH-EXPORT (§2.1–2.12). This section reuses their AD3D keys (`photos`, `polarity`, `relief_faces`, `thickness_min`, `thickness_max`, `pixel_size`, `base_length`, `base_thickness`, `base_fill`, `socket_diameter`, `socket_style`, `socket_height`, `print_orientation`, `split_parts`). Each entry below lists which shared settings apply and fully specifies the shape-specific parameters; a matrix after the entries summarises applicability.

Resolution: §2.21.2 (PDF p.41) states that it "is default to 0.1 mm/pixel in all shapes of lithophane except for the tattoo", so 0.1 applies to every shape in this section, yet Fig. 10 shows 0.12 for Flat (conflict, UNCONFIRMED). Values quoted from screenshots are what the figure shows, marked "shown": Fig. 10 (PDF p.17) is the panel as it opens under File → Create → Lithophane, before a photo is loaded, but LuBan stores the parameters of many functions in `MU_Setting.txt` and loads them at start-up (§1.6, PDF p.14), so a shown value may be a last-used value rather than the factory default. LuBan's official Chinese decks contain nothing on lithophanes (notes luban-docs §0), so none of their facts apply here. Anything marked "(suggest: …)", "(ours)" or "(our reading)" is our proposal or interpretation, not a LuBan fact.

#### LITH-FLAT — Flat panel lithophane (LuBan: Flat)

- **LuBan path:** File → Create → Lithophane, Shape = Flat (§2 intro and Fig. 10, PDF p.17; §2.13–2.13.3, PDF pp.23–25). The first lithophane release (2019-04-25) turned "any 2D photo into a 3D printed photo with a frame" (blog: lithophane-1st-release); that this was the Flat shape is our inference.
- **What it makes:** A rectangular photo panel that "resembles a conventional framed photo" (§2.13). Options: a backward slant, a base (stand) extending to the back, an O- or U-shaped light socket on the base, and a hanger tab (§2.13, §2.13.2, §2.13.3; §2.9 and Fig. 19, PDF p.21).
- **Fabrication:**
  - FDM 3D print. CNC also works for any material light can pass through (§2 intro, PDF p.17); in practice that means flat panels (our note).
  - Print the panel vertical: deposition is continuous in X/Y but layered in Z, so a vertical flat gets richer thickness variation than one laid on the bed (§2.23, PDF p.44).
  - On "Save model" LuBan rotates a slanted model back to vertical, and "some support is needed under a base" (§2.13.2, Fig. 24, PDF p.24).
  - Tall or large panels: use the detachable edge support (§2.10, Fig. 21, PDF p.22; blog: flat-lithophane-support, "A tall flat lithophane is particularly sensitive to nozzle movement").
- **Inputs:** One photo via the "Browse" button next to "Select photo" (§2 intro; Fig. 10). One photo is implied: §2.13.1 speaks of "the selected photo". The panel's aspect ratio always equals the photo's (§2.13.1). LuBan's crop recipe saves BMP, JPG or PNG (§2.13.1); the full input list is in LITH-COMMON.
- **Parameters:** Shared (LITH-COMMON and companions): Positive/Negative (`polarity`), Min/Max thickness (`thickness_min`, `thickness_max`), Resolution (`pixel_size`), File size, Border (Bright/Dark, size, thickness), Hanger (LITH-HANGER), Support (LITH-EDGE-SUPPORT), Backlight (LITH-BACKLIGHT-PREVIEW), Save model (LITH-EXPORT).
  - Fig. 10 shows, top to bottom: "Shape" Flat, "Select photo" + "Browse", "Positive" (selected) / "Negative", "Model size X" 50, "Model size Z" 50, "Min thickness" 0.8, "Max thickness" 3.2, "Resolution" 0.12, "Slant (deg)" 10 with spin arrows, "File size" 13 KB (read-only), and a half-hidden row "Border ○ Bright ◉ Dark" (Dark selected). There is no "Model size Y". The panel has a scroll bar, so the base, socket, hanger, support, backlight and Save model controls sit below the visible area, and no figure shows their labels (Fig. 10, PDF p.17, read at 300 dpi).
  - Resolution: §2.21.2 states a 0.1 mm/pixel default for all non-tattoo shapes; Fig. 10 shows 0.12 (conflict, UNCONFIRMED).
  - Exterior/Interior appears not to be offered on Flat (inference; see rules).
  - Label convention for all tables in this section: a label marked "(text)", "(caption)", "(blog)" or "(annotation)" comes from the manual's prose, a figure caption, a blog post or a figure annotation, so its exact UI string is UNCONFIRMED. Unmarked labels are read from a panel screenshot.
  - Shape-specific:

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |

| Model size Z | `size_z` | Panel height, mm; changing Z recomputes X | 50 (shown, Fig. 10) | as Model size X | §2.13.1; Fig. 10 (PDF p.17) |

In Figs. 24–26 the panel leans back while the base lies flat on the table (our reading) | 10 (shown, Fig. 10) | text box with spin arrows; Fig. 24 uses 20; range, step and sign UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0–45, step 1) | §2.13.2; Fig. 10 (PDF p.17); Fig. 24 (PDF p.24) |
| base length (text) | `base_length` | Depth of the stand behind the panel, mm; 0 hides the base. Text box, applied on Enter | UNCONFIRMED | ≥ 0; Fig. 25 uses 30 | §2.13.3; Fig. 25 (PDF p.25) |

| socket diameter (text) | `socket_diameter` | Light-socket diameter, mm; 0 = no socket. A socket is generated only if base length and socket diameter are both non-zero | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0) | ≥ 0; inner or outer diameter UNCONFIRMED for Flat (suggest: inner, as §2.17.3 states for the sphere) | §2.13.3; Fig. 26 (PDF p.25) |
| O-shape / U-shape (text) | `socket_style` | O: a tube standing on the rear end of the base. U: a notch open to the rear edge of the base (our reading of Fig. 26) | UNCONFIRMED | `ring` (O-shape), `slot` (U-shape) | §2.13.3; Fig. 26 (PDF p.25); blog: lithophane-update |
| socket height (text) | `socket_height` | Height of the O-shape tube, mm; configurable only for O-shape | UNCONFIRMED | Fig. 26 uses 10 and 20; range UNCONFIRMED | §2.13.3; Fig. 26 (PDF p.25) |
| Exterior / Interior (shared; manual wording) | `relief_faces` (LITH-COMMON) | Which way the rough relief faces | LuBan: apparently not offered on Flat (inference from §2.14 "In addition"); UNCONFIRMED | AD3D: `viewer` (Exterior), `light` (Interior), offered on Flat too | §2.14; LITH-COMMON; ours |

LITH-COMMON defines `fit_photo` (LuBan behaviour) and `crop_to_size`; Flat adds `pad` (extend with border) and `stretch` | `fit_photo` (suggest) | `fit_photo`, `crop_to_size`, `pad`, `stretch` | LITH-COMMON; ours |
