| — (AD3D only) | `stand_mode` | `fused` = one body as in LuBan; `separate` = stand printed flat and slot-joined to the panel. With `separate`, LITH-EXPORT `split_parts` writes panel and stand as two objects | `fused` (suggest) | `fused`, `separate` | ours; addresses §2.13.2 |
| — (AD3D only) | `print_orientation` (LITH-EXPORT) | `upright` = panel vertical (what LuBan does on save); `flat` = laid on the bed (allowed but inferior, §2.23); `as_modelled` = slant kept | `upright` (suggest) | `upright`, `flat`, `as_modelled` | §2.13.2; §2.23 (PDF p.44); LITH-EXPORT; ours |

- **Outputs:**
  - LuBan: an export folder named from photo, shape and time, e.g. "family_LP_Arc_10-25-29", holding `family_LP_Model.stl`, `LuBan_Model.fgd` + `.fgs`, `family_Setting.txt`, `MU_Setting.txt` and a colour image `Color_46_46.jpg` (§2.12, PDF p.23; §2.22). The STL holds panel, base and socket as one body (blog: lithophane-update). A slanted model is saved rotated to vertical (§2.13.2).
  - The colour image is generated for "All lithophane shapes except for balloon and tattoo"; its file name carries its physical size in mm, e.g. "Color_105_86.jpg" = 105 × 86 mm (§2.22, PDF p.42). It arrived with the 9th lithophane release, 2020-09-16 (blog: lithophane-9th-release).
  - AD3D: `<name>.3mf` (mm, print orientation applied; panel and stand as separate objects when `stand_mode = separate`), a streamed binary STL per object, the colour-filter image at true scale (PDF and PNG), and the `.ad3d` project (file set as in LITH-EXPORT).
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Aspect lock: after changing X and pressing Enter, Z follows, and vice versa; a 100 × 50 mm panel needs a 2:1 photo (§2.13.1).
  - LuBan's crop recipe: File → Invoke 2D window → File → Open → Tool → Body → Crop, then click two points. The dialog shows the region as x1 y1 x2 y2: (x1, y1) is the left-top corner and (x2, y2) the right-bottom corner, so width = x2 − x1 and height = y2 − y1 (§2.13.1). The "Crop" dialog reads "Enter crop region: left top right bottom." with the example "26 11 400 300" = "x: [26, 400), y: [11, 300)" ("x = 400, y = 300 are not included"); in Fig. 23 its box holds "266 171 523 348", and the overlay puts (0,0) at the image's top-left with Y pointing down. Edit the numbers to the wanted ratio, then File → Export → BMP, JPG, or PNG; the lithophane then takes that ratio (§2.13.1, Fig. 23, PDF p.24).
  - Text-box values apply only after Enter (§1.8, PDF pp.15–16; repeated in §2.13.1 and §2.13.3). The slant spin arrows are a non-text control, which §1.8 says updates the display automatically (our reading).
  - LuBan draws the panel in the XZ plane with Z up (Fig. 10 axes).
  - Slant tilts the panel for top-down viewing; Save model rotates the whole model so the panel is vertical, and the base then needs support. The manual judges that the print quality "should be better then doing it at an angle" (§2.13.2, Fig. 24). In Fig. 24 (right) the rotated base sticks out at an upward angle, which is why it needs support (our reading).
  - Base length 0 hides the base; base thickness can be set only when base length is non-zero (§2.13.3, Fig. 25). Figs. 25–26 show the base as a plate that narrows from the panel's bottom edge towards the back (our reading).
  - A socket is generated only when base length and socket diameter are both non-zero. It is O-shape or U-shape; socket height can be configured for O-shape (§2.13.3, Fig. 26). In Fig. 26 the O tube stands on a rounded rear end of the base, and the U is a notch in the rear edge (our reading).
  - Since 2020-03-01 panel, base and socket are generated as one body, and Flat and Arc have the O and U socket types (blog: lithophane-update, items 1–2).
  - Hanger: "The hanger hole size is customizable" and the hanger can double as a key chain hole (§2.9, Figs. 19–20, PDF pp.21–22). Fig. 19 shows a rounded triangular tab with a round hole, centred on the top edge, in two hole sizes; the larger hole comes with a larger tab (our reading).
  - Exterior/Interior: §2.14 gives the arc that option "In addition", which implies Flat lacks it; Fig. 11 (PDF p.17) shows flat panels with the relief facing the viewer (UNCONFIRMED).
  - Border thickness must exceed Max thickness by 5% (§2.7; LITH-COMMON).
  - AD3D rules (ours): the photo reads correctly, not mirrored, from the viewing side whichever face carries the relief; the socket must fit inside the base outline; all checks run live, not on Enter.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Live preview: dragging size, slant, base or socket sliders refreshes a coarse preview in ≤ 50 ms and the full mesh on release; LuBan needs type-then-Enter (§1.8, §2.13.1, §2.13.3; PLAN §4).
  - Built-in crop: aspect-locked crop/pan/zoom inside the panel, plus `pad` and `stretch`, instead of a 2D-window round trip with typed pixel coordinates (§2.13.1, Fig. 23).
  - Slant without supports: `stand_mode = separate` prints the panel vertical and the stand flat, joined by a slot sized from the printer profile's tolerance, both as named objects in one 3MF. `fused` keeps LuBan's one-body stand and shows the support area before export (§2.13.2; PLAN §4).
  - Rough-side choice on Flat too, e.g. a smooth face outwards for a window panel, which LuBan's Flat lacks (§2.14 wording).
  - Socket sized from a saved light-source profile (measured LED or puck diameter plus clearance; LITH-BASE-SOCKET `fitting_preset`, `socket_clearance`). LuBan gives a bare diameter with no fit allowance. Its convention elsewhere is that socket size is the inner dimension, measured on your light source (Projection method, video VA67Jm3ijHg @03:00–04:00; sphere socket, §2.17.3).
  - Backlight preview with the light at the socket position, plus an ambient-light slider (§2.11; PLAN §4).
  - Watertight by construction: panel, border, base, socket and hanger form one closed, consistently wound shell, checked by `validate()` and a randomised-parameter test (CLAUDE.md; PLAN §5). LuBan emitted disconnected parts until 2020 (blog: lithophane-update).
  - Generation runs off the UI thread on all cores (grid rows in parallel with rayon) as a latest-wins, cancellable job (PLAN §1, §4).
  - Exports: 3MF in mm with print orientation applied, streamed binary STL, and a true-scale colour filter instead of a JPG you must resize in MS Word (§2.22; PLAN §4).
  - `.ad3d` project files with undo/redo and recent files; LuBan rolls settings back by copying `MU_Setting.txt` next to the program and restarting (§2.12).
  - CLI/batch: one panel per photo in a folder, same settings (PLAN §4).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - Grayscale, area-averaged resample to the grid at `pixel_size` mm/px, thickness t = t_min + (1 − I)(t_max − t_min), flipped for Negative (research 04 §B.1; pipeline in LITH-COMMON).
  - Front surface = heightfield grid; back = a plane triangulated from its boundary ring only (no interior vertices); side walls stitched to both. The shell is closed, has no T-junctions and needs about half the triangles (ours).
  - Border, hanger, base and socket are parametric solids that share boundary vertices with the panel; a manifold boolean union is used only where parts overlap (research 03 §13; PLAN §1).
  - Slant = rotation about the panel's bottom edge; `print_orientation = upright` applies the inverse rotation to the whole body (ours).
  - Size: 0.1 mm/px can reach about 6M triangles (≈ 300 MB STL), so stream the STL and prefer 3MF (research 00 §6; research 08 §3).
  - OSS: s1lentCommit/stl-ready-image (MIT), yomboprime/lithofun (MIT), colbrydi/Lithophane (MIT), furti/FreeCAD-Lithophane (MIT), muldjord/lithomaker (GPL-3.0, fine for personal use) (research 03 §3).
  - Tests (ours): a proptest over size 10–300 mm, slant 0–45°, base length 0–80 mm, socket 0–40 mm (O and U) and resolution 0.1–1 mm/px must pass `validate()`; a criterion bench at 100 × 100 mm and 0.1 mm/px.
- **Milestone:** M2 (part 9, after LITH-COMMON), step 1. It builds the shared heightfield, shell, base/socket and export code that the other shapes reuse (PLAN §3).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - UI labels, defaults and ranges of base length, base thickness, socket diameter, socket style and socket height; they sit below the visible part of Fig. 10's scrolling panel.
  - The resolution default: 0.1 mm/px stated in §2.21.2, 0.12 shown in Fig. 10.
  - Whether socket diameter is the inner diameter on Flat.
  - Slant range, step and sign; whether the base stays horizontal at every slant (Fig. 24 suggests so).
  - The base outline (tapered in Figs. 25–26?) and where the socket sits on it.
  - Whether model size includes the border (LITH-COMMON).
  - Whether Flat really has no Exterior/Interior option.
  - The shape token in the export-folder name for Flat (the manual's only example is "Arc").
  - Related videos (titles only, not transcribed): fKl1rsrthcg "LuBan Lithophane" (0:45) and ba6xj2IISNU "LuBan Lithophane 2" (13:05), both 2019 (dates approximate).

#### LITH-ARC — Curved panel lithophane (LuBan: Arc)

- **LuBan path:** File → Create → Lithophane, Shape = Arc (§2.14, PDF pp.25–26). "Arc" is the shape token in the export-folder example "family_LP_Arc_10-25-29" (§2.12, PDF p.23).
- **What it makes:** "a warped flat lithophane" (§2.14): the Flat panel bent into a circular arc about a vertical axis (our reading of Fig. 27, which shows panels curved horizontally with straight vertical edges and dark frames). It shares all Flat settings except that Model size X is replaced by the arc angle, and it adds Exterior vs. Interior (§2.14, Fig. 27, PDF p.26).
- **Fabrication:**
  - 3D print. Exterior arcs print sharper, even though LuBan renders interior arcs better (§2.14; §2.2 and Fig. 13, PDF p.18). With special filament an interior print can also be sharp (Fig. 14: Eryone silk silver filament, min/max 0.6/2.4 mm).
  - Large arcs: edge support (§2.10; blog: flat-lithophane-support, "flat and arc lithophane").
  - Print standing on the bottom edge like the flat (UNCONFIRMED; suggest, since the arc stands by itself).
- **Inputs:** One photo; the aspect ratio is locked as on Flat (§2.14 → §2.13.1).
- **Parameters:** Shared (LITH-COMMON and companions): Positive/Negative, Exterior/Interior (`relief_faces`, offered here, §2.14), Min/Max thickness, Resolution (0.1 mm/px default, §2.21.2), File size, Border (Fig. 27 shows dark frames), Support (§2.10; LITH-EDGE-SUPPORT), Backlight, Save model. Hanger applies by "share all settings" (UNCONFIRMED). Shape-specific:

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shape | `shape` | Lithophane type | UNCONFIRMED | `arc` | §2.14; §2.12 (PDF p.23) |
| Select photo / Browse | `photos` | The input photo; aspect locked as on Flat | none | one image (as Flat) | §2.14 ("share all settings"); §2.13.1 |
| arc angle (text) | `arc_angle` | Angle the panel subtends about its vertical axis, degrees; replaces Model size X | UNCONFIRMED | Fig. 27 shows 30, 90 and 120; range UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 5–300) | §2.14; Fig. 27 (PDF p.26) |
| Model size Z | `size_z` | Panel height, mm. With the photo's aspect it fixes the arc length (our inference) | UNCONFIRMED (Flat shows 50, Fig. 10) | positive | §2.14; §2.13.1 |
| Exterior / Interior (manual wording; panel label UNCONFIRMED) | `relief_faces` (LITH-COMMON) | Exterior: relief on the convex (exterior) surface, facing the viewer. Interior: relief on the concave surface, facing the light | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: `viewer`, since exterior prints are sharper) | `viewer` (Exterior), `light` (Interior) | §2.14 (convex = exterior); §2.2 (rough side faces the viewer in Exterior) |
| Slant (deg) | `slant` | As Flat | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED | §2.14 ("share all settings"); §2.13.2 |
| base length, base thickness, socket diameter, O-shape / U-shape, socket height (text) | `base_length`, `base_thickness`, `socket_diameter`, `socket_style`, `socket_height` | As Flat | UNCONFIRMED | as Flat; O and U confirmed for Arc | §2.14; blog: lithophane-update ("Flat and Arc lithophane have socket types: O and U") |
| — (AD3D only) | `radius` | Arc radius, with chord width and depth, shown live; optionally drives the arc instead of the angle | derived | read-out, or driver (radius or chord) | ours |
| — (AD3D only) | `print_orientation` (LITH-EXPORT) | As Flat | `upright` (suggest) | `upright`, `flat` (not useful for an arc), `as_modelled` | LITH-EXPORT; ours |

- **Outputs:** As LITH-FLAT; LuBan's export folder carries the token "Arc" and holds the colour image `Color_46_46.jpg` (§2.12, PDF p.23). AD3D: 3MF in mm plus STL, colour filter at true scale (unrolled rectangle, ours), project file.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Aspect lock, Enter-to-update and the base/socket rules are as on Flat (§2.14).
  - The convex surface is the exterior surface and the concave surface the interior (§2.14). In both modes the viewer is on the convex side and the light on the concave side; only the side carrying the relief changes (§2.2: exterior = rough surface towards the viewer, smooth towards the light) (our reading).
  - On screen interior looks better, but exterior prints sharper; LuBan users tune with the interior display and switch to exterior just before saving (§2.14).
  - Geometry (our inference, UNCONFIRMED): arc length = Model size Z × photo aspect, and radius = arc length / arc angle in radians, so changing the angle at a fixed Z changes the radius.
  - The arc axis is vertical: Fig. 27 shows panels curved horizontally with straight vertical edges (our reading).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Truthful preview: transmitted-light rendering from thickness (Beer–Lambert) looks the same for exterior and interior, optionally with a slight blur on interior to mimic the softer look §2.2 describes. There is no "preview as interior, switch to exterior before saving" step (§2.14, §2.2; PLAN §4).
  - Live radius, chord and depth read-outs, and the option to drive the arc by radius or chord (e.g. to wrap a known lamp or fit a shelf); LuBan exposes only the angle (§2.14).
  - Arc-angle and height sliders update live (≤ 50 ms preview) instead of on Enter (§1.8).
  - Light-position preview at the centre of curvature, where an LED is equidistant from the whole panel (ours; LuBan's base placement for arcs is UNCONFIRMED).
  - Plus the shared improvements listed under LITH-FLAT (cancellable multi-core jobs, 3MF and streamed STL, project files, CLI).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - Map photo u ∈ [0, 1] to φ = (u − ½)·arc_angle and v to z = v·Z; the smooth surface is the cylinder of radius R; offset along the radial normal by t, outwards for exterior relief and inwards for interior relief (research 04 §B.1).
  - The smooth surface has straight vertical rulings, so it can be triangulated as full-height strips between top and bottom boundary vertices (ours); side walls and rims close the shell.
  - Base, socket, border and hanger reuse LITH-FLAT code.
  - Tests (ours): proptest over arc angle 5–300°, Z 10–200 mm and both rough sides.
- **Milestone:** M2 (part 9, after LITH-COLOR-FILTER), step 2: reuses LITH-FLAT (PLAN §3; research 07 groups flat, arc and cylinder).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Label, default and range of the arc angle, and what stays fixed when it changes (arc length assumed).
  - Whether slant and hanger really apply; how a base meets a curved panel; where the socket sits.
  - Behaviour near or at 360° (does it become a cylinder?).

#### LITH-POLY — Prism lantern lithophane, one body (LuBan: Poly-face: Rectangle, Hexagon, Octagon, Dodecagon)

- **LuBan path:** File → Create → Lithophane, Shape = Rectangle, Hexagon, Octagon or Dodecagon (§2.15, PDF pp.26–28: "rectangle and polygon lithophanes"; the four names from blog: lithophane-update; "Hexagon" also in Fig. 19's caption, PDF p.21). "One body vs. Assembly" = One body (§2.15.3).
- **What it makes:** A lantern whose sides are flat lithophane panels around a rectangle or a polygon (regular, by our reading of Figs. 19, 30 and 31). Each face carries its own photo, or one photo repeats on every face (our reading of Figs. 19 and 28). Photos can be upright (to sit on a lamp) or inverted (to hang upside down) (§2.15, §2.15.1, §2.15.2; Figs. 28–30, PDF p.27).
- **Fabrication:** 3D print in one job: easy to set up, but "if the print fails midway, all is lost" (§2.15.3). Print orientation is not stated (suggest: base on the bed, faces vertical). For hanging, use hanger tabs (Fig. 19).
- **Inputs:** One or several photos picked in one "Select photo" dialog (§2.15.1).
- **Parameters:** The poly-face shapes "share most of the settings" with each other (§2.15). Shared (LITH-COMMON and companions): Positive/Negative, Min/Max thickness, Resolution (0.1 mm/px default, §2.21.2), File size, Border (Figs. 28–31 dark; Fig. 19 bright), Hanger (Fig. 19), Backlight, Save model. Exterior/Interior: UNCONFIRMED. Support: not mentioned (§2.10 names only Flat and Arc). Shape-specific:

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shape | `shape` = `prism`, `face_count` | Number of side faces, chosen through the shape | UNCONFIRMED | Rectangle = 4, Hexagon = 6, Octagon = 8, Dodecagon = 12 | blog: lithophane-update; §2.15 |
| Model size X | `size_x` | Footprint width, mm | UNCONFIRMED (Fig. 15 shows 50, generic) | positive | §2.15; Fig. 15 (PDF p.19) |
| Model size Y | `size_y` | Footprint depth, mm: free for Rectangle, "determined by the model size X and the number of faces" for the other poly-faces | UNCONFIRMED | Rectangle: positive; polygons: derived (read-only presumed; UNCONFIRMED) | §2.15 |
| Model size Z | `size_z` | Face height, mm (our reading: Z is the vertical axis, Fig. 10) | UNCONFIRMED | positive | §2.15 |
| Select photo | `photos` | One or several images, ordered by file name and applied to the faces in sequence | none | 1 … n files | §2.15.1 |
| Upright / Inverted (text) | `photo_orientation` | Upright: sits on a lamp. Inverted: photos upside down so they read upright when the lantern hangs upside down | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: `upright`) | `upright`, `inverted` | §2.15.2; Fig. 30 (PDF p.27) |
| One body / Assembly (text) | `construction` | `one_body` here; `assembly` is LITH-POLY-ASSEMBLY | UNCONFIRMED | `one_body`, `assembly` | §2.15.3; blog: lithophane-3rd-release |
| base thickness (blog) | `base_thickness` | Thickness of the bottom base, mm | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED | blog: lithophane-update (item 3) |
| — (AD3D only) | `faces` | Per-face slot: photo, empty flag, crop offset and zoom | photos in order, centre crop | list of `face_count` slots | ours |
| — (AD3D only) | `face_count` (free) | Any regular n-gon, not just the four LuBan shapes | — | 3–24 | ours |

- **Outputs:** One STL for the whole lantern, named as in §2.12, plus the colour image (§2.22; layout for poly-faces UNCONFIRMED). AD3D: one 3MF in mm plus STL, a per-face colour filter at true scale, project file.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Rectangle: X, Y and Z are independent. Other poly-faces: Y follows from X and the number of faces (§2.15).
  - Unlike Flat and Arc, which size the model to include the whole photo, poly-faces centre-crop each photo to the face size dictated by the model size, so changing the size changes the visible region (§2.15, Fig. 28).
  - With one photo, Fig. 28 shows it on the side face too, and Fig. 19's hexagon shows the same photo on two faces, i.e. the photo repeats on every face (our reading).
  - Several photos are ordered by file name and applied face by face; to swap two, rename the files and select them again (§2.15.1, example p1.jpg … p4.jpg). Fig. 30 shows a different photo on each face.
  - Empty face: create a white image with a thin black border and "name all the photos according to a desired face sequence" (§2.15.1, Fig. 29). It gives a plain, thin face with a frame line (our reading of Fig. 29).
  - Upright vs. Inverted (§2.15.2): Fig. 30 shows a many-sided lantern (about 12 faces) whose base looks like a ring with radial spokes meeting at a small central ring (our reading); hung upside down, the inverted photos read upright (Fig. 30 caption).
  - One-body lanterns are open at the top (our reading of Figs. 19, 28, 29 and 31 left).
  - Fig. 19 shows three hanger tabs with holes on alternate top edges of a hexagon (our reading; §2.9: "a hanging lamp shade").
  - Poly-faces got a base-thickness control on 2020-03-01 (blog: lithophane-update, item 3).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - A face list instead of file names: drag to reorder, a photo per face, an "empty" toggle and per-face crop/pan/zoom. LuBan orders by file name, needs renaming to swap, needs a white bordered image for blanks, and only crops from the centre (§2.15, §2.15.1, Figs. 28–29).
  - Any face count from 3 to 24 (LuBan: 4, 6, 8 or 12 per blog: lithophane-update).
  - Live preview of each face's crop while dragging the size sliders; the crop moves with the size (Fig. 28), and LuBan only updates on Enter (§1.8).
  - Backlight preview with a lamp inside, and a "hang" preview that flips the model for inverted lanterns (PLAN §4; §2.15.2).
  - One watertight shell including corners, spokes and hangers, checked by `validate()` (CLAUDE.md).
  - Plus the shared improvements listed under LITH-FLAT.
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - n planar heightfield panels on a regular n-gon (rectangle: two face widths); adjacent faces meet in a mitred corner post of border thickness (ours).
  - Per face: centre-crop (or user-crop) the photo to the face aspect (face width = side length, height = Z), then reuse the LITH-FLAT panel code.
  - Base ring and spokes as 2D polygons (Clipper2 offsets), extruded and fused with the panels (research 03 §13).
  - Tests (ours): proptest over n 3–24, X 30–250 mm, Z 20–250 mm, 1…n photos, upright and inverted.
- **Milestone:** M2 (part 9, after LITH-BALLOON), second wave ("more shapes", PLAN §3), after Flat, Arc, Revolve and Sphere.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Whether X is measured across corners or across flats, and the exact Y formula.
  - Whether the shape list has other polygons (triangle, pentagon …).
  - Whether Exterior/Interior is offered.
  - Base geometry: is the spoke count tied to the face count (Fig. 30 is too small to count reliably)? Is the central ring a lamp interface? Base-thickness default?
  - What happens with more, or fewer, photos than faces.
  - Hanger count and placement rules; colour-image layout for poly-faces (§2.22); exact dropdown strings.

#### LITH-POLY-ASSEMBLY — Prism lantern kit (LuBan: Poly-face, Assembly)

- **LuBan path:** As LITH-POLY with "One body vs. Assembly" = Assembly (§2.15.3, PDF p.28; blog: lithophane-3rd-release, "one body vs. assembly").
- **What it makes:** Each face as its own single-face lithophane, plus a base and a cap with slots that hold the faces. Optional pillars on the base block light that would leak through the gaps between adjacent faces (§2.15.3, Fig. 31, PDF p.28).
- **Fabrication:** 3D print each part separately, so a failed print costs only that part; after printing, fix the faces in the slots of the base and cap (§2.15.3). Part orientation is not stated (suggest: faces vertical, base and cap flat).
- **Inputs:** As LITH-POLY.
- **Parameters:** Shared as LITH-POLY, and all LITH-POLY shape parameters apply. Kit-specific:

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| One body / Assembly (text) | `construction` | Kit mode | — | `assembly` | §2.15.3 |
| tolerance (text) | `slot_tolerance` | Fit of the faces in the slots, mm. Negative widens each slot by that amount on both sides | negative, "e.g. -0.3" (exact default UNCONFIRMED) | range UNCONFIRMED; tune in about 0.1 steps: too tight → −0.4, too loose → −0.2 | §2.15.3 |
| pillars (text) | `pillars` | Posts "connected to the base" that "block light from the gap between two adjacent faces"; at the corners by our reading of Fig. 31 | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: on) | on, off ("You may also enable pillars") | §2.15.3; Fig. 31 (PDF p.28) |
| base thickness (blog) | `base_thickness` | As LITH-POLY | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED | blog: lithophane-update |
| — (AD3D only) | `explode` | Viewport explode factor for the parts | 0 (suggest) | 0–1 | ours (LuBan: "Object → Select", Fig. 31 caption; "Object -> Explode" / "Object -> Restore", blog: exploded-view) |
| — (AD3D only) | `part_labels` | Emboss face numbers on hidden edges of faces and slots | on | on, off | ours |
| — (AD3D only) | `cap_style` | Closed plate, open ring, or plate with hanger tabs | `closed` (as Fig. 31) | `closed`, `ring`, `hanger` | ours; Fig. 31 |

- **Outputs:** LuBan saves each face "as an STL file", plus the base and cap (§2.15.3); file names UNCONFIRMED. AD3D: one 3MF with every face, the base and the cap as named objects in mm, one STL per part, and a one-page assembly sheet.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Tolerance is "defaulted to a negative value, e.g. -0.3, meaning a slot is expanded by 0.3 mm on both sides". A printed part comes out slightly bigger than its model (the printed shell), which narrows the slots; the expansion compensates. Too tight: reduce it (−0.3 → −0.4). Too loose: increase it (−0.3 → −0.2). The best value depends on printer and profile and is found by trial and error (§2.15.3).
  - The faces are "fixed in the slots on the base and cap" (§2.15.3).
  - Exploded view: the Fig. 31 caption says "To enable the exploded view, use "Object → Select"", while the 2019-04-03 blog post gives "Object -> Explode" and "Object -> Restore" for exploded views (blog: exploded-view). Which applies to this kit is UNCONFIRMED. In the Projection method, Object → Select (shortcut J) lists the generated components and E explodes them (video VA67Jm3ijHg @00:00–02:00). In the 2018 build, Object → Select was a small floating dialog with a slider that steps through the parts and a Delete button (notes luban-docs §2.4, Get started p.24; a mesh method, not a lithophane).
  - Fig. 31 (a hexagon): assembled, the kit has a closed dark hexagonal cap and a light base frame; exploded, the base shows corner pillars and radial bars underneath (our reading).
  - AD3D keeps LuBan's sign convention (negative = looser, for FDM), consistent with LuBan's other tolerance settings (research 04 §B.16) and with the Projection method, where a negative tolerance is recommended for 3D-printed parts (video VA67Jm3ijHg @05:00–06:00).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Tolerance from the printer profile, plus a printable slot-gauge coupon (e.g. −0.1 … −0.5 mm in 0.1 steps) so the first kit fits; LuBan leaves this to trial and error (§2.15.3; PLAN §4 machine profiles).
  - An explode slider and assembly preview in the viewport instead of a menu round trip (Object → Select, Fig. 31; Object → Explode / Restore, blog: exploded-view).
  - Multi-part 3MF with names and units plus per-part STL, and "re-export face N" for reprints (§2.15.3; PLAN §4).
  - Embossed face and slot numbers, so the photo order survives assembly (ours).
  - Plus the LITH-POLY and LITH-FLAT improvements.
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - Slot profiles as 2D polygons widened by −tolerance per side with Clipper2, extruded into the base and cap frames (research 03 §13; research 04 §B.16).
  - Pillars: prisms at the polygon corners fused to the base. Faces: LITH-FLAT panels with plain edges sized to the slot depth.
  - Every part is its own closed manifold, and `validate()` runs per part (CLAUDE.md).
  - Tests (ours): proptest over n 3–24, tolerance −0.6…+0.2 mm, pillars on/off; check that each face's edge fits its slot with the requested clearance.
- **Milestone:** M2 (part 9, after LITH-POLY), second wave, right after LITH-POLY.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Slot depth and width rules; whether faces have tabs; pillar size.
  - Cap geometry: closed in Fig. 31, but is there any hole for heat or a cable?
  - Tolerance range, step and UI label; part file names.
  - Whether only the base carries pillars (the text says pillars are "connected to the base").
  - Which menu explodes the kit: "Object → Select" (Fig. 31 caption) or "Object -> Explode" / "Object -> Restore" (blog: exploded-view).

#### LITH-REVOLVE — Revolved shade lithophane (LuBan: Cylinder, Cone, Vase)

- **LuBan path:** File → Create → Lithophane, Shape = Cylinder, Cone or Vase (§2.16–2.16.2, PDF pp.28–30; blog: lithophane-5th-release, "Cone shape lithophane"; blog: lithophane-6th-release, "An adjustable vase-like shape is added").
- **What it makes:** A lamp shade or vessel revolved about a vertical axis: a cylinder (one diameter), a cone (top and bottom diameters) or a vase whose diameter varies with height, set by "several sliders" or control points. One or more photos wrap around it (§2.16, Fig. 32, PDF p.29; blog: lithophane-6th-release, "Through control points, the shape can take various different forms").
- **Fabrication:**
  - 3D print. A solid base makes a watertight vessel: "You may pour water into the lithophane and drop some waterproof LED light in it" (§2.16.2).
  - A hollow base leaves the bottom open, with an optional light socket, for a standing lamp shade; for a hanging shade use the inverted option (§2.16.2 → §2.15.2).
  - Exterior prints sharper; interior can be sharp with special filament (§2.2; Figs. 13–14, PDF p.18, the latter an interior trophy with a vase-shaped body, Eryone silk silver filament, min/max 0.6/2.4 mm).
- **Inputs:** One or several photos, selected "in one go" with "Select photo" (§2.16).
- **Parameters:** Shared (LITH-COMMON and companions): Positive/Negative, Exterior/Interior (`relief_faces`; likely offered: Fig. 13 shows cylinder-like prints with the rough side and with the smooth side facing the viewer, and Fig. 14 an interior vase-like trophy (our reading); blog: lithophane-4th-release "Lithophane on the interior surface"), Min/Max thickness, Resolution (0.1 mm/px default, §2.21.2), File size, Border (Fig. 32 shows bands at top and bottom; fixed mode "extends the top and bottom border", §2.16.1), Backlight, Save model. Hanger: UNCONFIRMED. Support: not mentioned. Shape-specific:

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shape | `shape` = `revolve`, `profile` | Profile type | UNCONFIRMED | `cylinder`, `cone`, `vase` | §2.16 |
| diameter (text) | `diameter` | Cylinder diameter, mm ("a cylinder has a fixed diameter") | UNCONFIRMED | positive | §2.16 |
| top / bottom diameter (text) | `top_diameter`, `bottom_diameter` | Cone end diameters, mm | UNCONFIRMED | positive; Figs. 33–36 show bottom larger than top; top larger than bottom UNCONFIRMED | §2.16; Figs. 33–36 (PDF pp.29–30) |
| sliders (text) | `profile_diameters` | Vase diameters at control heights | UNCONFIRMED | count and limits UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 5 control points, evenly spaced) | §2.16; blog: lithophane-6th-release ("control points") |
| height (caption) | `size_z` | Overall height, mm | UNCONFIRMED | positive; Fig. 33 uses 50, 70 and 90 | Fig. 33 (PDF p.29) |
| Select photo | `photos` | One or several photos wrapped around the circumference, selected "in one go" | none | 1 … n | §2.16 |
| Fixed / Stretch (text) | `photo_fit` | Fixed keeps the photo's aspect (adds gaps between photos or extends the top and bottom border); Stretch stretches photos over the whole surface | UNCONFIRMED | `fixed`, `stretch` | §2.16.1; Figs. 33–35; blog: stretch-to-cover-full-surface |
| solid / hollow (text) | `base_fill` (LITH-BASE-SOCKET) | Solid = closed bottom, so "a watertight lithophane will be produced"; Hollow = open bottom ring | UNCONFIRMED | `solid`, `hollow` | §2.16.2; Fig. 36 (PDF p.30); blog: lithophane-update (item 4) |
| socket diameter (text) | `socket_diameter` | Light socket in a hollow base, mm; 0 = none | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0) | ≥ 0; hollow base only; inner or outer UNCONFIRMED | §2.16.2; Fig. 36 |
| socket height (text) | `socket_height` | Height of the socket ring, mm, set separately | UNCONFIRMED | ≥ 0 | §2.16.2 |
| inverted option (text) | `photo_orientation` | Inverted photos for a hanging shade | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: `upright`) | `upright`, `inverted` | §2.16.2 → §2.15.2 |
| — (AD3D only) | `repeat_count` | Copies of the photo set around the circumference | `auto` (suggest) | `auto`, 1–12 | ours (LuBan decides itself, §2.16.1, Fig. 34) |
| — (AD3D only) | `gap_fill` | Fill used for gaps and extended borders in fixed mode | `border` (suggest) | `border`, `max_thickness`, `min_thickness` | ours (Figs. 33–35) |
| — (AD3D only) | `mapping` | `average`: photo spread evenly round each row, scale fitted to the average perimeter (LuBan's fixed mode, §2.16.1). `developable` (cone only): photo placed undistorted on the unrolled annular sector; leftover sector area gets `gap_fill`. `conformal` (any profile): local aspect exact at every height, scale follows the radius | `average` (suggest; matches LuBan) | `average`, `developable`, `conformal` | ours (§2.16.1 says LuBan "does not deal with the distortion") |
| — (AD3D only) | `spokes`, `spoke_width` | Spokes that hold the socket ring | 3 spokes (suggest, as Fig. 36 shows); width UNCONFIRMED | 2–8 spokes | Fig. 36; ours |

- **Outputs:** One STL plus the colour image (§2.12, §2.22). Fig. 61 (PDF p.44) shows the cone's colour image as an annular sector and the vase's as a row of 12 gores whose widths follow the profile (gore count is our count). The cylinder's is presumably a rectangle (UNCONFIRMED). The user cuts the printed image "along the edges of the irregular pattern" and attaches it behind the lithophane (§2.22, PDF p.43). AD3D: 3MF in mm plus STL, colour filter at true scale with cut lines, project file.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - The shapes revolve about a vertical axis; flexibility rises from cylinder to cone to vase (§2.16).
  - Fixed mode adds a gap between photos or extends the top and bottom border to keep the aspect. On a cone or vase regional distortion is unavoidable; fixed mode preserves only the average aspect ratio (§2.16.1).
  - In both modes LuBan may duplicate photos to keep the original aspect "as much as possible" (§2.16.1, Fig. 34, PDF p.30). To prevent duplication, crop the photo so width / height is "roughly the average perimeter / the height of the lithophane" (§2.16.1, Fig. 35). In Fig. 34 a tall photo appears twice in both modes, with dark gaps in fixed mode; in Fig. 35 a wide photo appears once, with one dark gap in fixed mode (our reading).
  - Fig. 33 (cone, heights 50/70/90 mm): fixed mode shows dark vertical gaps at 50 mm and dark top and bottom bands at 90 mm; stretch fills the surface. Dark renders as thick, so the gaps appear filled at full thickness (our reading; exact thickness UNCONFIRMED).
  - Solid base: watertight vessel. Hollow base: optional socket via a non-zero socket diameter, with socket height set separately (§2.16.2). Fig. 36 shows the socket as a central ring held by three radial spokes inside the bottom ring (our reading).
  - Inverted option for hanging shades (§2.16.2 refers to §2.15.2).
  - Vase sliders are not text boxes, so per §1.8 the display updates automatically when they change (our reading of §1.8, which exempts only text boxes; whether it updates during the drag is UNCONFIRMED).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Explicit layout: repeat count, gap fill and a live read-out of the ideal crop ratio (average perimeter / height) with one-click crop. LuBan decides duplication itself, and avoiding it means cropping the photo in a separate step, in an image editor or LuBan's 2D window (§2.16.1, Figs. 33–35; crop recipe §2.13.1).
  - Real answers to the distortion LuBan "does not deal with" (§2.16.1): a distortion-free `developable` mapping for cones, placing the photo on the cone's unrolled annular sector (LuBan already unrolls the cone for the colour image, Fig. 61), and a `conformal` mapping for any profile that keeps the local aspect exact at every height, so faces do not get squashed where a vase narrows. A live distortion heat map shows what each choice does (ours).
  - Vase profile editor: draggable control points on a 2D profile with a live 3D view, an overhang limit for support-free printing (suggest: 45°) and a minimum opening for the LED or socket; LuBan has "several sliders" (§2.16).
  - Vessel check: with a solid base, warn when Min thickness is under two extrusion widths (leak risk; our suggestion), because LuBan promises a water-holding vessel (§2.16.2).
  - Socket sized from a light-source profile; spoke count and width adjustable (Fig. 36 shows three).
  - Backlight preview with the LED inside; a seam-free wrap (the periodic grid shares its seam vertices) checked watertight by `validate()` (PLAN §4; CLAUDE.md).
  - Plus the shared improvements listed under LITH-FLAT.
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - Profile r(z): constant, linear, or a smooth monotone cubic through the control points (ours). Grid in (θ, z), periodic in θ.
  - Thickness offset along the profile's surface normal, not radially, so sloped walls keep their true thickness (ours).
  - Mapping (ours): `average` u = θ/2π, v linear in z. Per-row arc-length normalisation gives the same u on any surface of revolution, because every row is a circle, so it is not a separate option. `conformal` uses isothermal coordinates: u = θ/2π, v ∝ σ(z) = ∫ √(1 + r′(z)²) / r(z) dz, which keeps the local aspect exact while the scale follows r(z). `developable` (cone) places the photo on the unrolled annular sector of slant radius ρ and sector angle 2π·sin α, with α the cone's half-angle.
  - Base: a disk (solid) or an annulus with spokes and a socket tube (hollow), fused to the shell (research 04 §B.1; manifold for validation, PLAN §1).
  - Tests (ours): proptest over diameters 20–250 mm, height 20–250 mm, vase control diameters within ±40% of their mean, fixed/stretch, 1–6 photos, solid/hollow, socket 0–40 mm.
- **Milestone:** M2 (part 9, after LITH-ARC), first wave (PLAN §3 lists cylinder/cone/vase with flat, arc and sphere); step 3, after LITH-ARC.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - UI labels, defaults and ranges for diameters and height (they may follow the "Model size" / "Model diameter" pattern of Figs. 10 and 40; a guess), and the vase sliders' count, placement and limits.
  - Whether "height" in the crop rule is vertical or slant height; the exact duplication rule; how several photos are ordered (by file name as in §2.15.1?).
  - Solid-base thickness; whether socket diameter is inner; whether the spoke count is fixed; border band widths; hanger availability; whether an inverted cone (top wider) is allowed.

#### LITH-SPHERE — Globe lithophane (LuBan: Sphere)

- **LuBan path:** File → Create → Lithophane, Shape = Sphere (§2.17–2.17.3, PDF pp.31–34; blog: lithophane-2nd-release, "Sphere lithophane"; blog: sphere-lithophane-base, "Base socket option is added to sphere lithophane").
- **What it makes:** A spherical shell with a circular opening for the light, optionally with a socket beyond the opening. One photo is mapped onto it by one of three alignments (§2.17, Figs. 37–41, PDF pp.31–34).
- **Fabrication:**
  - 3D print; it "can be tricky" because support may be needed (§2.17).
  - Without support either orientation can work. With support: an exterior sphere prints with the opening facing down (support touches only the smooth inner surface), an interior sphere with the opening facing up (support touches only the smooth outer surface). LuBan flips the sphere when you switch exterior/interior (§2.17, Fig. 37).
  - Small spheres: disable support and let the printer close the upper gap (§2.23, PDF p.45).
  - Colour lithophane of a full sphere: generate two semi-spheres, attach the colour photo, glue them together (§2.22, PDF p.43).
- **Inputs:** Exactly one photo: "the sphere lithophane only takes one photo" (§2.17.1). To use several, join them first in the 2D window: File → Invoke 2D window, File → Open two images, Tool → Body → `Join <left, right>` or `Join <top, bottom>` and click the two images, repeat as needed, then File → Export → BMP, JPG, or PNG; or use File → Create → Collage (§2.17.1, PDF p.33; Collage added 2020-01-27, blog: collage; specified as TOOL-COLLAGE (part 7)).
- **Parameters:** Shared (LITH-COMMON and companions): Positive/Negative, Exterior/Interior (also flips the model's orientation, §2.17), Min/Max thickness, Resolution (0.1 mm/px default, §2.21.2), File size, Backlight, Save model. Border: UNCONFIRMED (Fig. 37 shows a light rim around the opening, Fig. 41 a dark ring line on the plain sphere). Hanger: UNCONFIRMED. Support: no LuBan support option is mentioned for the sphere; §2.10 names only Flat and Arc, and §2.17 and §2.23 discuss slicer support (inference). Shape-specific:

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |

On the sphere, switching also reverses the model: Exterior = opening facing down, Interior = opening facing up | UNCONFIRMED | `viewer` (Exterior), `light` (Interior) | §2.17; Fig. 37 (PDF p.31); §2.17.1 |

- **Outputs:** One STL, shown opening-down for exterior and opening-up for interior (whether the saved STL keeps that orientation is UNCONFIRMED), plus the colour image, which Fig. 61 (PDF p.44) shows as a row of 12 sphere gores (gore count is our count), to be cut out along its edges (§2.12, §2.22). AD3D: 3MF in mm with print orientation set from the rough side (one object, or two halves with `split`), STL, gore colour filter at true scale with cut lines, project file.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Switching exterior/interior flips the sphere: exterior opening down, interior opening up (§2.17, Fig. 37).
  - Photo alignment (§2.17.1): `top` maps the photo top to the sphere surface centre, for a standing lamp with the light at the bottom opening (Fig. 38 row 1). `bottom` maps the photo bottom there, which inverts the photo, for a hanging lamp (row 2). `center` maps the photo centre there: only the central circular region of the photo is used, which distorts normal photos badly but suits special-effect photos (Fig. 39 row 2: a circular "little planet"-style image).
  - Figures assume an exterior sphere; with interior the orientation is reversed (§2.17.1).
  - The offsets work with the `top` and `bottom` alignments only. They confine the photo to a central band, which reduces distortion, and take values between 0 and 1 (§2.17.1; Fig. 38 row 3 uses 0.5 and 0.5). Since 0.5 + 0.5 still leaves a band, each offset is not a fraction of the full photo height (our reading).
  - The sphere takes one photo (§2.17.1). It "tries to maintain the aspect ratio of a photo in similar ways as the cylinder, cone, and vase lithophanes", so a photo may be duplicated; to avoid that, make the photo's width/height "roughly 3:1" (§2.17.1).
  - Angle and diameter are typed in (Enter); the opening diameter is computed and displayed. It is proportional to the diameter, and for angles above 180° reducing the angle enlarges the opening. Usually you adapt the light with a socket instead of tuning the opening (§2.17.2).
  - Our inference (UNCONFIRMED): Fig. 40's 53.7 equals the chord on a radius 3.2 mm inside D/2: 2 × 46.8 × sin 35° = 53.69, whereas the outer chord is 100 × sin 35° = 57.4. 3.2 mm is the Max thickness in Fig. 10, so the opening is probably measured on the inner surface, which makes it affine rather than strictly proportional in D.
  - Socket: enabled by a non-zero socket diameter, which is the socket's inner diameter and should be less than the opening diameter, otherwise a warning appears on Enter. Base thickness and socket height shape the socket (§2.17.3, Fig. 41).
  - Fig. 41's first case (300°, D 100, socket 50) has a socket no smaller than the opening (50 on the outer chord, about 46.8 by our inference), yet a model is shown, so the warning seems not to block generation (our reading).
  - Fig. 41 shows the base as a funnel from the opening to a cylindrical socket tube; at base thickness 10 the tube is visibly thicker than at 4 (our reading).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Drive any two of angle, diameter and opening: e.g. "opening = 42 mm for this LED puck" solves for the angle. LuBan only computes the opening (§2.17.2).
  - Live socket validation while dragging, with an inline error and clamping; invalid geometry is never exported. LuBan warns after Enter and appears to build anyway (§2.17.3, Fig. 41).
  - A projection choice with a distortion heat-map overlay, and the exact non-duplicating aspect computed from angle and offsets instead of the rule of thumb "roughly 3:1" (§2.17.1).
  - Several photos placed natively around the band; no 2D-window join or collage step (§2.17.1).
  - Print planning: orientation set by the rough side (as in LuBan), a preview of where slicer supports would touch, and a one-click two-half export with the photo continuous across the seam. LuBan makes you generate the two semi-spheres yourself for colour work (§2.17, §2.22).
  - No pinched pole: a proper pole fan and a watertight `validate()` check; research 04 §B.1 lists "sphere poles and seam stitching" as an edge case.
  - Point-light backlight preview at the socket position (PLAN §4).
  - Plus the shared improvements listed under LITH-FLAT.
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - Polar angle θ from the pole (0) to θ_max = sphere_angle_deg / 2 at the opening edge, azimuth φ. `top`: v = (θ − θ_top) / (θ_bottom − θ_top) after the offsets; `bottom`: v reversed; `center`: azimuthal map, photo radius ∝ θ / θ_max inside the inscribed circle (ours).
  - Thickness along the radial normal. One pole vertex per surface with a triangle fan (no degenerate quads); the opening rim closes the shell; the socket funnel and tube share rings with the rim (research 04 §B.1; manifold for validation, PLAN §1).
  - Opening for display: 2·r·sin((360° − sphere_angle_deg) / 2), with r = D/2 (outer) or D/2 − t_max (inner, which matches Fig. 40); choose after checking (ours).
  - Tests (ours): proptest over angle 120–350°, D 30–250 mm, offsets 0–0.9, all three alignments, socket from 0 to just under the opening, both rough sides.
- **Milestone:** M2 (part 9, after LITH-REVOLVE), first wave; step 4, the last of the four first shapes, since it carries the most mapping and print-orientation work (PLAN §3).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Angle range (is 360° allowed? what minimum?), diameter range, default alignment, and the alignment option labels.
  - What the offsets are fractions of, and which projection LuBan uses.
  - The exact opening formula (inner or outer surface), and whether the socket warning blocks generation.
  - Socket and base geometry (the funnel profile), and whether base thickness matters without a socket.
  - Border and hanger availability; whether the gore count of the colour image (12 in Fig. 61, our count) is fixed or depends on size; the orientation of the saved STL.
  - Whether the sphere offers Fixed/Stretch like the revolve shapes; §2.17.1 says only that it keeps the aspect "in similar ways".
  - Related video (title only, not transcribed): short K98rQvMhx2g "LuBan Moon Light #3dprinting"; Fig. 37 shows a moon-textured sphere.

### Lithophane: Spiral, Stencil, Balloon, Tattoo, Color, printing tips (2.18–2.23)

This section covers LuBan's four special lithophane shapes: **Spiral** (a long strip printed as a roll, then flattened in hot water), **Stencil** (a flat lithophane cut to a black-and-white outline), **Balloon** (an inflated, two-sided, hollow lithophane) and **Tattoo** (a photo wrapped around any closed 3D model). It also covers the colour-filter image LuBan saves next to most lithophanes and the manual's printing tips, turned into a reusable hand-over checklist; the blog-only CMYK mode is specified in LITH-CMYK (part 7) and only cross-referenced here; the double-sided stencil is LITH-STENCIL's `double_sided` switch. Shared lithophane settings (§2.1–2.12) are specified in LITH-COMMON and its sub-entries (LITH-BASE-SOCKET, LITH-HANGER, LITH-EDGE-SUPPORT, LITH-BACKLIGHT-PREVIEW, LITH-EXPORT); each entry here lists which of them apply and then specifies only its own parameters, reusing LITH-COMMON's keys. The in-scope pages (PDF pp.34–45) show no parameter panel for Spiral, Stencil, Balloon or Tattoo. The only panel excerpt in range is Fig. 40 on PDF p.34, which belongs to Sphere (§2.17), and the only other dialogs are the 2D-window Properties and Crop boxes in Fig. 52–53. So nearly every default and range below is UNCONFIRMED, and our proposals are marked "(suggest: …)".

**Conventions for this section**
- In this range, PDF page = printed page + 1 (printed p.33 is PDF p.34).
- "Observed" means read from a figure, not stated in the text.
- The "LuBan label" column gives the manual's own wording (section headings or body text, typos kept). No panel screenshot in this range confirms the exact on-screen labels.
- Video dates in `videos_dated.txt` that end in -1019 are relative dates converted on 2026-10-19, so only the year (marked ~) means anything. Only titles are known: no video about these features has a transcript in the repo.
- Keys follow LITH-COMMON's style: snake_case, no unit suffix, lengths in mm and angles in degrees (stated in the Meaning column).
- `pixel_size` default: §2.21.2 says 0.1 mm/px for every shape except Tattoo, but Fig. 10 (PDF p.17) shows "Resolution 0.12" for Flat. LITH-COMMON records the conflict, and every "default 0.1" below carries this caveat.
- "luban-docs Get started p.N" cites LuBan's official Chinese deck of March 2019, through `docs/wip/spec-sections/00-luban-docs-notes.md`. The deck predates every shape in this section, so it is used only for the 2D window and for model import.

#### LITH-SPIRAL — Rolled-strip lithophane (LuBan: Spiral lithophane)

- **LuBan path:** File → Create → Lithophane, Shape = Spiral (manual §2.18, PDF p.34–35). The Shape drop-down is described in §2 intro and shown in Fig. 10 (PDF p.17). The drop-down text "Spiral" is UNCONFIRMED: the heading says "Spiral lithophane", and blog: lithophane-7th-release (2019-09-28) says "A new shape ,spiral,".
- **What it makes:** A long flat lithophane printed as a standing spiral roll, so that a strip too long for the printer fits on the bed. For example, a 500 × 50 mm lithophane prints as a roll 90 mm in diameter. After printing, the roll is softened in hot water and unfolded into a long flat lithophane (§2.18; Fig. 42, PDF p.35; blog: lithophane-7th-release, "enables the print of very large lithohphane").
- **Fabrication:**
  - 3D print. Fig. 42 shows the roll with its axis vertical, so the strip's height runs along Z and the photo prints upright, as §2.23 recommends (observed; LuBan's export orientation UNCONFIRMED).
  - Post-process: dip in hot water to soften, then unfold to a flat lithophane (§2.18; blog: lithophane-7th-release, "put in hot water and be reshaped to a long, flat lithophane").
  - The unrolled strip in Fig. 42 is still slightly curved (observed). A larger diameter gives less curvature and easier flattening (§2.18).
  - Material and water temperature are not stated (UNCONFIRMED; suggest: test a cut-off piece of the same filament first).
  - CNC/laser: not applicable (ours).
- **Inputs:** One photo, usually a wide panorama (the §2.18 example is 500 × 50 mm). Formats as LITH-COMMON (BMP/JPG/PNG implied).
- **Parameters:**
  - Shared (LITH-COMMON).
    - **Apply (stated):** `pixel_size`, default 0.1 mm/px (§2.21.2: every shape except Tattoo); Save model with the colour-filter image (§2.22: every shape except Balloon and Tattoo), see LITH-EXPORT and LITH-COLOR-FILTER.
    - **Seen in a figure:** border (`frame_tone`, `frame_width`, `frame_thickness`). Fig. 42 shows a frame along all four edges of the strip, rendered dark grey (observed). Its default, tone and thickness are UNCONFIRMED. A dark border must be thicker than the max thickness by 5 % (§2.7), which matters for the roll pitch below.
    - **UNCONFIRMED (suggest: apply):** `polarity` (§2.1); `relief_faces` (§2.2); `size_x`/`size_z` as the unrolled strip's length and height (aspect locked to the photo as for Flat, §2.13.1; UNCONFIRMED for Spiral); `thickness_min`/`thickness_max` (§2.4); `predicted_file_size` (§2.6); backlight preview (§2.11), shown on the unrolled strip.
    - **UNCONFIRMED (suggest: not offered):** base and socket (§2.8), hanger (§2.9), print stabilisers (§2.10 names only Flat and Arc).

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| diameter (manual wording: "The diameter of a spiral lithophane can be user specified"; panel label UNCONFIRMED, cf. Sphere's "Model diameter", Fig. 40, PDF p.34) | `spiral_diameter` | Diameter of the roll on the bed, mm. Larger = less curvature = easier to unfold and flatten | UNCONFIRMED (text example: 90 for a 500 × 50 mm strip) (suggest: automatic, the largest that fits the printer profile) | Lower limit: the smallest diameter that holds the whole strip, otherwise a warning. Upper limit UNCONFIRMED (suggest: the bed's shorter side minus 10 mm). Outer or inner diameter UNCONFIRMED (suggest: outer) | §2.18 (PDF p.34–35) |
| Model size (wording: "a 500 by 50 mm flat lithophane"; labels UNCONFIRMED) | `size_x`, `size_z` (LITH-COMMON) | Length and height of the strip once unrolled, mm | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED | §2.18; §2.3 |
| — (not in the sources) | `turn_gap` | Air gap between neighbouring turns, mm, so turns cannot fuse and hot water reaches every turn | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 1.0) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: ≥ 2 nozzle widths, ≤ 5) | Fig. 42 shows a gap between turns (observed) |
| — | `roll_outer_face` | Which face of the strip is on the outside of the roll | UNCONFIRMED (Fig. 42 shows the relief outside) (suggest: `relief`) | `relief`, `smooth` | Fig. 42 (observed) |
| — | `winding` | Direction of the spiral seen from above | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: `ccw`) | `cw`, `ccw` | ours |
| — | `fit_to_bed` | Set `spiral_diameter` to the largest value the active printer profile allows | (suggest: on) | on/off | ours; PLAN §4 machine profiles |
| — | `layout` | `roll` (LuBan's behaviour) or `tiles`: split the strip into bed-sized flat panels joined by alignment keys | (suggest: `roll`) | `roll`, `tiles` | ours; PLAN §4 tiling; LITH-COMMON names tiling as the alternative to §2.18 |
| — (read-only) | `turns`, `inner_diameter`, `min_diameter` | Number of turns, diameter where the strip starts, and the smallest diameter that holds the strip, mm | computed | — | ours (turns the §2.18 warning into a number) |

- **Outputs:**
  - LuBan: the §2.12 export folder, holding `<photo>_LP_Model.stl`, `Color_<W>_<H>.jpg` and LuBan's scene and settings files (see LITH-EXPORT). The shape token in the folder name is UNCONFIRMED.
  - AD3D: one watertight body as 3MF (mm) and streamed binary STL, the colour filter of the flat strip as PDF/PNG (LITH-COLOR-FILTER), the project file and `PRINT-CHECKLIST.txt` (LITH-EXPORT, LITH-PRINT-TIPS). With `layout = tiles`, each tile is a separate 3MF object.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - If the diameter is too small to make a spiral that holds the photo, LuBan shows a warning (§2.18).
  - Set the diameter "as large as possible": the larger it is, the smaller the curvature, and the easier the strip unfolds and flattens (§2.18).
  - Example: a 500 × 50 mm lithophane that does not fit a printer fits as a 90 mm spiral (§2.18).
  - Neighbouring turns do not touch (Fig. 42, observed).
  - About two turns are visible in Fig. 42, and the strip's inner end shows as a step on the inner turn (observed).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - **Fits the bed by default.** `fit_to_bed` picks the largest diameter the printer profile allows, which is exactly the manual's advice (§2.18). `min_diameter` is shown live instead of as a warning after Enter (§1.8, §2.18; PLAN §4 machine profiles).
  - **Live preview while dragging** diameter, gap and size, at low resolution during the drag and full resolution on release (PLAN §4). LuBan applies text boxes only on Enter (§1.8).
  - **Preview the result, not just the roll.** A rolled ⇄ unrolled toggle, with the light-through preview (LITH-BACKLIGHT-PREVIEW) on the unrolled strip (PLAN §4 realistic preview).
  - **Turns that cannot fuse.** The pitch is max(`thickness_max`, `frame_thickness`) + `turn_gap`, checked analytically. The border term matters because a dark border is thicker than the relief (§2.7) and Fig. 42 shows one. The roll is therefore free of self-intersection and watertight by construction, proven by a randomised-parameter test (CLAUDE.md).
  - **Tiles instead of a roll** (`layout = tiles`), for anyone who would rather skip the hot-water step (PLAN §4 tiling with alignment keys).
  - **Large-file safe.** 500 × 50 mm at 0.1 mm/px is about 2.5M relief samples: roughly 5M triangles, or 250 MB of binary STL (our arithmetic). The smooth face is triangulated only as finely as its curvature needs, the STL is streamed, and 3MF is offered (PLAN §4; research 00 §6; LITH-COMMON).
  - **Colour filter at 1:1** as a PDF strip. LuBan writes a JPG that has to be resized in MS Word (§2.22).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - Generator `lithophane/spiral`. The thickness field, shell, frame and validation come from the LITH-COMMON pipeline; only the surface mapping S(u, v) is new.
  - Archimedean spiral r(θ) = r_in + p·θ/2π, with pitch p = max(`thickness_max`, `frame_thickness`) + `turn_gap`. The strip length is L ≈ π(R² − r_in²)/p, so the minimum outer diameter is ≈ 2·√(r_in² + L·p/π) (our derivation, valid when r ≫ p).
  - Check against §2.18: with p ≈ 4–5 mm, a 500 mm strip fits a 90 mm roll starting at r_in ≈ 35–37 mm, in about two turns. That matches the roughly two turns visible in Fig. 42 (our arithmetic; observed).
  - Photo column u (mm along the strip) maps to θ by inverting the arc length. Arc length is measured on the strip's mid-surface, because bending preserves the mid-surface length, so the unrolled image comes out at the designed length (our design; LuBan's choice UNCONFIRMED).
  - The smooth face lies on the spiral; the relief face is offset along the normal by t(u, v) (research 04 §B.1: "map pixel (u,v) onto the parametric surface (cylinder, cone, sphere, spiral) and offset along the surface normal by t"). The frame band, top and bottom faces and end caps close the shell. No booleans are needed.
  - Heightmap references: s1lentCommit/stl-ready-image (MIT) and yomboprime/lithofun (MIT) (research 03 §3). rayon over rows; `image` + `fast_image_resize` (PLAN §1).
- **Milestone:** M2 (part 9, after LITH-POLY-ASSEMBLY), in the "+ more shapes" band after the first shape set (PLAN §3).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - The drop-down text, panel labels and defaults, and whether "diameter" means the outer or the inner diameter.
  - The turn gap, winding direction, start radius, and which face is outside (Fig. 42 suggests the relief).
  - Which shared options Spiral offers (polarity, thickness, border, base, hanger, stabilisers).
  - Whether LuBan lays the photo out along the inner face, the outer face or the mid-surface. This changes the flattened length.
  - Material, water temperature and flattening method. The manual only says "hot water".
  - No Spiral video is listed. ba6xj2IISNU "LuBan Lithophane 2" (13:05, ~2019) may show it (title only).

#### LITH-STENCIL — Shaped lithophane (LuBan: Stencil lithophane)

- **LuBan path:** File → Create → Lithophane, Shape = Stencil (manual §2.19, PDF p.35). The manual says "In the stencil mode"; the drop-down text is UNCONFIRMED. History from the blog:
  - stencil added 2021-04-18 (blog: lithophane-11th-release, "Generate a stencil lithophane based on a template image and a photo");
  - CMYK stencil 2024-01-30 (blog: lithophane-17th-release);
  - vector templates 2024-02-05 (blog: vector-image-template);
  - double-sided stencil 2026-01-03 (blog: lithophane-20th-release).
- **What it makes:** A flat lithophane with any outline. A black-and-white template sets the shape (white pixels = lithophane, black pixels = background) and the photo fills it (§2.19; Fig. 43, PDF p.35). It can take the shape of an object (§2.19). Fig. 44 (PDF p.36) shows a figure-shaped stencil by LuBan user Kennet McCoy, lit and unlit.
- **Fabrication:**
  - 3D print. As a flat lithophane, it follows §2.23's advice: print it standing up.
  - LuBan's stencil model stands upright in the XZ plane. §3.2.9 resizes a stencil lithophane in X and Z, "not X and Y, due to different orientation of the two models" (§3.2.9, PDF p.58).
  - Thin outline features stand unsupported in an upright print (ours; see `min_feature`).
  - CNC: lithophanes can be machined from a translucent material (§2 intro); the manual does not discuss this for Stencil.
- **Inputs:**
  - The template image first, then the photo (§2.19).
  - Templates: a black-and-white bitmap (§2.19), or a DXF or SHP vector (blog: vector-image-template). The blog says vectors help make "a box with smooth surface, free from bumpy artifacts when dealing with a bitmap template"; it says this of the box lithophane, and the same template input serves Stencil. AD3D accepts PNG/JPG/BMP/TIFF masks, SVG and DXF. SHP is LuBan's own format and is not supported (clean room, research 07 §f).
  - LuBan's 2D window can convert a binary bitmap to a vector with "Tool -> Convert -> Bitmap (binary image) -> Vector" (blog: bitmap-to-vector-conversion). Whether its output can be used as a Stencil template is UNCONFIRMED.
  - Photo: as LITH-COMMON.
- **Parameters:**
  - Shared (LITH-COMMON).
    - **Apply (stated):** `pixel_size`, default 0.1 mm/px (§2.21.2); `size_x`, the stencil's size in X (§3.2.9, PDF p.57: "Set the lithophane's size in X the same as that of the box"); Save model with the colour-filter image (§2.22). The size in the filter's file name is a bounding rectangle, because a colour photo "may not be a rectangle" (§2.22). Whether the Stencil filter follows the outline is UNCONFIRMED: Fig. 61 shows only a cone, a vase and a sphere.
    - **UNCONFIRMED (suggest: apply):** `polarity`; `relief_faces`; `size_z` (suggest: locked to the template's aspect ratio, as Flat locks it to the photo's, §2.13.1); `thickness_min`/`thickness_max`; `predicted_file_size`; backlight preview; `print_stabilisers` (suggest: offer it, as for Flat, §2.10).
    - **Hanger: UNCONFIRMED whether LuBan offers one (§2.9).** The template in Fig. 43 carries its own hanging hole, a black dot inside the white star, and the generated stencil has that hole, so black islands become holes (observed). AD3D needs no separate hanger for Stencil (suggest).
    - **UNCONFIRMED (suggest: not offered):** border (none visible in Fig. 43–44); base and socket.

- **Outputs:**
  - LuBan: one STL plus the colour-filter image, in the §2.12 export folder.
  - AD3D: one watertight body (3MF/STL), the colour filter as PDF/PNG with the outline as its cut line, the project file and the checklist (LITH-EXPORT).
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Choose the template first, then the photo (§2.19).
  - Center X and Y position the photo relative to the template; photo scale enlarges or reduces it (§2.19).
  - To make a photo match an object-shaped template, prepare it as described in §2.20.4 (§2.19); see LITH-TEMPLATE-FIT.
  - Double-sided (2026, blog-only): none stated. Related: the balloon lithophane also starts from a black-and-white template plus "one or two photos" (§2.20, PDF p.35), maps up to two photos to its front and back surfaces ordered by file name, shows the same photo on both if only one is given (§2.20, PDF p.36), and with a small non-zero expansion "such as 0.01" gives "a double-sided flat lithophane" (§2.20.1, PDF p.36). Whether the 2026 double-sided stencil differs from that balloon route is UNCONFIRMED.
  - §2.19 points to Figure 50 (a balloon motorcycle) for an object-shaped stencil. The stencil example is Fig. 44, so this is probably a cross-reference slip.
  - Box lithophane (§3.2.9, PDF p.56–58; PHOTO-BOX-LITHO): a new template is extracted from the 3D view of the box's inlay lid (View → Copy in the 3D window, View → Paste in the 2D window, then threshold and invert), and a stencil lithophane is generated from it with its size in X set to the box's. The letters in that template are "shrunk by half of the box thickness", so the sizes can still mismatch. The manual's fix is to read the lid's size with "Mesh → Statistics", then rescale the stencil with "Object → Transform" (size and flexible options, X and Z) and export the STL again.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - **Drag the photo on the outline**, with move and scale handles and a live preview. LuBan takes typed center/scale values that apply only on Enter (§2.19, §1.8; PLAN §4 live preview).
  - **Auto-fit the photo to the outline** in one step (LITH-TEMPLATE-FIT), instead of the 10-step crop in the 2D window (§2.20.4).
  - **Template from the photo**, by threshold or background removal. LuBan sends users to Photoshop or an image search (§2.20, §2.20.4).
  - **Smooth edges from any template.** Bitmaps are traced to smoothed polygons, and SVG/DXF files load directly. The blog says vector templates avoid the "bumpy artifacts" of bitmap templates, so in LuBan a bitmap template gives bumpy edges (blog: vector-image-template).
  - **Exact, watertight edges.** The outline is a true polygon with holes and the walls follow it, so there are no pixel steps. Narrow features are flagged against the nozzle width (CLAUDE.md watertight rule; research 04 §B.1).
  - **Colour filter cut to the outline** at 1:1 (PDF), instead of a bounding-box JPG resized in MS Word (§2.22).
  - **Exact size for box lids.** `size_x` measures the outline's own bounding box, and a "match lid" option takes the size from the lid's outline. That removes §3.2.9's screenshot-template, Mesh → Statistics and Object → Transform round trip.
  - **Batch:** one template and a folder of photos from the CLI (PLAN §4 batch/CLI).
  - **Two faces as an option, with a front/back preview toggle** and the backlight on either side. LuBan shipped the double-sided stencil as a separate release (blog: lithophane-20th-release; PLAN §4 realistic preview).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - Generator `lithophane/stencil`, on the LITH-COMMON pipeline.
  - Double-sided: two heightfields offset from a mid-surface, clipped to the template polygon (research 04 §B.1).
  - Template → threshold → contours (marching squares) → simplify and smooth → polygons with holes, cleaned with Clipper2 or i_overlay (PLAN §1). SVG/DXF paths are flattened to polygons. vtracer (MIT) is an alternative tracer (research 03 §5); research 04 §C lists OpenCV-style contours plus Douglas–Peucker.
  - Relief: sample the photo on the `pixel_size` grid and keep the interior cells. Boundary cells are clipped against the polygon and triangulated (constrained triangulation; crate UNCONFIRMED). The flat back is the outline polygon triangulated once, sharing its boundary vertices with the walls, so there are no T-junctions.
  - Template from the photo: a threshold on a chosen channel, as Photo magic does (§3 intro, Fig. 63), or background removal with BiRefNet (MIT; research 04 §C).
- **Milestone:** M2 (part 9, after LITH-SPHERE), in the "+ more shapes" band (PLAN §3). Build it first among this section's shapes, because Balloon, the Box lithophane (PHOTO-BOX-LITHO, §3.2.9; LITH-BOX) and LITH-CMYK reuse its outline pipeline.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Defaults, units and ranges of center X/Y and photo scale.
  - How model size is tied to the template: whether size X spans the white region or the whole template image (§3.2.9 hints at a mismatch), whether Z follows the aspect ratio, and what thickness uncovered areas get.
  - Whether Stencil offers a border, hanger, base or stabilisers.
  - How the double-sided stencil works, and whether it uses a second photo. It is blog-only, and video yOfBTv3PrMI "LuBan Lithophane v20 Double sided lithophane" (7:40) is known by title only.
  - Which DXF entities LuBan accepts.
  - The content of video aFwIDWrhkxk "LuBan Stencil lithophane" (4:08, ~2021; title only).

#### LITH-BALLOON — Pillow lithophane (LuBan: Balloon lithophane)

- **LuBan path:** File → Create → Lithophane, Shape = Balloon (manual §2.20–2.20.3, PDF p.35–37; drop-down text UNCONFIRMED). Added 2020-06-11 (blog: lithophane-8th-release, "Generate balloon lithophane").
- **What it makes:** A two-sided, balloon-like lithophane. A template outline is inflated into a pillow whose front and back surfaces each show a photo (§2.20; Fig. 45–48, PDF p.36–37). It is a double-surface, hollow model, unlike Photo magic's single-surface, solid balloon (§3.1, PDF p.46–47). In the shape of an object and lit from inside, it shows a picture of that object (§2.20.4; Fig. 50, PDF p.38).
- **Fabrication:**
  - 3D print, with a light inside (§2.20.4).
  - Fig. 50 (PDF p.38) shows a white motorcycle balloon by LuBan user Cyril Burnet, unlit and lit, with the relief on the outside (observed). In both photos a short cylinder enters the lower left of the print, probably the lamp or its holder (observed; UNCONFIRMED).
  - LuBan has no socket option. The manual's route is to intersect the exported balloon with a cylinder tube in other software such as MeshMixer, which leaves the tube as an open socket (§2.20; video tjD-cq9AjkQ, title only).
  - Filament colour changes the preview: "Changing the filament color can produce vivid rendering effects" (Fig. 54 caption, PDF p.40). Fig. 54 shows the same lotus rendered in white, pink and deep pink (observed).
  - Print orientation and supports are not discussed (UNCONFIRMED). Suggest: stand it on its rim so both faces print upright, as §2.23 prefers, and print without supports, because supports inside a closed shell cannot be removed (ours).
- **Inputs:**
  - A balloon template: a black-and-white image where white = balloon and black = background. Templates are easy to find online, for example by searching "star black and white" (§2.20, Fig. 45).
  - One or two photos (§2.20).
  - Photo formats as LITH-COMMON. Template formats as LITH-STENCIL (UNCONFIRMED for Balloon).
- **Parameters:**
  - Shared (LITH-COMMON).
    - **Apply (stated):** `pixel_size`, default 0.1 mm/px (§2.21.2); `filament_color` in the preview (Fig. 54 caption).
    - **Not offered by LuBan (stated):** the socket (§2.20) and the colour-filter image (§2.22). AD3D adds both (LITH-BASE-SOCKET; `split_halves`).
    - **UNCONFIRMED (suggest: apply):** `polarity`; `thickness_min`/`thickness_max`; size (suggest: `size_x`, with `size_z` from the template's aspect ratio); `predicted_file_size`.
    - **Fixed in AD3D (suggest):** `relief_faces` = `viewer` (relief outside, lamp inside), as Fig. 50 shows (observed). Whether LuBan offers Exterior/Interior for Balloon is UNCONFIRMED.
    - **UNCONFIRMED (suggest: not offered):** border, hanger, stabilisers.

Where white reaches the image edge, the edge becomes the outline: the black-heart template gives a square pillow with a heart-shaped hole (Fig. 45 right, observed) | none (required) | B/W image (formats UNCONFIRMED; suggest: as LITH-STENCIL) | §2.20; Fig. 45 (PDF p.36) |

- **Outputs:**
  - LuBan: one STL in the §2.12 folder, with no colour-filter image (§2.22).
  - AD3D: one watertight hollow body (3MF/STL), or two halves with `split_halves`; optional colour filters for each half (LITH-COLOR-FILTER); the project file and checklist.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - The white region becomes the balloon. With a black heart on white, the surrounding region becomes a balloon with a heart-shaped hole (Fig. 45).
  - Up to two photos map to the front and back. They are ordered by file name, and with one photo both faces show it (§2.20). Fig. 46 shows each face reading correctly from its own side (observed).
  - A larger expansion blows the balloon up more. A small non-zero value such as 0.01 gives a double-sided flat lithophane (§2.20.1).
  - There is a default space between front and back, "often very small"; extra space adds to it, for example to fit a socket (§2.20.2). In Fig. 48 the extra space appears as a straight wall between the two domes (observed). A thin straight band along the outline is visible even at extra space 0 (Fig. 48 left) and in Fig. 45 and 47, which fits the "very small" default space (observed).
  - Center X/Y position the photo on the balloon, and photo scale enlarges or reduces it (§2.20.3).
  - If the photo has a dark boundary or does not match the outline, the result is poor (Fig. 51). Crop the photo to the template's bounding box first (§2.20.4; see LITH-TEMPLATE-FIT).
  - Photo magic → Balloon (§3.1; PHOTO-BALLOON) uses "similar" settings without photo mapping and makes a single-surface solid.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - **A built-in light socket.** Pick a point on the rim and a lamp size; a tube is merged and bored with a robust boolean, and `extra_gap` grows to fit it. LuBan has no socket and points to MeshMixer (§2.20; video tjD-cq9AjkQ "Use MeshMixer to create a light socket for LuBan balloon lithophane", 13:28).
  - **Front and back photo slots** with a swap button. LuBan orders photos by file name (§2.20), and the manual's way to reorder photos is to rename the files and select them again (§2.15.1, for poly-face).
  - **One-click fit to the outline** (LITH-TEMPLATE-FIT), replacing §2.20.4's 10 steps and fixing the dark rim in Fig. 51.
  - **Flat double-sided is simply `inflation = 0`**, not the 0.01 workaround (§2.20.1).
  - **A smooth or ridged profile.** `round` avoids the medial-axis creases visible at expansion 2 in Fig. 47; `ridge` keeps that look.
  - **A lamp-inside preview.** LITH-BACKLIGHT-PREVIEW with `lamp_position` inside the shell and transmission based on thickness (PLAN §4 realistic preview). The manual admits that "Computer graphics rendering cannot fully simulate the actual physical process" (§2.2).
  - **Colour for balloons.** With `split_halves`, a colour filter can go inside before the halves are glued, which is the method the manual gives for spheres (§2.22). LuBan writes no colour photo for Balloon (§2.22).
  - **Live preview while dragging** inflation, gap and photo placement (PLAN §4; §1.8).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - Generator `lithophane/balloon`, on the LITH-COMMON pipeline.
  - Outline polygons with holes come from the template, as in LITH-STENCIL.
  - Inflation height h(x, y) comes either from the distance to the outline with a round profile, or from solving Poisson's equation (∇²h = −c, with h = 0 on the outline) and taking a square root. Research 04 §B.1 calls LuBan's method UNCONFIRMED ("likely distance-transform or Poisson inflation, as in Teddy-style inflation"). The creases at expansion 2 in Fig. 47 fit a distance-transform profile (our reading).
  - The outer surfaces are z = ±(g/2 + h), where g = `rim_gap` + `extra_gap`, joined by a straight wall along the outline (Fig. 48).
  - Photos are projected orthogonally onto the template plane, with offset and scale. The back photo is mirrored so it reads correctly from behind (Fig. 46).
  - Thickness t is applied inward along the normal. Near the rim, where the two inner surfaces would cross, the shell becomes solid and the cavity is closed along that contour. The result is watertight by construction. Fallback: a level-set offset through manifold's `levelSet`, which needs our own signed-distance function; research 08 §2.10 warns that it is not ready-made.
  - The socket is the only boolean: a manifold union with the tube, then subtraction of its bore, on the local region only (LITH-BASE-SOCKET; manifold, Apache-2.0, research 03 §13).
- **Milestone:** M2 (part 9, after LITH-TEMPLATE-FIT), in the "+ more shapes" band, after LITH-STENCIL (they share the outline pipeline). Research 04 rates it difficulty 3.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Panel labels and defaults; what Expansion measures (no unit is given), whether 0 is accepted, and its upper limit; the unit of Extra space and the size of the default space.
  - How thick the uncovered areas are (Fig. 49 renders them plain), and what center X/Y and photo scale are measured in (Fig. 49 suggests fractions of the outline's size).
  - Which photo, by file-name order, goes on the front.
  - Whether the polarity, thickness, border and hanger settings apply.
  - How LuBan closes the rim region, and whether the relief is always outside (Fig. 50 suggests so).
  - Print orientation and supports.
  - Ghosting in a backlit double-sided flat lithophane (expansion 0.01): with no room for a lamp inside, both layers are seen at once (our concern; not discussed).
  - The content of videos emF-SL3TSbk "LuBan Lithophane Balloon" (6:11, ~2020), Br-ojEQmZUM "How to prepare template and picture for Balloon lithophane" (4:35, ~2020) and tjD-cq9AjkQ (13:28, ~2020); titles only. 9scNC9aa5D0 "Easter egg lithophane" (2:37) may be a balloon (UNCONFIRMED).
