#### LITH-TEMPLATE-FIT — Fit photo to outline (LuBan: Balloon of an object, 2D-window crop workflow)

- **LuBan path:** Manual §2.20.4 (PDF p.37–40), in ten numbered steps. Steps 2–8 run in LuBan's 2D window (Fig. 52–53, PDF p.39), and steps 9–10 return to the 3D window. The manual's step numbers are kept:
  1. Run LuBan.
  2. File → Invoke 2D window.
  3. File → Open, open the template image.
  4. Tool → Geometry → Labeling. Accept the default parameters, then close the generated labeling image.
  5. Right-click the light-blue rectangle → Properties, and copy the coordinates.
  6. File → Open, open the original photo.
  7. Tool → Body → Crop. Pick any two points, then overwrite the dialog's coordinates by pasting.
  8. File → Export → BMP, JPG, or PNG.
  9. File → Invoke 3D window.
  10. File → Create → Lithophane, then generate the balloon from the template and the cropped photo.

  §2.19 sends Stencil users to the same procedure.
  - The 2D window is LuBan's image-processing frame, switched with "File → Invoke 2/3D window" (§1.7). In the 2019 Chinese build the item reads 切换到 2D 窗口 [Switch to 2D window], with shortcut U (luban-docs Get started p.2).
  - Fig. 52's 2D windows show the menus File, Batch, View, Tool, 3D, Draw, Help (observed). The 2019 build's 2D window also had 光测 [Optical measurement] (luban-docs Get started p.8).
- **What it makes:** A copy of the photo cropped to the bounding box of the template's white region, so that the photo lines up exactly with a Balloon or Stencil outline (§2.20.4; Fig. 54, PDF p.40). In AD3D this is a step inside the shape generators, not a separate file.
- **Fabrication:** None (image preparation).
- **Inputs:** The template and the original photo. The template is extracted from the photo in any image editor, for example Photoshop (§2.20.4). The pasted coordinates only work if both images share pixel coordinates (our inference).
- **Parameters:**
  - Shared (LITH-COMMON): `crop` (the crop rectangle on the photo) is reused for the fitted crop.

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tool → Geometry → Labeling (dialog: "just use the default parameters and click OK") | — (replaced by `template_fit`) | Labels the template's regions (our reading of "Labeling") and adds a light-blue rectangle around the white region; the generated labeling image "can be closed" (§2.20.4 step 4) | dialog values not shown (UNCONFIRMED) | UNCONFIRMED | §2.20.4 step 4; Fig. 52 (PDF p.39) |
| Properties → FRGD, BKGD | — | Foreground and background colour of the rectangle (our reading of the labels) | cyan swatches (shown in Fig. 52; not stated as defaults) | colour | Fig. 52 |
| Properties → Solid | — | Fill the rectangle (our reading) | unchecked (shown) | check box | Fig. 52 |
| Properties → Movable | — | Allow the rectangle to be dragged (our reading) | unchecked (shown) | check box | Fig. 52 |
| Properties → Line width | — | Width of the rectangle's outline (our reading); unit UNCONFIRMED | 10 (shown) | spin box | Fig. 52 |

The dialog explains: "Example: 26 11 400 300 / Crop region: x: [26, 400), y: [11, 300) / Note: x = 400, y = 300 are not included." The same Tool → Body → Crop dialog appears in §2.13.1 (Fig. 23, PDF p.24), which calls the values x1 y1 x2 y2 and says "x2 − x1 is the width" | the region picked with the mouse (step 7: "A dialogue box will show the coordinates of the selected region"); Fig. 53 shows it overwritten with 108 91 1393 1200 | 4 integers; right and bottom exclusive | Fig. 53 (PDF p.39); §2.20.4 step 7; §2.13.1 |
| File → Export → BMP, JPG, or PNG | — (no file: the crop is stored in the project) | Save the cropped photo | — | BMP, JPG, PNG | §2.20.4 step 8 |

| — | `edge_bleed` | Replace photo pixels within this distance inside the outline with the nearest inner colour, so no dark rim shows, px | (suggest: 2) | 0–20 | ours; Fig. 51 (PDF p.38) |
| — | `template_source` | Where the outline comes from | (suggest: `file`) | `file`, `threshold` (of the photo), `segment` (background removal) | ours; §2.20.4 (template made in "any image processing software, such as Photoshop") |

- **Outputs:**
  - LuBan: a new cropped image file (§2.20.4 step 8).
  - AD3D: no extra file. The crop, offset and scale are parameters in the project, so they support undo/redo (PLAN §4).
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Using the photo and template as they are gives a poor result: the lotus has a dark boundary and does not match the balloon's shape (Fig. 51, PDF p.38).
  - The fix is to crop the photo so it has no extra boundary pixels. The two crop points picked with the mouse need not be accurate, because the pasted coordinates replace them (§2.20.4 step 7).
  - After the crop, the photo matches the outline exactly (Fig. 54).
  - The crop rectangle is given as "left top right bottom", with the right and bottom edges excluded (Fig. 53).
  - Implied (our inference): at the default center and scale, LuBan stretches the photo over the bounding box of the template's white region, not over the whole template image. A template cut from the same photo would already line up if the photo were mapped to the whole image, yet Fig. 51 shows a mismatch that the bounding-box crop fixes.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - **One step instead of ten across two windows** (§2.20.4). AD3D finds the outline's bounding box and crops the photo automatically; the result can still be dragged on the canvas.
  - **Works when the two images differ in size:** fit by bounding box, then adjust. LuBan's copy-and-paste only works when the pixel coordinates match (our inference from §2.20.4 steps 5–7).
  - **No dark rim.** `edge_bleed` fixes Fig. 51's boundary problem even after a slightly loose cut-out.
  - **Template from the photo** (`template_source`): a channel threshold, or background removal with BiRefNet (MIT, research 04 §C), instead of Photoshop (§2.20.4).
  - **Non-destructive.** The fit is stored in the project and can be undone, with no stray image files (PLAN §4 projects, undo/redo).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - Take the bounding box of the thresholded white region (all components; LuBan's choice UNCONFIRMED), set `crop` in shared pixel coordinates, and map the photo to the outline's bounding box in mm.
  - Edge bleed: a distance transform, or jump flooding from the interior, copies the nearest interior colour into the rim band (ours).
  - `image` crate; tracing as in LITH-STENCIL.
- **Milestone:** M2 (part 9, after LITH-STENCIL), together with LITH-STENCIL.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - The Labeling dialog's parameters and defaults.
  - Whether LuBan uses the bounding box of the largest region or of all regions.
  - Whether LuBan maps the photo to the region's bounding box at default settings (inferred, not stated).
  - In Fig. 52 the template window is titled "Dilation" (observed), which hints that the template was dilated. Whether dilation is a recommended step is UNCONFIRMED.
  - The content of videos Br-ojEQmZUM "How to prepare template and picture for Balloon lithophane" (4:35, ~2020), ue0o2PnOfZU "Photo to Template" (13:08, ~2025) and wDikiVpunws "Add background shape to an image" (3:15, ~2020); titles only.

#### LITH-TATTOO — Model-wrap lithophane (LuBan: Tattoo lithophane)

- **LuBan path:** File → Create → Lithophane, Shape = Tattoo (manual §2.21–2.21.4, PDF p.40–43; drop-down text UNCONFIRMED). Added 2020-11-07 (blog: lithophane-10th-release, "Generate a tattoo lithophane based on any 3D model").
- **What it makes:** A photo applied continuously over the surface of any 3D model (Fig. 55, PDF p.40). Unlike a balloon, there is no gap between the front and back surfaces. In fact there is no front or back, only an axis that the photo wraps around (§2.21). The result is a double-surface, hollow model (§2.21).
- **Fabrication:**
  - 3D print, as a hollow shell (§2.21). Fig. 55 shows the relief on the outside (observed).
  - LuBan makes no socket: one "may be inserted using other software, such as MeshMixer" (§2.21).
  - A hollow input model gives four layers of surfaces, which can cause printing errors (§2.21).
  - Orientation and supports are not discussed (UNCONFIRMED). Suggest: print support-free, because supports inside a closed shell cannot be removed (ours); any support must touch only the smooth side (§2.23).
- **Inputs:**
  - A 3D model, selected before the photo (the order implied by §2.21.2). Any model works in principle, but a single-surface, closed (solid) model is recommended (§2.21), ideally relatively smooth and low density (§2.21.2).
  - Formats: UNCONFIRMED for this mode. LuBan opens STL and OBJ (blog: password-protected-3d-file), and the 2019 build's File → Open caption says it opens a 3D model in OBJ, PLY or STL format [打开一个 OBJ, PLY, 或 STL 文件格式的三维模型] (luban-docs Get started p.2). AD3D accepts STL, OBJ, PLY and 3MF through the shared import and repair (research 00 §4; PLAN §3 M3).
  - One photo (§2.21).
- **Parameters:**
  - Shared (LITH-COMMON).
    - **Apply (stated):** `pixel_size`, but with a Tattoo default of 10 mm/px (§2.21.2); Save model, without the colour-filter image (§2.22).
    - **Not offered by LuBan (implied):** the socket, since §2.21 sends users to other software for it. AD3D adds it (LITH-BASE-SOCKET).
    - **No front and back (stated, §2.21):** the photo wraps around an axis instead of mapping to two faces. Whether LuBan offers Exterior/Interior (`relief_faces`) for Tattoo is UNCONFIRMED; Fig. 55 shows the relief outside (observed). AD3D: `relief_faces` = `viewer` (suggest).
    - **UNCONFIRMED (suggest: apply):** `polarity`; `thickness_min`/`thickness_max`; `predicted_file_size` (Fig. 58 quotes file sizes); backlight preview with a lamp inside (`lamp_position`).
    - **UNCONFIRMED (suggest: replace):** `size_x`/`size_y`/`size_z` with a uniform `model_scale`, since the model defines the shape.
    - **UNCONFIRMED (suggest: not offered):** border, base, hanger, stabilisers.

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3D model (selected before the photo; selection control UNCONFIRMED) | `model` | Mesh to wrap the photo around. Recommended: closed, single-surface, smooth, low density | none (required) | A hollow input gives four surface layers and print errors. AD3D: STL, OBJ, PLY, 3MF | §2.21; §2.21.2 |
| — | `model_scale`, `model_unit` | Uniform scale of the input model, and the unit assumed for a unitless STL/OBJ | (suggest: 1, mm) | scale > 0; unit mm, cm, m, inch | ours. The 2019 build asked for a unit (m, dm, cm, mm, inch) on entering Mesh → LuBan (luban-docs Get started p.3–4); whether Tattoo asks is UNCONFIRMED |
| photo | `photos` (one) | Image wrapped onto the model | required | as LITH-COMMON | §2.21 |
| Axis to wrap a photo around | `wrap_axis` | Axis the photo wraps around; it "determines the orientation of the photo on a 3D model" (§2.21.1). In Fig. 57 the photo's "up" points along the chosen axis and its width runs around it (observed) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: `+z`) | `+x`, `-x`, `+y`, `-y`, `+z`, `-z` ("Six possible options", §2.21.1; Fig. 57 caption) | §2.21.1; Fig. 56–57 (PDF p.41) |

| Resolution (the panel label Fig. 10 shows for Flat; for Tattoo UNCONFIRMED) | `pixel_size` (LITH-COMMON) | Size of one photo pixel on the surface, mm/px; sets mesh density and file size | 10 for Tattoo (§2.21.2). Every other shape: 0.1 per §2.21.2, though Fig. 10 shows 0.12 for Flat | Fig. 58: 10, 1 and 0.2 mm/px give 1 MB, 8 MB and 190 MB. Lower limit UNCONFIRMED. LuBan locks it at 10 between choosing a model and choosing a photo | §2.21.2; Fig. 58 (PDF p.42); Fig. 10 (PDF p.17) |

If 1 spans one full turn, 1.2 spans more than a turn; how LuBan handles the overlap is UNCONFIRMED | §2.21.4; Fig. 60 (PDF p.43) |

At 0.8 the photo no longer covers the full height: the bottom tip is plain and a dashed seam shows near the top of the lobes (Fig. 60 right, observed) | §2.21.4; Fig. 60 |

- **Outputs:**
  - LuBan: one STL in the §2.12 folder, with no colour-filter image (§2.22). The file size depends on the resolution: 1 MB at 10, 8 MB at 1 and 190 MB at 0.2 mm/px (Fig. 58).
  - AD3D: one watertight hollow body (zip-compressed 3MF and streamed STL), the project file and the checklist.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - The photo is mapped to the surface continuously (§2.21). Fig. 55 and Fig. 59 show it wrapping the whole circumference: the front shows one part of the photo and the back shows the rest (observed).
  - Generation is slow, so the resolution defaults to 10 mm/px "to speed up the display". Until a photo is chosen it stays at 10 even if another value is entered, because the resolution is not really used to display a model without a photo (§2.21.2).
  - Small values render at high quality but take long to generate. Use a large value while adjusting position and scale, then a small value for the final model (§2.21.2).
  - A high-density input is slow even at a large resolution value, so prefer smooth, low-density models. View the vertices and edges with Edit → Edge → Enable (§2.21.2).
  - Fig. 58's file sizes grow about 24× from 1 to 0.2 mm/px (8 → 190 MB, close to the 25× pixel count) but only 8× from 10 to 1 mm/px (1 → 8 MB). That fits a mesh refined to the pixel size but never coarser than the input model (our reading, UNCONFIRMED).
  - Center X moves the photo around the axis and Center Y moves it up and down (§2.21.3). Photo scale X/Y scale it horizontally and vertically (§2.21.4).
  - The input should be solid; a hollow input gives four surface layers and printing errors (§2.21).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - **Instant placement preview.** While you drag the axis, centre and scale, the photo is projected onto the model as a GPU texture, with no mesh rebuild. The full-resolution mesh is built on release or at export. LuBan needs the 10 mm/px workaround and locks the value (§2.21.2; PLAN §1 preview vs final quality).
  - **Speed independent of the input's density.** The input is remeshed once to the target pixel size and the result is cached, so each regeneration costs the same for a dense model as for a light one. The manual says dense models are slow "even with a large resolution value" (§2.21.2).
  - **Multi-core and cancellable, with progress** (PLAN §4). LuBan calls tattoo generation "time-consuming" (§2.21.2).
  - **Mesh doctor on input.** Hollow, double-walled or open models are detected and fixed or rejected before generation, which avoids the four-layer failure (§2.21; PLAN §4 mesh doctor).
  - **Any axis**, set with a gizmo, besides the six presets. §2.21.1 offers only ±X/±Y/±Z.
  - **A built-in socket or opening** (LITH-BASE-SOCKET), instead of MeshMixer (§2.21).
  - **No self-intersections.** In concave regions the inner surface falls back to a signed-distance offset, so the shell stays watertight (research 04 §B.1 edge case "self-intersection when offsetting concave tattoo regions"; CLAUDE.md).
  - **Big files handled.** The exact size is predicted before export, the STL is streamed and the 3MF is zip-compressed (PLAN §4). Fig. 58 shows 190 MB at 0.2 mm/px.
  - **Colour, later.** Per-vertex colour or a texture in 3MF for colour printers. LuBan makes no colour photo for Tattoo (§2.22).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - Generator `lithophane/tattoo`.
    1. Import, weld and validate the model, requiring a closed manifold. Detect nested shells with a winding-number test (libigl, MPL-2.0; research 08 §2.10). This is the import and repair of PLAN §3 M3, which is on the critical path.
    2. Remesh isotropically to an edge length of about `pixel_size` (pmp-library, MIT; research 00 §3). Where the input is already finer than `pixel_size`, keep its detail instead of coarsening the shape (ours; Fig. 58's file sizes suggest LuBan behaves this way, our reading).
    3. Map cylindrically about the axis: azimuth φ → u and height along the axis → v, applying `photo_azimuth`, `photo_offset_axial` and the two scales. At scale 1 the photo spans the full circumference and the model's height along the axis (our reading of Fig. 55 and Fig. 59; LuBan's normalisation UNCONFIRMED). Caps that face along the axis make the projection degenerate, so they are treated as uncovered (suggest; LuBan's behaviour UNCONFIRMED).
    4. Compute thickness from intensity (LITH-COMMON). The outer surface is the remeshed model with relief; the inner surface is offset inward along the vertex normals. Concave regions fall back to a level-set offset (manifold, Apache-2.0), which needs our own signed-distance function and a robust winding number (research 08 §2.10).
    5. Stitch and run `validate()`, with property tests over random axes, offsets and scales (PLAN §5).
  - GPU preview: a three.js shader computes the same cylindrical UV and shades with the photo's intensity.
  - Research 00 §3 describes the method as "photo mapped along an axis onto a remeshed model and offset along normals" (pmp-library, manifold). Difficulty 4 (research 04 §D).
- **Milestone:** M12 (part 9, after CUT-NATURAL). PLAN §3 lists it under Later. Depends on M3 import and repair.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - The default axis and its origin; the mapping (cylindrical is our reading); how caps and the seam are handled.
  - Defaults, units and signs of Center X/Y and photo scale.
  - The thickness rule: min/max thickness, and whether the relief goes inward or outward.
  - Supported model formats, whether model size can rescale the model, and whether LuBan asks for the model's unit, as Mesh → LuBan did in 2019 (luban-docs Get started p.3–4).
  - How LuBan handles photo scale X above 1, where the photo spans more than one turn (Fig. 60 shows no obvious overlap), and where the wrap seam goes.
  - Whether Fig. 58's file sizes mean LuBan never coarsens the input mesh.
  - Related features that also take a 3D model are blog-only and specified in part 7, not here. Whether they share code with Tattoo is UNCONFIRMED:
    - LITH-BRONZE (blog: lithophane-12th-release; videos aBlgIgK6R64, UkeI-zNIxk4, S-EyVL_ZmqU; short 6TAGFHFhbZI);
    - LITH-TILE (blog: lithophane-21st-release; videos TC0TzSb50zc, DipWb-mT2rM; short xhc5zq-IIwc);
    - FORM-TILING (blog: tiling, "Map a texture photo onto a 3D model"; video oVdtZBxa9UM).
  - The content of videos OA_BKXg3kHo "LuBan Lithophane v10" (3:50; v10 is the tattoo release) and OaBs6k90h_o "Apply a face image on a 3D model" (7:35); titles only.

#### LITH-COLOR-FILTER — Colour filter sheet (LuBan: Color lithophane)

- **LuBan path:** The manual describes no control for it. Save model writes the colour image into the export folder for every shape except Balloon and Tattoo (manual §2.22, PDF p.42–45; §2.12, PDF p.22–23). Added 2020-09-16 (blog: lithophane-9th-release, "Generate a color image for making a color lithophane").
- **What it makes:** A colour image with the intensity removed, to be printed on transparent paper and attached to the back of the lithophane. When lit from behind, the print acts as a colour filter while the lithophane's thickness modulates the intensity (§2.22; Fig. 62, PDF p.45).
- **Fabrication:**
  - Print on transparent paper; normal white paper may work if the light is strong (§2.22).
  - Before printing, resize the image to the size in its file name, for example in MS Word. The resize may not keep the aspect ratio, because the image's aspect ratio in pixels can differ from its aspect ratio in mm (§2.22).
  - The image may not be a rectangle. In Fig. 61 (PDF p.44) a cone gives an annular sector, and a vase and a sphere give vertical gores (observed). Cut along the outline and attach it to the back of the lithophane (§2.22).
  - For a full sphere, make two half spheres, attach the colour print, then glue the halves together (§2.22).
- **Inputs:** The lithophane's colour photo, and the shape's surface (for unrolling).
- **Parameters:**
  - Shared (LITH-EXPORT): the `export_formats` values `color_filter_pdf` and `color_filter_png` switch the filter on. The AD3D file name is `<photo>_color_filter_<W>x<H>mm.pdf` (LITH-EXPORT).

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (automatic; no control described) | `export_formats` ∋ `color_filter_pdf`, `color_filter_png` (LITH-EXPORT) | Write the colour filter | LuBan: for "All lithophane shapes except for balloon and tattoo" (§2.22). Whether it is also written for a greyscale photo is UNCONFIRMED | AD3D: on/off per format (suggest: on when the photo is in colour) | §2.22; §2.12 |
| file name "Color_105_86.jpg" | — (LuBan naming) | The bounding rectangle's physical size in mm, written into the file name | `Color_<W>_<H>.jpg` | — | §2.22 (PDF p.42); §2.12 lists `Color_46_46.jpg` (PDF p.23) |
| — | `color_filter_media` | Print medium, which sets the ink density | (suggest: `transparency`) | `transparency`, `white_paper` | ours; §2.22 (names both media) |
| — | `color_filter_dpi` | Raster resolution embedded in the file, so that pixels map to mm exactly | (suggest: 300) | 150–1200 | ours; §2.22 (pixel vs mm aspect problem) |
| — | `color_filter_cut_line` | Draw the outline to cut along, plus gore labels and alignment ticks | (suggest: on) | on/off | ours; §2.22, Fig. 61 |
| — | `color_filter_bleed` | Colour extended beyond the cut line, mm | (suggest: 1) | 0–5 | ours |
| — | `color_filter_gain` | Saturation gain, to offset the filament's own tint | (suggest: 1.0) | 0–2 | ours |

- **Outputs:**
  - LuBan: `Color_<W>_<H>.jpg` in the export folder (§2.22, §2.12).
  - AD3D: `<photo>_color_filter_<W>x<H>mm.pdf` at 1:1 with the cut line, plus a PNG with its DPI set (LITH-EXPORT).
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - LuBan makes it for every lithophane shape except Balloon and Tattoo (§2.22).
  - The size in the file name is the bounding rectangle of a pattern that may be irregular (§2.22, Fig. 61).
  - The colour image looks quite different from the photo: as much of the intensity as possible is removed, because the lithophane's thickness does the intensity modulation (§2.22, Fig. 62).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - **Exact size, no MS Word.** A 1:1 PDF and a PNG with the right DPI, so the aspect error the manual warns about cannot happen (§2.22).
  - **Cut lines and labels** for sectors and gores (Fig. 61), with alignment ticks that match marks on the lithophane's frame (ours).
  - **See the colour before printing.** The light-through preview multiplies the filter by the lithophane's transmission (LITH-BACKLIGHT-PREVIEW; PLAN §4 realistic preview). LuBan's backlight sets the light colour, the filament colour and the light intensity (§2.11); the manual does not say it previews the colour filter.
  - **Also for Balloon** (one filter per half, with `split_halves`) and, later, Tattoo. LuBan excludes both (§2.22).
  - **A media setting** for transparency or white paper (§2.22 names both).
  - **Batch** export from the CLI, together with the lithophane (PLAN §4).
  - A colour lithophane printed in several filaments, with no paper filter, is a separate blog-only mode: see LITH-CMYK (part 7).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - Chroma-only filter (ours): in linear RGB, F = RGB / max(R, G, B). This keeps hue and saturation and removes intensity. Near-black pixels become neutral white. Then apply the gain and convert to sRGB. LuBan's formula is UNCONFIRMED, but Fig. 62's washed-out result is consistent with removing intensity.
  - Unrolling depends on the shape:
    - the plane, for Flat, Stencil and the Spiral strip;
    - a rectangle, for Cylinder;
    - an annular sector, for Cone (Fig. 61);
    - gores, for Vase and Sphere (Fig. 61);
    - a projection onto the template plane, for Balloon halves;
    - xatlas or boundary-first-flattening (MIT; research 03 §7), for general surfaces.
  - PDF writer: crate UNCONFIRMED, with an SVG in mm units as the fallback (LITH-EXPORT).
- **Milestone:** M2 (part 9, after LITH-EXPORT), as an export add-on to the first shapes.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - LuBan's intensity-removal formula, and the JPG's DPI.
  - How the filter is registered against the lithophane, and whether it is mirrored for the back face.
  - Whether LuBan makes the Spiral filter as one long strip.
  - The content of video xgMMR_TL08c "LuBan Lithophane v9 Color lithophane" (11:15, ~2020; title only).

#### LITH-PRINT-TIPS — Lithophane print-and-light checklist (LuBan: Tips for 3D printing lithophane)

- **LuBan path:** Manual §2.23 (PDF p.43–45). There is no UI: the manual gives general guidance "not restricted to a type of printer or slicing software" (§2.23).
- **What it makes:** No geometry. A reusable print-and-light checklist that the hand-over step fills in with each job's numbers (CLAUDE.md: hand over the output path and a short checklist). LITH-EXPORT writes it as `PRINT-CHECKLIST.txt` (`write_checklist`).
- **Fabrication:** FDM printing, for every lithophane shape. The Squama plate (M1) reuses the orientation, speed, support and layer-height items, because it is printed standing "just as with a lithophane" (research 01 §2).
- **Inputs:** The job's parameters (shape, size, `thickness_min`/`thickness_max`, `print_orientation`) and the `machine_profile` (nozzle diameter, bed size).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vertical vs. horizontal printing orientation | `checklist_orientation` (follows `print_orientation`, LITH-EXPORT) | Print flat lithophanes standing up. Filament is laid continuously in X/Y but in layers in Z, so the layer height limits resolution in Z; a vertical print shows richer thickness variation | vertical ("The vertical orientation is preferred") | vertical, horizontal (flat on the bed) | §2.23 (PDF p.44) |
| Low vs. high printing speed | `checklist_speed` | 80–100 mm/s may make the printer vibrate and cause line strips; 30–50 mm/s reduces them | 30–50 mm/s (the manual's low-speed example) | mm/s | §2.23 (PDF p.44–45) |
| Support | `checklist_support` | Support "can be disabled", because removing it may damage the rough surface. Where support is unavoidable (e.g. a sphere), orient the part so support touches only the smooth surface. A small sphere may print without support, with the printer closing the upper gap "with any luck". Deeper relief makes support more likely to be needed (§2.4) | off (recommended, §2.23) | off; smooth side only | §2.23 (PDF p.45); §2.17 (PDF p.31); §2.4 |
| Printer belt | `checklist_belt` | Tighten the drive belt; a loose belt causes vibration | — | check item | §2.23 |
| Extruder | `checklist_extruder` | Clean the extruder regularly by running filament through it at a relatively high feed rate. Dust can clog it, giving uneven extrusion and regions that lack material | — | check item | §2.23 |
| Layer height | `checklist_layer_height` | Usually half the nozzle diameter, e.g. 0.1 mm with a 0.2 mm nozzle. A small nozzle gives a high-resolution lithophane but a longer print | nozzle / 2 | mm | §2.23 |
| — | `machine_profile` (LITH-COMMON) | Nozzle diameter and bed size, used to fill in the numbers | (suggest: the owner's printer profile) | profile list | PLAN §4 machine profiles |

- **Outputs:** Checklist text, shown at export and saved as `PRINT-CHECKLIST.txt` next to the model (LITH-EXPORT). The template below keeps each line's source; lines marked "ours" do not come from LuBan.
  1. **Printer:** belts tight; extruder flushed by feeding filament through at a high rate (§2.23).
  2. **Slicer:** layer height {nozzle/2} mm (§2.23); speed 30–50 mm/s, not 80–100 (§2.23); walls/infill set so the part prints fully solid (ours; UNCONFIRMED in the sources).
  3. **Orientation:** as exported, with the image face vertical (§2.23), or a spiral roll's axis vertical (ours, from Fig. 42). Do not lay a flat lithophane on the bed.
  4. **Supports:** off. If the model needs them, only on the smooth side (§2.23, §2.17). Hollow shells (Balloon, Tattoo) must print support-free, because supports inside cannot be removed (ours).
  5. **Large or tall flat parts:** enable print stabilisers (§2.10, for a large Flat or Arc; blog: flat-lithophane-support, "A tall flat lithophane is particularly sensitive to nozzle movement"; LITH-EDGE-SUPPORT).
  6. **Spiral, after printing:** soften in hot water and unroll (§2.18); hold it flat while it cools (ours).
  7. **Colour:** print the filter on transparency at 100 % scale, cut along the line, and fix it to the side that faces the lamp (§2.22).
  8. **Lighting check:** put the lamp behind the part, with the rough side toward the viewer for exterior prints (§2.2). A thick lithophane needs a strong lamp (§2.4). For Balloon and Tattoo, the lamp goes inside, through the socket (§2.20, §2.21).
  9. **Log** the printer, filament, thicknesses, layer height and lamp in `docs/test-log.md` (PLAN §5).
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - The six tips in the table, from §2.23.
  - Related tips from other sections that the checklist reuses:
    - print stabilisers for large Flat/Arc lithophanes (§2.10; blog: flat-lithophane-support, "A tall flat lithophane is particularly sensitive to nozzle movement");
    - a slanted Flat is turned upright on save (§2.13.2);
    - the thickness trade-off (§2.4);
    - exterior prints look sharper (§2.2);
    - detail finer than the machine can resolve is wasted (§2.5);
    - sphere orientation: opening down for exterior, opening up for interior, so support touches only the smooth side (§2.17);
    - filament colour changes the preview: "Changing the filament color can produce vivid rendering effects" (Fig. 54 caption).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - **The checklist carries real numbers:** layer height from the nozzle, the part's height and its thickness range. It is generated with every export (CLAUDE.md hand-over rule; PLAN §4 machine profiles). LuBan has one generic list (§2.23).
  - **Every shape exported in its print orientation.** The manual describes print orientation only for the slanted Flat, which is rotated upright on save (§2.13.2), and the sphere, which flips with exterior/interior (§2.17). AD3D's `print_orientation` defaults to upright for every shape (LITH-EXPORT).
  - **Overhang and thin-spot warnings** in the print orientation, so the "support on the smooth side" rule (§2.23, §2.17) is checked rather than remembered, and thin spots are checked against the nozzle (research 04 §B.1).
  - **A calibration wedge** for the owner's filament and lamp, shared with LITH-BACKLIGHT-PREVIEW's `tone_curve` (PLAN §4 calibration tile; §2.4 trade-off).
  - **Logged results** in `docs/test-log.md` (PLAN §5), so the settings improve from print to print.
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** No geometry. The template is filled from the job's parameters and the machine profile. Overhang check: flag faces whose downward slope in the print orientation exceeds a threshold (suggest: 45°, ours; LITH-COMMON's `max_overhang`). Thin-spot check: thickness below 2 × layer height, or an outline narrower than 2 nozzle widths (ours).
- **Milestone:** M1 (part 9, after APP-BATCH; the Squama hand-over reuses items 1–4 and 9) and M2.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Filament type and colour. The manual names only Eryone silk silver (Fig. 14 caption, PDF p.18) and shows white prints.
  - Walls/infill, temperatures, brim, and lamp type and brightness.
  - Recommended thickness ranges per material. The only material-specific data point is Fig. 14's interior trophy in Eryone silk silver, with min and max thickness 0.6 and 2.4 mm (Fig. 14 caption, PDF p.18).

### Part 2 notes

#### Related blog-only shapes (outside §2.13–2.17.3)

Frustum ("Generate a frustum lithophane.", blog: lithophane-14th-release, 2022-12-23) and Perspective frustum ("Generate a perspective frustum lithophane.", blog: lithophane-19th-release, 2024-11-13) are not in the manual. They are specified once, as LITH-FRUSTUM (part 7), so this section does not repeat that ID. Videos, titles only: 5KDVcwZzvt0 "LuBan Lithophane v14 Frustum" (1:54) and 3Oncrnefbtk "LuBan Lithophane v19 Perspective Frustrum" (8:12; spelling as in the title). Notes for that entry from this family (ours):
- A faceted frustum is LITH-POLY with separate top and bottom sizes, i.e. tilted planar faces.
- A round frustum is LITH-REVOLVE's cone, whose `developable` mapping already places a photo without distortion.
- A perspective mode could pre-warp each face's photo with a homography, so it reads as a rectangle from a chosen eye point.

## 3. Photo magic

### Photo magic: intro, Balloon, Box (3 intro, 3.1–3.2)

Photo magic is LuBan's family of generators that turn one image, normally reduced to black and white first, into a model for 3D printing, laser cutting or CNC machining (§3 intro, PDF p.46). This part covers the shared photo-to-shape front end (PHOTO-COMMON), Balloon (a solid inflated silhouette) and Box (a base and lid outlined by the image), with Box split into its body, lid styles, inner pattern, nested sets and two recipes, box light and box lithophane. The manual has no settings-panel screenshot for Balloon or Box (the only Photo magic panel screenshot in PDF p.46–58, Fig. 64 on PDF p.46, shows the Cutter), so nearly every default and range below is UNCONFIRMED; the options, behaviour and the height formulas of Table 1 are stated. Steps that LuBan leaves to manual work in its 2D and 3D windows (outline images, screenshot templates, resizing by hand) become one-step options in AD3D.

Conventions for this part:
- "PDF p." is the page in `Hello LuBan.pdf`; in this range it is the printed page + 1.
- A row whose LuBan label reads "— (AD3D-only)" is our addition, not a LuBan setting, and its default is our suggestion.
- No Box panel screenshot exists, so Box labels are the manual's wording; their on-screen spelling is UNCONFIRMED.
- Lengths are in mm, angles in degrees in the UI, keys in snake_case. In formulas, T is the box thickness, E the exterior outline and C the cavity outline.

---

#### PHOTO-COMMON — Photo-to-shape front end (LuBan: Photo magic)

- **LuBan path:** File → Create → Photo magic. Pick a generator from the "Method" drop-down, then load the image with the "Browse" button next to "Select photo" (§3 intro, Fig. 64, PDF p.46).
- **What it makes:** No model of its own. It is the front end every Photo magic method shares: load an image, reduce it to a black-and-white mask, split the shape into an outer boundary and inner features, run the chosen generator with a live 3D display, and save the model files (§3 intro, PDF p.46; §3.2, PDF p.47; §3.2.9, PDF p.57).
- **Fabrication:** The family targets 3D printing, laser cutting or CNC machining (§3 intro, PDF p.46). Box is described only for 3D printing (§3.2, PDF p.47–58); §3.1 names no process for Balloon.
- **Inputs:**
  - One image. "To optimize a photo for photo magic functions it is first manually converted to black and white" before a balloon, box, cutter, extrusion or morphing is made (§3 intro, PDF p.46). Fig. 63 (PDF p.46) compares an algorithmic conversion with a hand-picked threshold on the blue channel; the blue-channel version gives the cleaner sunflower silhouette (as the figure shows).
  - "In general, any black and white image is a template" (§3.2.8, PDF p.54).
  - An image that was not converted by hand is converted automatically. §3.9 says that for the methods in the earlier sections, converting by hand "may help you obtain better results than leaving LuBan to do the auto conversion" (§3.9 intro, PDF p.76). The algorithm and any controls of that auto conversion are UNCONFIRMED.
  - Image formats: UNCONFIRMED. The manual's prep workflows save PNG (§3.2.8 step 6, PDF p.55; §3.2.9, PDF p.57) or BMP/JPG/PNG (§2.20.4 step 8, PDF p.39). The Squama video's image dialog filter begins "*.bmp;*.j…" (research 01, workflow step 4).
  - The stencil and box lithophanes accept vector templates (DXF or SHP) (blog: vector-image-template), and LuBan's 2D window converts a bitmap to a vector with Tool → Convert → Bitmap (binary image) → Vector (blog: bitmap-to-vector-conversion). Whether Photo magic methods accept vector templates is UNCONFIRMED.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Method | `method` | Which Photo magic generator runs | UNCONFIRMED (Fig. 64 shows "Cutter" selected) | drop-down; this part covers Balloon and Box | §3 intro, Fig. 64 (PDF p.46) |
| Select photo → Browse | `image` | Input image | none | file dialog; formats UNCONFIRMED | §3 intro, Fig. 64 (PDF p.46) |
| Tool → Threshold → Manual (2D window) | `mask_threshold` | Intensity cut-off between object and background | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: Otsu auto-threshold, then user-adjustable) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0–255 for 8-bit images) | Fig. 63 caption (PDF p.46); §3.2.9 (PDF p.57) |
| — (Fig. 63: "converted from the blue component") | `mask_channel` | Image channel fed to the threshold | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: luminance) | luminance, red, green, blue | Fig. 63 caption (PDF p.46) |
| Tool → Data → Invert (2D window) | `mask_invert` | Swap object and background | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: off) | on, off | §3.2.9 (PDF p.57) |
| — (AD3D-only) | `mask_foreground` | Which colour is the object | (suggest: `auto_border`: the colour touching the image border is background) | `auto_border`, `white`, `black` | AD3D proposal; Fig. 67 (PDF p.48) shows dark-on-white and white-on-dark templates both in use |
| — (AD3D-only) | `mask_despeckle_px`, `mask_fill_holes_px` | Drop islands and fill holes smaller than N px before tracing | (suggest: 4 px each) | ≥ 0 | AD3D proposal |
| — (AD3D-only) | `contour_smooth_mm`, `contour_simplify_mm` | Sub-pixel smoothing and simplification of traced outlines | (suggest: 0.05 mm and 0.02 mm) | ≥ 0 | AD3D proposal; answers the "bumpy artifacts" of bitmap templates (blog: vector-image-template) |
| Save model (button at the bottom of the control panel) | export action | Writes the model files into a chosen export folder | — | — | §3.2.9 (PDF p.57); §2.12 (PDF p.22–23) |

- **Outputs:**
  - "Save model" asks for an export folder and writes "several files" (§3.2.9, PDF p.57).
  - For lithophanes the folder is named `<photo> LP <shape> <hh-mm-ss>` and holds `<photo> LP Model.stl`, `LuBan Model.fgd` / `.fgs`, `<photo> Setting.txt` and `MU Setting.txt` (§2.12, PDF p.22–23). Whether Photo magic uses the same naming and side files is UNCONFIRMED.
  - AD3D: one 3MF with units and named parts, optional per-part binary STL, and the `.ad3d` project file (see LITH-EXPORT for the shared export rules).
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Settings sit in a left control panel; the right side shows a live 3D display (§3 intro, PDF p.46).
  - Drop-down lists, radio buttons, check boxes and spin buttons update the display at once. A text box updates only after Enter (or Return), which stands in for an Apply button (§1.8, PDF p.15–16; luban-docs Get started p.6). §3.2.2 repeats this for box size (PDF p.48).
  - LuBan stores "parameters in many functions" in MU Setting.txt and loads them at start; without that file it applies its default settings (§1.6, PDF p.14). A value seen in a screenshot may therefore be a last-used value, not a factory default.
  - Multi-part results are inspected with Object → Select and "the slider on the toolbar", which highlights one part at a time (§3.2.5, PDF p.51; a greyed toolbar slider is visible in Fig. 64). In a 2018 build, Object → Select instead opened a small floating dialog titled "选择J" with the part name ("Part_01"), a slider and a Delete button (luban-docs Get started p.24). In the Projection video, J is the shortcut for Object → Select and E explodes the parts (video VA67Jm3ijHg @00:01). Object → Explode and Object → Restore show and undo an exploded view (blog: exploded-view).
  - Manual image prep happens outside the method, in LuBan's 2D window (File → Invoke 2D window): Threshold → Manual or Between, Data → Invert, Geometry → Distance transform, File → Export → PNG (§3.2.8–3.2.9, PDF p.54–57).
  - Size checks also happen outside the method: Mesh → Statistics shows the bounding cube (Fig. 86, PDF p.58), and Object → Transform resizes with "Scale or Size" and "Fixed / Flexible" options (Fig. 87, PDF p.58).
  - Fig. 64 (PDF p.46) is the Cutter's panel. For the Cutter section (PHOTO-CUTTER) it shows: Flip photo Yes/No (No), Photo/Text (Photo), Font "Arial", Text (empty), Width in X 40, Depth in Z 10, Inner pattern "Integrate", Inner depth 7, with more fields below the scroll.
  - Photo magic converts an image to black and white itself when the user has not ("the auto conversion", §3.9 intro, PDF p.76; Fig. 63 centre shows an image "converted by an algorithm"). The Projection method likewise converts colour or grayscale input automatically (video VA67Jm3ijHg @00:00). The algorithm, and whether its threshold can be set, are UNCONFIRMED.
  - Cutter (§3.4.2), Extrusion (§3.5.2) and Morphing (§3.7.2) have a "Photo vs. Text" choice (TOC). The manual documents none for Balloon or Box, and with no Box screenshot whether they have one is UNCONFIRMED. The box-light recipe prepares its overlapping letters in Microsoft Word (§3.2.8, PDF p.54). That is the same route §3.4.2 gives for overlapping letters even in the Cutter, which does have a text mode (PDF p.62).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - The mask step lives in the method panel with a live overlay: channel picker, threshold slider, Otsu auto, invert, despeckle, hole fill and crop. No source documents any control over LuBan's auto conversion, and the manual recommends a manual round trip through its 2D window for better results (§3 intro; §3.9, PDF p.76; §3.2.8–3.2.9).
  - Text input with any installed font, plus SVG/DXF import, for every outline-based method including Box. The manual documents no text mode for Box (its box-light letters come from a Word screenshot, §3.2.8). LuBan itself added DXF/SHP templates to its stencil and box lithophanes to avoid the "bumpy artifacts" of bitmap templates (blog: vector-image-template).
  - Sub-pixel contour tracing with smoothing set in mm, so walls come out smooth even from bitmaps.
  - Live preview while dragging (low-res while the slider moves, full-res on release) instead of type-then-Enter (§1.8; PLAN §4).
  - A parts list with names, colours, visibility and an explode toggle (APP-OBJECTS) replaces the Object → Select slider (§3.2.5). Live dimension read-outs replace Mesh → Statistics (Fig. 86).
  - 3MF with units and named parts, streamed binary STL, `.ad3d` project files that embed the source image, and undo/redo (PLAN §4).
  - One fit tolerance per printer and material profile, reused by every method. The manual tells users to do this by hand (§3.2.7, PDF p.53; PLAN §4 machine profiles).
  - Every Photo magic generator runs from `ad3d-cli` with a params JSON, for batch jobs (PLAN §4).
  - Every generator is pure, cancellable and watertight by construction, backed by a randomised-parameter `validate()` test (CLAUDE.md).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - Binarize (threshold one channel), trace contours with their hole hierarchy, split them into outer boundary and inner pattern, then offset, extrude or inflate. Research 04 §B.10 and §C conclude this is classical image processing, not ML.
  - Tracing: marching squares on the grayscale image at the threshold (sub-pixel; our choice), then Douglas–Peucker simplification. Research 04 §C names OpenCV findContours plus Douglas–Peucker; vtracer (MIT; research 03 §5) is the alternative.
  - Offsets: Clipper2 or `i_overlay` (PLAN §1; research 03 §13). Images: `image` + `fast_image_resize` (PLAN §1).
  - Later: background removal with BiRefNet (MIT) instead of manual thresholding (research 04 §C).
- **Milestone:** M5 (part 9, first in its row). Photo loading and grayscale conversion already land in M1 for Squama; the mask, tracing and offset pipeline arrives with the first M5 method.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Accepted image formats. How the automatic black-and-white conversion works (it exists, §3.9) and whether it can be tuned.
  - Polarity rule. Fig. 67 (PDF p.48) treats a white-on-dark heart, a dark-on-white heart and a white-on-dark logo all as the object, and Fig. 63 shows a dark sunflower on white. Our guess: the colour touching the image border is background.
  - Export folder naming and side files (Setting.txt, .fgd/.fgs) for Photo magic.
  - The full Method list (other sections cover the remaining methods).

---

#### PHOTO-BALLOON — Inflated silhouette (LuBan: Balloon)

- **LuBan path:** File → Create → Photo magic, Method = Balloon (§3.1, PDF p.46–47). The manual calls it "the balloon method"; the exact drop-down text is UNCONFIRMED.
- **What it makes:** A smooth, pillow-like solid whose outline comes from a black-and-white image (Fig. 65, PDF p.47). It is the balloon lithophane (§2.20) without a photo mapped onto it: "a single-surface, solid model", where the balloon lithophane is "a double-surface, hollow model" (§3.1, PDF p.47).
- **Fabrication:** 3D print (implied: §3.1 names no process, and §3 intro lists 3D printing, laser cutting and CNC for the family). The sources give no orientation, support or material advice for this method. Fig. 65 (PDF p.47) shows both faces inflated, with a thin band along the silhouette (our reading). Our assessment: a shape like that needs supports to print in one piece.
- **Inputs:** One silhouette image. In the balloon lithophane, white is the balloon region and black is background, so a black shape on white inflates the region around it (§2.20, PDF p.35; Fig. 45, PDF p.36). Fig. 65 uses a white silhouette on a dark background. Whether Photo magic Balloon keeps that strict white-is-balloon rule, or picks the object automatically as Box appears to (Fig. 67, PDF p.48), is UNCONFIRMED.
- **Parameters:** The manual lists no settings for this method. It says only "The settings of the two methods are similar" (§3.1, PDF p.47). The LuBan rows below are the balloon-lithophane settings that don't involve a photo; whether the Balloon panel has them is UNCONFIRMED.

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Select photo → Browse | `image` | Silhouette image. In the balloon lithophane white = balloon region; that rule is UNCONFIRMED for this method | none | B/W image | §3 intro (PDF p.46); §2.20, Fig. 45 (PDF p.35–36) |
| Expansion (balloon lithophane) | `inflation` (same key and AD3D definition as LITH-BALLOON) | How far the shape is blown up; "The larger the value, the more blown up is the balloon" | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED. Fig. 47 shows 0.2, 1 and 2. For a nearly flat double-sided result the manual suggests "a small non-zero value, such as 0.01", so 0 is apparently not accepted (our reading). Unit UNCONFIRMED (appears unitless) | §2.20.1 (PDF p.36); Fig. 47 (PDF p.37) |
| Extra space (balloon lithophane) | `extra_gap` (same key as LITH-BALLOON) | Extra wall between the front and back surfaces, added to the default space; straight in Fig. 48 (our reading) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0) | ≥ 0 (0 is shown); Fig. 48 shows 0, 10 and 20; upper limit UNCONFIRMED; unit UNCONFIRMED (suggest: mm) | §2.20.2 (PDF p.36–37); Fig. 48 (PDF p.37) |
| (default space; not a control) | `rim_gap` (automatic; as LITH-BALLOON) | Built-in space between the front and back surfaces, "often very small" | UNCONFIRMED | automatic | §2.20.2 (PDF p.36) |
| model size (label UNCONFIRMED) | `size_x_mm`, `size_y_mm` | Footprint; Y presumably follows the shape's aspect ratio, as in Box | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED (by analogy with §3.2.2, PDF p.48) |
| Center X and Y, Photo scale (balloon lithophane) | — (not used) | Position and size a photo on the balloon; this method maps no photo | — | — | §2.20.3 (PDF p.37); §3.1 (PDF p.47) |
| — (AD3D-only) | `inflation_height_mm` | Peak height of each face above the seam; drives `inflation` (LITH-BALLOON shows the same quantity read-only as `dome_height`) | (suggest: 0.25 × the radius of the largest inscribed circle) | > 0 | AD3D proposal |
| — (AD3D-only) | `inflation_profile` (same key as LITH-BALLOON) | Cross-section of the inflation | (suggest: `round`) | `round`; `ridge` (creases along the medial axis, as Fig. 47 shows at expansion 2; our reading); `plateau` (flat top; ours) | AD3D proposal; Fig. 47 (PDF p.37) |
| — (AD3D-only) | `back_style` | Treatment of the back | (suggest: `mirrored`, as in Fig. 65) | `mirrored`; `flat` (prints without supports); `split_halves` (two flat-backed halves with locating pins) | AD3D proposal |
| — (AD3D-only) | `min_edge_mm` | Minimum thickness at the rim, so the seam is never a knife edge | (suggest: 0.8 mm) | ≥ 0 | AD3D proposal |
| — (AD3D-only) | `mesh_step_mm` | Sample spacing of the inflated surface | (suggest: 0.5 mm preview, 0.2 mm final) | > 0 | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** One closed solid. File name and format UNCONFIRMED (probably STL, as with Save model in §2.12).
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - The result is solid, with a single closed surface (§3.1, PDF p.47).
  - From the balloon lithophane: a larger expansion inflates more, and about 0.01 gives a nearly flat double-sided shape (§2.20.1, PDF p.36). A small default space always separates front and back, and extra space widens it (§2.20.2, PDF p.36–37).
  - Fig. 65 (PDF p.47) shows the result from several angles, inflated on both faces.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Inflation set in millimetres (`inflation_height_mm`), with the resulting maximum thickness shown live. LuBan's expansion appears unitless (Fig. 47).
  - `back_style` = flat or split_halves for support-free printing. LuBan shows only the two-sided pillow and gives no print advice (Fig. 65).
  - A guaranteed rim thickness (`min_edge_mm`) instead of a hidden "very small" default band (§2.20.2).
  - Live preview while dragging, from a downsampled mask, then full resolution on release (PLAN §4; CLAUDE.md speed rule). The distance transform and meshing use all cores and can be cancelled.
  - Watertight by construction, checked by `validate()` with randomised parameters (CLAUDE.md).
  - One inflation kernel and one set of keys (`inflation`, `extra_gap`, `rim_gap`, `inflation_profile`) shared with the balloon lithophane (LITH-BALLOON), so the two stay consistent. LuBan only says the settings "are similar" (§3.1).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - Exact Euclidean distance transform d of the mask. Height h = H·√(1 − (1 − d/R)²) with R = max d (round profile), or Poisson inflation for a smoother ridge. Research 04 §B.1 calls LuBan's method "likely distance-transform or Poisson inflation, as in Teddy-style inflation" (UNCONFIRMED).
  - Mesh: constrained Delaunay triangulation of the traced outline plus interior samples. Front z = s/2 + h, back z = −(s/2 + h) (or a flat back), and a vertical band of height s = `rim_gap` + `extra_gap` along the outline, welded into one closed surface.
  - Distance-transform rows run in parallel with rayon.
- **Milestone:** M5 (part 9, after PHOTO-MORPH-TEXT), stretch. It is not in PLAN §3's M5 list. Build the inflation kernel once and share it with the balloon lithophane (LITH-BALLOON, M2). Research 04 §B.10 rates Photo Magic methods difficulty 2–3.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Panel labels, defaults and ranges (no screenshot).
  - Units of expansion; whether front and back always inflate equally; whether there is a size or resolution setting.
  - How holes in the silhouette and several separate islands are handled.
  - Polarity: the strict white = balloon rule of the balloon lithophane (Fig. 45), or automatic object detection.
  - Related videos (titles only): emF-SL3TSbk "LuBan Lithophane Balloon", Br-ojEQmZUM "How to prepare template and picture for Balloon lithophane", tjD-cq9AjkQ "Use MeshMixer to create a light socket for LuBan balloon lithophane". No blog post or video covers the Photo magic Balloon itself; the balloon lithophane arrived in blog: lithophane-8th-release.

#### PHOTO-BOX — Silhouette box: body, sizing, chamfer and fit (LuBan: Box)

- **LuBan path:** File → Create → Photo magic, Method = Box (§3.2, PDF p.47). Release history: blog: __box ("Generate a box from a picture"), box-2nd-release (flat and inlay lids, magnet sinks), box-3rd-release (outer size option, nested box), box-intrude-inner-pattern ("intrude" pattern option).
- **What it makes:** A two-part box, base and lid, whose outline is the outer boundary of the image (§3.2, Fig. 66, PDF p.47). Features inside the boundary form an "inner pattern" that can decorate or hollow the lid, or hollow the whole box (§3.2.4; PHOTO-BOX-PATTERN). This entry covers the body, sizing, chamfer and tolerance. Lids (PHOTO-BOX-LID), pattern, nesting (PHOTO-BOX-NESTED) and the two recipes (PHOTO-BOX-LIGHT, PHOTO-BOX-LITHO) have their own entries.
- **Fabrication:**
  - 3D print.
  - Printed parts come out a little larger than the model, so a base and lid with zero tolerance are unlikely to fit; start trials at −0.2 mm (§3.2.4, PDF p.50; §3.2.7, PDF p.53).
  - Without a chamfer, the upper layers compress the base and leave extra material at the edge between the flat base and the wall, which "can make the edge look ugly and sometimes may even cut one's finger". A chamfer of a few layer heights often noticeably improves that edge and needs no support (§3.2.6, PDF p.52).
  - Flat and inlay lids print with little support (§3.2.8, PDF p.55–56).
- **Inputs:**
  - One B/W template image: "any black and white image is a template" (§3.2.8, PDF p.54).
  - The outer boundary becomes the box outline. "Any feature inside the outer boundary" is the inner pattern (§3.2, Fig. 67, PDF p.47–48).
  - If the image has disjoint features and no enclosing outline, LuBan generates a boundary itself and treats all features as the inner pattern (§3.2, Fig. 67 second column, PDF p.47–48).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Method: "the box method" | `method` = `photo_box` | Selects the box generator | — | — | §3.2 (PDF p.47) |
| Select photo → Browse | `image` | Template: outer boundary plus inner pattern | none | B/W image | §3 intro (PDF p.46); §3.2.8 (PDF p.54) |
| Inner size / Outer size (Table 1 headers; §3.2.1: "inner and outer size options") | `size_ref` | Whether base size X/Y/Z and lid size Z are inside or outside dimensions | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: `inner`; the outer option arrived later, in blog: box-3rd-release, so inner was the original behaviour) | `inner`, `outer`; outer cannot use the inlay lid | §3.2.1 (PDF p.47); Table 1 note (PDF p.48); blog: box-3rd-release |
| base size X | `base_x_mm` | Footprint X (inside or outside per `size_ref`) | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: up to the printer bed) | §3.2.2 (PDF p.48) |
| base size Y | `base_y_mm` | Footprint Y, locked to X by the shape's aspect ratio | derived from X | UNCONFIRMED | §3.2.2 (PDF p.48) |
| base size Z (Zb) | `base_z_mm` | Base height; its meaning depends on `size_ref` and lid type (Table 1) | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED | §3.2.2, Table 1 (PDF p.48) |
| lid size Z (Zl) | `lid_z_mm` | Lid height; appears in Table 1 for basic and twist only | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED | §3.2.2, Table 1 (PDF p.48) |
| box thickness / thickness (T) | `wall_mm` | Wall thickness; by our reading of Table 1 also the floor, the flat or inlay lid and the top plate of a basic or twist lid | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED; 1–3 mm lets light through (§3.2.8) | §3.2.2, Table 1 (PDF p.48); §3.2.8 (PDF p.54) |
| lid type, lid indent, twist and sink settings | see PHOTO-BOX-LID | | | | §3.2.3 |
| inner pattern, pattern depth | see PHOTO-BOX-PATTERN | | | | §3.2.4 |
| nested box, nested box clearance | see PHOTO-BOX-NESTED | | | | §3.2.5 |
| edge chamfer | `edge_chamfer_mm` | Size of the 45° bevel between a flat face and a vertical wall | UNCONFIRMED (Fig. 76 compares 0 and 1 mm; suggest: 3 × the printer profile's layer height) | ≥ 0; "a few layer heights" advised | §3.2.6, Fig. 76 (PDF p.52) |
| tolerance | `fit_tolerance_mm` | Signed size change of base and lid so they fit; more negative = bigger gap | UNCONFIRMED (manual: start trials at −0.2 mm; suggest: printer-profile value) | ≤ 0 in Box ("cannot be set to a positive value"); lower limit UNCONFIRMED. Fig. 77 shows 0, −0.2 and −0.5 mm | §3.2.7, Fig. 77 (PDF p.53) |
| save model button | export action | Writes base, lid (and pattern) files, including "a lid.stl file" | — | — | §3.2.9 (PDF p.57) |
| — (AD3D-only) | `height_target` | Type the total exterior or interior height directly; AD3D solves Zb and keeps Zl, Dl and T | (suggest: `off`) | `off`, `exterior_mm`, `interior_mm` | AD3D proposal; LuBan has "no setting to directly specify the overall height" (§3.2.2) |
| — (AD3D-only) | `auto_boundary` | Outline used when the features are disjoint | (suggest: `convex_hull`) | `convex_hull`; `offset_union` (union of features grown by `boundary_margin_mm`); `manual` | AD3D proposal; Fig. 67 (PDF p.48); Cutter's convex mutual outline (§3.4.4, PDF p.63) |
| — (AD3D-only) | `boundary_margin_mm` | Gap between pattern features and an auto-generated boundary | (suggest: 2 mm) | ≥ 0 | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:**
  - Separate model files for base and lid. The indent pattern mode adds a third file, the inner pattern (§3.2.4, PDF p.50; §3.2.8, PDF p.55).
  - Save model writes "several files", among them "a lid.stl file" (§3.2.9, PDF p.57). Names of the other files are UNCONFIRMED.
  - The saved lid sits at its assembled height, not on the bed: in Fig. 86 the lid.stl spans Z 25–30 (PDF p.58; our reading).
  - AD3D: one 3MF with parts `base`, `lid` and `motif`, laid out ready to print with the lid flipped, plus optional per-part STL.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Aspect lock: base size X and Y keep the aspect ratio of the 2D feature, not of the whole image. Changing X (and pressing Enter) changes Y, and vice versa. Base size Z and lid size Z are independent (§3.2.2, PDF p.48).
  - Size reference: inner means the sizes are inside dimensions, for a box that must hold a given object; outer means outside dimensions, for a box that must fit a shelf (§3.2.1, PDF p.47). With inner, the cavity follows the template and the exterior grows by the thickness; with outer, the exterior matches the template and the interior shrinks by the thickness (§3.2.8, Fig. 79, PDF p.54).
  - No overall-height setting. Exterior and interior height follow from the size reference, Zb, T, lid type, Zl and Dl (§3.2.2, PDF p.48):

| Lid type | Exterior height, inner size | Exterior height, outer size | Interior height, inner size | Interior height, outer size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Basic or Twist | Zb + Zl − Dl + 2T | Zb + Zl − Dl | Zb + Zl − Dl | Zb + Zl − Dl − 2T |
| Flat | Zb + 2T | Zb + T | Zb | Zb − T |
| Inlay | Zb | — | Zb − 2T | — |

  Table 1 (PDF p.48). Zb = base size Z, Zl = lid size Z, Dl = lid indent, T = box thickness. "When the outer size option is selected, the lid type cannot be inlay."

  - Our reading of Table 1 (UNCONFIRMED): the floor is T thick; flat and inlay lids, and the top plate of a basic or twist lid, are T thick; Zl and Dl only matter for basic and twist.
  - Table 1 quirk: for the inlay lid with inner size, exterior = Zb and interior = Zb − 2T. Zb therefore acts as an outside height even under the inner option, unlike every other inner-size cell. Whether that is intended or a manual error is UNCONFIRMED (Table 1, PDF p.48; our reading).
  - Edge chamfer: "a 45-degree slanted surface between a flat base and a vertical wall" (§3.2.6, PDF p.52). Fig. 76 shows it on the lid's top outer edge, at 0 and 1 mm.
  - Tolerance (§3.2.7, PDF p.53):
    - It slightly adjusts the base and lid sizes so they fit; the gap grows as it gets more negative (Fig. 77: 0, −0.2 and −0.5 mm). In Box it cannot be positive.
    - Fig. 77 shows the gap on a lid that sits inside the base rim, which looks like an inlay lid (our reading). So the tolerance does act on inlay lids.
    - The sign convention matches LuBan's older slides: "A negative tolerance compensates for the edge thickening caused by 3-D printing" (luban-docs Get started p.12).
    - Zero is unlikely to work. There is no single best value, because printer, slicer, print profile, filament and preferred tightness all matter; find it by trial starting at −0.2 mm.
    - Once found, the value can "probably" be reused in every LuBan function that requires a tolerance, as long as those factors don't change much.
  - The tolerance is not applied to the inner-pattern part (§3.2.4, PDF p.50).
  - For comparison, in connectors a −0.2 mm tolerance gives a 0.4 mm gap between the walls (§4.6.6, PDF p.94–95).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Live preview while dragging size, thickness, chamfer and tolerance (PLAN §4); §3.2.2 explicitly needs Enter. Keep the preview within 50 ms at typical sizes by using a coarser outline while dragging (CLAUDE.md speed rule).
  - A dimensions panel shows exterior and interior height, footprint and wall live (Table 1 maths). `height_target` lets the user type the total height directly, which LuBan cannot do (§3.2.2).
  - Every lid style works with both size references, with formulas defined for all eight cases. LuBan forbids outer + inlay (Table 1), yet its own box-lithophane recipe uses it (§3.2.9).
  - The fit tolerance comes from the printer and material profile, with a printable fit coupon: short rim-and-lid rings from −0.1 to −0.5 mm in 0.1 mm steps. This replaces the trial and error in §3.2.7 (PLAN §4 machine profiles).
  - The clearance is shown as a real gap per side in mm. LuBan doesn't say how Box splits it (§3.2.7), and for connectors −0.2 mm means a 0.4 mm gap (§4.6.6).
  - Print-ready export: one 3MF with units and named parts (base, lid, motif), the lid flipped as §3.2.4 advises for indent lids, laid out on the profile's bed with a fit check (PLAN §4). LuBan saves the lid at its assembled height (Fig. 86: Z 25–30), so the user must re-orient it in the slicer.
  - Smooth walls from sub-pixel tracing or SVG/DXF import. The LuBan blog notes that bitmap templates leave "bumpy artifacts" on the walls of its lithophane boxes, which is why it added DXF/SHP templates there (blog: vector-image-template).
  - The chamfer default is 3 × the profile's layer height, matching "a few layer heights" (§3.2.6).
  - Output is watertight and consistently wound by construction, with a property test over random sizes, thicknesses, lid styles and patterns (CLAUDE.md).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - Trace the template into an outer polygon P (with an auto boundary when needed) plus pattern polygons, then scale so the bounding box X equals `base_x_mm`.
  - Inner size: cavity C = P and exterior E = offset(P, +T). Outer size: E = P and C = offset(P, −T). This matches the box-light behaviour in §3.2.8. Use Clipper2 offsets with round joins (PLAN §1; research 03 §13).
  - Base = a floor slab of outline E, thickness T, plus the wall ring E minus C up to the base height. The lid follows PHOTO-BOX-LID; heights follow Table 1.
  - Build the stepped extrusions directly as one mesh (shared rings, caps triangulated by constrained Delaunay or ear clipping), and fall back to manifold unions where features overlap (PLAN §1). Run `validate()` afterwards.
  - Chamfer: loft from offset(E, −c) at the bed face to E at height c. Where the inset changes topology (thin features), approximate the slope with stacked steps no taller than one layer.
  - Research 04 §B.10 summarises Box as "base plus lid", and §D rates Box difficulty 1–2.
- **Milestone:** M5 (part 9, after PHOTO-CUTTER).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Every on-screen label, default and range. There is no Box screenshot; Fig. 64 shows the Cutter.
  - Contradiction: Table 1 says outer size cannot use an inlay lid, but §3.2.9 builds a box lithophane with an inlay lid and the outer size option.
  - How the tolerance is split between base and lid, whether it is per side or total, and whether it does anything on a flat lid, which has no overlap.
  - Which edges get the chamfer. Fig. 76 shows only the lid's top edge; the base's bottom edge is our guess and is not shown.
  - The rule for the auto-generated boundary. Fig. 67 looks like a convex hull, and the Cutter uses "a bounding convex polygon" for its mutual outline (§3.4.4, PDF p.63).
  - File names other than lid.stl; whether a contour-resolution setting exists.
  - Related videos (titles only): uL4tD0AGTqg "LuBan Box", hAUgk1H4-XY "LuBan Box v2", aUYYmJLh1_k "LuBan Box v3", zNQmO7yB0-A "LuBan Box v3 amendment".
  - Fig. 86 puts the example's inlay lid at X 4.694–199.3, Y 4.898–112.1, Z 25–30: 5 mm thick, on a box about 30 mm tall (our reading). The example's T and base size X are not given, so the lid's thickness and inset cannot be checked against Table 1 or the "half the thickness" rule.
  - Not to be confused with Mesh → Box (blog: mesh-box-update; FORM-ENCASE (part 5)) or the Painting box (blog: painting-box, double-sided-painting-box; video kNaPEE9p0w4, title only; PHOTO-PAINTING-BOX). Manual §3.8 "Painting" says only "This method is still under development" (PDF p.76).

#### PHOTO-BOX-LID — Box closures and magnet pockets (LuBan: Lid type — basic, twist, flat, inlay)

- **LuBan path:** File → Create → Photo magic, Method = Box, lid type (§3.2.3, PDF p.48–50). Flat and inlay were added in blog: box-2nd-release.
- **What it makes:** The joint between base and lid, in one of four styles (§3.2.3, PDF p.48–50):
  - Basic: base and lid each get an indent so they overlap by the lid indent Dl and hold by friction (Fig. 68).
  - Twist: "rotates the indent region by an angle of twist", which adds a locking mechanism on top of the friction (Fig. 69).
  - Flat: a flat lid with optional circular sinks in the base and lid edges for magnets (Fig. 70).
  - Inlay: the lid sinks into the base, enclosed by a wall half as thick as the base wall (Fig. 71).
- **Fabrication:** 3D print.
  - Twist with a small indent and a large angle may need support, and limited printer precision may stop the parts fitting. Use a large indent for a large angle (§3.2.3, Fig. 69, PDF p.49).
  - Flat and inlay lids print with little support (§3.2.8, PDF p.55–56).
  - Magnets go in the flat-lid sinks to hold the lid firmly (§3.2.3, Fig. 70, PDF p.49–50); the blog speaks of "button magnets" (blog: box-2nd-release).
- **Inputs:** The box outline and sizes from PHOTO-BOX.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| lid type | `lid_style` | Closure style | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: `basic`) | `basic`, `twist`, `flat`, `inlay`; inlay is unavailable with outer size | §3.2.3 (PDF p.48); Table 1 note (PDF p.48); blog: box-2nd-release |
| lid indent (Dl) | `lid_overlap_mm` | Height over which base and lid overlap (basic, twist); shortened at each nested level | UNCONFIRMED | > 0 (our reading: nested generation stops once it reaches zero or below, §3.2.5); upper limit UNCONFIRMED (suggest: ≤ min(Zb, Zl)) | §3.2.3, Fig. 68 (PDF p.48–49); §3.2.5 (PDF p.51) |
| angle of twist (Fig. 69 caption: "twist angle") | `twist_deg` | Rotation of the indent region (spread over its height: our reading of Fig. 69) | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED (unit presumably degrees); a large angle needs a large Dl | §3.2.3, Fig. 69 (PDF p.49) |
| number of sinks (§3.2.3 calls them "small circular sinks (sockets)") | `magnet_count` | Magnet sinks on the base and lid edges (flat lid) | UNCONFIRMED (Fig. 70 shows 5, one per star lobe, in both the base rim and the lid underside) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0–12) | §3.2.3, Fig. 70 (PDF p.49–50) |
| sinks' diameter | `magnet_d_mm` | Sink diameter | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: magnet Ø + 0.2 mm) | §3.2.3 (PDF p.49) |
| sinks' depth | `magnet_depth_mm` | Sink depth | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: magnet height + 0.2 mm, in both base and lid) | §3.2.3 (PDF p.49) |
| sink index | `magnet_index` (UI selection, not saved geometry) | Which sink the position setting moves; the selected sink is drawn red | UNCONFIRMED | 0- or 1-based UNCONFIRMED | §3.2.3, Fig. 70 (PDF p.49–50) |
| position (of the selected sink) | `magnet_pos` (one value per sink) | Location along the box perimeter, as a fraction | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: evenly spaced, i / n) | 0–1, "a fraction of the perimeter of the box" | §3.2.3 (PDF p.49) |
| — (the manual names no setting; the wall is "half the thickness") | `inlay_rim_fraction` (AD3D-only) | Share of T kept as the outer wall around an inlay lid | 0.5 (the manual's stated value) | (suggest: 0.3–0.7) | §3.2.3 (PDF p.49); AD3D proposal to expose it |
| — (AD3D-only) | `twist_max_overhang_deg` | Warn when the twisted lip overhangs more than this | (suggest: 45°) | 30–60° | AD3D proposal; LuBan warns only in prose (§3.2.3) |
| — (AD3D-only) | `magnet_preset` | Fills diameter and depth from a common magnet size (Ø × height, mm) | (suggest: `6x3`) | `5x2`, `6x2`, `6x3`, `8x2`, `8x3`, `10x3`, `custom` | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** A base and lid shaped for the chosen closure; part files as in PHOTO-BOX.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Basic: the overlap creates friction, tuned by the tolerance (§3.2.3, PDF p.48; §3.2.7).
  - Twist: the twisted overlap adds a lock on top of the friction. With a small Dl, avoid a large angle: the shape may need support and may not fit. Fig. 69 shows a large Dl with a small angle working, a small Dl with a large angle failing, and a large angle working with a large Dl (§3.2.3, Fig. 69, PDF p.49).
  - Flat: sinks sit on the edge of the base and of the lid. The panel sets their number, diameter and depth and the position of each one. "sink index" picks the sink to move, shown red, and its position runs from 0 to 1 as a fraction of the box perimeter (§3.2.3, PDF p.49). Fig. 70 shows five sinks, one per star lobe.
  - Inlay: the lid sinks into the base, and the wall around the lid is half the base wall thickness (§3.2.3, PDF p.49). Not available with outer size (Table 1 note).
  - Heights per lid type follow Table 1 (see PHOTO-BOX).
  - Nested boxes shorten the lid indent at each level, for basic and twist (§3.2.5, PDF p.51).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Drag magnet sinks along the rim in the viewport, with a "distribute evenly" action, instead of moving one sink at a time by index and a 0–1 number (§3.2.3).
  - Magnet presets, and a check that each sink keeps a minimum skin of material to the cavity and the outside (suggest: 0.8 mm). The manual describes no such check (§3.2.3).
  - Twist feasibility check: compute the lip overhang as atan(r·θ / Dl), with r the largest radius from the twist axis and θ in radians, then warn or suggest the minimum Dl. For example, r = 30 mm and θ = 30° need Dl ≥ 15.7 mm to stay within 45°. This turns the manual's prose warning (§3.2.3, Fig. 69) into numbers.
  - Inlay works with outer size, and the inlay rim width is adjustable. LuBan forbids the first (Table 1), and the manual describes no rim setting: the rim is half the thickness (§3.2.3).
  - The clearance appears as a real gap per side in mm next to the tolerance (§3.2.7).
  - A cut-away section view shows how base and lid mate, updating live while dragging (PLAN §4).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - Basic: complementary half-wall rings of height Dl on base and lid, split at offset(E, −T/2), with the tolerance opening the gap (Clipper2 offsets; manifold booleans; PLAN §1). Fig. 68 appears to show the base's top band recessed on the outside so the lid skirt slides over it (our reading).
  - Twist: the same rings extruded with a twist. manifold's extrude accepts a twist angle and a number of divisions (our knowledge of its API; confirm the C binding in the spike, PLAN §1); use enough divisions that each step turns ≤ 1°. The mating cavity is the twisted lip grown by the tolerance. Warn if the twisted lip would break through the outer wall.
  - Flat: sinks are cylinders placed at arc-length fraction s along the wall's mid-line, offset(E, −T/2), and subtracted from the base rim and the lid underside.
  - Inlay: the base gets a ledge, with the recess offset(E, −T/2) cut to the lid's depth, while the outer half-wall keeps full height. Lid = offset(E, −T/2 + `fit_tolerance_mm`), extruded to thickness T (Table 1 reading).
- **Milestone:** M5 (part 9, after PHOTO-BOX).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Defaults and ranges for every setting, and the on-screen label for twist ("twist angle" or "angle of twist").
  - Whether the basic/twist lip is on the inner or outer half of the wall.
  - Twist axis (outline centroid? bounding-box centre?) and direction. Whether the lid's outer wall stays straight around the twisted lip: Fig. 69 left shows a straight-sided lid, while Fig. 69 right shows a tall base twisted over most of its height inside a translucent lid (our reading).
  - Sink perimeter: start point, direction, and which line (inner, outer or mid-wall). Whether the depth applies equally to base and lid. Whether sinks exist on other lid types.
  - Flat-lid and inlay-lid thickness (Table 1 implies T). Whether a flat lid has a locating lip (Fig. 70 shows a plain plate).
