#### PHOTO-PUZZLE-COLOR — Colour-Layer Jigsaw (LuBan: Puzzle 2nd release, "Color layered puzzle")

- **LuBan path:** Puzzle method (§3.10), colour-layer variant. The only text source is blog: puzzle-2nd-release (Nov 2021): "Color layered puzzle. Each puzzle piece consists of several color layers, similar to the Painting method." How it is selected in the panel is UNCONFIRMED. The manual text does not mention it, although Fig. 142 (PDF p.80) appears to show such a puzzle (see Behaviour).
- **What it makes:** a jigsaw whose pieces are built from stacked colour layers, like PHOTO-PAINTING, instead of (or as well as) an intensity relief. Which of the two is UNCONFIRMED.
- **Fabrication:** UNCONFIRMED. It is presumably a multi-colour print (filament changes or a multi-material printer; our inference). Fig. 142's pieces look multi-colour printed (figure observation). Painting itself is "3D printed or laser cut" (blog: painting).
- **Inputs:** one colour photo (blog: puzzle-2nd-release, implied).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| UNCONFIRMED | `surface` | What forms the top of each piece: `relief` (PHOTO-PUZZLE) or `colour_layers` | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: `colour_layers` in this mode) | `relief`, `colour_layers` (ours) | blog: puzzle-2nd-release |
| Model size X / Y, X section / Y section, Edge chamfer, Tolerance (as §3.10) | `size_x_mm`, `size_y_mm`, `pieces_x`, `pieces_y`, `edge_chamfer_mm`, `tolerance_mm`, `seed` | Jigsaw layout, as PHOTO-PUZZLE. Tolerance: "For 3D printing, it is often set to a negative value, such as -0.2 mm" (§3.10.6, PDF p.82); X and Y section examples are 3 × 2 and 12 × 9 (Fig. 145, PDF p.82) | As PHOTO-PUZZLE | As PHOTO-PUZZLE | §3.10.1, §3.10.3, §3.10.5–3.10.7 |
| UNCONFIRMED | `n_colours`, `palette`, `layer_order`, `layer_thickness_mm`, `min_region_mm2` | Colour layers, as PHOTO-PAINTING | As PHOTO-PAINTING | As PHOTO-PAINTING | blog: puzzle-2nd-release ("similar to the Painting method") |
| — (AD3D) | `fabrication` | `print_multi_material` or `print_filament_swap` | ours: `print_filament_swap` | As listed | AD3D |

- **Outputs:** UNCONFIRMED. The base Puzzle exports pieces as STL, colour as OBJ, and the 2D pattern as DXF, SVG and SHP (§3.10.7, PDF p.82). Ours: a 3MF with one object per piece, where each piece holds one part per colour layer, so multi-material printers assign filaments automatically. Also a filament-change height list for single-nozzle printers, and SVG/DXF of the cut graph.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Only the blog sentence is known from text.
  - Fig. 142 (PDF p.80), figure observation: on the loose pieces the lighter colours (yellow, light blue) stand as raised layers on a dark-blue base, and the assembled picture is posterised into about five colours (dark blue, mid blue, light blue, yellow, black).
  - Our requirement: every piece is cut from the same colour-layer stack, so colours line up across the seams.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - **Registered layers.** Colour layers are computed once for the whole picture and then cut by the jigsaw graph, so the regions line up exactly across neighbouring pieces (ours).
  - **No specks at seams.** Slivers of a colour narrower than the minimum feature, created where a seam crosses a colour region, are merged away (ours).
  - **Printer-ready output.** A multi-material 3MF with named parts, and a filament-change list for single-nozzle printers (PLAN §4 3MF). Plus the PHOTO-PUZZLE improvements: seed, live preview, bed packing.
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - Run the PHOTO-PAINTING colour stack (palette quantisation, k-means in Lab) for the whole image.
  - Intersect each layer's polygons with each piece outline (Clipper2; research 03 §13).
  - Extrude each layer as a prism inside the piece's chamfered outline, sharing boundary vertices so the piece stays watertight per part.
- **Milestone:** M7 (part 9, after PHOTO-PAINTING-BOX). It needs PHOTO-PAINTING and PHOTO-PUZZLE (M6).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - The panel controls.
  - Whether a relief and colour layers can be combined.
  - Layer thicknesses and count.
  - Output formats.
  - Whether Fig. 142's user build was made with this mode.
  - No specific video title; the base method's video is l3kbfVe7dEQ "LuBan Puzzle" (title only).

---

#### PHOTO-PUZZLE-MESH — Model Relief Jigsaw (LuBan: Puzzle of a 3D model)

- **LuBan path:** five steps (§3.10.8, PDF p.83):
  1. Run LuBan.
  2. File → Open, to open a 3D model.
  3. Mesh → Depth map: set the direction and the resolution. The result is a 2D image of the model's surface height distribution.
  4. In the depth map's window, File → Save, as FLT: "a LuBan-defined file format" that stores floating-point values, so it is more accurate than BMP, JPG or PNG.
  5. In the 3D window, File → Create → Photo magic, Method = Puzzle, then select the depth map.

  Blog: depth-map-of-a-3d-mesh (Jun 13, 2019; updated Jun 16, 2019): "Get the depth map of a 3D mesh using "Mesh -> Depth map"."
- **What it makes:** a relief jigsaw of a 3D model. The model's depth, seen from a chosen direction, becomes the puzzle's surface (Fig. 147, PDF p.83).
- **Fabrication:**
  - As PHOTO-PUZZLE.
  - Fig. 147 (right), figure observation: a tall relief whose walls are nearly vertical where the depth jumps. Tall cliffs on small pieces may print poorly or snap (our note; research 04 §B.6: "depth discontinuities give vertical cliffs").
- **Inputs:**
  - LuBan: "a 3D model"; formats are not stated in §3.10.8. In the 2018 build shown in the Chinese deck, File → Open took OBJ, PLY or STL (luban-docs Get started p.2). The depth image travels as an FLT file.
  - Ours: STL, OBJ, PLY or 3MF, through mesh import. Depth capture with a z-buffer works on a raw triangle soup, so the mesh does not need repairing first (our note).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| File → Open (3D model) | `mesh` | The 3D model to make a puzzle of | — | LuBan: not stated in §3.10.8; OBJ, PLY or STL in the 2018 build (luban-docs Get started p.2). Ours: STL, OBJ, PLY, 3MF | §3.10.8 step 2 (PDF p.83); luban-docs Get started p.2 |
| Mesh → Depth map: direction | `view_direction` | The direction from which depth is captured (the same setting as TOOL-DEPTHMAP's `direction`) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: `+z`) | Options UNCONFIRMED (LuBan's Relief has six axis directions and needs Object → Transform for any other: §5.6.1, PDF p.108). Ours: `+x`, `-x`, `+y`, `-y`, `+z`, `-z`, `custom` (viewport gizmo) | §3.10.8 step 3 |
| Mesh → Depth map: resolution | `depth_resolution_mm_per_px` | Pixel size of the depth map (the same setting as TOOL-DEPTHMAP's `resolution_mm_px`) | UNCONFIRMED | Unit UNCONFIRMED. Ours: mm/px, tied to the puzzle's `resolution_mm_per_px` by default | §3.10.8 step 3 |
| File → Save (FLT) | (internal, no key) | The depth map is saved as FLT, a LuBan float image, which is more accurate than BMP, JPG or PNG | — | Ours: the depth stays float in memory and in the project file; optional export as 16-bit PNG or 32-bit float TIFF | §3.10.8 step 4 |
| (all Puzzle settings) | PHOTO-PUZZLE keys | Size, min/max thickness, X/Y sections, resolution, edge chamfer and tolerance apply unchanged | As PHOTO-PUZZLE (with `polarity` = `bright_high`) | As PHOTO-PUZZLE | §3.10.8 step 5 |
| — (AD3D) | `depth_mapping` | `normalise`: the depth range maps onto min..max thickness. `true_scale`: height = model depth × `model_scale`, on top of `min_thickness_mm` | ours: `normalise` | As listed | AD3D |
| — (AD3D) | `model_scale` | Scale factor for `true_scale` | ours: 1.0 | ours: > 0 | AD3D |
| — (AD3D) | `depth_compression` | Bas-relief compression strength: flattens cliffs and keeps surface detail | ours: 0 | ours: 0–1 | AD3D; research 04 §A (Weyrich et al. 2007), §B.6 |
| — (AD3D) | `bury_percent` | Cut off the lowest depths so only the top part remains, as in LuBan's Relief "bury" | ours: 0 | ours: 0–90 (Relief's Fig. 204 shows 0, 20, 40, 60 and 80 %) | AD3D; analogue in §5.6.5, Fig. 204 (PDF p.110); research 04 §B.6 |
| — (AD3D) | `crop_to_model` | Shrink the puzzle rectangle to the model's projected bounds plus a margin | ours: on, margin 5 mm | on/off, margin ≥ 0 | AD3D; Fig. 147 shows a black background around the model (figure observation) |

- **Outputs:** as PHOTO-PUZZLE. Ours also offers an optional depth image (16-bit PNG or 32-bit float TIFF) for use elsewhere.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - The depth map "describes the surface height distribution of the model" (§3.10.8 step 3).
  - FLT keeps floating-point accuracy, unlike BMP, JPG or PNG (step 4).
  - "All these can be done in LuBan" (§3.10.8 intro).
  - Fig. 147, figure observation: the left image shows the model in LuBan's height colour map (blue at the bottom to red at the top), which is how a newly opened model is drawn (luban-docs Get started p.3, p.17). The centre image (depth map) has a black background with nearer surfaces brighter. The right image is a puzzle (about 4 × 3 pieces by our count) with the model raised above a flat base, so the bright parts of the depth map became the high parts.
  - LuBan's Relief method, the documented analogue, allows six axis directions and needs Object → Transform for any other (§5.6.1, PDF p.108). Whether Mesh → Depth map has the same limit is UNCONFIRMED.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - **One step, no intermediate file.** Pick a mesh and a direction and get a puzzle. LuBan takes five steps across two windows with a saved FLT file (§3.10.8).
  - **Open formats.** Depth stays float internally; exports use 16-bit PNG or 32-bit float TIFF, not a proprietary format (CLAUDE.md: our own formats).
  - **Any direction, live.** A viewport gizmo sets any view direction with a live depth preview, instead of axis-only directions plus a manual Transform (as §5.6.1 requires for Relief).
  - **True scale.** `true_scale` keeps real model proportions in mm instead of re-stretching the depth to min/max thickness (ours).
  - **Tamed cliffs.** Bas-relief compression and bury reduce the vertical walls seen in Fig. 147. Optionally, the seam lattice is nudged so knobs do not land on steep depth jumps (research 04 §B.6; wingated/digital-bas-relief MIT, research 03 §4).
  - **No repair step.** Depth capture works on unrepaired meshes (a z-buffer needs only triangles), so dirty STLs from M3 import still work. The Mesh doctor (PLAN §4) is offered but not required.
  - **Fast and cancellable.** Multi-core rasterisation, with progress and cancel (PLAN §4).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  1. Orthographic z-buffer rasterisation of the mesh along `view_direction`. On the CPU it runs in Rust, tiled with rayon, for the final result; the viewport's GPU depth render is used for the preview. Research 04 §B.6: "Choose a direction (±X/±Y/±Z), rasterize a depth map (z-buffer), and build a heightfield". Research 04 §C: "The 3D 'puzzle of a model' uses a rendered z-buffer depth map, not monocular depth."
  2. Pixels that miss the model get `min_thickness_mm`.
  3. Optional bas-relief compression (Weyrich et al. 2007, research 04 §A; wingated/digital-bas-relief MIT, research 03 §4), then bury and normalisation.
  4. Hand the float heightfield to the PHOTO-PUZZLE generator unchanged.
  5. Tests: random meshes from the corpus and random directions → `validate()` on every piece; a golden test on one fixed mesh (PLAN §5).
- **Milestone:** M6 (part 9, after PHOTO-PUZZLE). It needs M3's mesh import, but not its repair.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - The depth map's direction options and resolution unit.
  - How LuBan normalises depth, and what value the background gets.
  - Whether the puzzle rescales the depth to min/max thickness (it is treated as an image, so probably yes).
  - Orthographic or perspective capture.
  - The FLT internals; we do not need them, because we use open formats.

---

## 4. Mesh → Cut

LuBan's Mesh → Cut mode splits an opened mesh into smaller solid parts: with one or more planes (planar, regional, natural), with a grid or a radial fan of planes, or automatically so that every part fits one or more printers (modular cut), adding plug or dowel connectors, part numbers and an assembly-order file (§4–§4.6, PDF p.84–95). AD3D builds all of this as one cut engine in `ad3d-core`: a pure, cancellable generator that takes a repaired watertight mesh plus a cut plan and returns watertight parts and a cut tree. Cut-to-bed (CUT-MODULAR) and connectors (CUT-CONNECTOR) are milestone M3, with mesh import and repair on its critical path. Conventions used below:
- A Default of "shown: v (Fig. N)" is a value visible in a screenshot. It may be the default or a remembered last-used setting (§1.6).
- A LuBan label marked "(text)" comes from the manual's prose because no screenshot shows it.
- "CN Get started p.N" is a PDF page of LuBan's official Chinese quick-start guide in `docs/reference/luban-docs/`, which shows an older UI from about 2018–2019.
- Rows labelled "— (AD3D only)" are our additions, with suggested values.

---

### CUT-WORKSPACE — Cut workspace (LuBan: Mesh → Cut)

- **LuBan path:** File → Open a 3D model, then Mesh → Cut; choose a method from the drop-down method list (manual §4 intro, PDF p.84, Fig. 149). LuBan's start-up "Tip" dialog lists Mesh > Cut as available "after opening a model" (research 01, Squama video, workflow step 1). Older names:
  - The mode itself was "Mesh -> Split" in 2019 (blog: grid-cut, staggered-cut-pattern, flexible-grid-cut, d-shape-plug-and-dowel). The 2018 Mesh menu shows "分割" (Split) (CN Get started p.3). The current name first appears in the blog as "Mesh -> Cut, Modular cut" (blog: multi-thread-modular-cut, 2023-11-15).
  - The cut-to-bed method began as "Mesh -> LuBan, Method Module" (blog: printer-bed-shape, d-shape-plug-and-dowel, _test). Its older panel is "三维模块" ("3D module", CN Get started p.5, p.22).
- **What it makes:** A mode for splitting one model into parts, with uses "from extracting components of a model to printing a model bigger than the working dimension of a 3D printer" (§4 intro; Fig. 148: a printed castle assembled from parts by user Burkhard Effertz). It hosts CUT-PLANAR (with CUT-REGIONAL and CUT-NATURAL), CUT-GRID, CUT-RADIAL and CUT-MODULAR (§4.2–§4.5). The blog-only CUT-CONIC and CUT-FLEXI probably live here too (our reading; their posts give no menu path).
- **Fabrication:** 3D printing (FDM) of parts that are then joined with connectors, glue or pins (§4.6). Scale examples:
  - the Fig. 148 castle;
  - a 0.5 m dragon (CN Get started p.25);
  - a 1.0 m dragon in 129 parts (CN Introduction p.22). Paper CAD19 (Camburn, Wee, Chen, Sass, Wood 2019) gives the same dragon as 1000 × 800 × 600 mm and 129 components, printed in parallel.
- **Inputs:** One mesh already open in the 3D window (§4 intro). See CUT-IMPORT and CUT-REPAIR.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| "Method" | `method` | Which cut method the panel shows | shown: "Planar cut" (Fig. 149) | Planar cut, Grid cut, Radial cut, Modular cut (§4.2–§4.5); probably also Conic cut (blog: conic-cut gives no menu path). The full list and its order are UNCONFIRMED | §4 intro; Fig. 149 (PDF p.84) |
| "Unit", "Model size X/Y/Z" | see CUT-IMPORT | Input section shared by all methods | — | — | Fig. 149; §4.1 |
| "Cut" (button) | `run` (action) | Performs the cut. In planar cut, each part is saved as an individual STL file in a folder the user selects | — | — | §4.2 (PDF p.85) |
| "关闭" ("Close", button, older UI) | (leave mode) | Leaves the method panel | — | — | CN Get started p.5, p.22 |
| "Object → Explode", "Object → Restore", "Object → Select" + toolbar slider | see TOOL-EXPLODE (part 7) | Explode the parts, restore them, highlight one part and step through parts with the toolbar slider. Shortcuts: E explodes, J selects (both said in videos of other modes; the older Select dialog's title "选择J" agrees) | — | — | §4.3 (PDF p.87–88), Fig. 156; video VA67Jm3ijHg @00:01; video F20FZvL0r9g @00:05; CN Get started p.24; blog: exploded-view |
| "删除" ("Delete") in the older "选择" (Select) dialog | `delete_part` (action) | Removes the highlighted part from the result | — | — | CN Get started p.24 (older UI; the dialog shows "Part_01", a Delete button and a slider); current UI UNCONFIRMED |
| — (AD3D only) | `preview_quality` | Proxy preview while dragging, full resolution on release | n/a in LuBan (suggest: auto) | auto, proxy, full | AD3D proposal; CLAUDE.md speed rules |

- **Outputs:**
  - Planar cut writes per-part STL files into a chosen folder (§4.2).
  - Modular cut also writes Tiny_N debris files and a *_Sequence.txt file (§4.5.2–§4.5.3).
  - After a cut, LuBan shows the parts in different colours in the 3D view (Fig. 150, Fig. 156).
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - The control panel is on the left and the "live display" on the right (§4 intro). The Input section holds Method, Unit and Model size X/Y/Z. A method-specific section follows; Fig. 149 shows "Cutting Plane".
  - The panel scrolls: Fig. 149 shows a vertical scroll bar and stops at D. The "Cut" button is "at the bottom of the control panel" (§4.2), so it and the Regional cut, Close cut and Natural cut controls sit below the visible area; their on-screen labels and order are not shown in any figure (UNCONFIRMED). Long panels also scrolled in the older UI (CN notes §2.6, Get started p.12, p.18).
  - Changing a selection (drop-down list, radio button, check box, spin button) updates the display automatically, "with one exception: changes in a text box will not trigger an automatic update". A typed value applies only after Enter, because there is no Apply button (§1.8, PDF p.15–16; §4.1).
  - Settings persist between sessions in MU_Setting.txt (§1.6, PDF p.14).
  - Files are written as part of the cut action (§4.2). In the older module, parts were generated only after clicking "导出部件" ("Export parts") (CN Get started p.22–23).
  - Viewing parts afterwards: Object → Explode / Restore / Select, plus the toolbar slider (§4.3; a slider sits at the right end of the toolbar in Fig. 149). Selection is the suggested way to understand part relations for fewer than about 20 parts (§4.5.3).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - **One engine for every method.** Each method is a planner that outputs a cut tree (planes or surfaces, plus the order of the cuts), and one executor runs it. Connectors, labels, assembly order, repair and export then behave the same for every method. LuBan's manual never says which methods get connectors: §4.6 figures show a single flat section (Fig. 166, Fig. 169–171), and the older panel puts them in the module/modular cut (CN Get started p.22). Part numbers and the sequence file are described only for modular cut (§4.5.2–§4.5.3).
  - **Live preview.** While a control is dragged, the planned cuts and coloured part regions update within the 50 ms budget on a decimated proxy. The full-resolution cut then runs as a cancellable job on all cores (CLAUDE.md; PLAN §4). LuBan needs text box + Enter (§1.8), and you cut before you see parts.
  - **Non-destructive.** A cut creates parts inside the project, with undo/redo and the `.ad3d` project file. Exporting is a separate step with 3MF or STL output (PLAN §1, §4). LuBan saves straight to a folder (§4.2).
  - **Scriptable.** The same generators run from `ad3d-cli` for batch jobs (PLAN §4).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - Generator `cut(params, mesh) -> (parts, cut_tree)` in `ad3d-core`.
  - manifold (C API through FFI) for splits and booleans; Clipper2 for 2D section work (PLAN §1; research 03 §13).
  - meshoptimizer for display and preview proxies (research 03 §13).
  - three.js clipping planes and three-mesh-bvh slicing for previews (PLAN §1; research 03 §13).
- **Milestone:** M3 (part 9, after APP-MESH-DOCTOR).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - The full method list and its order in today's drop-down, and whether Flexi cut lives here (blog: flexi-cut gives no menu path).
  - Video aQl8_1Gl79U "LuBan Mesh Cut" (25:59, title only) probably shows the full panel; it was not transcribed.

### CUT-IMPORT — Mesh import, units and model size (LuBan: File → Open; "Unit"; "Model size X/Y/Z")

- **LuBan path:**
  - File → Open. The quick-start guide says "打开一个 OBJ, PLY, 或 STL 文件格式的三维模型" ("open a 3D model in OBJ, PLY or STL format", CN Get started p.2).
  - Then "Unit" and "Model size X/Y/Z" in the Input section of Mesh → Cut (Fig. 149, PDF p.84; §4.1, PDF p.85).
- **What it makes:** Loads a mesh, records which unit its coordinates are in, and scales it uniformly to the physical size wanted before cutting (§4.1).
- **Fabrication:** Sets the real printed size. Modular cut uses this size to decide whether, and into how many parts, to cut (§4.5).
- **Inputs:**
  - OBJ, PLY and STL (CN Get started p.2); STL and OBJ (blog: password-protected-3d-file).
  - LuBan's own FGS/FGD scene pair also opens in the 3D window (§5 intro, PDF p.96; blog: password-protected-3d-file). AD3D will not read it (clean room: our own formats).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| "Unit"; dialog "选择单位" ("Select unit", older UI) | `source_unit` | Unit of the file's raw coordinates (STL, OBJ and PLY carry none) | shown: "mm" (Fig. 149). In the older dialog, Cancel keeps the last unit used: "按撤销键即为使用上一次的单位" (CN Get started p.4). A 2026 video picks "millimeter" after opening an STL in Mesh → LuBan (video F20FZvL0r9g @00:03) | m, dm, cm, mm, inch ("米 / 分米 / 厘米 / 毫米 / 英寸", CN Get started p.4); the current list is UNCONFIRMED | Fig. 149; CN Get started p.4 |
| "Model size X", "Model size Y", "Model size Z" | `model_size_mm` [x, y, z] | Overall size of the model. The X:Y:Z ratio is fixed to the model's aspect ratio; editing one value updates the other two after Enter | UNCONFIRMED (Fig. 149 shows 242 / 187 / 300 for its sample model; suggest: the imported bounding box in `source_unit`) | > 0; limits UNCONFIRMED | §4.1; Fig. 149 |
| — (AD3D only) | `lock_aspect` | Keep the X:Y:Z ratio | n/a in LuBan, which always locks (§4.1) (suggest: true) | true, false | AD3D proposal |
| — (AD3D only) | `auto_unit` | Suggest a unit from the bounding box when the file has none | n/a (suggest: on) | on, off | AD3D proposal; video F20FZvL0r9g @00:11 shows a model with tiny coordinates going wrong until resized |
| — (AD3D only) | `orientation` | Rotation and placement applied before cutting (gizmo, lay flat on a face, drop to bed) | n/a (suggest: as imported) | rotation in degrees in the UI, translation in mm | AD3D proposal; LuBan uses Object → Transform (§3.2.9, PDF p.57–58; §5.2.2, PDF p.99) |

- **Outputs:** A scaled, oriented mesh in mm inside the project. No file is written.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - The X:Y:Z ratio is locked, and typed values apply on Enter (§4.1).
  - With unit mm, the model size equals the raw coordinate extent. The duck is about 100 units wide in CN Get started p.3 and shows "模型X尺寸" (Model X size) 98.5 in mm on p.6. This is our inference and is UNCONFIRMED for other units.
  - A horse with very small coordinates "produces something nasty" until its model size is set to a reasonable value (video F20FZvL0r9g @00:11). That video is Mesh → LuBan, which shares this Input section (§5 intro).
  - LuBan's size and placement tools:
    - Mesh → Statistics reports the bounding cube (§3.2.9).
    - Object → Transform resizes, by size or by scale, and rotates (§3.2.9, §5.2.2, §5.6.1).
    - The 2018 Mesh menu also has rotate about X/Y/Z, "刚体移动" (rigid move), "改变比例" (change scale) and "Z 基面置零" (set Z base to zero) (CN Get started p.3).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - **Formats with units.** Import STL (binary and ASCII), OBJ, PLY and 3MF. 3MF carries units, so it needs no unit question (PLAN §4; research 00 I/O; research 07 effort table). For unitless files we suggest a unit from the bounding box and show the result against the printer bed and a ruler, instead of LuBan's blind unit dialog (CN Get started p.4).
  - **Live resize.** The size updates while dragging, with no Enter (§4.1; PLAN §4).
  - **Fast, non-blocking load.** Drag-and-drop and recent files (PLAN §4). Parsing and welding run on a background thread with progress. Huge meshes are decimated for display only; cutting always uses full resolution (PLAN §1).
  - **Orientation in the viewport.** An orientation gizmo and "lay flat on face" replace the Object → Transform dialog (§3.2.9).
  - **Non-destructive.** The original file is never modified; transforms live in the project with undo/redo (PLAN §4).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - A streaming binary/ASCII STL reader (`stl_io` or hand-rolled), plus OBJ and PLY readers (PLAN §1).
  - 3MF read through the `zip` crate and XML (PLAN §1).
  - Welding on import (CUT-REPAIR).
  - Unit guess: map the largest bounding-box extent to the most plausible unit (our heuristic), always confirmed by the user.
- **Milestone:** M3 (part 9, first in its row). Import is on the critical path for every mesh feature (PLAN §3; research 08 §2.11).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - The current Unit options and default, and whether changing Unit rescales the model or only relabels the numbers.
  - Whether Model size starts at the imported bounding box.
  - Research 02 lists more LuBan input formats, but that list was read from LuBan's binary, so it is not used here (clean room).

### CUT-REPAIR — Mesh doctor for cutting (LuBan: Mesh → "修复" Repair / "反转" Reverse, 2018 menu; no repair step in Mesh → Cut)

- **LuBan path:**
  - The 2018 Mesh menu has "修复" (Repair) and "反转" (Reverse) (CN Get started p.3).
  - Video ce6XCcfx2DA "LuBan Mesh Repair" (10:51, title only).
  - The 2025 manual's cut chapter has no repair step.
- **What it makes:** A closed, consistently oriented, non-self-intersecting solid that the cut engine can split and cap, plus a report of what was wrong and what was fixed.
- **Fabrication:** Prevents broken caps and debris parts. LuBan's "Tiny 1, Tiny 2" files are "often caused by defects in the original model or residual errors produced in the cutting process" (§4.5.2, PDF p.90).
- **Inputs:** The imported mesh (CUT-IMPORT).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| "修复" (Repair) | `repair` (action) | Run the repair pipeline | — | parameters UNCONFIRMED | CN Get started p.3; video ce6XCcfx2DA (title) |
| "反转" (Reverse) | `flip_winding` (action) | Flip face orientation | — | — | CN Get started p.3 |
| — (AD3D only) | `weld_tolerance_mm` | Merge vertices closer than this | n/a (suggest: 1e-3) | 0–0.1 | AD3D proposal |
| — (AD3D only) | `fill_holes` | Close boundary loops | n/a (suggest: on) | on, off | AD3D proposal |
| — (AD3D only) | `max_hole_perimeter_mm` | Larger holes are reported, not auto-filled | n/a (suggest: 50) | > 0 | AD3D proposal |
| — (AD3D only) | `fix_self_intersections` | Resolve intersecting triangles and shells | n/a (suggest: on) | on, off | AD3D proposal |
| — (AD3D only) | `min_part_volume_mm3` (APP-VALIDATE key) | Remove specks smaller than this before cutting | from APP-VALIDATE (suggest: 50) | ≥ 0 | AD3D proposal; §4.5.2 (Tiny parts) |
| — (AD3D only) | `voxel_fallback_mm` | Voxel size for the last-resort remesh | n/a (suggest: 0.2, or bounding-box diagonal / 1024) | 0.05–2 | AD3D proposal; PLAN §6 |

- **Outputs:** The repaired mesh plus a report: counts of holes, non-manifold edges and vertices, flipped faces, self-intersections, degenerate and duplicate faces, shells, and the volume change.
- **Behaviour and rules:** What the cut tools need, from the sources:
  - Closing a cut section is what makes each part a solid (§4.2.2). That needs a closed input; a non-watertight input breaks cap triangulation (research 04 §B.7).
  - Every modular-cut step needs a manifold input, so "import repair is on the critical path for every mesh feature" (research 08 §2.11; PLAN §3).
  - A robust inside/outside test on a dirty mesh needs a generalised or fast winding number (research 08 §2.10). Dirty STLs break slicing and booleans: repair everything on import, with a voxel remesh as the last resort (PLAN §6).
  - Splitting into loose shells is TOOL-SEPARATE (part 7; blog: separate).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - **Diagnosis you can see.** Holes, non-manifold edges, flipped faces and self-intersections are highlighted in the viewport with counts (PLAN §4 "Mesh doctor"). LuBan instead exports leftover debris as Tiny_N files (§4.5.2).
  - **One click, then a guard.** A "fix all" pipeline shows before/after statistics. A cut will not run on a mesh that still fails `validate()`; it says why, instead of producing debris.
  - **Last resort is explicit.** Voxel/SDF remeshing shows its resolution and the volume change before it is accepted (PLAN §6).
  - **Fast.** Runs on all cores and can be cancelled (PLAN §4).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - Weld with a spatial hash; remove degenerate and duplicate faces.
  - Orient faces by BFS over edge adjacency, with the global sign set by signed volume.
  - Fill holes: ear clipping for small loops; advancing front plus fairing for large ones (pmp-library, geometry-central; research 03 §13).
  - Resolve self-intersections with a manifold union of shells.
  - Last resort: fast winding number (libigl, MPL-2.0) → SDF grid → marching cubes or manifold `levelSet` (research 08 §2.10; research 00 table; PLAN §6).
  - MeshFix and CGAL (GPL) may be read or ported for personal use (PLAN §1).
  - Test corpus of 30–100 CC0 meshes, some deliberately broken (PLAN §5).
- **Milestone:** M3 (part 9, after CUT-IMPORT; critical path).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Parameters of LuBan's Repair, and whether Mesh → Cut repairs anything automatically.
  - The size threshold below which LuBan names a part "Tiny".

### CUT-PLANAR — Plane cut (LuBan: Planar cut)

- **LuBan path:** Mesh → Cut, Method = "Planar cut" (§4.2, PDF p.85; Fig. 149, PDF p.84). Later additions:
  - several planes in one go (blog: multi-planar-cut, 2025-04-06; video PuY5inToqIQ "LuBan Multi planar cut", 13:21, title only);
  - planes selected and moved with the mouse (blog: mouse-movable-cutting-plane, 2025-05-16; video 6Z05ckh7hkI, 3:24, title only).
- **What it makes:** "Splits a model into two parts, one on each side of a cutting plane", given by Ax + By + Cz = D (§4.2, Fig. 150).
- **Fabrication:** Two (or more) solid parts printed separately, for example to fit the bed or to remove an overhang. Connectors can be added (CUT-CONNECTOR): Fig. 166 and Fig. 169–171 show plugs and dowels on a single flat section of a sphere or cylinder, but the manual does not say which method made those cuts, so whether Planar cut offers connectors is UNCONFIRMED. Blog: d-shape-plug-and-dowel lists "Mesh -> Split", the old name of this mode, as offering plugs and dowels.
- **Inputs:** One mesh.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| "Cutting Plane", "Plane: Ax + By + Cz = D" (headings) | — | Section title and the plane equation shown in the panel | — | — | Fig. 149 |
| "A", "B", "C" (text box + slider each) | `plane_normal` [a, b, c] | Normal direction of the plane (normalised by AD3D) | shown: 0, 0, 1 (Fig. 149) | UNCONFIRMED. In Fig. 149, C = 1 puts its slider at the right end and A = B = 0 sit at the centre, which suggests −1…1 | §4.2; Fig. 149 |
| "D" (text box + slider) | `plane_offset_mm` | Offset of the plane | shown: 0 (Fig. 149) | UNCONFIRMED: unit and origin. In Fig. 149, D = 0 draws the plane near the model's mid-height, not at Z = 0 | §4.2; Fig. 149 |
| "Cut" (button at the bottom of the panel) | `run` (action) | Splits the model; each part is saved as an individual STL in a selected folder | — | — | §4.2 |
| "Close cut" (text) | `close_cut` | Cap the cut section so each part is a solid; No leaves the section open | Yes ("By default, LuBan will close a cut section", §4.2.2) | Yes, No | §4.2.2, Fig. 152 (PDF p.86) |
| "regional cut" (text) | `regional` | Shrink the plane to a disk; see CUT-REGIONAL | UNCONFIRMED (the text implies No: "you can set the regional cut to Yes") | Yes, No | §4.2.1 |
| "natural cut" option (text) | `natural` | Curved cut guided by the plane; see CUT-NATURAL | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: off) | on, off | §4.2.3 |
| several planes (blog wording) | `planes[]` | A list of planes applied in one go | 1 plane | list of {`plane_normal`, `plane_offset_mm`, `enabled`} | blog: multi-planar-cut |
| mouse-movable planes (blog wording) | (viewport gizmo) | "In the Planar cut method, cutting planes can now be selected and moved by a mouse device" | — | — | blog: mouse-movable-cutting-plane |
| — (AD3D only) | `plane_tilt_deg`, `plane_azimuth_deg` | The normal as two angles in the UI (radians in code) | n/a (suggest: 0, 0 = horizontal plane) | tilt 0–180, azimuth −180–180 | AD3D proposal; CLAUDE.md units rule |
| — (AD3D only) | `plane_reference` | What the offset is measured from | n/a (suggest: `bbox_center`, matching Fig. 149) | `bbox_center`, `bed`, `world_origin` | AD3D proposal |
| — (AD3D only) | `split_shells` | Save each connected piece on a side as its own part | n/a (suggest: on) | on, off | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:**
  - Each part as an individual STL file in a selected folder (§4.2).
  - Close cut = No gives open, non-solid parts (§4.2.2, Fig. 152).
  - AD3D: parts in the project; export to one 3MF holding all named parts in mm, or one binary STL per part.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - A, B, C and D can be set with text boxes or sliders (§4.2). Only text boxes need Enter; other controls update automatically (§1.8).
  - The "Cut" button at the bottom of the panel splits the model. LuBan then shows the two parts in colour, with an exploded view available (§4.2, Fig. 150).
  - Close cut Yes caps each section into a solid. With No, "the cut section is open; you do not get a solid model" (Fig. 152 caption).
  - Regional and natural modify the plane cut (CUT-REGIONAL, CUT-NATURAL).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - **A gizmo and human units.** Drag or rotate the plane in the viewport, or type tilt and azimuth in degrees and an offset in mm from a chosen reference. Snap to X/Y/Z and to 15° steps, and offer "cut at height Z". LuBan uses raw A/B/C/D (Fig. 149), and mouse dragging arrived only in 2025 (blog: mouse-movable-cutting-plane).
  - **See the result while dragging.** A GPU clip shader tints the two sides and a BVH slice draws the section outline, both within 50 ms. The real split runs on release (CLAUDE.md; PLAN §4). LuBan shows only the plane until you press "Cut".
  - **Editable plane lists.** Several planes form one ordered cut tree that stays editable later (undo/redo, project file; blog: multi-planar-cut; PLAN §4). LuBan writes files at once (§4.2).
  - **Section readout.** Shows section area, the largest circle that fits (connector room), and whether each resulting part fits the bed from the machine profile (PLAN §4).
  - **Honest open cuts.** Close cut = No still works, but its parts are flagged "open, not printable" and left out of watertight export unless forced (CLAUDE.md watertight rule).
  - **Better export.** 3MF with units and named parts, or streamed per-part binary STL (PLAN §4).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - manifold `SplitByPlane` / `TrimByPlane` (caps come by construction), then `Decompose()` for loose pieces (research 08 §1.4, §2.11). Research 08 measured `splitByPlane` at 0.58 s for 131k and 2.63 s for 524k triangles in single-threaded WASM; native is faster.
  - Close cut = No uses our own half-space triangle clipper that emits no caps.
  - Preview: three.js clipping planes, plus a three-mesh-bvh plane–mesh intersection polyline (research 03 §13).
- **Milestone:** M3 (part 9, after TOOL-BOOLEAN). The same split is the core of CUT-MODULAR: "The modular cut consists of several planar cuts" (§4.5.3).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - The slider range of A/B/C, and D's unit and origin.
  - Whether a side that falls into several separate pieces is saved as one STL or several; part file names for planar cuts.
  - How multi-planar cut orders and combines its planes, and how planes are added or removed.

### CUT-REGIONAL — Disk-limited cut (LuBan: Regional cut / Cutting region)

- **LuBan path:** Mesh → Cut, Planar cut, "regional cut" set to Yes (§4.2.1, PDF p.85; Fig. 151, PDF p.86). Blog: cutting-region (2019-09-05): "Split a model by a cutting region instead of a basic cutting plane."
- **What it makes:** Cuts off one local piece, "such as an arm from a body", without cutting other parts the full plane would also cross; "the cutting plane will become a disk" (§4.2.1).
- **Fabrication:** Print a limb or other appendage separately, for example to avoid supports.
- **Inputs:** One mesh, and the plane from CUT-PLANAR.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| "regional cut" (text) | `regional` | Limit the cutting plane to a disk | UNCONFIRMED (the text implies No) | Yes, No | §4.2.1 |
| disk radius (text; label UNCONFIRMED) | `disk_radius_mm` | Radius of the disk (text box and slider) | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED | §4.2.1 |
| disk centre position (text; label UNCONFIRMED) | `disk_center_mm` | Centre of the disk in the plane (text boxes and sliders) | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED | §4.2.1 |
| "A", "B", "C", "D" | from CUT-PLANAR | The plane that holds the disk | shown: 0, 0, 1, 0 (Fig. 149) | see CUT-PLANAR | §4.2.1; Fig. 149 |
| — (AD3D only) | `region_shape` | Shape of the cutting region | n/a (suggest: disk) | disk, rectangle, polygon | AD3D proposal; blog: cutting-region says "region" |

- **Outputs:** As CUT-PLANAR: one STL per part.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - "Parts of the model that are completely separated by the disk will be cut off. Other parts that do not fully intersect the disk will remain unchanged" (§4.2.1).
  - Fig. 151: the whole plane splits the model along a diagonal through the forearm, hips and kicking leg, while the disk, placed at the elbow, cuts off only the forearm.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - **Live feedback.** While the disk is dragged, the section loops it will cut are highlighted, so a disk that cuts nothing is obvious. In LuBan, unaffected parts simply "remain unchanged" with no feedback (§4.2.1).
  - **More region shapes.** Rectangle and polygon as well as disk. LuBan later added a cone (blog: conic-cut), which shows demand for non-plane cutting surfaces.
  - **Same downstream as every cut.** Connectors, labels and export work as for any other cut (CUT-CONNECTOR).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  1. Intersect the mesh with the plane and chain the segments into section loops.
  2. Keep the loops that lie fully inside the region (Clipper2 polygon tests).
  3. Split only the triangles those loops cross, cap the loops, then `Decompose()`.
  4. Loops that cross the region's edge stay uncut, matching §4.2.1.
- **Milestone:** M10 (part 9, after CUT-LAPJOINT).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Labels, units and ranges of radius and centre; whether the centre is a 3D point or an in-plane offset.
  - What happens when a loop inside the disk does not separate the shape (for example a ring cut once).

### CUT-NATURAL — Shape-following cut (LuBan: Natural cut)

- **LuBan path:**
  - Mesh → Cut, Planar cut, "natural cut" option (§4.2.3, PDF p.86; Fig. 153).
  - The older module offers a radio choice "平面切割 / 自然切割" ("planar cut / natural cut") (CN Get started p.22–23).
  - Blog: _test "Natural cut" (2019; menus "Mesh -> LuBan", Method Module, and "Mesh -> Split").
- **What it makes:** "A curved cut on a model based on its local shape". The algorithm "takes the cutting plane as a guide and searches for local concave regions to place the cut. The end result is a curved cut section" (§4.2.3; Fig. 153, horse). "自然切割生成曲面切割面" ("natural cut generates curved cut faces") (CN Get started p.23).
- **Fabrication:** Seams fall in natural creases, such as where a leg meets the body, so they show less after assembly. How LuBan places connectors on curved sections is UNCONFIRMED.
- **Inputs:** A mesh plus a guide plane.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| "natural cut" option (text); "自然切割" (older UI) | `natural` | Use the plane as a guide for a curved cut | UNCONFIRMED (CN Get started p.22 shows planar selected) | on, off; the control type is UNCONFIRMED (radio button in the older UI) | §4.2.3; CN Get started p.22 |
| — (AD3D only) | `search_band_mm` | How far the seam may wander from the guide plane | n/a (suggest: 15% of the section width) | > 0 | AD3D proposal |
| — (AD3D only) | `crease_weight` | Trade-off between a short seam and staying in concave creases | n/a (suggest: 0.7) | 0–1 | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** As CUT-PLANAR.
- **Behaviour and rules:** "The algorithm may not work on complex local shapes. If it fails to make a natural cut, LuBan will roll back to the pure planar cut" (§4.2.3).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - **No silent fallback.** Show the proposed seam before cutting, let the user nudge it, and say clearly when it falls back to a plane. The manual describes the rollback without mentioning any notice (§4.2.3).
  - **Check that it comes apart.** Before accepting a curved seam, check that the two sides can be pulled apart in a straight line with no undercut lock; warn otherwise.
  - **Watertight caps.** Caps are watertight by construction and checked by `validate()` (CLAUDE.md).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - LuBan's internals are UNCONFIRMED; research 04 §B.7 suggests a min-cut or graph cut in a band around the plane.
  - Ours: in a band around the guide plane, find a shortest closed cycle on the mesh whose edge costs are low in concave creases and high on convex areas. Cut along it, then cap with a faired minimal-surface patch shared by both parts (pmp-library or geometry-central for fairing; research 03 §13).
- **Milestone:** M12 (part 9, first in its row). PLAN §3 lists natural cut under Later; research 07 estimates 3 weeks and research 08 4–8 weeks.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Control label and type in today's UI; the search method.
  - Connectors on curved sections; whether natural cut is still offered inside Modular cut.

### CUT-CONIC — Cone cut (LuBan: Conic cut)

- **LuBan path:** UNCONFIRMED; not in the manual (probably Mesh → Cut, chosen from the drop-down method list, §4, PDF p.84; our reading). Blog: conic-cut (2024-12-31): "Cut a model by a cone." Videos VP0ZWQGMku8 "LuBan Conic cut" (10:24) and Hgqn-1M3yTQ "LuBan Conic cut 2" (6:36), titles only.
- **What it makes:** Splits a model with a conical surface instead of a plane (blog).
- **Fabrication:** UNCONFIRMED. Our reading: separating a dome, nose or pointed top along a cone.
- **Inputs:** A mesh.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — (none stated) | — | The post names no setting | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED | blog: conic-cut |
| — (AD3D only) | `cone_apex_mm` | Apex position | n/a (suggest: top centre of the bounding box) | any point | AD3D proposal |
| — (AD3D only) | `cone_axis` | Axis direction | n/a (suggest: −Z) | unit vector | AD3D proposal |
| — (AD3D only) | `cone_half_angle_deg` | Half opening angle | n/a (suggest: 45) | 1–89 | AD3D proposal |
| Close cut (Planar cut option) | `close_cut` | Cap the cut so each part is solid | UNCONFIRMED for this method (Yes by default in Planar cut) | Yes, No | §4.2.2 (PDF p.85) |

- **Outputs:** UNCONFIRMED. LuBan's planar cut saves "each part after cutting" as an individual STL (§4.2, PDF p.85). Ours: an inside part and an outside part, as STL or 3MF.
- **Behaviour and rules:** None stated.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - A gizmo for apex, axis and angle, with the parts previewed while dragging. LuBan's manual planar cut is driven by A, B, C, D text boxes and sliders (§4.2, PDF p.85); mouse-moved planes arrived only in 2025 and only for Planar cut (blog: mouse-movable-cutting-plane).
  - Parts are exported together as one 3MF with named parts. LuBan saves one STL per part (§4.2, PDF p.85; PLAN §4).
  - Cuts run on all cores and can be cancelled (PLAN §4).
  - Watertight conical caps by construction, checked by `validate()` (CLAUDE.md).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Build a large cone solid (manifold `Extrude` with `scaleTop` = 0, or a revolve), then intersect it with and subtract it from the model (manifold). Repair the input first (PLAN §6: dirty STLs break booleans).
- **Milestone:** M10 (part 9, after CUT-REGIONAL). Gated: not started until videos VP0ZWQGMku8 and Hgqn-1M3yTQ are transcribed (part 9).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Everything beyond the one-sentence post, including whether connectors are added on the conical faces. Watch the two videos first.

### CUT-GRID — Grid split (LuBan: Grid cut)

- **LuBan path:** Mesh → Cut, Method = Grid cut (§4.3, PDF p.87). History:
  - first released under "Mesh -> Split", Method Grid cut (blog: grid-cut, 2019-02-12);
  - staggered option added (blog: staggered-cut-pattern, 2019-04-02);
  - per-plane adjustment added (blog: flexible-grid-cut, 2019-07-07: "Adjust each cutting plane").
- **What it makes:** "Splits a model by a grid of cutting planes" in X, Y and Z (§4.3); "Grid cut split an object into equal-sized blocks" (blog: grid-cut). A staggered pattern "may strengthen the assembly of a model compared to a grid without staggering" (§4.3, Fig. 154).
- **Fabrication:** Block-wise printing (Fig. 156, elephant). Staggering stops a seam plane from running "through the whole body" (Fig. 154 caption).
- **Inputs:** A mesh.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| number of sections in X, Y, Z (text: "spin controls"; labels UNCONFIRMED) | `sections` [nx, ny, nz] | Number of blocks along each axis; planes evenly spaced | UNCONFIRMED (Fig. 154 appears to show three planes per axis, i.e. four sections; Fig. 155 shows three planes in X, i.e. four sections) | integers; minimum (suggest: 1 = no cut on that axis) and maximum UNCONFIRMED | §4.3; Fig. 154–155 (PDF p.87); blog: grid-cut |
| staggered (text: "a staggered cutting pattern"; label UNCONFIRMED) | `staggered` | Shift the X/Y planes in alternate Z sections | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: off) | Yes, No | §4.3; Fig. 154; blog: staggered-cut-pattern |
| "adjust plane" control (text) | `adjust_plane` | Picks one plane to move; it is drawn in red | UNCONFIRMED | a plane index; only available when not staggered | §4.3; Fig. 155; blog: flexible-grid-cut |
| position slider / text box (text) | `plane_positions_mm` | Position of the picked plane | evenly spaced | within the bounding box (UNCONFIRMED) | §4.3 |
| — (AD3D only) | `stagger_fraction` | Shift of alternate layers as a fraction of the cell size | n/a (suggest: 0.5) | 0–1 | AD3D proposal; Fig. 154 shows a shift of roughly half a cell (UNCONFIRMED) |
| — (AD3D only) | `stagger_axis` | Axis whose layers alternate | n/a (suggest: z, as LuBan) | x, y, z | AD3D proposal; §4.3 (LuBan staggers "in each Z section") |
| — (AD3D only) | `min_part_volume_mm3` (APP-VALIDATE key) | Merge cells smaller than this into a neighbour | from APP-VALIDATE (suggest: 50) | ≥ 0 | AD3D proposal; §4.5.2 (Tiny parts) |

- **Outputs:** One part per occupied cell, saved as for CUT-PLANAR; naming UNCONFIRMED. Parts can be browsed with Explode and Select (§4.3, Fig. 156).
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - The number of sections along X, Y and Z is set with spin controls (§4.3).
  - Staggered: "the cutting planes changes their positions in each Z section" (Fig. 154 caption).
  - "If staggering is not used, you can adjust the position of each cutting plane": pick a plane (shown in red), then move it with the slider or text box (§4.3, Fig. 155: "the middle cutting plane is repositioned"). Fig. 154 also shows one plane in dark red.
  - Grid cut was introduced as splitting "an object into equal-sized blocks" (blog: grid-cut), so the planes start evenly spaced.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - **Live readout.** Part count and largest-part size update while sections change, and any part larger than the bed (machine profile) is flagged. LuBan shows neither.
  - **Adjust planes in staggered mode too.** Per-layer offsets, and planes dragged directly in the viewport. LuBan allows adjustment only without staggering (§4.3).
  - **Flexible staggering.** Stagger on any axis by a chosen fraction; LuBan staggers per Z section only (§4.3).
  - **No slivers.** Planes are nudged away from thin necks and tiny slivers (research 08 §2.11), and specks merge into a neighbour instead of becoming Tiny parts (§4.5.2).
  - **"Grid to fit bed".** Picks section counts from the bed size, as a bridge to CUT-MODULAR.
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - Compute the plane positions. Cut Z slabs first, then each slab's X/Y planes, shifted for staggered layers.
  - Run the slabs in parallel with rayon, using manifold `SplitByPlane` and `Decompose()` (research 08 §1.4; PLAN §1).
- **Milestone:** M3 (part 9, after APP-ESTIMATE-PRINT), stretch goal: cheap once CUT-PLANAR exists, otherwise Later.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Labels, defaults and maximum section counts; the stagger shift; plane-position units.
  - Whether connectors apply to grid parts.

### CUT-RADIAL — Radial split (LuBan: Radial cut)

- **LuBan path:** Mesh → Cut, Method = Radial cut (§4.4, PDF p.88). Blog: radial-cut (2019-11-01): "Radially cut a 3D object." Video ahuRvQt3OqM "LuBan Radial cut" (3:07, title only).
- **What it makes:** Splits a model by "a set of radially arranged cutting planes" around an axis (§4.4; Fig. 157, a torus).
- **Fabrication:** Pie-slice parts for round objects such as rings, domes and vases.
- **Inputs:** A mesh.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| radial axis (text; Fig. 157 caption: "Radial cut direction") | `axis` | Axis the planes turn about | UNCONFIRMED | X, Y, Z | §4.4; Fig. 157 (PDF p.88) |
| "start angle" (Fig. 158 caption: "Start angle") | `start_angle_deg` | Rotates all planes about the axis | shown: 0 (Fig. 158 left) | degrees; Fig. 158 shows 0 and 10; range UNCONFIRMED | §4.4; Fig. 158 |
| "center X", "center Y" (text) | `center_norm` [x, y] | Radial centre, normalised to the bounding box | shown: (0, 0) (Fig. 159 left) | "normalized to [-0.5, 0.5]. Values beyond this range are valid" | §4.4; Fig. 159 shows (0, 0) and (−0.2, 0.2) |
| — (no count control is mentioned) | `sector_count` | How many sectors | UNCONFIRMED (Fig. 157–159 show three planes through the axis, i.e. six sectors) | UNCONFIRMED | Fig. 157–159 |
| — (AD3D only) | `center_mm` | The centre in mm, as an alternative to normalised values | n/a (suggest: bounding-box centre) | any | AD3D proposal |
| — (AD3D only) | `axis_dir` | Any axis direction, not only X/Y/Z | n/a (suggest: Z) | unit vector | AD3D proposal |
| — (AD3D only) | `sector_angles_deg` | Uneven sector angles | n/a (suggest: equal) | list summing to 360 | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** One part per sector (Fig. 159: six coloured parts); naming UNCONFIRMED.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Changing the start angle rotates the planes around the axis (§4.4).
  - "If a plane does not intersect with the bounding box of the object, it will not be shown" (§4.4).
  - Blog: radial-center-adjustment (2019-09-28): "Adjust the radial center of the Radial method." It predates blog: radial-cut, so it may describe another "Radial" method (UNCONFIRMED). Video BGaO2QMWJdg "LuBan Radial" (3:00, title only) is likewise unclear.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - **Direct placement.** Drag the centre in the viewport or type it in mm, with snaps to the bounding-box centre and the centroid. LuBan takes normalised numbers (§4.4).
  - **More control.** An explicit sector count, optional uneven sectors, and any axis direction.
  - **No hidden planes.** Planes that miss the model are drawn ghosted with a warning instead of hidden (§4.4).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Each sector is the mesh intersected with a wedge (two half-spaces), computed with manifold and run in parallel with rayon. Alternatively, successive `SplitByPlane` calls plus `Decompose()`.
- **Milestone:** M10 (part 9, first in its row). Cheap once CUT-PLANAR exists.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - The control for the number of planes; the default axis.
  - What "center X/Y" means when the axis is X or Y.
  - Whether the planes are full planes through the centre or half-planes from it.
  - Whether connectors apply.

### CUT-MODULAR — Cut to bed (LuBan: Modular cut)

- **LuBan path:** Mesh → Cut, Method = Modular cut (§4.5, PDF p.89). History:
  - **Up to 2019:** first documented as "Mesh -> LuBan, Method Module" (2019 blog posts), whose panel is "三维模块" ("3D module", CN Get started p.22–24, about 2018–2019). Circular beds were added 2019-02-12 (blog: printer-bed-shape).
  - **2021:** multi-printer mode (blog: multi-printer-modular-cut; video CX5Q9yAN0uU, title only).
  - **2023:** multi-threaded (blog: multi-thread-modular-cut).
  - **2024:** non-axial planes (blog: non-axial-cut; video q-opnBCkeZI, title only).
  - **2025:** fewer parts (blog: fewer-parts-of-the-modular-cut; video EuSTuybHofg, title only).
- **What it makes:** Cuts a model that is bigger than the build volume into parts that each fit a printer. The method "is not directly based on cutting planes but is based on the build volume of one or more 3D printers" (§4.5). Optional connectors (CUT-CONNECTOR), imprinted part numbers (CUT-LABEL) and an assembly-order file (CUT-SEQUENCE).
- **Fabrication:**
  - FDM parts printed separately, possibly on several printers in parallel (§4.5.1; paper CAD19), then joined with plugs, dowels or glue (§4.6).
  - A part may need a 90° turn about Z to fit (§4.5.2).
  - Example: a dragon of 138 × 163 × 259 mm on a 200 × 150 × 140 mm bed gave 5 parts (CN Get started p.22–24).
  - Larger examples: the 1.0 m, 129-part dragon, segmented with build volume as the criterion (CN Introduction p.22; paper CAD19), and the Fig. 148 castle (cut method not stated).
- **Inputs:**
  - One repaired mesh (CUT-REPAIR) at its target size (CUT-IMPORT).
  - Either one printer (single-printer mode) or a printer table (CUT-MULTIPRINTER).
- **Parameters:**
