- **Outputs:**
  - LuBan: nested sheets as DXF, SVG and SHP (§5 intro). The 2D views draw cut outlines red and labels and engrave lines black (Figs. 182, 187; CN-GS p.8); the manual states the same red-cut / black-engrave convention for wireframe exports (§5.10.1). Stack exports also contain per-layer assembly drawings, "Asm" (CN-GS p.10).
  - AD3D:
    - `sheets/sheet_001.svg` and `sheets/sheet_001.dxf` …, one pair per sheet, in mm (SVG width and height in mm; DXF header unit = millimetres).
    - `parts.csv`: label, sheet, position, rotation, area, cut length.
    - `assembly_guide.pdf`: layer-by-layer or rib-by-rib diagrams, label index, dowel and slot tables (PLAN §4 "PDF assembly guides").
    - `assembly.3mf`: every part as a named, watertight, extruded solid, with units (PLAN §4).
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - LuBan nesting (§5.2.5): "compact" packs as tightly as possible regardless of order; "ordered" keeps the default order, so the frames on each sheet have consecutive numbers; "balanced" is a compromise, with frames on a sheet not consecutive but less scattered than compact. Fig. 182 (PDF p.101) shows one sheet holding frames 10, 7, 9 and 8 side by side, all in the same orientation with their socket tabs on one long side, each number engraved in an empty corner (near the top for 10 and 7, near the bottom for 9 and 8). Each frame's tab reaches to, or almost to, the next frame's edge, so no part spacing is visible (observation at 300 dpi, not a stated rule).
  - When a Stack model is saved, all contours are nested on cut sheets and displayed in a 2D window; the 2D label size is fixed; labels are meant to be engraved so parts can be found during assembly (§5.3.3).
  - The 2019 nested sheet "Sheet_1.shp" (CN-GS p.8; observations, not stated rules): the parts are packed in a narrow strip along one sheet edge with outlines touching or nearly touching; parts and labels are turned to any angle; a small part sits inside the hole of ring part 1.1; outlines are red on a grey fill.
  - LuBan's tolerance advice, given outside §5: no value suits every setup, so find one by trial and error; start printed fits at −0.2 mm; if parts are too tight, reduce the tolerance (0.2 → 0.1 mm, or −0.2 → −0.3 mm), and if too loose, increase it; once found, "you can probably use it in all LuBan functions that require a tolerance" (§3.2.7, §3.9.6).
  - The research behind LuBan describes its packing as: sort the polygons from largest to smallest and put the largest on a sheet first; numbering starts at the bottom front, rises with elevation, then runs left to right (papers/Sass-2025, Stage 3; research 04 §A.8).
  - AD3D rule (research 08 §2.6): offset every cut path by `kerf`/2 — outer outlines outward; holes, slots and dowel holes inward. Engrave paths, guides and labels are never offset.
  - AD3D rule: as-cut slot width = `sheet_thickness_measured` + `fit_allowance`; the drawn slot width is that minus `kerf` (research 08 §2.6).
  - AD3D rule: `part_spacing` ≥ `kerf` (laser) or ≥ `tool_diameter` (router); no part crosses `sheet_margin`; every part must fit a sheet in an allowed rotation, or the form splits it (FORM-STACK, FORM-WAFFLE) or reports which part is too big.
  - AD3D rule (ours): the stock sheet must fit `machine_bed` in some orientation; export is blocked otherwise. On the owner's machines a 2440 × 1220 board fits both the 3015 (3000 × 1500) and the 1325 (1300 × 2500, turned lengthwise) (START_HERE bed classes; the board size is an example, not the owner's confirmed stock).
  - AD3D rule (ours, router): every drawn slot, finger notch and square dowel hole must be wider than `tool_diameter`, or the bit cannot enter it; export is blocked with the offending parts listed, and the fix offered is a smaller bit or a thicker sheet. Example: a 3 mm plywood slot cannot be cut with a 3.175 mm bit at all.
  - AD3D rule (ours, router): with `tool_compensation` = cam the SVG/DXF carry the finished part outlines on separate inside-cut and outside-cut layers, so the CAM program knows which side of each line the bit runs on; with ad3d the paths are already offset by `tool_diameter` / 2 and the file says so in its layer names.
  - AD3D rule: when `corner_relief` is not none, every inside corner of a slot, finger notch or square dowel hole gets a relief of `tool_diameter` (research 08 §2.7). Free outlines such as ring interiors keep the bit's natural radius.
  - AD3D rule (ours): labels are single-stroke paths inside their part, anchored at a pole of inaccessibility, never crossing a cut path or hole, with at least 1 mm clearance (research 04 §B.13). If no spot fits the minimum `label_height_2d`, engrave a short code and list it in `parts.csv`.
  - AD3D rule (ours): within each part, inner cuts are written before its outer cut so parts do not drop or shift before they are finished.
  - AD3D rule: nesting is seeded and deterministic, so re-exporting an unchanged project gives the same sheets (PLAN §1 "Generators are pure and deterministic").
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Kerf, measured thickness and fit are three separate inputs, set once per machine and material and applied to every form, instead of one signed Tolerance per panel that only changes slot width (research 08 §2.6; §5.4.1). LuBan's own advice is to find one tolerance by trial and reuse it everywhere (§3.2.7); the profile does that automatically. No tolerance at all is documented for Stack (§5.3) and the 2019 Stack panel has none (CN-GS p.6).
  - A fit-test comb (slots stepping from t − 0.3 to t + 0.3 mm in 0.05 mm steps) to calibrate `kerf` and `fit_allowance` before a big job (research 07 §e.4 "a generator for test coupons"; research 00 §6).
  - Configurable, auto-fitted 2D label size; LuBan's is fixed (§5.3.3).
  - True-shape nesting with parts in holes, grain lock, margins and multiple sheets, plus a utilisation report; LuBan's three order modes are kept as policies (§5.2.5; research 08 §2.9).
  - CNC dogbones or T-bones and tool compensation driven by the profile's tool diameter, plus a hard check that the bit fits every slot. The manual mentions neither; its only CNC advice is to make toolpaths in external CAM software such as MasterCAM (§5.6), and research 08 §2.7 says LuBan has a Draw → Toolpath function that the manual does not document. This matters for the owner's 1325 router: without dogbones, router-cut waffle parts will not assemble (research 08 §2.7).
  - Sheets sized from the owner's real machines (3015 laser, 1325 router) and the stock actually loaded, checked against the bed, instead of LuBan's bare width/height boxes, whose screenshots show 600 × 450 and 800 × 400 sheets (CN-GS p.6; Fig. 172). On sheets that large one nest often holds a whole model, so the "ordered" policy and the parts list keep assembly manageable.
  - Spacing that knows the tool: LuBan's 2019 sheet and Fig. 182 show parts touching (CN-GS p.8; Fig. 182), which a laser tolerates but a router bit of several millimetres does not; AD3D spaces router parts by at least the bit diameter (research 08 §2.6–2.7).
  - A thickness check across the whole sheet, because the owner's machines take full-size boards and research 08 §2.6 reports that nominal 3 mm plywood runs 2.7–3.2 mm.
  - Separate cut, engrave and guide layers in both SVG and DXF, in mm, ready for laser software (PLAN §4); LuBan documents a colour convention only (§5.10.1).
  - One PDF assembly guide instead of loose per-layer drawings (PLAN §4; CN-GS p.10).
  - SVG and DXF streamed to disk part by part, so a 30,000-part job (CN-IN p.9) never sits in memory as one document (CLAUDE.md speed rules).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - Offsets and polygon booleans: Clipper2 (BSL-1.0) through the `clipper2` crate, or pure-Rust `i_overlay` (PLAN §1; research 03 §13).
  - Nesting: jagua-rs (MPL-2.0, Rust, has bin packing) or a wrapper around sparrow (MIT, strip packing only); packingsolver (MIT, C++); no-fit-polygon search as in SVGnest (MIT) or `@deepnest/calculate-nfp` (MIT); greedy first-fit-decreasing (papers/Sass-2025) and skyline packing for very large jobs (research 03 §12; research 08 §1.3, §2.9). deepnest.js is GPLv3, allowed for personal use (CLAUDE.md) but not needed.
  - Label anchor: pole of inaccessibility (mapbox/polylabel, ISC) (research 00 §3). Font: single-stroke Hershey data, keeping its attribution notice (research 08 §2.13).
  - Our own SVG and DXF writers (research 07 §a).
  - Validation, as randomised property tests (CLAUDE.md; PLAN §5): every exported part is a closed, non-self-intersecting polygon set with outer loops counter-clockwise and holes clockwise; no two nested parts overlap after spacing; every part lies inside its sheet minus the margin; every label lies inside its part and clear of cut paths; every slot's as-cut width equals the rule above.
- **Milestone:** M4 (part 9, after FORM-WORKSPACE; PLAN §3).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - LuBan's default sheet size and thickness, and whether they depend on the unit or model size.
  - Whether LuBan compensates kerf on part outlines at all; no source says so.
  - LuBan's part spacing, sheet margin and rotation rules (CN-GS p.8 shows parts and labels at mixed rotations and outlines touching), and whether parts are always nested inside holes.
  - How "balanced" is computed.
  - LuBan's DXF layer names and colours for Contour, Stack, Hash and Plate; only the wireframe red/black convention is stated (§5.10.1).
  - The fixed 2D label height and the font LuBan uses.
  - Owner side (START_HERE): whether the 3015 is a CO2 or a fiber laser; its measured kerf per material; the stock sheet sizes actually used on each machine; the router's spindle, bits and CAM program (which decides `tool_compensation` and `hold_tabs`).

#### FORM-ENCASE — Encase shell (LuBan: Cocoon)

- **LuBan path:** Mesh → LuBan, Method = Cocoon (manual §5.1, PDF p.97). Blog: cocoon (2020-12-11: "Generate an outer surface of a 3D model."). Video XHy9W0Ifpuo "LuBan Cocoon" (title only). Possible forerunner: "Mesh -> Box" (blog: mesh-box-update, 2020-05-10: "Add cylindrical and spherical box shapes in addition to a cubic box."), which is not in the 2018 Mesh menu, so it was added between 2018 and 2020 (luban-docs Get started p.3, via luban-docs notes §2.3). Our reading: an enclosing shape around the model; what it produced is UNCONFIRMED.
- **What it makes:** A new hollow model: an outer surface (cube, cylinder, sphere, or a "native" offset of the model) around the original, whose inner surface is the original model (§5.1, §5.1.2). Printed in clear resin and polished, the model appears suspended inside a transparent block (§5.1; Fig. 173, PDF p.97: a non-cubic rectangular block holding a head, and a green sphere, both by LuBan user Tom Lewis).
- **Fabrication:** 3D printing. The manual's use case: print in clear resin, then polish the outer surface until it is transparent (§5.1). It is also the starting point for a two-part mold (§5.1.4 → FORM-ENCASE-MOLD). The owner's only listed printer is the FDM Creality CR-6 SE, 235 × 235 × 250 mm (START_HERE); whether a resin printer is available, and whether an FDM print can give the clear-block effect, is UNCONFIRMED, so for the owner the mold use and opaque display shells may matter more than the clear block.
- **Inputs:** one mesh (FORM-WORKSPACE); its model size sets the inner surface (§5.1.2).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shape (section title "Shape and Direction") | `shell_shape` | Type of outer surface. | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: cube) | cube, cylinder, sphere, native (follows the model); AD3D adds rounded box, ellipsoid, capsule, custom mesh (ours) | §5.1.1 (PDF p.97); Fig. 174 |
| Direction | `cylinder_axis` | Axis of the cylinder. | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: Z) | X, Y, Z; only when Shape = cylinder | §5.1.1; Fig. 174 second row |
| Clearance | `clearance` | Shortest distance between the outer and inner surfaces; a larger value gives a bigger cocoon, while the inner surface stays at the model size. | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 5 mm) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: ≥ 0 mm); Fig. 175 shows 0, 5 and 10, with no unit given | §5.1.2 (PDF p.98); Fig. 175 |
| Offset X | `shell_offset_x` | Shifts the outer surface from its default position along X. | UNCONFIRMED (Fig. 176 left shows 0) | signed (Fig. 176 shows −5 and 10); unit not stated (presumably the model unit, UNCONFIRMED) | §5.1.3 (PDF p.98); Fig. 176 |
| Offset Y | `shell_offset_y` | As X, along Y. | UNCONFIRMED (Fig. 176 shows 0 throughout) | presumably signed like X; unit not stated (UNCONFIRMED) | §5.1.3; Fig. 176 |
| Offset Z | `shell_offset_z` | As X, along Z. | UNCONFIRMED (Fig. 176 left shows 0) | signed; Fig. 176 shows 5; unit not stated (UNCONFIRMED) | §5.1.3; Fig. 176 |
| Model size X / Y / Z | `model_size_*` (FORM-WORKSPACE) | Fixes the size of the inner surface. | — | aspect-locked | §5.1.2; §5 intro |
| — (AD3D only) | `fit_mode` | How the default shell is placed and sized. | min_enclosing (suggest) | bbox_center, min_enclosing (smallest sphere or circle), oriented_box | ours; §5.1.3 |
| — (AD3D only) | `min_wall` | Thinnest allowed wall between model and shell; anything thinner is shown and blocks export unless overridden. | 1.0 mm (suggest) | ≥ 0 mm | ours; §5.1.3; Fig. 175 left |
| — (AD3D only) | `output_bodies` | One solid with a cavity, or two bodies (shell and figure) for two-material printing. | one_solid (suggest) | one_solid, shell_and_figure | ours; PLAN §4 (3MF with multiple parts) |
| — (AD3D only) | `drain_holes` | Drain or vent holes from the cavity to the outside, for resin printing. | 0 (suggest) | count 0–4; diameter mm | ours |
| — (AD3D only) | `native_cell_mm` | Voxel size of the native offset. | auto: coarse while dragging, fine on release (suggest) | > 0 mm | ours; §5.1.1 |

- **Outputs:** LuBan: STL or OBJ for printing, plus the FGD/FGS scene; the Measure section shows the size of the generated model (§5 intro). AD3D: one closed solid with two shells — the outer surface with normals out, and the model surface reversed with normals into the cavity — as binary STL and 3MF; or, with `output_bodies` = shell_and_figure, two named bodies in one 3MF.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - "The native shape requires much longer processing time than the rest" (§5.1.1).
  - The cylinder's centre axis can be parallel to X, Y or Z (§5.1.1; Fig. 174).
  - Clearance is the shortest distance from outer to inner surface; increasing it enlarges the cocoon; the inner surface is fixed to the model size (§5.1.2). At clearance 0 the shell touches the model (Fig. 175 left: the trunk reaches the cylinder), which means a zero-thickness wall at the contact points. In Fig. 175 the cylinder grows in length as well as radius as the clearance rises, so the clearance also applies at the end caps (observation).
  - In Fig. 176 left, at offset (0, 0, 0), the figure's raised hand already almost touches the sphere, which is the misalignment the offsets are meant to fix (observation).
  - Offsets move the outer surface for cases where "the default position may not visually align the outer and inter surfaces" (verbatim, §5.1.3); a user offset can make the two surfaces intersect (Fig. 176 right: at (10, 0, 0) part of the model pokes through the sphere).
  - AD3D rule (ours): primitives are sized so the smallest gap equals `clearance`. Box: the model's bounding box grown by `clearance` on every side. Sphere: smallest enclosing sphere (or bounding-box-centred, per `fit_mode`), radius + `clearance`. Cylinder: smallest enclosing circle of the projection along `cylinder_axis`, radius + `clearance`, height = extent + 2 × `clearance`. Native: offset surface at distance `clearance`. Then apply `shell_offset_*`.
  - AD3D rule: the result passes `validate()` (closed, edge-manifold, consistent winding, no degenerate triangles) with exactly two shells (PLAN §1). If the thinnest wall is below `min_wall`, show a wall-thickness heatmap and block export unless overridden.
  - AD3D rule (ours): the Measure panel compares the shell's size with the printer profile's build volume (235 × 235 × 250 mm for the CR-6 SE, START_HERE) and offers to scale it down, or to split it with Mesh Cut (M3), when it does not fit. LuBan's Measure shows the size only (§5 intro).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - The native offset is a multi-core narrow-band signed-distance computation with a coarse preview and a cancellable fine pass; LuBan warns it takes "much longer" (§5.1.1; PLAN §4).
  - Offsets are dragged with a gizmo while a live min-wall heatmap shows where the surfaces get close; intersection is flagged instead of silently allowed (§5.1.3; PLAN §4 live preview).
  - Smallest-enclosing sphere and cylinder and an oriented-box fit save resin and fix the "default position may not visually align" problem at the source (§5.1.3).
  - A two-body 3MF (figure plus clear shell) for two-material FDM, which LuBan's STL/OBJ export cannot carry (§5 intro; PLAN §4). Whether the owner's CR-6 SE can print two materials is UNCONFIRMED (START_HERE gives no extruder details).
  - A build-volume check against the printer profile, so a shell that will not fit the CR-6 SE is caught before export; LuBan only reports the size (§5 intro).
  - Optional drain and vent holes for resin printing (ours; the manual says nothing about the sealed cavity).
  - A transparent-material preview of the polished block (PLAN §4 realistic preview).
  - Watertight by construction, proven by property tests with random shape, clearance and offset values (CLAUDE.md).
  - One generator covers both Cocoon and the older Mesh → Box shapes (cube, cylinder, sphere), so there is no second enclosing-shape tool. LuBan has both a Mesh-menu Box and the Cocoon method (blog: mesh-box-update; §5.1).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** repair the input first (M3). Primitive fits: Welzl's smallest enclosing sphere or circle (ours). Native: signed-distance offset (research 04 §B.15 "SDF offset (cocoon, mold)") using a generalized winding-number inside test (libigl, MPL-2.0) on a sparse grid plus marching cubes, or manifold's `levelSet` (research 08 §2.10), or OpenVDB (research 07 §e.1; licence UNCONFIRMED there). Cavity: boolean difference of shell minus model with manifold (Apache-2.0). Prior use: the CAD'19 mold study used "one of the LuBan features [that] supports expanding the model's thickness by a predefined value" and subtracted the original to get a one-piece mold (papers/CAD19, case study 1).
- **Milestone:** M11 (part 9, first in its row). PLAN §3 does not list Cocoon by name; it is part of CLAUDE.md build order step 5, "the rest of the manual".
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Default shape, clearance, offsets and cylinder axis.
  - Whether "cube" is a true cube or a box with the model's proportions: Fig. 173 left shows a clearly non-cubic block.
  - How the default position and size are computed (bounding-box centre, centroid, smallest enclosing sphere?).
  - Offset units (presumably mm).
  - Whether clearance 0 is allowed to produce a zero-thickness wall, and how the native offset distance is defined.
  - Whether LuBan exports one solid or separate shells, and whether the cavity is sealed.
  - Owner side: whether a resin printer is available, and whether the CR-6 SE has more than one extruder (START_HERE lists neither).
  - Exact panel labels: "Shape", "Direction", "Clearance" and "Offset X/Y/Z" are inferred from the §5.1 section titles.
  - What Mesh → Box produces and whether it still exists (blog: mesh-box-update; no matching video title).

#### FORM-ENCASE-MOLD — Two-part casting mold from the shell (LuBan: Cocoon → Mold workflow)

- **LuBan path:** Mesh → LuBan, Method = Cocoon, then Mesh → Cut → Planar cut to split the cocoon in half (§5.1.4, PDF p.98; §4.2). Videos oNQARGHis8s "Mold making", 3qNtXBbKUfI "LuBan Mold" and aQl8_1Gl79U "LuBan Mesh Cut" (titles only). LuBan's newer separate Mold method (blog: _mold, 2026-05-26: "Generate a mold model from a 3D model.") is not in the manual and needs its own entry elsewhere in the spec.
- **What it makes:** A two-part mold. The cocoon is split by a plane; a liquid ("some solution") is injected into the hollow, left to settle, and the mold is opened to take out the cast (§5.1.4; Fig. 177, PDF p.99: mold halves for lips and a torso, with their casts, by LuBan user Picco Balla).
- **Fabrication:** 3D print both halves (inferred: the cocoon is a printed model, §5.1). §5.1.4 names no casting material ("some solution"); Fig. 177 shows a red lips cast and a flesh-coloured torso cast without naming the material, and the CAD'19 mold study cast silicone (papers/CAD19, case study 1). AD3D targets silicone, resin, wax or plaster (ours).
- **Inputs:** a FORM-ENCASE result, or the model plus shell parameters.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Planar cut plane A, B, C, D (in Mesh → Cut) | `parting_plane` | Plane Ax + By + Cz + D = 0 that splits the shell. | UNCONFIRMED | set "through text boxes or sliders" | §4.2; research 04 §B.7 (plane equation) |
| Close cut | — (always closed) | Close the cut section so each half is a solid. | Yes ("Be default, LuBan will close a cut section", verbatim) | Yes, No | §4.2.2 |
| Cut (button, "at the bottom of the control panel") | — (AD3D: the split is part of the generator) | Splits the model; each part is saved as an individual STL file in a selected folder. | — | — | §4.2 |
| — (AD3D only) | `parting_mode` | Automatic plane (largest silhouette, fewest undercuts) or manual gizmo. | auto (suggest) | auto, manual | ours |
| — (AD3D only) | `key_count` | Registration keys on the parting face. | 4 (suggest) | 0–8 | ours |
| — (AD3D only) | `key_shape` | Key form. | cone (suggest) | cone, hemisphere, square | ours |
| — (AD3D only) | `key_size` | Key base diameter or side. | 6 mm (suggest) | > 0 mm | ours |
| — (AD3D only) | `key_fit_allowance` | Clearance between key and socket. | 0.2 mm (suggest; §3.2.7 advises starting printed fits at a LuBan tolerance of −0.2 mm) | signed mm | ours; §3.2.7 |
| — (AD3D only) | `sprue_diameter` | Pour channel from the cavity to the outside. | 6 mm (suggest) | > 0 mm | ours; §5.1.4 ("Inject some solution") |
| — (AD3D only) | `vent_count`, `vent_diameter` | Air vents at the cavity's high points. | 2 and 2 mm (suggest) | count, mm | ours |
| — (AD3D only) | `clamp_holes` | Bolt holes through both halves. | 0 (suggest) | count, diameter | ours |

- **Outputs:** LuBan: each part after cutting is saved as an individual STL in a chosen folder (§4.2). AD3D: `mold_a` and `mold_b` as named bodies in one 3MF, plus one STL each.
- **Behaviour and rules:** LuBan leaves the cut to the user and documents no keys, pour hole or vents (§5.1.4). Fig. 177 shows round holes near the corners of one mold half; their purpose is not stated. AD3D rule (ours): both halves pass `validate()` and each must fit the printer profile's build volume (235 × 235 × 250 mm for the owner's CR-6 SE, START_HERE), laid parting-face down; keys never break into the cavity (wall ≥ `min_wall`); the sprue enters the cavity at its lowest point for the chosen pour direction, vents at its highest.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - One click from shell to finished two-part mold with keys, sprue and vents, instead of a manual planar cut with none of them (§5.1.4).
  - Undercut check: faces that would lock the cast in either half are highlighted, and more parts can be made by recursive segmentation until no inner-surface overhang is left, as in LuBan's own research (papers/CAD19 case study: a naive 216-part split still had overhangs; recursion gave 17 parts).
  - Live preview of the parting plane, keys and sprue (PLAN §4).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** manifold split-by-plane, `decompose()` and booleans (research 08 §2.11; research 00 §3); undercut test from face normals against the pull direction (ours); CAD'19 recursion (research 04 §B.12).
- **Milestone:** M11 (part 9, after FORM-ENCASE). With FORM-MOLD.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:** what the holes in Fig. 177 are (keys, bolts?); whether LuBan's newer Mold method replaces this workflow; which casting materials the author recommends.

#### FORM-ETCHED — Etched slice display (LuBan: Contour)

- **LuBan path:** Mesh → LuBan, Method = Contour (§5.2, PDF p.99). Blog: contour (2019-06-09: "Turn a 3D mesh into a set of 2D contours, which can be laser engraved on transparent sheets, giving a 3D perspective effect."). Video c44s9Hp_I6Y "LuBan Contour" (title only).
- **What it makes:** One transparent sheet per 2D section of the model. Every sheet is cut to the same frame outline and engraved with its section; stacked and lit, the engraved lines scatter the light and the viewer sees the 3D model (§5.2; Fig. 178, PDF p.99: a sphere's contours in a lit base).
- **Fabrication:** laser: engrave the section lines, cut the frame (§5.2). Sheets stand back to back or with gaps (§5.2.1) in a base light whose socket takes a tab at the bottom of each frame (§5.2.4; Fig. 178 right). The manual says "transparent sheet"; it does not name acrylic. Owner: this form needs a laser that engraves and cuts clear sheet. Whether the 3015 can is UNCONFIRMED until its type is known (header note); the 1325 router can cut frames but engraving section lines would need a V-bit pass (ours), so the router is a fallback, not the target.
- **Inputs:** one mesh.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sheet width | `sheet_width` | X size of the sheet stock; "should be larger than the size of a contour frame", because Contour, unlike Stack, does not segment frames (implied by §5.3). | UNCONFIRMED | > frame width | §5.2.1 (PDF p.99); §5.3 |
| Sheet height | `sheet_height` | Y size of the sheet stock; must be larger than one frame. | UNCONFIRMED | > frame height | §5.2.1 |
| Sheet thickness | `layer_pitch` | In LuBan this "thickness" is the gap between adjacent sheets, i.e. the slice pitch: equal to the real thickness → sheets back to back; larger → gaps between sheets. | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: = `sheet_thickness_measured`) | LuBan: UNCONFIRMED (§5.2.1 covers equal and larger values only). AD3D: ≥ `sheet_thickness_measured` (ours) | §5.2.1 |
| — (AD3D only) | `sheet_thickness_measured` | Real material thickness (FORM-SHEETS), kept separate from the pitch. | user | > 0 mm | research 08 §2.6 |
| Direction | `slice_axis` | Normal of the contour planes. Any other direction needs a pre-rotation with Object → Transform. | UNCONFIRMED | X, Y, Z | §5.2.2 (PDF p.99); Fig. 179 (PDF p.100) |
| — (AD3D only) | `slice_direction` | Any direction, set with a gizmo (vector or yaw/pitch). | = Z (suggest) | unit vector | ours; §5.2.2 |
| Frame | `frame_shape` | Outline shared by every sheet. | UNCONFIRMED | "Several frame shapes": rectangle (Figs. 179, 181, 182), pentagon, hexagon, circle (Fig. 180). AD3D adds rounded rectangle, n-gon, ellipse, silhouette offset and custom SVG (ours) | §5.2.3 (PDF p.100); Figs. 179–182 |
| Clearance ("boundary clearance" in the text) | `frame_clearance` | Shortest distance from the frame to the set of contours; larger → larger frame; contour size stays fixed by the model size. | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 10 mm) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: ≥ 0 mm); Fig. 180 shows 0, 5 and 10, with no unit given | §5.2.3; Fig. 180 |
| Base light socket | `base_tab` | Check box: adds an extended region at the bottom of each frame that plugs into the socket of a base light. | UNCONFIRMED | on, off | §5.2.4 (PDF p.100); Fig. 181 |
| (socket width, "w" in Fig. 181; on-screen label UNCONFIRMED) | `base_tab_width` | Width of that region ("user specified"). | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: > 0 mm, ≤ frame width) | §5.2.4; Fig. 181 |
| (socket height, "h" in Fig. 181; on-screen label UNCONFIRMED) | `base_tab_height` | Height of that region ("user specified"). | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: > 0 mm) | §5.2.4; Fig. 181 |
| Nesting | `nesting_mode` | Frame order on the cut sheets (FORM-SHEETS). | UNCONFIRMED | compact, ordered, balanced | §5.2.5 (PDF p.101); Fig. 182 |
| — (AD3D only) | `engrave_style` | How a section is engraved. | outline (suggest) | outline, outline + hatch, filled | ours; Fig. 182 shows outlines only |
| — (AD3D only) | `engrave_face` | Engrave the front face, or the back face mirrored so the front stays glossy. | back_mirrored (suggest) | front, back_mirrored | ours |
| — (AD3D only) | `frame_marks` | Engraved sheet number plus an orientation mark (corner notch or arrow). | on (suggest) | on, off | ours; Fig. 182 shows numbers |
| — (AD3D only) | `holder` | Also generate the base: slots at `layer_pitch`, sized from the measured thickness and `fit_allowance`, with an LED channel; 3D-printed (3MF) or laser-cut. | off (suggest) | off, printed, laser | ours; §5.2.4 |
| — (AD3D only) | `depth_cue` | Vary engrave line weight or hatch density with depth. | off (suggest) | off, weight, density | ours |
| — (AD3D only) | `min_loop_length` | Drop section loops shorter than this (mesh noise). | 2 mm (suggest) | ≥ 0 mm | ours |

- **Outputs:** LuBan: frames nested on cut sheets, saved as DXF, SVG and SHP (§5 intro); in Fig. 182 the frame outline is red (cut) and the section lines and a large frame number are black (engrave). AD3D: per-sheet SVG and DXF with CUT_OUTER (frame and tab), ENGRAVE_LINE (sections), ENGRAVE_TEXT (number and mark); optional holder as 3MF/STL or as extra sheets; a stacking guide in the PDF; `parts.csv`.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Sheets must be larger than a frame (§5.2.1): Contour never splits a frame, unlike Stack (§5.3).
  - Sheet thickness doubles as the gap between sheets (§5.2.1).
  - Direction is X, Y or Z; any other direction needs Object → Transform first (§5.2.2).
  - The frame grows with the clearance; the contours are fixed by the model size (§5.2.3). All frames in a stack are identical in Figs. 179–181.
  - Base light socket: an extended region at the bottom of a frame; its width and height are user-set (§5.2.4).
  - Nesting modes as in FORM-SHEETS (§5.2.5). In Fig. 182 one sheet holds frames 10, 7, 9 and 8 side by side in the same orientation, with tabs on one long side. The numbers 7–10 fit the ordered option, but the caption does not say which mode made the sheet.
  - AD3D rule (ours): slice planes sit at `z_min + (i + 0.5) × layer_pitch` along `slice_direction`. The frame is `frame_shape` sized to enclose the union of all sections offset by `frame_clearance`, so every sheet is identical; the tab sits at the same place on every frame so all tabs line up in the holder.
  - AD3D rule: frame and tab outlines get the kerf offset; engraved lines and numbers do not (research 08 §2.6). Tab width and thickness fit the holder slot through `fit_allowance`, and holder slots use `sheet_thickness_measured`, because clear sheet also varies from its nominal thickness (UNCONFIRMED for acrylic; research 08 §2.6 measures plywood only).
  - AD3D rule (ours): engraved lines are closed and simplified (Douglas–Peucker, tolerance ≤ 0.05 mm); a section that enters the frame's clearance band is an error.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - A live preview that simulates the base light — glowing lines in a dark, transparent stack, with parallax as you orbit — instead of orange wireframes (Figs. 178–180; PLAN §4 realistic preview).
  - Any slicing direction from a gizmo, without a separate transform step (§5.2.2).
  - Pitch and real material thickness are separate inputs, so gaps, holder slots and spacers come out exact; LuBan's one "thickness" field means both (§5.2.1).
  - AD3D generates the holder itself, sized to the measured sheet, while LuBan only adds a tab for a base light bought elsewhere (§5.2.4).
  - More frame shapes, including a silhouette-following outline and custom SVG; the manual offers "several" (§5.2.3).
  - Numbers plus orientation marks on every sheet and a stacking order in the PDF guide, so sheets go in the right way round (Fig. 182 shows numbers only).
  - Identical frames are packed by exact grid tiling, trying a 180° turn of alternate frames when it lets the tabs interlock, with general nesting only for leftovers (ours; Fig. 182 tiles frames side by side).
  - Optional depth cueing (`depth_cue`) (ours).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** research 04 §B.3 ("Slice into contours, engrave each on a transparent sheet inside a frame shape with clearance, add an optional base light-socket tab, and nest"). Plane slicing with segment chaining (manifold cross-sections or our own slicer; research 03 §13), parallel over planes with rayon; Clipper2 for union and offset; regular-polygon and ellipse frame fits (ours); FORM-SHEETS for nesting and export. Validation (property tests): every section lies inside its frame minus the clearance; all frames identical; all tabs aligned; random direction, pitch and clearance values.
- **Milestone:** M4 (part 9, after FORM-STACK; PLAN §3; research 00 §3 rates it about 1 developer-week).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - All defaults: no Contour panel screenshot exists in the sources.
  - The full frame-shape list, and how polygon or circle frames are sized (bounding box or best fit).
  - Where the socket sits along the bottom edge (Fig. 181 suggests near the middle) and any limits on its width and height.
  - Whether section lines are simplified or offset, and the cut/engrave colour mapping of Contour exports (inferred from Fig. 182 and §5.10.1).
  - Where the first slice plane sits and how many sheets a given thickness produces.
  - Size and placement rule of the engraved frame numbers, and whether any control (e.g. a Text size) sets them: Fig. 182 shows large numbers, each in an empty corner of its frame, but no source names a control.
  - Owner side: whether the 3015 laser can engrave and cut clear sheet (depends on CO2 versus fiber, START_HERE open question 1).

#### FORM-STACK — Layer stack (LuBan: Stack)

- **LuBan path:** Mesh → LuBan, Method = Stack (§5.3, PDF p.101). 2019 deck: 一维切片 "1D slicing" (CN-GS p.5, p.6, p.11). Video Cfz6fh0bLI8 "LuBan Stack" (title only). Research lineage: "1D contouring" (papers/CAD16), the CAD'15 sub-plane work (papers/CAD15) and MIT DDF "LuBan Stacking" (research 04 §A).
- **What it makes:** The model sliced into parallel layers. Each layer's sections become flat parts — optionally hollow rings — with hidden square holes for alignment dowels. Sections bigger than the sheet are split into segments. Parts are labelled, nested on sheets and glued back into the shape (§5.3; papers/CAD16: "Assembly is achieved by sticking adjacent contours").
- **Fabrication:**
  - Laser-cut (or CNC-cut) sheet; the examples are plywood and cardboard (Figs. 183–184, PDF pp.101–102; CN-GS p.11; CN-IN p.8).
  - Dowels of "any feasible material, such as wood or metal" fill the holes for alignment (§5.3.1); layers are glued (papers/CAD16).
  - LuBan also writes an STL folder for 3D printing (CN-GS p.10).
  - Owner (START_HERE): plywood or cardboard on the 3015 laser if it is a CO2 machine (UNCONFIRMED), otherwise on the 1325 router, which can also take thicker boards for large stacks with fewer layers (ours). With full-size boards on either machine, segmentation (§5.3) only triggers for big models; the 2019 example used a 600 × 450 sheet (CN-GS p.6).
  - Scale: a "3-meter long" triceratops (Fig. 184); a triceratops captioned "1,200 层, 30,000 部件, 3.6*1.8*1.6米" = 1,200 layers, 30,000 parts, 3.6 × 1.8 × 1.6 m (CN-IN p.9), apparently the same model, so the two sources disagree on its length; a 5,425-part bust (papers/CAD16).
- **Inputs:** one mesh.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sheet width; 2019: 板材宽度 | `sheet_width` | Sheet X size; may be smaller than a section, which is then split. | UNCONFIRMED (CN-GS p.6: 600) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: > 0 mm); may be smaller than a contour (§5.3) | §5.3; CN-GS p.6 |
| Sheet height; 2019: 板材长度 "sheet length" | `sheet_height` | Sheet Y size. | UNCONFIRMED (CN-GS p.6: 450) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: > 0 mm) | §5.3; CN-GS p.6 |
| Sheet thickness; 2019: 板材厚度 | `sheet_thickness_measured` → `layer_pitch` | Material thickness. The manual does not say what it controls in Stack; AD3D uses the measured value as the layer pitch so the stack keeps the model's height (ours). | UNCONFIRMED (CN-GS p.6: 5) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: > 0 mm) | CN-GS p.6; research 08 §2.6 |
| Direction | `slice_axis` / `slice_direction` | Stacking axis, as in Contour. The 2019 Stack panel has no direction control (CN-GS p.6). | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: Z) | LuBan: X, Y, Z; AD3D: any direction | §5.3 ("exactly the same as those of the contour method"); §5.2.2; CN-GS p.6 |

| Text size | `label_height_3d` | Size of the 3D labels in the viewport. The 2019 Stack panel has no text-size control (CN-GS p.6). | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: > 0; unit UNCONFIRMED) | §5.3.3 (PDF p.102); Fig. 187 left; CN-GS p.6 |

| — (AD3D only) | `slice_phase` | Where each layer samples the model. | middle (suggest) | bottom, middle, top, inner (smaller of the two faces), outer (larger) | ours |

- **Outputs:**
  - LuBan: on save, all contours are nested on cut sheets and shown in a 2D window (§5.3.3); laser files in DXF, SVG and SHP (§5 intro). The export folder holds Cut (DXF, SHP), Asm (one assembly drawing per layer, DXF and SHP), STL, `Asm3D.dxf/.fgd/.fgs` and `Readme.txt` (CN-GS p.10). The 2019 sheet view shows grey parts with red outlines and engraved labels such as "1.1", "2.1", "3.1", "4.1", "5.2" (CN-GS p.8).
  - AD3D: sheets in SVG and DXF (FORM-SHEETS); `parts.csv`; `dowels.csv` (one row per dowel run: position, first and last layer, length = layers × pitch − end clearance); `assembly_guide.pdf` (per layer group: outline, labels, dowel positions); `assembly.3mf` (every part an extruded, named, watertight solid, also printable).

- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - LuBan:
    - Stack slices like Contour but adds alignment dowels "that are invisible on the surface of a model" (§5.3).
    - The sheet can be smaller than a contour: LuBan "will automatically segment a large contour into smaller parts" so a small laser cutter can make them (§5.3; Fig. 184).
    - Dowel holes are square and user-sized; a value roughly above 1/3 of the smallest contour dimension prevents the holes (§5.3.1). Fig. 185 (PDF p.102) highlights one layer in each of its two views, each with a single square hole near the middle; the translucent layers above show holes in line with it.
    - The 2019 duck preview and photo show a hole in the top layer of the head (CN-GS p.11; CN-IN p.8), although §5.3 says the dowels are invisible on the surface. Whether that hole is a dowel hole is UNCONFIRMED.
    - Contours are rings with a hollow interior, which saves material and weight; a ring width larger than the model gives solid contours (§5.3.2).
    - Labels such as "2.1" or "10.3.4" read layer.contour[.segment]; a layer may hold several contours; the third number appears when a contour larger than the sheet is split into segments (§5.3.3). The 3D label size is set by Text size; the 2D label size cannot be changed; labels are meant to be engraved (§5.3.3).
    - Fig. 187 right (PDF p.103): 2D labels "11.1.5", "14.1.1", "18.2.2", "20.1.2" run along C-shaped ring segments whose ends are plain straight cuts with no joint.
    - Direction and nesting work exactly as in Contour (§5.3).
    - No tolerance field is documented for Stack (§5.3), and the 2019 Stack panel shows only sheet width/length/thickness, dowel size, ring width and layout (CN-GS p.6).
  - Research behind LuBan:
    - Contours larger than the cutter are partitioned; layers are hollowed with an "inner rim"; alignment uses "automatically generated reference holes" (papers/CAD16).
    - A user variable caps component length (45 cm in the example); fabricators found that where sub-planes are split affects strength and handling, and that reading labels slowed assembly (papers/CAD15).
    - Splits should avoid vertices and corners (papers/Sass-2025). That paper also says LuBan does not code splitting and rejoining for its house-scale grammar, so joints at Stack seams are not documented anywhere.
  - AD3D generator steps (ours):
    1. Input is a repaired closed mesh (M3), scaled to the model size.
    2. Layers: pitch = `sheet_thickness_measured`; N = round(H / pitch); with `snap_height` the model is rescaled so H = N × pitch; plane i sits at `z_min + (i + phase) × pitch` along the stacking direction.
    3. Section every plane (nonzero fill) into polygons with holes; drop loops below `min_feature`; each connected region is a contour. Number layers bottom to top and contours left to right (papers/Sass-2025: numbering "starts at the bottom front", rises with elevation, then runs left to right); ties are broken front to back (ours).
    4. Rings. Uniform: ring = contour − offset(contour, −`ring_width`). Adaptive: core = contour ∩ contour_below ∩ contour_above; ring = contour − offset(core, −`ring_width`). A ring is never narrower than `dowel_size` + 2 × `dowel_min_wall` where a dowel passes.
    5. Dowels. A dowel run spans consecutive layers; its feasible area is the intersection, over those layers, of offset(ring, −(`dowel_size` / 2 + `dowel_min_wall`)); the dowel goes at that area's pole of inaccessibility. The layers just above and below the run must cover the hole, so the dowel stays hidden (§5.3). Contours that get no dowel are reported, not skipped silently (§5.3.1).
    6. Segmentation. If a part plus `sheet_margin` fits no sheet in any allowed rotation, or exceeds `max_part_length`, cut it across the ring with straight cuts perpendicular to the local ring direction. Cut positions avoid vertices, dowel holes and labels, and stay at least `stagger_seams` away from the seams of the adjacent layers; optional `seam_joint`.
    7. Labels from `label_template`, placed at a pole of inaccessibility inside the region the next layer covers (`label_hidden`) and clear of holes, with `front_arrow` beside them.
    8. Placement guides: engrave the outline and dowel holes of layer i + 1 onto layer i.
    9. Kerf and fit: outer outlines out by `kerf` / 2, ring interiors and dowel holes in by `kerf` / 2; as-cut dowel hole = `dowel_size` + `dowel_fit_allowance`. CNC: square dowel holes get dogbones, or use `dowel_shape` = round, which needs none (research 08 §2.7).
    10. Nest and export (FORM-SHEETS); "ordered" keeps neighbouring layers on the same sheet.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Live re-slicing while ring width, dowel size, pitch or direction is dragged. Research 08 §1.4 measured 40 slices of a 524k-triangle mesh in 0.04 s even in single-threaded WASM, so native multi-core slicing fits the 50 ms preview budget; nesting runs in the background after release (CLAUDE.md speed rules; PLAN §4). LuBan needs Enter for its text fields (§1.8).
  - Measured thickness, kerf and a dowel fit allowance; LuBan documents no Stack tolerance at all (§5.3; CN-GS p.6; research 08 §2.6).
  - Dowel diagnostics show which contours got no dowel and the largest size that would fit; in LuBan a too-big value just prevents the holes, and the manual mentions no warning (§5.3.1).
  - Adaptive rings guarantee glue overlap and room for dowels; LuBan applies one ring width everywhere (§5.3.2; Fig. 186).
  - Staggered segment seams and optional puzzle or dovetail joints; LuBan's segments end in plain straight cuts (Fig. 187) and its seam placement is undocumented.
  - Configurable 2D label size, labels hidden under the next layer, and a front arrow on every part; LuBan's 2D labels have a fixed size (§5.3.3).
  - Engraved placement guides on the parts and one PDF guide, instead of separate per-layer "Asm" drawings (CN-GS p.10).
  - A dowel cut list with the length of every run (ours).
  - Built for 30,000 parts: rayon over layers, streamed SVG/DXF, skyline nesting fallback (CN-IN p.9; research 08 §2.9).
  - One 3MF of the whole assembly with named parts (PLAN §4) instead of a folder of STLs (CN-GS p.10).
  - Any stacking direction from the gizmo (§5.3 → §5.2.2).
  - CNC-ready for the owner's 1325 router: dogbones on square holes, or round dowel holes sized to the dowel stock, and ring interiors checked against the bit diameter (research 08 §2.7). LuBan's square dowel holes (§5.3.1) cannot be cut square by a round bit.
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - Pipeline: research 04 §B.2 (slice → loops → ring offset → dowels → split to sheet → labels → nest); research 00 §3 ("dowel holes at polylabel → split to sheet (staggered seams) → labels").
  - Slicing: manifold cross-sections or our own plane slicer with segment chaining, parallel over layers; offsets and booleans with Clipper2; pole of inaccessibility (polylabel); FORM-SHEETS for nesting and export.
  - OSS references (research 03 §1): marcelfarres/lamina (stacked mode with dowels, pegs and spacers; AGPL, portable for personal use per CLAUDE.md), rgsouthall/laser_slicer, frezik/laser_slicer, Kiri:Moto's laser mode.
  - Effort 5–9 developer-weeks (research 08 §3).
  - Validation (randomised property tests): each layer's parts union equals its ring set; every part fits its sheet; every dowel run is covered at both ends; every extruded 3MF part passes `validate()`; random pitch, ring width, dowel size and direction.
- **Milestone:** M4 (part 9, after APP-2D; PLAN §3).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - All defaults; the CN-GS values come from one 2019 example.
  - How many dowels LuBan places per contour, where, and whether dowel runs span all layers.
  - How LuBan chooses segment cut positions and whether it staggers seams between layers.
  - Whether the layer pitch equals the sheet thickness exactly, and where the first plane sits.
  - Whether ring width is global or per layer, and how thin rings and tiny islands are handled.
  - The fixed 2D label height, its font and its placement rule.
  - What the STL folder contains (extruded parts?) and what `Asm3D.dxf` holds.
  - Whether video MZWfjyJSqYE "Photo display stack" uses this method (title only).

#### FORM-WAFFLE — Waffle, orthogonal (LuBan: Hash, Orthogonal)

- **LuBan path:** Mesh → LuBan, Method = Hash, radio button Orthogonal (§5.4, §5.4.2, PDF pp.103–104; Fig. 172 shows the Hash panel). In 2019 a separate method, 正交网格 "orthogonal grid" (CN-GS p.5, p.12–13). Video FJ6VU2wmcp8 "LuBan Hash" (title only). Research lineage: "2D contouring" (papers/CAD16), the 2013 SPIE skeleton paper and the CAD'15 interlocking planes with symbol labels (research 04 §A), and the hashing schema in papers/Sass-2025.
- **What it makes:** Interlocking flat ribs in X (vertical) and Z (horizontal) layers, with slots where they cross; slotted together they form a 3D lattice of the model (§5.4; Fig. 188, PDF p.103, a half-metre horse).
- **Fabrication:** laser-cut sheet, with a positive tolerance to make up for material burnt by the laser, or 3D-printed ribs, with a negative tolerance for print expansion (§5.4.1; CN-GS p.12). Examples: cardboard horses (CN-IN p.13), a plywood duck with engraved labels and laser-darkened edges (CN-GS p.13). CNC routers need dogbones at slot corners (research 08 §2.7). Owner (START_HERE): the 3015 laser (plywood or cardboard if CO2; sheet-metal ribs if fiber, UNCONFIRMED) or the 1325 router, where the bit must be narrower than the slot (FORM-SHEETS rule), so thin sheets need small bits; printed ribs must fit the CR-6 SE's 235 × 235 mm bed.
- **Inputs:** one mesh.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| Sheet height; 2019: 板材长度 | `sheet_height` | Shared with Stack. | UNCONFIRMED (Fig. 172: 400; CN-GS p.12: 450) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: > 0 mm) | §5.4; Fig. 172; CN-GS p.12 |
| Sheet thickness; 2019: 板材厚度 | `sheet_thickness_measured` | Rib thickness; sets the slot width (zero tolerance makes the slot exactly the sheet thickness). | UNCONFIRMED (Fig. 172: 3.2; CN-GS p.12: 5) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: > 0 mm) | §5.4.1; Fig. 172; papers/CAD16 ("thickness of the slots is determined by that of the cut sheet") |
| Tolerance; 2019: 公差 | `fit_allowance` (with machine `kerf`) | LuBan: slot tightness. 0 makes the slot exactly the sheet thickness; positive makes it narrower than the sheet, compensating laser burn; negative makes it wider, for print expansion. - **Outputs:** LuBan: ribs nested on sheets as DXF, SVG and SHP (§5 intro); labels start with X or Z (§5.4.3); Measure shows parts, machine time and assembly time (CN-GS p.12: 21 parts, 20 min, 24 min). AD3D: the FORM-SHEETS outputs plus `joints.csv` (slot id, rib A, rib B, position) and an assembly-order page in the PDF guide; for printing, `ribs.3mf` with every rib as a flat, named, watertight solid.

- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - LuBan:
    - Interlocking contours with slots in X and Z directions; sheet size, ring width, text size and nesting are shared with Stack (§5.4). Hash generates no Y layers (§5.10).
    - Tolerance as in the table (§5.4.1). The 2019 deck says the same: a positive tolerance compensates the material lost at part edges by laser cutting, a negative one compensates the edge thickening of 3D prints (CN-GS p.12). It speaks of part edges (部件边缘), not slots, so whether the old tolerance offset whole outlines or only slots is UNCONFIRMED.
    - Sign conflict: the CAD'16 paper says "Larger tolerance leads to relatively wide slots" (papers/CAD16), the opposite of the manual. The manual governs for LuBan; AD3D's `fit_allowance` has one meaning (positive = looser) and no sign ambiguity.
    - X and Z layers are evenly spaced (§5.4.3). Each label starts with X or Z, followed by numbers meaning layer.contour[.segment] as in Stack (§5.4.3 → §5.3.3).
    - "Depending on the shape of the model and the number of layers, there may be some contours that do not interlock with the others", and those cannot be assembled to the main body (§5.4.3).
    - Tilt gives an artistic version; Object → Select and Object → Explode show each contour (§5.4.4). In Fig. 192 (left: orthogonal, 20°) the vertical family leans while the horizontal layers stay level.
    - Slot size comes from the local geometry, slot thickness from the sheet; the user tolerance depends on material (cardboard, plywood, plastic) and laser settings (speed, power) (papers/CAD16).
  - AD3D generator steps (ours):
    1. Input is a repaired closed mesh (M3). Rib planes: the X family at x_i = x_min + (i + 0.5) × Lx / `x_layers` (+ `grid_offset_x`), the Z family likewise; or fixed pitch.
    2. Section every plane into polygons with holes, hollow them into rings (`ring_width`, as in Stack), drop pieces below `min_feature`; each connected region is a rib.
    3. For every X-rib a and Z-rib b whose planes meet, the crossing line ℓ (plane_a ∩ plane_b) runs along Y. Compute the 1D intervals of ℓ that lie inside both ribs (research 04 §B.4). Each interval of length C ≥ `min_joint_len` is a joint.
    4. Slots: a gets a slot of depth `slot_depth_ratio` × C from one end of the interval and b the complementary slot from the other end (papers/Sass-2025 Fig. 5: half depth each). Each slot must open onto its own rib's boundary. When both ends of an interval lie on the same rib's boundary, the other rib's slot is extended to its nearest edge (warning: open channel) or the joint is dropped (cf. crdbrd; research 04 §B.4; research 08 §2.8). All X-ribs open their slots towards one side (e.g. +Y) and all Z-ribs towards the other, so a whole family slides on along Y.
    5. Slot width: as-cut w = t + `fit_allowance`; drawn w − `kerf`. With tilt, ribs meet at a dihedral angle θ = 90° − `tilt_deg`. A laser cuts perpendicular to the sheet, so each slot must widen to w = t × (1 + cos θ) / sin θ + `fit_allowance` — about 1.43 t at 20° tilt and 2.41 t at 45° — and AD3D warns about the loose joint; for printing it can export exact angled slots instead (ours, geometry).
    6. Checks: `min_bridge` between slots, edges and holes; a slot that runs into a ring hollow or an internal hole is moved or merged (research 08 §2.8).
    7. Interlock graph: nodes are ribs, edges are joints. Ribs outside the largest connected component are orphans (§5.4.3) and follow `orphan_policy`. Assembly order: check that every rib can slide into place given the slots already engaged, and report deadlocks (research 07 §e.7; crdbrd in research 04 §B.4).
    8. Oversize ribs: split between slots, never through one; add a lap or finger joint or a splice plate; stagger splits between neighbouring ribs; re-slot (research 08 §2.8; papers/CAD15 sub-planes).
    9. Labels `X{i}.{c}[.{s}]` and `Z{j}.{c}[.{s}]` (X/Z prefix per §5.4.3; template ours), plus `slot_labels`.
    10. Kerf and fit per FORM-SHEETS. CNC: dogbones at both bottom corners of every slot (research 08 §2.7); on the `router_1325` profile, export is blocked if `tool_diameter` ≥ the drawn slot width (FORM-SHEETS rule).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Live preview for every field. By §1.8's rule LuBan's sliders (layers, tilt, ring width, font size) already update live, but sheet size, thickness and tolerance are text fields that need Enter (§1.8; CN-GS p.12). AD3D recomputes slots and rings while you drag and nests after release (PLAN §4).
  - Kerf, measured thickness and fit allowance instead of one signed Tolerance whose sign the sources themselves contradict (research 08 §2.6; §5.4.1 vs papers/CAD16).
  - Orphan ribs are found, highlighted and offered fixes (remove, add a linking rib, glue), instead of being left for the user to discover at assembly time (§5.4.3).
  - Thin-bridge, slot-into-hole and assembly-order checks (research 08 §2.8; research 07 §e.7).
  - Ribs bigger than the sheet are split with real joints and re-slotted (research 08 §2.8); LuBan's behaviour for oversize ribs is undocumented.
  - Tilt handled honestly: slots widened for perpendicular cuts, or exact angled slots for printing (ours); LuBan's handling is undocumented.
  - Every slot engraved with its mating rib's label, plus an ordered assembly page in the PDF guide (ours; PLAN §4); LuBan's labels only identify the rib (§5.4.3).
  - CNC dogbones and a bit-fits-slot check for the owner's 1325 router (research 08 §2.7: without dogbones, CNC-cut waffle parts will not assemble); LuBan documents no CNC handling for Hash (§5.4).
  - Fixed pitch and grid offset in mm and a choice of axis pair (ours); LuBan offers counts only, on X and Z only (§5.4.3, §5.10).
  - A 3D-print variant as one 3MF of flat, watertight ribs with a print fit (§5.4.1; PLAN §4).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - Method: research 04 §B.4; Schwartzburg & Pauly 2013, Hildebrand et al. 2012 (crdbrd), McCrae et al. 2011 (research 04 §A); papers/Sass-2025 Fig. 5.
  - OSS references (research 03 §2): marcelfarres/lamina (interlocked mode; AGPL, portable for personal use), yqlu/sliceformstudio (slot math, MIT), execuc/LCInterlocking (LGPL-2.1), whatmakeart/make-slice (GPL-3.0).
  - Clipper2 for rings and slots; FORM-SHEETS for nesting and export.
  - Effort 8–14 developer-weeks including oversize splitting and assemblability (research 08 §3).
  - Validation (randomised property tests): the two slots of every joint add up to the crossing length; slot widths follow the rule; extruded ribs do not interpenetrate beyond `fit_allowance`; the interlock graph is connected or its orphans are reported; random counts, tilt, ring width and thickness.
- **Milestone:** M4 (part 9, after APP-NEST; PLAN §3).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - All defaults, and whether the 2019 values (7 X, 8 Z, 8°, font 16) are LuBan defaults.
  - The plane spacing rule (edge or half-pitch) and the slot side convention.
  - Whether Tolerance changes the total slot width or each side (for connectors, −0.2 mm gives a 0.4 mm gap, §4.6.6).
  - Whether LuBan splits ribs larger than the sheet (labels may carry a segment number, §5.4.3 → §5.3.3) and how it rejoins them. In 2019 radial mode the third number appears even on a model smaller than the sheet (CN-GS p.14), so it may also mark a split at the axis, not only an oversize split.
  - The tilt rotation axis and how slots are adapted to non-perpendicular crossings.
  - How LuBan handles several intervals on one crossing line, and intervals contained in one rib.
  - Label format beyond the X/Z prefix; Text size units.

#### FORM-WAFFLE-RADIAL — Radial waffle (LuBan: Hash, Radial)

- **LuBan path:** Mesh → LuBan, Method = Hash, radio button Radial (§5.4.2, PDF p.104; Fig. 172 shows Radial selected). In 2019 a separate method, 环状网格 "ring grid" (CN-GS p.5, p.14–16). Blog: radial-center-adjustment (2019-09-28: "Adjust the radial center of the Radial method."). Video BGaO2QMWJdg "LuBan Radial" (title only).
- **What it makes:** Vertical ribs radiating around an axis parallel to Z, interlocked with horizontal Z ribs (§5.4.2; Fig. 190 centre and right, PDF p.104). CN-GS p.16 shows a ring-grid example: a large cardboard model, roughly 1 m tall by eye, beside a small cardboard copy and a small white print. CN-IN p.11–12 files the same photo under orthogonal-grid examples, so the decks disagree.
- **Fabrication:** as FORM-WAFFLE.
- **Inputs:** one mesh.
- **Parameters:**

- **Outputs:** as FORM-WAFFLE (CN-GS p.14: 24 parts and 34 min machine time for a 210 × 164 × 150 mm duck; CN-GS p.15: 21 parts, 31 min with 32° tilt).
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - LuBan: the radial axis is parallel to Z and placed on the XY plane by center X and Y (§5.4.2). Vertical slices are generated around a rotation axis; ring width makes slices hollow; the X and Z counts are the vertical and horizontal slices; changing the turn angle (tilt) changes the slice direction (CN-GS p.14–15). In 2019 Radial was its own method (CN-GS p.5), and the 2019 blog still calls it "the Radial method" (blog: radial-center-adjustment); the Aug 2025 manual shows it as a Hash option (Fig. 172).
  - LuBan 2019 labels (CN-GS p.14, read at 400 dpi): the radial ribs' 3D labels also start with X and carry three numbers, e.g. "X5.1.2", "X6.1.2", "X3.1.1", "X4.1.1", beside horizontal labels such as "Z2.2", although the 210 × 164 mm duck fits the 600 × 450 sheet. This suggests each radial X layer is a full plane through the axis, split there into two segments (inferred, UNCONFIRMED); it would also fit the count of 24 parts for 7 X and 8 Z layers (7 × 2 = 14 half-planes plus 10 Z parts), which is likewise an inference.
  - Research: in the "Planar Volume" case the horizontal planes are cylinder-like around a central axis, and the cross-plane slots are arranged around that axis "to allow vertical contours to be assembled from the outside" (papers/CAD15).
  - AD3D rules (ours):
    - Fin k sits at `fin_angle_offset_deg` + k × 360° / `fin_count` (fins) or k × 180° / `fin_count` (full planes).
    - Each fin meets each Z rib along a radial line. Z ribs are slotted from their outer edge and fins from their inner edge, so fins slide on radially from outside (papers/CAD15).
    - Neighbouring fins of thickness t collide near the axis. Trim fins inside r_min = t / (2 × tan(π / N_fins)) plus a clearance (about 3.6 mm for 8 fins of 3 mm), or add a hub per `hub`.
    - Tilt leans each fin about its radial crossing line, which keeps the insertion direction; slots widen as in FORM-WAFFLE step 5.
    - The centre is set in mm, with snaps to the bounding-box centre and the centroid and an on-canvas handle.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - The centre is dragged on the canvas or snapped, in mm. In Fig. 190 the small values (0.1, −0.2) visibly move the axis on a sphere, which suggests relative units that the manual never explains (§5.4.2).
  - Fin collisions at the axis are resolved by trimming or a hub, instead of being left to the user (LuBan's handling is undocumented).
  - The assemble-from-outside slot scheme is built in (papers/CAD15).
  - Everything in FORM-WAFFLE: kerf and fit, orphans, assembly order, dogbones, live preview, 3MF.
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** as FORM-WAFFLE, with a polar set of planes; lamina's radial mode as a reference (research 03 §2; AGPL, portable for personal use). Research 07 §d budgets radial at 1.5 developer-weeks after orthogonal Hash.
- **Milestone:** M4 (part 9, after FORM-WAFFLE), after orthogonal. PLAN §3 names only "Hash (waffle)" for M4; research 07 §c orders it "Hash (waffle, then radial)". It may slip to Later.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Units of center X and Y (relative or mm) and their defaults.
  - Whether "X layers" counts full planes or fins, and how LuBan handles ribs meeting at the axis. The 2019 labels (X5.1.1 / X5.1.2 pattern, CN-GS p.14) point to full planes split at the axis, but no source states it.
  - The tilt axis in radial mode.
  - Whether ring width defaults differ from orthogonal Hash (CN-GS shows 13 and 29, for different model sizes).

#### FORM-WAFFLE-SKIN — Waffle skin (LuBan: Hash surface)

- **LuBan path:** UNCONFIRMED; known only from the blog (probably beside or inside Mesh → LuBan, Method Hash, §5.4, PDF p.103; our reading). Blog: hash-surface (2025-03-01: "Generate surface patches of a hash structure."). Video w670LBsdFzY "LuBan Hash Surface" (9:25, title only). Not in the Aug 2025 manual.
- **What it makes:** surface patches for a hash structure (blog). Hash makes interlocking X and Z contours with slots (§5.4, PDF p.103). Our reading: panels that cover the cells between the ribs on the outer surface. What they look like, how they attach and how they are made is UNCONFIRMED.
- **Fabrication:** UNCONFIRMED.
- **Inputs:** a 3D model and a hash structure (blog); presumably the mesh plus Hash settings (UNCONFIRMED).
- **Parameters:**

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| — (AD3D only) | `skin_thickness` | (ours) Patch thickness. | (suggest: = `sheet_thickness_measured`) | > 0 mm | ours |

| X layers / Z layers; Tilt; Tolerance (Hash settings) | `x_layers`, `z_layers`, `tilt_deg`, `tolerance_mm` (FORM-WAFFLE keys) | The base hash settings, if shared; the patches follow FORM-WAFFLE's rib grid | UNCONFIRMED (as FORM-WAFFLE) | as FORM-WAFFLE | §5.4.1–§5.4.4 (PDF p.104–105) |

- **Behaviour and rules:** UNCONFIRMED.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - None until the source is watched (video w670LBsdFzY). Candidates to check against it: patch fit from the measured sheet thickness and kerf instead of one Tolerance value (research 08 §2.6), and each patch labelled with the X/Z rib labels it sits between (§5.4.3, PDF p.104).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** (ours) split the outer surface by the rib planes into cells; for each cell bounded by four ribs, fit a plane (or cut out the mesh patch), offset it by `skin_inset` to `skin_thickness`, add tabs that clip onto the ribs (manifold); reuse FORM-WAFFLE's rib grid and FORM-SHEETS.
- **Milestone:** M12 (part 9, after FORM-TILING). A blog-only extension of the M4 waffle; not in PLAN §3. Gated: not started until video w670LBsdFzY is transcribed (part 9).

#### FORM-PANELS — Finger-jointed panels (LuBan: Plate)

- **LuBan path:** Mesh → LuBan, Method = Plate (§5.5, PDF p.105). In 2019: 互锁面板 "interlocking panels" (CN-GS p.5, p.17–21). Videos RO3x-qvo2UQ "LuBan Plate" and RL7edYvsPGo "LuBan Plate 2" (titles only). Research lineage: Fresh Press Modeler (Chen & Sass 2016), "plate forming" (papers/CAD16), bevel joints (Su et al. 2018) (research 04 §A).
- **What it makes:** Every planar face of a (simplified) model becomes a flat plate with finger joints along its edges; the fingers of neighbouring plates interlock, so the plates assemble into the shape (§5.5; Fig. 193, PDF p.106, a cube frame).
- **Fabrication:**
  - Laser-cut plywood in the examples (Fig. 193; CN-GS p.20; CN-IN p.15–16). The 2019 pipeline runs triangle mesh → coloured planar regions → finger-jointed plates → cut parts → assembly with engraved numbers (CN-GS p.20; CN-IN p.15). A 2 × 2 × 2 lattice cube has its many small strips nested in rows on one sheet (CN-IN p.16), and a spiral staircase's curved wall becomes many narrow numbered strips (CN-IN p.18).
  - 3D printing, with a negative tolerance (§5.5.2).
  - Molds and casting formwork: plywood staircase plates used as a mold for cast silicone gel (Fig. 198, PDF p.108; CN-IN p.17–19).
  - CNC routers need dogbones in finger notches (research 08 §2.7); angled bevel joints need a CNC or a printer, not a laser (research 04 §A.4).
  - Owner (START_HERE): the 3015 laser for thin plywood if it is a CO2 machine (UNCONFIRMED), and the 1325 router for thicker boards, where furniture-scale plates such as the stool of Fig. 196 become practical (ours); a printed variant must fit the CR-6 SE's 235 × 235 mm bed per plate.
- **Inputs:** one mesh. Faces should be thin surfaces, not solids with thickness; in software such as Solidworks a thin surface is drafted "in a surface-modeling mode as opposed to a solid-modeling mode" (§5.5). The 2019 deck recommends Plate for models whose surface "shows large angle changes" (CN-GS p.17).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sheet thickness; 2019: 板材厚度 | `sheet_thickness_measured` | Plate thickness ("user specified"). | UNCONFIRMED (CN-GS p.18: 3.2, with a text cursor in the field, so typed by the user) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: > 0 mm) | §5.5; CN-GS p.18 |
| Sheet width / Sheet height; 2019: 板材宽度 / 板材长度 | `sheet_width` / `sheet_height` | Nesting sheet size; shown in the 2019 panel, not described in §5.5. | UNCONFIRMED (CN-GS p.18: 600 / 450) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: > 0 mm) | CN-GS p.18 |
| Low poly | `max_deviation_mm` (replaces LuBan's rate) | LuBan: a simplification rate that replaces many small faces with fewer large ones; computed automatically on entering Plate; a user value is "only a guide". The 2019 Plate panel has no such control (CN-GS p.18). AD3D: the largest allowed distance between the plates and the original surface. | LuBan: computed automatically on entering Plate (§5.5.1); the value and its rule are UNCONFIRMED. AD3D (suggest): 1% of the bounding-box diagonal | LuBan examples 0.0005, 0.0015, 0.005; in Fig. 194 a higher value keeps more faces | §5.5.1 (PDF p.106); Fig. 194 |
| — (AD3D only) | `target_plate_count` | Alternative to `max_deviation_mm`: aim for this many plates. | — | integer | ours |
| Tolerance; 2019: 公差 | `fit_allowance` (with machine `kerf`) | Finger tightness: 0 makes paired fingers exactly the same size; negative for printing, positive for laser (burn). AD3D sign inverted and kerf separate (FORM-SHEETS). | UNCONFIRMED (CN-GS p.18: 0) | signed mm; Fig. 195 shows −0.5, 0, 0.5 mm | §5.5.2 (PDF p.106); Fig. 195 (PDF p.107) |
| Finger width; 2019: 指槽宽度 "finger-slot width" slider | `finger_width` | Target finger width; at least the sheet thickness; LuBan adjusts it per edge so the fingers pair up. | UNCONFIRMED (CN-GS p.18: 7) (suggest: max(3 × t, 10 mm)) | ≥ t; Fig. 196 shows 5, 10, 20 mm | §5.5.3 (PDF pp.106–107); Fig. 196; CN-GS p.18 |
| Mold; 2019: 生成模具 "generate mold" check box | `surface_side` | Yes: the plate structure's INTERIOR volume equals the original. No: its EXTERIOR volume equals the original. | UNCONFIRMED (CN-GS p.18 shows it unchecked) | Yes, No → AD3D: inner (= Yes), outer (= No) | §5.5.4 (PDF p.107); Fig. 197; CN-GS p.18–19 |
| Text size; 2019: 字体大小 slider | `label_height_3d` | Size of the plate numbers (inferred; the manual's §5.5 lists no text size, but numbers show in Fig. 194 and the 2019 panel has the slider). | UNCONFIRMED (CN-GS p.18: 16) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: > 0) | CN-GS p.18; Fig. 194 |
| Nesting (for Plate: UNCONFIRMED) | `nesting_mode` | As FORM-SHEETS. | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED for Plate (Contour, Stack and Hash offer compact, ordered, balanced) | §5.2.5; CN-GS p.18 shows a drop-down cut off at the bottom of the Plate panel, possibly 布局 Layout (UNCONFIRMED) |
| — (AD3D only) | `planarity_tol_mm` | Largest out-of-plane deviation when faces merge into one plate. | 0.2 mm (suggest) | ≥ 0 mm | ours |
| — (AD3D only) | `min_edge_len` | Edges shorter than this get no fingers (glued edge). | 2 × t (suggest) | mm | ours; research 04 §B.5 |

| — (AD3D only) | `thin_wall_merge` | Detect solid walls up to about 2 × t thick and replace their two faces with one plate. | on (suggest) | on, off | ours; §5.5 |

- **Outputs:** LuBan: plates nested on sheets (DXF, SVG, SHP) and STL or OBJ (§5 intro). Measure in the 2019 deck: 30 parts, 16 min machine, 41 min assembly, 57 min total for a 70 mm cube frame at 3.2 mm, identical with the mold option off and on (CN-GS p.18–19). Plates carry numbers (Fig. 194; engraved numbers are visible in the photos of Fig. 193 and CN-GS p.20). In the assembled cube of Fig. 193 (right photo, read at 300 dpi) numbers such as "7", "14" and "20" sit on the outer, visible faces, and the loose parts show "6", "8" and "15" (observation). AD3D: the FORM-SHEETS outputs, plus `assembly.3mf` (every plate a named, watertight solid, printable with a print fit) and an edge-pair table in the PDF guide.

- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - LuBan:
    - Plate thickness is user-set, so the model should not give a face its own thickness; faces should be thin surfaces (§5.5). If a wall is modelled as a solid, each of its faces becomes a plate (inferred from §5.5 and the solid cube frame in CN-GS p.17–18).
    - Low poly is needed for dense meshes: it replaces many small faces "that are infeasible for finger joint generation" with fewer large ones, and speeds up joint generation (§5.5.1). A default rate is computed when you enter Plate mode; your rate is only a guide and LuBan decides the actual rate (§5.5.1).
    - Fingers are equally spaced on an edge. The finger width can be any value not less than the sheet thickness, but it is a guide: LuBan computes a width per edge, so widths differ slightly between edges, and the fingers on adjacent edges always pair (§5.5.3).
    - Mold: Yes → interior volume = original; No → exterior volume = original (§5.5.4). 2019 deck: unchecked, "the outer surface equals the input model size"; checked, "the inner surface equals the input model size" (CN-GS p.18–19).
    - Plate structures can be molds; in building construction such molds are drafted by hand, and "based on the plate method, the mold making process can be more automated" (§5.5.4; Fig. 198; CN-IN p.17 formwork photos).
    - The result is a watertight representation, unlike the discrete Stack and Hash forms, so it can serve as casting formwork (papers/CAD16).
  - AD3D generator steps (ours):
    1. Repaired mesh; optional `thin_wall_merge` collapses pairs of parallel, opposite faces closer than about 2 × t into one mid-surface.
    2. Planar segmentation within `max_deviation_mm` (variational shape approximation, or QEM simplification plus coplanar merging; research 04 §B.5); each region becomes a planar polygon, holes allowed; slivers are dropped.
    3. Plate placement: `surface_side` = outer puts each plate's outer face on the surface with the thickness inward; inner puts its inner face on the surface with the thickness outward (§5.5.4; CN-GS p.18–19). Research 04 §B.5 words the offset direction the other way round; the manual and the 2019 deck govern.
    4. For each shared edge with dihedral angle θ: trim both plates to meet; finger count n = max(1, round(L / `finger_width`)), adjusted so both ends of the edge match; finger width L / n ≥ t (§5.5.3); finger depth from t and θ (t at 90°). Acute or reflex angles use angle-corrected square fingers (laser) or bevel joints (CNC, print) (research 04 §A.4, §B.5).
    5. Corners where three or more plates meet get notch clearance (research 04 §B.5).
    6. Kerf, fit and dogbones per FORM-SHEETS; labels: plate number plus `edge_pair_labels`, on the face chosen by `label_face` (mirrored on the sheet when inner).
    7. Nest and export (FORM-SHEETS).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Simplification is set by an explicit deviation in mm or a plate count, with a live coloured preview of the plates and a deviation heatmap. LuBan's rate is "only a guide" and "the actual rate is still determined by LuBan" (§5.5.1).
  - A per-edge finger report (count, width, depth) with manual overrides; LuBan's finger width is only a guide (§5.5.3).
  - Solid models are accepted: thin walls become single plates. LuBan asks for thin-surface models drawn in a CAD surface mode (§5.5).
  - Dihedral-aware fingers plus bevel joints for CNC and printing (research 04 §A.4); LuBan's handling of non-right angles is undocumented.
  - Matching edge codes on both plates of every joint, beyond the plate numbers LuBan shows (Fig. 194), with a choice of the inner face for labels so the finished piece stays clean; LuBan's engraved numbers end up on the outer faces of the assembled cube (Fig. 193).
  - Router-aware fingers for the owner's 1325: dogbones in every finger notch and a check that the bit is narrower than the narrowest notch; LuBan documents no CNC handling (§5.5; research 08 §2.7).
  - Kerf, measured thickness and CNC dogbones (research 08 §2.6–2.7).
  - For molds, flanges, clamp holes and a pour opening are generated, taking up the manual's own remark that mold making "can be more automated" (§5.5.4).
  - One 3MF with all plates, and live preview (PLAN §4).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  - Method: research 04 §B.5; Fresh Press Modeler; Chen et al. 2013 multiplanar models; Su et al. 2018 bevel joints (research 04 §A).
  - Decimation: meshoptimizer (MIT) (research 07 §b).
  - Finger-joint references: florianfesti/boxes (GPL-3.0) and execuc/LCInterlocking (LGPL-2.1); no open-source mesh-to-plates generator exists (research 03 §9).
  - Effort 8–16 developer-weeks, research-grade (research 08 §3).
  - Validation (randomised property tests): every plate is planar within `planarity_tol_mm`; every shared edge has paired fingers (tab against notch); assembled plates do not interpenetrate beyond the fit; for closed inputs the union is watertight.
- **Milestone:** M9 (part 9, first in its row). PLAN §3 lists Plate under Later; part 9 promotes it for the 1325 router.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - What the Low poly number means (fraction of faces kept?) and how its automatic default is chosen.
  - Finger depth and corner handling at non-right angles; the pattern at the ends of an edge.
  - Label size and placement; whether Plate nests, and whether it splits plates larger than the sheet (papers/Sass-2025 says plate splitting is not coded in LuBan).
  - The current label of the mold option ("Mold" Yes/No in §5.5.4; a check box in 2019).
  - All defaults.

### Mesh → LuBan forms: Relief, Spin, Spring, Wave, Wireframe (5.6–5.10)

Each of these five LuBan methods takes one 3D mesh, chosen from the method list under Mesh → LuBan, and turns it into a 2.5D relief, a ring or spiral of bent copies, a layered hollow shell that compresses like a spring, a rippled deformation, or a wireframe that is laser-engraved or 3D-printed (§5 intro, PDF p.96). They all share LuBan's Input section (Unit, and Model size X/Y/Z of the original model with a locked aspect ratio, applied on Enter) and its Save model button, which writes STL/OBJ for printing and DXF/SVG/SHP for laser (§5 intro and Fig. 172, PDF p.96; §1.8, PDF pp.15–16). For relief, spin, spring and wave, the measure section shows the size of the generated model (§5 intro). In the 2019 build, Save model was labelled 导出部件 ("Export parts") and wrote a folder named model_Method_HH-MM-SS, e.g. "duck_Stack_13-42-02" (Get started (zh) pp.7, 9). The manual shows no parameter panel for any of them, and only the official Chinese Get-started guide shows one (the 2D wireframe), so most defaults and ranges below are UNCONFIRMED, and values taken from figures are labelled "figure values", never defaults. PLAN §3 lists "Relief (AI depth)" and "wireframe" under "Later"; Spin, Spring and Wave are not named there and fall under CLAUDE.md build-order step 5 ("the rest of the manual"), so all five are Later. Each Milestone line gives the order we suggest and what the feature reuses.

Source keys used in this section:
- "Get started (zh) p.N" = page N of `docs/reference/luban-docs/LuBan Get started 快速入门.pdf`, LuBan's official 29-page Chinese quick-start. Its PDF metadata dates it 2019-03-19, and its walkthrough shows an export folder dated 15/8/2018 (p.9), so its labels and shown values are historical.
- Transcript times for video F20FZvL0r9g ("LuBan Thermal", 12:12) are the transcript's one-minute chunks, written @mm:00 (the transcript labels them [00:mm]).
- PDF page = printed page + 1.

---

#### FORM-RELIEF — Bas-relief plaque (LuBan: Relief)

- **LuBan path:** Mesh → LuBan, Method = Relief (manual §5.6, PDF p.108; blog: relief, 2019-06-22). The double-sided option was added later (blog: double-sided-relief, 2019-07-09). Related videos (titles only): "LuBan Relief" (Yf1MTQKyl-A, 4:47) and "Relief on Lithophane" (lIWNKgNKYsU, 1:38).
- **What it makes:** A 2.5D relief of a 3D model: the model's surface as seen from one axis direction, either raised from a base plate (positive) or sunk into it (negative), with an optional frame (§5.6, §5.6.3; Figs. 199–208, PDF pp.108–112). A single-sided relief has a flat back. A double-sided relief carries the model's surface on both faces (§5.6.2).
- **Fabrication:**
  - **3D print:** the relief "can be readily 3D printed" (§5.6). It has no overhanging regions (§5.6), so a single-sided relief prints flat on its back with no supports (our reading). A double-sided relief has relief on both faces, so one face needs supports or a split (ours).
  - **CNC:** convert the STL to a toolpath in CAM software such as MasterCAM. A relief needs no undercut because it has no overhangs (§5.6).
  - **Laser:** the blog also lists laser engraving (blog: relief). How LuBan does it is UNCONFIRMED.
  - **Negative relief:** works as a casting mold, and gives "a special effect" when a printed face is viewed from different angles (§5.6.3; Fig. 202, PDF p.109). That this is the hollow-face illusion is our reading.
  - **Example:** Fig. 199 (PDF p.108) shows a user's print of a head on a round plate with a raised rim.
- **Inputs:** one 3D mesh opened in the 3D window (§5 intro), in OBJ, PLY or STL format (Get started (zh) p.2). For any direction other than the six axes, the model must first be rotated with Object → Transform (§5.6.1).
- **Parameters:**
