| — (ours) | tiling, keys, stand, lamp mount | Split to the bed, align, stand up and light the plate | see PROJ-SQUAMA-TILE | — | PLAN §3 (M1 scope) |
| — (ours) | calibration tile | Measure the real tilt → brightness response and the smallest legible cell | see PROJ-SQUAMA-CAL | — | PLAN §3 (M1 scope) |
| — (ours) | `image_b`, `light_b_azimuth_deg` | Second image for a second light direction (two-axis tilts, "Reliefs as Images" style) | (suggest: none) | Later | AD3D proposal, after Alexa & Matusik 2010 "Reliefs as Images", which the research names as prior art (research 04 §A; research 08 §1.7) but does not summarise; that paper's two-image capability is our recollection, UNCONFIRMED from repo sources |

- **Outputs:**
  - LuBan: one solid plate, with no separate parts, part numbers, flat sheets or nesting (research 01 §2). Its front is divided into square facets; small steps between neighbouring facets show as stripes (f_122). LuBan models the plate already upright, in the X–Z plane with Z up (f_096). File format UNCONFIRMED; by analogy LuBan's Projection save writes an "all in one" record plus STL files (video VA67Jm3ijHg @5:00–7:00), and Mesh → LuBan saves STL or OBJ plus an FGD/FGS scene pair (§5, PDF p.96), so STL is likely (research 00 §2). Other LuBan saves write a time-stamped folder: the lithophane writes "family_LP_Arc_10-25-29" holding the model STL, a LuBan_Model.fgd/.fgs pair (model plus viewing and lighting settings), a human-readable "family_Setting.txt" and "MU_Setting.txt" (§2.12, PDF p.23), and the 2018 Mesh → LuBan build named its folder "<model>_<Method>_<HH-MM-SS>" (luban-docs notes §5). Whether Squama follows either pattern is UNCONFIRMED.
  - AD3D: `shadow_plate.3mf` (unit = millimetre; one object per tile, plus the stand and lamp mount when requested; all parameters in the metadata) or one binary STL per part, streamed to disk; the project file (`.ad3d`); a PNG of the predicted appearance under the design light; the calibration tile on request.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - X and Z are always whole multiples of the cell size; a typed value is rounded to the nearest multiple when Enter is pressed (@5:16–5:54).
  - Loading a photo generates the plate at once (research 01 §2, step 5), enables Save model and sets Z from the photo's aspect (300 → 378, f_066). Entering X recomputes Z from the typed X (f_079, f_082, f_085). An Enter in the Z box changed 102 to 96 with X unchanged at 78 (f_085 → f_089); 96 is also the aspect value for X = 78, and 78 is also the X that the lithophane's "vice versa" rule (§2.13.1, PDF p.23) would derive from Z = 96, so whether a typed Z is kept is UNCONFIRMED; if it is kept, what happens to the photo (stretched or cropped) is UNCONFIRMED. AD3D: Z is always derived from X and the crop's aspect, and editing Z derives X (the lithophane rule).
  - Changing the cell size re-snaps X and Z without reapplying the aspect (f_099 → f_100). Later Z jumped from 96 to the aspect value 100 (round(80 × aspect / 4) × 4) between f_209, where the Cell size box is being retyped from "4j" to "4", and f_210, where the X box is selected; which entry triggered it is not visible.
  - Text boxes apply on Enter; drop-downs and spinners update at once (§1.8, PDF p.15–16; @5:11–5:14; the same rule in the 2018 build, luban-docs notes §4.1). In the Squama panel the text boxes are Model size X, Model size Z, Cell size and Thickness; the spinners are Light angle and Surface angle; Light source and Mode are drop-downs (f_060).
  - The pink markers follow Light source immediately; the rendered shading does not (see below).
  - Left/Right light tilts facets about the vertical axis (vertical columns, f_122); Top/Bottom light tilts them about the horizontal axis (rows, with a sawtooth visible on the side edge, f_148).
  - Facets tilted back against the light read black (@8:23–8:41). Contrast rises with the surface angle; at 1 the plate looks blank (@8:53–9:15, f_138).
  - More cells give a sharper picture: 80 mm wide at cell 4 is "not very clear", 200 mm wide is "much better" (@13:44–14:35, f_225).
  - The pink markers only show where the light is; the render light is set separately with Lighting angle or Move light. With the render light from below and Light source switched to Top the image shows reversed; Right is unclear; Left is only partly visible (@11:54–12:56). Under the default render light the plate "doesn't look very clear" (@10:44–10:54) and looks almost blank (f_165).
  - LuBan accepts malformed numbers ("4j" read as 4, f_101, f_122). AD3D: strict parsing with an inline error (APP-PANEL).
  - Rules we derive from the shading model (ours): true black needs `tilt_max_deg` ≥ `light_elev_deg`, otherwise the darkest facet still receives sin(α − S) > 0, so warn when it is violated. In `auto` print orientation the horizontal steps are at most cell × tan(S) deep (2.2 mm at cell 6 / 20°, 0.7 mm at cell 4 / 10°); warn above `ledge_warn_mm`.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - The plate updates while a slider is dragged (preview resolution, latest-wins jobs) and refines on release, instead of type-then-Enter (§1.8, PDF p.15–16; @5:11; PLAN §1, APP-LIVE).
  - The preview light follows the design light and casts real shadows. In LuBan the markers do not move the render light, so the user hunts for the view with Move light (@10:44–12:56).
  - An exact 2D "what you will see" map computed by the core sits next to the 3D view, because shadow maps alias badly at 5–10° grazing light (ours).
  - An ambient slider with a live contrast readout shows how much room light washes the image out (PLAN §4; research 08 §2.3).
  - Light from any azimuth, a wider elevation range, a point-lamp model with falloff correction and a printed lamp mount at that exact position. LuBan offers four sides, at most 20°, and an implied parallel light (@4:36–5:01, @7:31–7:51).
  - Hexagonal cells (PLAN §4): saddle-free topology, because only three cells meet at a corner (ours, see Algorithm step 8). Whether they also soften the step stripes seen in LuBan's render (f_122) is UNCONFIRMED until printed.
  - Crop, gamma, contrast, auto-levels and sharpen; LuBan's Squama panel has no image controls (f_060; PLAN §4).
  - Units, ranges and the snapped result shown beside every field (e.g. "200 → 198 mm, 33 cells"). LuBan's panel shows no units at all, and the snapped X and the re-derived Z appear only after Enter, with no explanation (f_060, f_079; @5:16–5:22, where the author has to explain why 200 became "slightly smaller").
  - Shadow-aware tone mapping: `shadow_free` now and an optimiser later. Cast shadows cost the prototypes 5–11 % of image match (START_HERE; ours (sim)).
  - A calibration tile (PROJ-SQUAMA-CAL), and tiling with keys, a stand and a lamp mount (PROJ-SQUAMA-TILE); LuBan's default plate is taller than the owner's 250 mm Z (research 08 §2.4; START_HERE).
  - Automatic print orientation (facet tilt axis vertical) turns the sawtooth steps that need support with Top/Bottom light (@9:30–10:07) into vertical walls, and runs the layer lines along the light so they cast no stripes; only ledges between unlike neighbouring cells remain, bounded by `ledge_warn_mm` (ours).
  - Watertight by construction and validated after welding by position; every prototype STL fails that check (prototypes/README.md; PLAN §6).
  - 3MF with units and parts, or streamed binary STL (PLAN §4).
  - Multi-core and cancellable; under 50 ms for 100 × 126 cells (PLAN §2, criterion 2).
  - Undo/redo, project files, presets per printer/lamp/room, and a CLI, e.g. `ad3d shadow-plate --image mona.jpg --width 196 --cell 4 --light-azimuth 180 --light-elev 10 --tilt-max 10 -o mona.3mf` (PLAN §4; ours).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:**
  1. **Image to target grey per cell.** Decode, apply EXIF orientation and crop, convert to luminance, apply the image controls, then box-average over each cell (the prototypes use a BOX resize; research 07 §(a)). Grid: nx = round(W / cell), nz from the aspect, then snap W and H (research 01 §2). Computing nz from the typed width, nz = round(W_typed × aspect / cell), is what matches the video's numbers (ours, from f_079, f_082, f_085; see Model size Z); both prototypes use the snapped width instead.
  2. **Inverse Lambert** (research 00 §2; research 04 §B.11). With the light at elevation α and a facet tilted by θ towards it, brightness E = max(0, sin(α + θ)). Map grey g ∈ [0, 1] linearly onto [E_min, E_max] with E_min = max(0, sin(α − S)) and E_max = sin(α + S), then θ = asin(E) − α, clamped to [−S, +S]; pure black gets −S (`squama.py` `tilts()`). So only tilts in [−α, +S] are used for g > 0; any tilt at or below −α is self-shadowed (research 07 §0). `shadow_free`: E = g × sin α, so θ ∈ [−α, 0].
  3. **Facet planes** (ours). For light azimuth φ, the facet in a cell centred at (x_c, z_c) is h(x, z) = c − tan θ × ((x − x_c) cos φ + (z − z_c) sin φ): it rises away from the light, so for Left light (φ = 180°) the right edge is higher, as in the prototype's `heights()`. `pivot = centre`: c = base + (cell/2) × tan S × (|cos φ| + |sin φ|) for every cell. `pivot = low_corner`: c = base + (cell/2) × tan|θ| × (|cos φ| + |sin φ|), which puts every facet's lowest corner on the datum (both prototypes; `squama-centre-pivot` adds a 0.4 mm pad, `squama-rising` a 1e-4 mm random tie-break). Relief above the base is at most cell × tan S for axis-aligned light: 1.06 mm at 6 mm / 10°, 0.71 mm at 4 mm / 10°, 1.46 mm at 4 mm / 20° (ours; research 07 §0 measured a 3.0–3.71 mm plate at cell 4, base 3).
  4. **Shading and cast shadows** (ours). A point is lit when it is above the upstream horizon H(s) = max over s′ < s of [h(s′) − (s − s′) × tan α] along the light direction: one O(N) sweep per light-aligned row (as in `shadow.py`). In a uniform area of positive tilt, each facet is shadowed by its neighbour's raised edge over a fraction tan θ / (tan α + tan θ) of its width, so its mean brightness is sin(α + θ) × tan α / (tan α + tan θ) = sin α × cos θ: never brighter than a flat plate. Ours (sim) measured 0.0867 against 0.0858 predicted at 5° / 10°; unshadowed it would be 0.259. Positive tilts only brighten facets whose upstream neighbour is lower, i.e. the light-side edges of bright areas. This is why the match falls to 0.89 at 5° / 10°, and why the light elevation matters more than the surface angle.
  5. **Ambient and contrast.** Observed brightness ≈ lamp term + ambient a. Research formula: contrast ≈ (sin(α + S) + a) / a, about 3.6:1 at α = 5°, S = 10°, a = 0.1 (research 08 §2.3; START_HERE). That is the bound for an unshadowed facet; a large uniform area is limited to (sin α + a) / a: 1.87:1 at 5°, 2.74:1 at 10°, 4.42:1 at 20° (ours). So a dark room and α = 10–20° matter most.
  6. **Shadow-aware optimiser** (`tone_mapping = optimised`, ours). Rows along the light are independent for axis-aligned light. Per row, choose each cell's tilt and height offset within [base, base + `relief_max_mm`] to minimise Σ(B_i − target_i)², where B_i includes cast shadows: dynamic programming over quantised (end height, shadow horizon) states, or coordinate descent starting from the pivot solution. It runs as a cancellable job on demand, not while dragging. Naive versions fail: continuous ramps that drop only at dark cells, or when the budget is exceeded, scored 0.60–0.84 at 5° / 10° with a 1–5 mm budget (0.60–0.94 across 5° / 10°, 10° / 10° and 10° / 20°, always below the pivot layouts in the table below), and unconstrained ramps reach 0.998–1.000 but need 23–50 mm of relief (ours (sim)). Its gain over `lambert` is UNCONFIRMED until prototyped, so `lambert` and `shadow_free` ship first.
  7. **Direct mesher** (no booleans: research 00 §4; research 08 §1.4, §2.2). Facets are planar polygons. For axis-aligned light, walls between columns are vertical rectangles; walls between rows are bounded by two sloped segments that can cross, so split them at the crossing and add that vertex to both facet edges (prototype `extra`). At every grid corner, collect all facet heights meeting on that vertical line and insert them into every wall touching it, so no T-junctions remain (prototype `vjump`). Add four side walls as planar polygons from the top outline down to the back, and a flat back. Triangulate planar polygons by ear clipping (the prototype uses mapbox_earcut; Rust: the earcut crate or our own). Key vertices by integer topology (corner id + height rank), not by float hashing. Expect about 10–16 triangles per cell (ours): 100 × 126 cells ≈ 0.13–0.2 M triangles, a 6–10 MB binary STL.
  8. **Watertightness pitfalls.**
     - T-junctions at corners and crossings open cracks once a slicer welds vertices by position; fix as in step 7.
     - Saddle pinches: where both cells of one diagonal are higher than both cells of the other, all four walls share the same vertical segment, giving an edge with four faces (research 07 §0: 62 bad edges). A tie-break ε does not fix this, because any strict saddle has it (ours). Duplicating vertices alone is undone by welding by position, which is our reading of why even the manifold-union STLs fail after welding (prototypes/README.md). Fix it geometrically, so the mesh stays 2-manifold after welding: a micro-gap (shrink the two high cells' shared corner by ε ≈ 0.02 mm) or a micro-bridge (fill an ε × ε corner square up to the lower of the two high heights) (ours). Hex cells avoid the case entirely.
     - Exact height ties give zero-area walls and degenerate triangles: skip zero-length wall segments and emit no face under 1e-12 mm² (ours; research 07 §(e).2 suggests a 1e-4 mm tie-break instead).
     - Walls emitted from both sides must keep opposite winding; the prototype hit "inverted wall normals" (research 07 §0).
  9. **Validation and tests** (PLAN §1, §5). Weld by position (quantised to 1e-5 mm); then every undirected edge has exactly two faces, every directed edge appears once, there are no degenerate faces, the Euler characteristic is 2 per shell, the signed volume is positive and equals the analytic Σ cell area × mean facet height (to 1e-4 relative, allowing for the saddle fixes), and the bounds equal (W, H, maximum height). proptest over W 20–400 mm, cell 1–20 mm, α 0–45°, S 1–30°, all azimuths, both pivots and both grids, with noise images, checkerboards (force saddles), constant images (force ties) and pure 0/1 images. Criterion benchmarks at 50 × 63 and 100 × 126 cells, preview and full resolution.
  10. **Performance.** O(cells); rayon over bands of rows with deterministic vertex numbering by prefix sums. Target < 50 ms at 100 × 126 cells (PLAN §2), against the Python direct mesher's 1.9 s at 50 × 63 and 6.6 s at 100 × 126, the Python manifold-union path's 0.2 s and 1.4 s, and the single-threaded WASM batch union's 5.4 s, 23.8 s and 162 s at 50 × 63, 100 × 126 and 150 × 189 (prototypes/README.md; research 08 §1.4).
  11. **Prior art.** Alexa & Matusik 2010 "Reliefs as Images"; Bermano et al. 2012 "ShadowPix"; amirhertz/shadowpix (MIT, reference only) (research 08 §1.7; research 04 §A). Our prototypes: `prototypes/squama-centre-pivot/`, `prototypes/squama-rising/`.

  Ours (sim): match and contrast (p99 / p1 brightness with ambient 0.10) for the synthetic target; the 0.891 and 0.953 reproduce the research's 0.89 and 0.95 (START_HERE). The `shadow_free` column uses `low_corner` heights; the formula column is the research's unshadowed bound.

  | α / S | lambert, low_corner | lambert, centre | shadow_free | research formula (sin(α+S)+a)/a |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 5° / 10° | match 0.891, 2.68:1 | 0.909, 2.39:1 | 1.000, 1.84:1 | 3.59:1 |
  | 10° / 10° | 0.953, 3.80:1 | 0.956, 3.40:1 | 1.000, 2.68:1 | 4.42:1 |
  | 10° / 20° | 0.888, 4.15:1 | 0.906, 3.68:1 | 1.000, 2.68:1 | 6.00:1 |
  | 20° / 20° | 0.958, 6.27:1 | 0.962, 5.53:1 | 1.000, 4.30:1 | 7.43:1 |

  `lambert` keeps more peak contrast (bright light-side edges) at the cost of fidelity; `shadow_free` is exact but flatter. Which looks better in print is UNCONFIRMED; the calibration tile prints both.
- **Milestone:** M1 (part 9, after PROJ-SQUAMA-CAL; PLAN §3; CLAUDE.md build order item 1).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - LuBan's export format and file names (Save model is never clicked; research 01 §2).
  - LuBan's actual grey → tilt rule (linear, or inverse Lambert) and its pivot (research 08 §5.1).
  - What Thickness means: announced but never explained (@8:46–8:53); base under the relief or minimum material (ours).
  - Ranges of Model size and Cell size; the full Mode list; the image formats.
  - Whether an Enter in Model size Z keeps the typed value, re-derives Z from X, or re-derives X from Z as the flat lithophane does (§2.13.1) (f_085 → f_089 fits all three), and whether changing Cell size ever reapplies the aspect (f_099 → f_100 says no; f_209 → f_210 is ambiguous).
  - Units of Model size, Cell size and Thickness (never spoken; mm presumed from the axes, f_225), and whether the angle spinners accept decimals.
  - Whether "Botton" in the closed Light source box is a typo or a clipped "Bottom" (f_150 vs f_151).
  - What LuBan does with the photo when Z is edited independently (stretch or crop), if it allows that.
  - LuBan's colour-to-grey conversion and whether it applies any gamma.
  - Physical results: legibility of cells under about 3 mm; real contrast under the owner's room light; plastic sheen and layer lines that break the Lambert model (research 08 §2.5, §5.6; research 07 §(e).5).
  - Whether a large plate printed upright on the CR-6 SE wobbles at the top without ribs.
  - The optimiser's real gain.

### PROJ-SQUAMA-CAL — Shadow Plate calibration tile (LuBan: none)
- **LuBan path:** None; the Squama panel has no calibration control (f_060). AD3D: Shadow Plate panel → "Print calibration tile", then "Measure photo".
- **What it makes:** A small test tile printed with the same settings as the final plate: (1) a ramp of uniform patches, one tilt each from below −α to +S; (2) a strip of the same pattern at several cell sizes; (3) a small grey ramp rendered as a real Shadow Plate twice, once with `lambert` and once with `shadow_free`. Photographed under the owner's lamp and room light, it gives a measured tilt → brightness table, the real contrast ratio and the smallest legible cell size (PLAN §4: "a calibration tile that prints a grey ramp so you can tune for your room"; research 07 §(c): "print a 16-step tilt ramp, photograph it under the real lamp, and build a lookup table"; research 08 §2.3: "measured under the expected ambient light").
- **Fabrication:** 3D print in the same orientation, material, layer height and speed as the final plate, or the measurement does not transfer (ours). Light it with the real lamp at the design elevation, keep the room light at its normal level and photograph straight on with exposure locked (ours).
- **Inputs:** The current Shadow Plate settings (α, S, pivot, base, cell, material preset); later, one photo of the printed tile (JPEG or PNG; HEIC UNCONFIRMED).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — (ours) | `cal_steps` | Number of tilt patches | (suggest: 16) | (suggest: 8–32) | AD3D proposal; research 07 §(c) |
| — (ours) | `cal_tilt_min_deg`, `cal_tilt_max_deg` | Tilt range of the ramp | (suggest: −max(S, α + 2°) to +S) | within ±30° | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `cal_patch_cells` | Patch size in cells; large enough that the patch interior behaves like a uniform area | (suggest: 4 × 4) | (suggest: 3 × 3 to 8 × 8) | AD3D proposal; PROJ-SQUAMA algorithm step 4 |
| — (ours) | `cal_cell_sizes_mm` | Cell sizes in the legibility strip | (suggest: 2, 3, 4, 6) | list | AD3D proposal; PLAN §6 |
| — (ours) | `cal_mapping_strip` | Grey ramp rendered with `lambert` and with `shadow_free` side by side | (suggest: on) | on / off | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `cal_labels` | Step numbers engraved on the flat back, plus a light-side arrow | (suggest: on) | on / off | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `cal_max_size_mm` | Tile envelope | (suggest: 120 × 90) | fits the active printer | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `measure_photo` | Photo of the lit tile | — | image file | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `measure_corners` | Four clicked tile corners for perspective correction | — | 4 points | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `response_fit` | Fit of the measured table | (suggest: monotone (isotonic) regression) | monotone / spline | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** `shadow_cal.3mf` (or `.stl`). After measurement: a response table stored in the printer/lamp/room preset (sets `response_model = measured`), and a short report with the measured contrast ratio, the darkest and brightest patch and the smallest cell size the owner confirms as legible.
- **Behaviour and rules:** (ours) Patches are sorted by tilt and labelled; a non-monotonic measured response is rejected with a message instead of being fitted; the self-shadowed patches give the ambient level directly; the measured table replaces Lambert only for the preset it was measured with.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - A printed grey-ramp tile turns the result into numbers measured under the real room light (research 08 §2.3). LuBan offers no calibration, only the advice that results depend on print quality and on how the light is installed (video Wd26qsSIRY8 @14:44–14:50; PLAN §4, Smarter Squama).
  - The mapping strip settles the `lambert` versus `shadow_free` question with a print. LuBan's Squama panel shows no tone-mapping setting (frame f_060; PROJ-SQUAMA; PLAN §4).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Patches come from the PROJ-SQUAMA mesher and pass the same validator. Photo → homography from the four corners → median of each patch interior in linear RGB → normalise to the θ = 0 patch → isotonic regression θ → B → invert for the generator. Building blocks: the `image` crate; homography with nalgebra or glam (ours).
- **Milestone:** M1 (part 9, first in its row; PLAN §3).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Whether a phone photo is accurate enough (auto exposure, tone curve); a grey card or RAW capture may be needed.
  - Whether 16 steps and 4 × 4-cell patches are enough.

### PROJ-SQUAMA-TILE — Shadow Plate tiling, keys, stand and lamp mount (LuBan: none)
- **LuBan path:** None. LuBan's Squama makes one plate and shows no tiling (research 01 §2); "'Fits the bed' is LuBan's headline claim, yet Squama apparently doesn't apply it (UNCONFIRMED)" (research 08 §2.4). AD3D: Shadow Plate panel → Fabrication tab.
- **What it makes:** Splits a plate that does not fit the printer into tiles on whole-cell boundaries, adds alignment keys, and generates a stand that holds the plate or tile assembly at a known angle, plus a lamp mount that fixes the lamp at the designed azimuth, elevation and distance (PLAN §3 M1: "tiling to the bed with alignment keys and a stand"; research 00 §3, Squama row; research 08 §2.4: "a printable stand or brim rib"; the lamp mount is ours, prompted by "how you install the light", video Wd26qsSIRY8 @14:44–14:50).
- **Fabrication:** 3D print the tiles in `auto` orientation, each inside the printer profile; print the stand and lamp mount flat (ours). Owner's CR-6 SE: 235 × 235 × 250 mm, face of a standing plate parallel to Y (START_HERE).
- **Inputs:** A Shadow Plate result; the printer profile (bed X, Y, Z and the axis the bed moves in); the lamp type (bulb or LED strip) and size.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — (ours) | `printer_profile` | Build volume and bed-motion axis | (suggest: CR-6 SE, 235 × 235 × 250 mm, bed moves in Y) | machine profiles | START_HERE; PLAN §4 |
| — (ours) | `print_margin_mm` | Clearance kept from the build-volume limits (brim, ribs) | (suggest: 5) | (suggest: 0–20) | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `tiles_x`, `tiles_z` | Tile grid | (suggest: auto = fewest tiles, balanced sizes) | integers | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `seam_policy` | Where seams go: always on cell boundaries; prefer the boundary with the smallest height step | (suggest: smallest_step) | grid / smallest_step | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `key_type` | Alignment between tiles | (suggest: pins) | none / pins / dovetail_back | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `pin_diameter_mm`, `key_clearance_mm` | Pin size (1.75 mm filament as pins) and hole clearance | (suggest: 1.75, 0.15) | — | AD3D proposal; research 04 §B.7 (a user used 1.7 mm filament as dowels) |
| — (ours) | `pin_spacing_mm`, `pin_depth_mm` | Pin pitch along a seam and hole depth | (suggest: 40, 6) | — | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `stand_type` | Support that holds the plate | (suggest: foot) | none / foot / easel | AD3D proposal; research 08 §2.4 |
| — (ours) | `stand_tilt_deg` | Plate lean; tilting the plate changes the light elevation unless the lamp mount is attached to the stand | (suggest: 0) | (suggest: 0–20) | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `lamp_mount` | Printed holder that fixes the lamp where the generator assumed it | (suggest: strip_rail for LED strips along the light-side edge; arm for a point lamp) | none / arm / strip_rail | AD3D proposal; video Wd26qsSIRY8 @13:15–13:25 |
| — (ours) | `lamp_mount_elev_deg`, `lamp_mount_distance_mm` | Mount geometry | (suggest: = `light_elev_deg`, = `lamp_distance_mm`) | — | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** One 3MF with each tile, the stand and the lamp mount as separate named objects, or one STL each; an assembly sheet (PNG, PDF Later) showing tile order and the lamp position.
- **Behaviour and rules:** (ours) Tiles never split a facet; keys stay in the base plate or on the back and never touch the facet relief; with `key_type = pins`, `base_mm` must be at least 4 (a 1.9 mm hole in a 3 mm base leaves 0.55 mm walls); the stand and lamp mount are derived from the same α, φ and lamp distance as the design.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Automatic tiling with keys. LuBan's plate at its default width (300 mm; 300 × 378 for the 4:5 Mona Lisa, f_060 → f_066) printed upright is taller than most printers' Z (research 08 §2.4) and than the owner's 250 mm (START_HERE), and LuBan offers no tiling (PLAN §4, Smarter Squama).
  - A printed stand. A 3 mm plate 250 mm tall wobbles (research 08 §2.4), and LuBan makes no stand (PLAN §4).
  - A printed lamp mount at the design's lamp distance. The author only explains "how you install the light" (video Wd26qsSIRY8 @14:44–14:50).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Partition nx and nz by the maximum cells per tile (floor((bed − margins) / cell)), balanced. Run the PROJ-SQUAMA mesher per tile with shared boundary heights, so each tile is watertight on its own. Pin holes can be built directly into the base walls; manifold booleans for the stand and mount (research 03).
- **Milestone:** M1 (part 9, after PROJ-SQUAMA; PLAN §3).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Strength of pin joints in a 3–4 mm base.
  - Whether a seam shows as a dark line under grazing light.
  - The best stand and lamp-mount designs; whether an LED strip along the edge is close enough to a directional light.

### PROJ-FENCE — Shadow fence (LuBan: Projection → Fence)
- **LuBan path:** File → Create → Projection, Mode = Fence ("It is under fire [file] create projection. I have added a new method called fence", video t2-1zMjWUAw @0:00; panel f_059 @3:52 in video Wd26qsSIRY8). Released 2026-08-08 (blog: fence, "Generate a fence projection from an image."). Bare times below refer to t2-1zMjWUAw.
- **What it makes:** A flat piece (the "yellow" object) that casts a shadow equal to the input image when lit by a single LED. Optional "fence bars" run through the image to hold disconnected parts together and end in a flat base (@0:00–2:00).
- **Fabrication:**
  - 3D print; demo thicknesses 3, 5 and 2 (@5:00). Print orientation UNCONFIRMED (suggest: flat on the bed, as it is a planar extrusion; ours). Laser cutting would also work (ours).
  - Use: "you have a light and then you project some pattern on the floor", the most common case; or the piece is inserted or glued on a wall, with the light mounted on the wall, to project onto the wall (@5:00–6:00). Where the light sits relative to the piece is set by Light distance and Light height.
  - "You have to accurately measure where is the center of your light"; deviation from the centre distorts the pattern (@5:00).
- **Inputs:** One image via "Shadow: Browse" (f_059). A black-and-white silhouette is implied; threshold UNCONFIRMED.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mode | generator `shadow_fence` | Projection sub-mode | Fence (initial) | Fence / Squama / others UNCONFIRMED | f_059 |
| Shadow (Browse) | `image` | Shadow image | none | Formats UNCONFIRMED | f_059; @0:00 |
| Number of fence | `bar_count` | Number of fence bars through the image. Bars are optional ("Optionally, you can generate some fence bars"); fewer bars keep only the region connected to them, and unconnected features are discarded | 5 (initial) | Integer spinner; whether 0 is allowed and the maximum are UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0–50) | f_059; @1:00–2:00 |
| Fence width | `bar_width_mm` | Bar width measured on the shadow. Printed bars taper: wider at the bottom, narrower at the top, because of the projection | 3 (initial) | Demo 3 → 5 | f_059; @2:00 |
| Shadow length | `shadow_length_mm` | Size of the shadow from its leftmost to its rightmost point; the object grows with it | 100 (initial) | UNCONFIRMED | f_059; @2:00–3:00 |
| Shadow offset | `shadow_offset_mm` | Distance from the bottom of the shadow pattern to the object. At 0 the pattern nearly touches the object and is hard to see; more moves it away from the light | 10 (initial) | 0 is allowed (@3:00); negative values and the maximum UNCONFIRMED | f_059; @3:00 |
| Light distance | `light_distance_mm` | Distance from the light to the printed object. Small = strong perspective; large (e.g. 300) ≈ parallel light | 50 (initial) | Demo up to 300 | f_059; @4:00 |
| Light height | `light_height_mm` | Height of the light source | 50 (initial) | UNCONFIRMED | f_059; @4:00–5:00 |
| Thickness | `thickness_mm` | Thickness of the printed piece | 3 (initial) | Demo 2–5 | f_059; @5:00 |
| Save model / Close | — | Export / close | Save model disabled before an image is loaded | — | f_059 |
| — (ours) | `surface` | Where the shadow lands | (suggest: floor) | floor / wall | AD3D proposal; @5:00–6:00 |
| — (ours) | `bar_placement` | `auto` places bars so every island is reached; `even` spaces them evenly (LuBan-like); `manual` | (suggest: auto) | auto / even / manual | AD3D proposal; @1:00 |
| — (ours) | `threshold` | Black/white threshold | (suggest: Otsu) | 0–255 | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `led_emitter_mm` | LED emitter size, for the blur preview | (suggest: 1.0) | (suggest: 0–20) | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `ray_aligned_walls` | Side walls aimed at the light, so thickness does not widen the shadow | (suggest: on) | on / off | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `light_jig` | Printed holder that places the LED at the designed distance and height | (suggest: on) | on / off | AD3D proposal; @5:00 |
| — (ours) | `export_2d` | SVG/DXF outline on a cut layer for laser cutting | (suggest: on) | on / off | AD3D proposal; PLAN §4 |

- **Outputs:** One printable piece; file format UNCONFIRMED (the Projection method's save writes STL plus 2D files, video VA67Jm3ijHg @5:00–7:00). Ours: `fence.3mf` or `.stl`, `fence.svg` and `.dxf` (cut layer), `light_jig.stl`, and a PNG of the predicted shadow.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Bars are optional. Without them, the disconnected parts of an image "will be printed separately"; with them, they connect the parts and produce a flat base, and parts not reached by the bars are discarded, so fewer bars keep only the central region (@1:00).
  - The bar width is specified on the shadow; perspective makes the printed bars taper (@2:00).
  - A large light distance approaches parallel projection (@4:00).
  - The light's centre must be placed as designed (@5:00).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - No silent discarding: unreachable islands are highlighted and `auto` bars reach them all (LuBan drops them, @1:00).
  - Live shadow preview with a real point light while dragging (PLAN §4; LuBan's text boxes need Enter, §1.8).
  - A blur preview from the LED size, and ray-aligned walls for crisp edges (ours).
  - A printed light jig removes the measuring the author warns about (@5:00).
  - Laser output with kerf from the machine profile, and 3MF (PLAN §4).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Threshold → contours → add bars and a base strip (Clipper2 union) → keep the components attached to the base → map floor coordinates to the piece by the perspective from the light point. This is a homography, so straight edges stay straight: a floor point at lateral position u and distance r from the point below the light lands at (u × D / r, H × (r − D) / r) on a vertical piece standing at horizontal distance D from a light at height H (ours; consistent with the tapering bars, @2:00). Extrude by thickness (ray-aligned walls) → validate. Penumbra width ≈ s × (r − D) / D across the ray for emitter size s, longer on the floor at grazing angles (ours). Placing bars to reach every island is an interval-stabbing problem, solved greedily (ours). Research 00 §3, Fence / Projection row: "Shadow geometry from a point light → bars or film plus socket", building block manifold, difficulty 2–3, about 2 developer-weeks.
- **Milestone:** M8 (part 9, first in its row). PLAN §3 lists "Projection (Fence/Pandora)" under Later; part 9 moves it here because it reuses M1's light model.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Whether the piece stands vertically on its base (implied by "flat base" and the tapering) or lies at an angle; the bar direction.
  - How Shadow length relates to the image's other dimension; units (presumably mm).
  - Export formats; whether the light is assumed on the piece's centre line.

### PROJ-PROJECTOR — Slide projector (LuBan: Projection)
- **LuBan path:** File → Create → Projection (video VA67Jm3ijHg @0:00, video of 2026-03-05; blog: projection, "Generate a projection from a photo."). The narration adds "Similar as little fan function" (@0:00), our reading "similar to the lithophane function", i.e. reached the same way from File → Create. This was the first Projection method; its Mode label is UNCONFIRMED (no frames; it predates Fence and Squama). Bare times below refer to VA67Jm3ijHg.
- **What it makes:** A small projector: a socket holds a point light at the back and a film at the front; the film "has a small sized image printed in the object", and light through it projects the image onto a screen (@0:00–2:00). Our reading: the film is a stencil (open where light passes), since disconnected film parts need bridges and its 2D output is a polygon for laser cutting (@4:00, @6:00).
- **Fabrication:** 3D print the film and the socket; the film can be laser-cut instead (@5:00). The light must be one single point source, the stronger the better; an LED with six chips gives six shifted images and a blurred projection (@7:00–10:00; the author mentions a tea light as an example of a single source, @9:00).
- **Inputs:** One image, treated as black and white; colour or grey images are converted automatically (@0:00). Threshold UNCONFIRMED.
- **Parameters:** Labels as narrated; on-screen text UNCONFIRMED.

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| positive / negative option (narrated) | `polarity` | Which image areas let light through | UNCONFIRMED | positive / negative | @1:00–2:00 |
| circle / square "connected shape" (narrated) | `socket_shape` | Socket cross-section, to fit round or square light sources | UNCONFIRMED | circle / square | @2:00 |
| Film size | `film_size_mm` | Size of the film; larger = bigger projected image | UNCONFIRMED | — | @2:00 |
| Film distance | `film_distance_mm` | Film to light source; shorter = bigger image ("a simple triangulation relationship") | UNCONFIRMED | — | @2:00 |
| Projection distance | `projection_distance_mm` | Film to screen; longer = bigger image | UNCONFIRMED | — | @2:00–3:00 |
| Socket size | `socket_inner_mm` | Inner size of the socket = the measured size of your light source | UNCONFIRMED | — | @3:00 |
| Socket depth | `socket_depth_mm` | Depth of the socket: small for narrow lights, longer for big ones | UNCONFIRMED | — | @3:00 |
| Thickness | `thickness_mm` | Thickness of socket and film; also the width of the bridges that hold floating parts of the film | UNCONFIRMED (demo set 3) | — | @3:00–4:00 |
| Tolerance | `fit_tolerance_mm` | Gap between film and socket. Negative for 3D printing ("you will have 0.2 mm gap"); positive for a laser-cut film if 0 is loose | 0 ("the default zero") | signed | @5:00 |
| — (ours) | `bridge_width_mm` | Bridge width, decoupled from thickness | (suggest: 1.0) | ≥ 2 extrusion widths | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `bridge_strategy` | How floating parts are tied to the frame | (suggest: mst = shortest total bridge length) | mst / manual | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `threshold` | Black/white threshold | (suggest: Otsu) | 0–255 | AD3D proposal; @0:00 |
| — (ours) | `led_emitter_mm` | Emitter size, for the sharpness preview | (suggest: 1.0) | (suggest: 0–20) | AD3D proposal; @8:00–9:00 |
| — (ours) | `screen_tilt_deg` | Keystone pre-correction for a tilted screen | (suggest: 0) | (suggest: −45 to 45) | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `film_kerf_mm` | Kerf offset for a laser-cut film | (suggest: from the laser profile) | — | PLAN §4 |
| — (ours) | `ray_aligned_walls` | Hole walls aimed at the light so a thick film does not vignette | (suggest: on) | on / off | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** Four components: "beam" and "projected image" (visualisation only, not printed), "socket" and "film" (blue); Object select (J) lists them and E explodes them (@0:00–1:00). Save writes an "all in one" record ("a representation of the whole thing"), a film STL and a socket STL; the 2D window shows an SHP (LuBan's own format) and an SVG polygon of the film for laser cutting; the output folder also has a DXF (@5:00–7:00). Ours: `projector.3mf` (film and socket objects), `film.svg` and `.dxf` (kerf-compensated cut layer), STLs, and a PNG of the predicted projection.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - Disconnected film parts get bridges as wide as Thickness; bridges block light in reality but are not drawn in the projected-image preview, and they must be printed (@4:00).
  - Films are interchangeable as long as Film size stays the same (@7:00).
  - More shapes are planned for the projection method (@10:00).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - The preview shows bridges and the penumbra blur; LuBan's hides the bridges (@4:00).
  - Minimum-length bridges with their own width, instead of bridges tied to Thickness (@4:00).
  - Keystone correction, laser kerf from the machine profile, 3MF with both parts, live preview (PLAN §4).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Magnification M = (film_distance + projection_distance) / film_distance; projected size = film_size × M (ours; "simple triangulation", @2:00). Film = outline minus the image regions (by polarity) → floating islands → bridges (minimum spanning tree on island distances, Clipper2) → extrude. Socket = tube with a light seat (inner size + tolerance) and a film holder at the film distance (manifold). Blur on the screen ≈ s × projection_distance / film_distance (ours). Research 00 §3, Fence / Projection row.
- **Milestone:** M8 (part 9, after PROJ-FENCE). PLAN §3 lists Projection under Later; part 9 moves it here because it reuses M1's light model.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - The Mode label, on-screen labels, defaults and units.
  - Polarity semantics; the threshold.
  - Tolerance convention: does −0.1 or −0.2 give "0.2 mm gap"? Connectors use −0.2 mm for a 0.4 mm gap (§4.6.6, PDF p.94–95).
  - What the "all in one" record is; how the film attaches to the socket.

- **Fabrication:** UNCONFIRMED. Our reading: 2021, two printed images; 2026, a 3D model (suggest: base printed in two colours or laser-engraved; grille 3D printed or laser-cut, or printed on transparency).
- **Inputs:** A series of images (2021) or several photos (2026) (blog).

| — (ours) | `size_mm` | Base width and height | (suggest: 120 × 90) | — | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** A base image and a slit image (2021); a moire model (2026) (blog). Formats UNCONFIRMED. Ours: base and grille as named objects in one 3MF; SVG layers for the laser.
- **Behaviour and rules:** None stated.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - The grille can be dragged over the base in the preview to watch the animation before printing. LuBan applies typed values on Enter (§1.8, PDF p.15–16; PLAN §4).
  - Slit width is clamped to the printer's line width or the laser kerf from the machine profile, in millimetres. No source shows LuBan checking either (PLAN §4, Machine profiles).
  - 3D version: base and grille as a multi-part, multi-colour 3MF, with a guide track and a fit tolerance for the sliding grille. LuBan exports no 3MF (PLAN §4).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Base column k shows frame (k mod N); the grille has opaque bars (N − 1) × p / N wide and slits p / N wide for period p (standard barrier-grid animation; ours). Clipper2 for the grille outlines.

### THERMAL-FORM — Thermoform kit (LuBan: Thermal, Mesh → LuBan method "thermo")
- **LuBan path:** Open an STL, then Mesh → LuBan, Unit = millimetre, Method = thermo ("Go to mesh, Luban's… select the unit millimeter. Set the method to thermo… I think thermo is simple. Thermoforming is too long", video F20FZvL0r9g @3:00–4:00). Blog and video title: "Thermal" (blog: thermal, 2026-10-14). This is a Mesh → LuBan method, not a File → Create item; it is here because it post-dates the manual. Bare times below refer to F20FZvL0r9g.
- **What it makes:** Three parts from any 3D model: a positive mold, a negative mold and a flat net (red). The net is printed flat, softened with heat and pressed between the molds into a 2.5D shell of one side of the model (@0:00–1:00, @4:00; blog: thermal, "Convert a 3D model to a positive mold, a negative mold, and a flat piece…"). It is not limited to bowls: "any 3D shape" (@3:00).
- **Fabrication:** 3D print all three parts; the net lies flat on the bed and needs no support (@1:00). Heat the net with a heat gun, hair dryer or hot water, press the positive mold into it and let the negative mold hold it tight (@1:00, @4:00). Filament choice and heating trade-offs are discussed on the MeshCast website, not in LuBan (@0:00–3:00). Net thickness depends on material and heating: "What is a good value? We don't know" (@10:00). Mold print orientation UNCONFIRMED.
- **Inputs:** One mesh (STL; the demo used a duck and a horse, @3:00, @10:00–11:00). Its size comes from the Mesh → LuBan input section (model size X/Y/Z, aspect locked; §5, PDF p.96). A very small model "produces something nasty" until the model size is set to a reasonable value (@11:00).
- **Parameters:** Narrated names. The author says they are "borrowed from a relief method" (@4:00), so the on-screen labels are probably Relief's; exact text UNCONFIRMED.

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Method | generator `thermoform` | Mesh → LuBan method; narrated as "thermo", short for thermoforming; the blog and video title say "Thermal" | — | one entry of the method list | @3:00–4:00; blog: thermal |
| Unit | `unit` | Unit of the input model's coordinates, chosen on entering Mesh → LuBan ("select the unit millimeter") | millimetre (selected in the demo) | Fig. 172 shows the Unit box set to "mm". A 2018 build asks in a Select-unit dialog offering metre, decimetre, centimetre, millimetre and inch, and Cancel keeps the last-used unit (luban-docs Get started p.3–4, per luban-docs notes §3); the current list is UNCONFIRMED | @3:00; Fig. 172 (PDF p.96) |
| Model size X / Y / Z | `model_size_mm` | Size of the input model, not of the output; aspect locked. It starts at the model's bounding box in the chosen unit (luban-docs Get started p.5–6, per luban-docs notes §4.3), which is why the tiny horse "produces something nasty" until the model size is set to "a reasonable value" | from the model | — | §5 (PDF p.96); @11:00 |
| projection direction (narrated; Relief's label is "Direction") | `direction` | Which side of the model becomes the relief (+X showed the duck's tail, −X its front, Y its side, +Z its top, −Z its bottom) | +X shown first; default UNCONFIRMED | +X / −X / +Y / −Y / +Z / −Z | @4:00–6:00; §5.6.1 (PDF p.108) |
| relief thickness | `relief_depth_mm` | Height of the relief; more pops the shape up and deforms the net more | 10 (initial) | Demo 10 → 20 | @6:00; §5.6.4 (PDF p.110) |
| bury | `bury_pct` | Buries the lower part of the relief in the base, so the edge is no longer a 90° wall that can break the heated net; 60 % "is a pretty nice shape" on the duck | UNCONFIRMED; apparently 0 at first ("without the bury, as you can see … 90° slope", @6:00). Demo values 10, 40, 70, 60 | %; Relief's figure shows 0–80 % (Fig. 204, PDF p.110) | @6:00–8:00; §5.6.5 (PDF p.110) |
| base thickness | `base_thickness_mm` | Base thickness; the same distance is used on the negative mold | 5 (initial) | Demo 5 → 1 | @8:00; §5.6.6 (PDF p.110–111) |
| border size | `border_mm` | Extended region around the contour | 5 (initial) | Demo 5 → 10 → 1 | @8:00–9:00; §5.6.7 (PDF p.111) |
| cell shape | `cell_shape` | Shape of the holes in the net | UNCONFIRMED | triangle / rectangle / hexagon / circle | @9:00 |
| cell size | `cell_mm` | Hole size; smaller = more cells | 10 (initial) | Demo 10 → 6 | @9:00 |
| line width | `line_width_mm` | Width of the net's struts; thin lines deform better | 1 (initial) | Demo 1 → 2 → 5 ("you can set any value") | @9:00 |
| thickness | `net_thickness_mm` | Thickness of the net (the red part); "cannot be too big" or it will not deform | UNCONFIRMED (demo 4 and 1) | — | @10:00 |
| — (ours) | `mold_clearance_mm` | Gap between the molds = net thickness + this | (suggest: 0.2) | (suggest: 0–1) | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `max_edge_slope_deg` | Target maximum slope; `bury_pct` is raised automatically until it is met | (suggest: 45) | (suggest: 20–80) | AD3D proposal; @6:00–8:00 |
| — (ours) | `strain_limit_pct` | Warn where the net must stretch more than this | (suggest: 30, per material preset) | — | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `register_pins` | Pins through the net's border into both molds, so the three parts line up | (suggest: on) | on / off | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `direction_vector` | Any direction, set with a gizmo | (suggest: off = use `direction`) | unit vector | AD3D proposal; §5.6.1 (other directions need Object → Transform first) |
| — (ours) | `material_preset` | Net material notes (PLA / PETG / TPU) kept as user notes | (suggest: PLA) | user-defined | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** Three components (positive, negative, net); E explodes them (@4:00–5:00). File names UNCONFIRMED (Mesh → LuBan saves STL or OBJ plus an FGD/FGS scene, §5, PDF p.96). Ours: `thermoform.3mf` with three named objects, or one STL each.
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - The direction picks a 2.5D view of any model (@5:00).
  - Bury tunes the slope at the edge of the mold (@7:00–8:00); base thickness also sets the negative mold (@8:00).
  - Thin lines deform better (@9:00); a thick net resists deformation (@10:00).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - A strain and slope preview over the net, with automatic bury, instead of judging by eye whether the net will tear (@6:00–8:00).
  - Explicit clearance between the molds for the net, and registration pins (ours).
  - Any direction, not only ±X/Y/Z (LuBan's relief needs a pre-rotation, §5.6.1, PDF p.108).
  - Live preview, 3MF with named parts, a validated watertight mesh (PLAN §4).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Depth map along the direction (z-buffer) → relief with bury clipping and scaling (research 04 §B.6) → positive mold = heightfield on a base; negative mold = the complementary block, offset by net thickness + clearance through a 2.5D dilation of the heightfield by a ball of that radius (ours); net = 2D lattice (Clipper2 offsets of the cell polygons) clipped to the outline plus border, then extruded; strain per net cell ≈ draped area / flat area (ours). Building blocks: the heightfield mesher shared with Shadow Plate and lithophanes, Clipper2, manifold. Relief details: FORM-RELIEF.
- **Milestone:** M11 (part 9, after FORM-MOLD). PLAN §3 predates it (released 2026-10-14).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - On-screen labels and defaults beyond those seen; whether LuBan leaves clearance between the molds.
  - How the net's outline is derived (contour + border?); mold print orientation; file names.

## 7. Features known only from the blog

These features and tools are described only in LuBan's blog posts (`docs/research/luban-blog/posts-all.txt`, 150 posts, Feb 2019 to Oct 2026): the manual ("Hello LuBan", Aug 19, 2025) has no section for them. I decided each case by reading the whole manual text and its table of contents and grepping it for every feature name; where the manual only mentions a tool in passing or describes it inside another feature's section (Depth map in §3.10.8, Explode/Restore in §4.3, Collage in §2.17.1), the entry says so and cites that text. Three drafted entries were options of a manual feature rather than features of their own (CUT-MULTIPLANAR extends §4.2 Planar cut, PHOTO-PUZZLE-LAYERS extends §3.10 Puzzle, LITH-STENCIL-2S extends §2.19 Stencil lithophane); they have been merged into the entries that own the manual feature and are now one-line stubs. LITH-BOX shares its name with the manual's §3.2.9 "Box lithophane" recipe. Other parts of this spec, written in parallel, also specified some of these features; the merge guide at the end of this part lists every overlap and the ID that was kept. Most posts are one or two sentences long, so nearly every parameter below is UNCONFIRMED, and each entry names the matching channel video (titles only: the repo has no transcripts for them) as the next source to watch.

**Conventions used in this section**
- Source tags: `blog: <slug>` = a post in posts-all.txt; `§x.y (PDF p.N)` = the manual (PDF page = printed page + 1); `video <id> @mm:ss` = a transcript or a frame in the repo (the transcript files in `docs/research/channel/subs/` only carry minute markers, so `@3:00` means the minute that starts at 3:00); `video <id> (title)` = only the title in `docs/research/channel/videos_dated.txt`, whose dates are approximate.
- "Our reading" marks our interpretation, not a source fact. "(suggest: …)" is our proposed value. Parameter rows whose LuBan label is "— (ours)" are AD3D proposals: LuBan's label is unknown.
- Menu paths that come only from a post's wording are UNCONFIRMED. "Turn a photo into…" posts are probably Photo magic methods (Photo magic converts a photo into 3D models, §3, PDF p.46); "…from a 3D model" posts are probably Mesh → LuBan methods (Mesh → LuBan converts a 3D model into new models, §5, PDF p.96; the 2026 Thermal method is confirmed there, video F20FZvL0r9g @3:00).
- The File → Create submenu of the 3D window lists 3D shape, Bamboo-copter, Bottle, Dice, Eyeglasses, Glider, Lithophane, Projection and Photo magic; the 3D window's menu bar is File, Batch, Edit, View, Mesh, Object, Draw, Help (video Wd26qsSIRY8 @3:36, frame `docs/research/squama-video/frames/f_055.jpg`).
- The same frame shows the 3D window's File menu: New, Open, Assemble, Set password, Save, Close, Invoke 2D window, Data receiver, Create, Import, Export, Multi-view sequence, Exit, Exit all; Set password and Save are greyed out while no model is open (frame f_055). In the 2018 Chinese deck the 2D window already had a Tools menu (工具 (T)) beside File, Batch, View, Optical measurement (光测), 3D (三维), Draw and Help (luban-docs Get started p.8, via luban-docs notes §2.5).
- That submenu was captured after every blog-only feature in this section had been announced (the frame's taskbar date reads 1/10/2026, which we read as 1 October 2026 because the Squama post and upload are dated 2026-10-01; if it meant 10 January 2026 this argument fails for features announced after that date), yet it has no item for Pandora, Moire, Lenticule, Painting or any other blog-only photo or mesh method. Our reading: those are modes or methods inside Projection, Photo magic or Mesh → LuBan rather than Create items of their own.
- Owner's machines (docs/START_HERE.md): the Creality CR-6 SE printer (235 × 235 × 250 mm, bed moves in Y), a "3015" laser (3000 × 1500 mm class; fiber or CO2 is UNCONFIRMED) and a "1325" CNC router (1300 × 2500 mm class). For the laser-cut or laser-engraved entries below (TOOL-VECTORIZE, TOOL-HALFTONE, TOOL-HALFTONE-LINE, FORM-FOLDING, FORM-STAR; also PHOTO-PAINTING-BOX (part 3) and FORM-WAFFLE-SKIN (part 5), which absorbed FORM-HASH-SURFACE), which sheet materials make sense depends on that open laser question: a fiber laser suits metal and engraving, a CO2 laser suits wood, card and acrylic (our note).
- Clean room: the binary-derived listings in research 02 §2–3 (method lists, menu groups and file formats read from LuBan's executables) are not used as sources here (CLAUDE.md ground rules).

### TOOL-VECTORIZE — Trace to vector (LuBan: Bitmap to vector conversion)
- **LuBan path:** 2D window → "Tool -> Convert -> Bitmap (binary image) -> Vector" and "Tool -> Convert -> Bitmap (natural image) -> Vector" (blog: bitmap-to-vector-conversion, 2019-03-28). Tool is a 2D-window menu: the manual only uses Tool → … after File → Invoke 2D window (§2.13.1, PDF p.23–24; §2.17.1, PDF p.33), and the 3D window's menu bar has no Tool menu (video Wd26qsSIRY8 @3:36). The 2018 Chinese deck shows the 2D window's Tools menu (工具 (T)), but not its items (luban-docs Get started p.8).
- **What it makes:** Converts a bitmap into a vector image "for the ease of laser cutting" (blog). There are two converters: one for binary (black-and-white) images and one for natural (photographic) images.
- **Fabrication:** Laser cutting (blog). The same outlines are what LuBan's outline-based Photo magic methods need: their photos are "first manually converted to black and white" (§3, PDF p.46).
- **Inputs:** One bitmap, either a binary image or a natural image (blog). Input formats UNCONFIRMED; the 2D window opens and exports BMP, JPG and PNG elsewhere (§2.13.1, PDF p.24).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bitmap (binary image) / Bitmap (natural image) | `source_kind` | Which converter runs: binary (already black and white) or natural (a photo that must be separated first) | UNCONFIRMED | binary / natural | blog: bitmap-to-vector-conversion |
| — (ours) | `threshold` | Grey level separating ink from background for natural images | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: Otsu automatic, manual override) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0–255) | AD3D proposal; LuBan's 2D window has a manual threshold tool, "Tool → Threshold → Manual" (§3.2.9, PDF p.57) |
| — (ours) | `invert` | Swap ink and background | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: off) | on / off | AD3D proposal; LuBan does this as a separate 2D step, "Tool → Data → Invert" (§3.2.9, PDF p.57) |
| — (ours) | `simplify_tol_mm` | Largest allowed deviation when simplifying traced outlines | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0.05 mm) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0–1 mm) | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `min_feature_mm` | Specks and holes smaller than this are dropped | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0.3 mm) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0–5 mm) | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `output_width_mm` | Physical width of the result; height follows the aspect ratio | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 100 mm, or the target generator's width) | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `corner_threshold_deg` | Angle above which a traced vertex stays a sharp corner instead of being smoothed | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: vtracer default) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0–180) | AD3D proposal; research 03 §5 (vtracer) |

- **Outputs:** UNCONFIRMED. LuBan's 2D vector outputs elsewhere are DXF, SVG and its own SHP format (§3.10.7, PDF p.82). Ours: SVG and DXF in millimetres, closed polygons with holes, on a cut layer.
- **Behaviour and rules:** Binary and natural images are separate menu items, so they are processed differently (blog). Nothing else is stated about the converter. Related manual facts: the 2D window turns a photo into a black-and-white image with "Tool → Threshold → Manual" (a threshold chosen by the user) and swaps black and white with "Tool → Data → Invert" (§3.2.9, PDF p.57); Photo magic's own black-and-white images are made with "An intensity threshold … manually chosen" (Fig. 63 caption, PDF p.46). Whether the natural-image converter runs this threshold step itself is UNCONFIRMED.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - The traced outline is drawn over the photo and updates while the threshold or simplify slider is dragged. LuBan's text boxes only apply after Enter (§1.8, PDF p.15–16).
  - Output is sized in millimetres and lands on the cut layer of our SVG/DXF export, which keeps cut and engrave layers separate (PLAN §4).
  - One tracing core serves every outline-based generator (Box, Cutter, Extrusion, lithophane templates). Smooth traced vectors avoid the "bumpy artifacts" LuBan reports for bitmap templates (blog: vector-image-template).
  - The CLI can trace a whole folder of logos in one run (PLAN §4, Batch / CLI).
  - Traced paths pass straight into the Photo magic generators without a file round trip. In LuBan the converter is a separate tool in the 2D window (blog: bitmap-to-vector-conversion; §2.13.1, PDF p.23–24).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Threshold (Otsu) → marching-squares contours → Douglas–Peucker or Bézier fitting (research 04 §C: "OpenCV findContours plus Douglas-Peucker, or potrace"). vtracer (MIT, Rust, also traces colour images) is the natural fit for a Rust core (research 03 §5). potrace is GPL, which is acceptable for personal use (CLAUDE.md). Clipper2 cleans up and offsets the polygons.
- **Milestone:** M5 (part 9, after TOOL-PHOTO-TEMPLATE; the tracing core is a prerequisite for Box, Cutter and Extrusion; the stand-alone tool is a thin wrapper around it).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - What the "natural image" converter does: a single threshold, or colour quantisation into several layers?
  - Its parameters and output format, and whether the result opens as an SHP drawing in the 2D window.
  - No channel video title matches. "Photo to Template" (ue0o2PnOfZU) and "Text outline" (BWqCCePXOIM) may be related (titles only).

### TOOL-HALFTONE — Halftone image (LuBan: Halftone)
- **LuBan path:** UNCONFIRMED. The output is an image, so it is probably a 2D-window tool like Tool → Convert (our reading).
- **What it makes:** A halftone version of an image. The 2019 post: "Convert a grayscale image to a halftone image for laser engraving" (blog: halftone, 2019-10-13). The 2022 post: "Convert a photo to a halftone image based on various patterns or a template image" (blog: halftone-1, 2022-02-21).
- **Fabrication:** Laser engraving (blog: halftone).
- **Inputs:** A grayscale image (2019) or a photo (2022); optionally a template image (2022).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| patterns (post wording) | `pattern` | Shape used to render tones (dot, line…) | UNCONFIRMED | "various patterns"; names UNCONFIRMED (suggest: circle, square, diamond, line, cross) | blog: halftone-1 |
| template image (post wording) | `template_image` | A user image used as the halftone pattern | none | any image | blog: halftone-1 |
| — (ours) | `cell_size_mm` | Pitch of the halftone grid | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 1.0 mm) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0.2–5 mm) | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `screen_angle_deg` | Rotation of the grid | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 45°) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0–90°) | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `gamma`, `contrast` | Tone curve applied before screening | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 1.0, 0) | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal (PLAN §4 image controls) |
| — (ours) | `output_kind` | Raster image for engraving, or vector dots | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: vector) | raster / vector | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** An image (blog). Format UNCONFIRMED. Ours: PNG at the laser's DPI plus SVG dots on an engrave layer.
- **Behaviour and rules:** None stated.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Cell size is in millimetres and the raster DPI comes from the laser's machine profile (PLAN §4, Machine profiles), so the engraving comes out at the size chosen.
  - True-scale live preview while sliders are dragged; LuBan needs Enter after typing (§1.8, PDF p.15–16).
  - Vector dots on their own engrave layer in SVG/DXF (PLAN §4, Better exports).
  - The same screening code drives PHOTO-HALFTONE-3D and PHOTO-CELL (§3.3; part 3): one core, three outputs.
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Amplitude-modulated screening (dot area ∝ darkness on a rotated grid), error diffusion (Floyd–Steinberg) as an option, and template screening by thresholding against a tiled template image. Not covered in research 03/04; difficulty about 1–2 (our estimate). `image` crate for raster work.
- **Milestone:** M7 (part 9, after PHOTO-PUZZLE-COLOR).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Where the tool sits, the list of patterns, and every parameter.
  - Videos: TIwrBJQrCGM "LuBan Halftone" (11:17, ~2022) and JwrUiKXbC5M "LuBan Halftone" (10:11, ~2024), matched to the posts by approximate year only; JwrUiKXbC5M probably shows PHOTO-HALFTONE-3D.

### TOOL-HALFTONE-LINE — Line halftone (LuBan: Halftone line)
- **LuBan path:** UNCONFIRMED (probably a 2D-window tool, our reading).
- **What it makes:** "Convert a grayscale image to a halftone line image. Base line intensity, line width, gap between lines, and line angle can be adjusted" (blog: halftone-line, 2019-10-15). Our reading: parallel lines whose weight follows the tone of the image.
- **Fabrication:** UNCONFIRMED. The halftone post from two days earlier targets laser engraving (blog: halftone), so probably the same.
- **Inputs:** A grayscale image (blog).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Base line intensity (post wording) | `base_intensity` | How much line remains in the lightest areas (our reading) | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED | blog: halftone-line |
| line width (post wording) | `line_width_mm` | Largest line width (our reading) | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED | blog: halftone-line |
| gap between lines (post wording) | `line_gap_mm` | Spacing between neighbouring lines | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED | blog: halftone-line |
| line angle (post wording) | `line_angle_deg` | Direction of the lines | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0–180°) | blog: halftone-line |
| — (ours) | `modulation` | Tone shown by varying width, or by a wave amplitude | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: width) | width / wave | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** An image (blog). Format UNCONFIRMED. Ours: SVG strips or polylines for engraving or pen plotting, plus PNG.
- **Behaviour and rules:** The four controls above are adjustable (blog). Exact UI labels UNCONFIRMED.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - The angle, width and gap sliders update the preview while dragging (LuBan applies a typed value only when Enter is pressed, §1.8, PDF p.15–16).
  - Lines are exported as vectors in millimetres, not only as an image, so they engrave or plot cleanly.
  - The minimum line width is taken from the laser profile's beam or kerf width, so no line is thinner than the machine can mark (PLAN §4, Machine profiles).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Sample the image along parallel lines at angle θ; local width w = w_min + (1 − I)(w_max − w_min); build each strip as a closed polygon with a Clipper2 offset of its centreline. Difficulty about 1 (our estimate).
- **Milestone:** M7 (part 9, after TOOL-HALFTONE).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - The exact meaning of "base line intensity", the units and the output format.
  - No matching video title.

### TOOL-COLLAGE — Photo collage (LuBan: Collage)
- **LuBan path:** File → Create → Collage (§2.17.1, PDF p.33, in a 2D-window workflow; blog: collage, 2020-01-27). The 3D window's Create submenu does not list Collage (video Wd26qsSIRY8 @3:36), so it is probably in the 2D window's File menu (our reading).
- **What it makes:** "Generate a collage of photos" (blog). The manual offers it as an alternative way "to put several images in one big picture" (§2.17.1, PDF p.33).
- **Fabrication:** None directly. It prepares input for single-photo generators: the sphere lithophane takes only one photo, so several photos must first be joined into one (§2.17.1, PDF p.32–33).
- **Inputs:** Several photos.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — (none stated) | — | Neither the post nor the manual names a setting | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED | blog: collage; §2.17.1 (PDF p.33) |
| — (ours) | `layout` | How photos are arranged | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: grid) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: grid / row / column) | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `target_aspect` | Aspect ratio of the result; for a sphere the manual recommends width : height ≈ 3 : 1 to avoid duplication | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: taken from the target generator) | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal; ratio from §2.17.1 (PDF p.33) |
| — (ours) | `gap_mm` | Spacing between photos | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0) | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** One image, "one big picture" (§2.17.1). Format UNCONFIRMED; the 2D window exports BMP, JPG or PNG (§2.13.1, PDF p.24).
- **Behaviour and rules:** None stated beyond the purpose. The related manual tool Tool → Body → Join <left, right> or <top, bottom> joins two images at a time and is repeated for more (§2.17.1, PDF p.33).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - No separate image step: our multi-photo lithophane panels lay photos out internally, with the aspect ratio computed from the shape. LuBan needs Join or Collage in the 2D window, an export and a re-import (§2.17.1).
  - Photos are reordered by drag and drop. LuBan orders photos by file name, so users rename files to change the order (§2.15.1, PDF p.26).
  - The layout previews live on the 3D shape.
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Grid or guillotine layout plus resize and crop with the `image` and `fast_image_resize` crates (PLAN §1). Trivial.
- **Milestone:** Later / maybe never (part 9). A minimal multi-photo layout may come with the M2 sphere and cylinder lithophanes.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Layout options, borders and output size.
  - Video jm1uDmZagjI "LuBan Collage" (5:48, title).

### TOOL-OVERLAY — Photo overlay (LuBan: Overlay photos)
- **LuBan path:** 2D window → "Draw -> Create -> Image", then right-click the overlaid photo → Properties → "Mask RGB" (blog: overlay-photos, 2020-02-21).
- **What it makes:** One photo placed over another, with transparency where the overlaid photo matches the Mask RGB value (blog; the colour-key reading is ours).
- **Fabrication:** None (image preparation for photo-based generators).
- **Inputs:** Two photos open in the 2D window (blog).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mask RGB | `mask_rgb` | Colour of the overlaid photo that becomes transparent (our reading) | UNCONFIRMED | an RGB value | blog: overlay-photos |
| — (ours) | `mask_tolerance` | How close a colour must be to Mask RGB to become transparent | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 10 of 255) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0–255) | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `offset_x_mm`, `offset_y_mm`, `scale` | Position and size of the overlaid photo | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0, 0, 1) | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** A composited image (our reading). Format UNCONFIRMED.
- **Behaviour and rules:** The overlaid photo is an object with its own Properties dialog (blog). The manual's 2D window also opens Properties on a drawn rectangle (§2.20.4, PDF p.39) and has Tool → Data → Set mask value for masking one image by another (§3.6.7, PDF p.72).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Real alpha: PNG transparency and a soft-edged colour key instead of one exact key colour.
  - The overlay is dragged into place with a live preview.
  - Layers stay non-destructive in the project file, with undo/redo (PLAN §4, Projects).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Colour-key alpha plus alpha compositing with the `image` crate. Trivial.
- **Milestone:** Later / maybe never (part 9).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Whether Mask RGB is an exact match; blend modes; whether the result can be flattened and exported.
  - Video xV3QRm2Io1Y "LuBan Overlaying photos" (5:22), linked from the post.
  - Overlap: the Draw → Create → Image and Mask RGB rows of APP-2D (part 1) stay as menu facts; this entry owns the feature (part 7 merge guide).

### TOOL-DEPTHMAP — Mesh depth map (LuBan: Depth map)
- **LuBan path:** "Mesh -> Depth map" (blog: depth-map-of-a-3d-mesh, 2019-06-13, updated 2019-06-16; also §3.10.8, PDF p.83).
- **What it makes:** A 2D image "that describes the surface height distribution of the model" seen from one direction (§3.10.8, PDF p.83). The manual mentions it only as a step in Puzzle of a 3D model; it has no section of its own.
- **Fabrication:** None directly. It feeds heightfield generators: the manual feeds it to Photo magic → Puzzle to make a puzzle of a 3D model (§3.10.8, Fig. 147, PDF p.83).
- **Inputs:** An open 3D model (§3.10.8).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| direction (manual wording: "Set the direction and the resolution of the depth map"; panel label UNCONFIRMED) | `direction` | Axis the model is viewed along | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: ±X / ±Y / ±Z, as Relief's six directions, §5.6.1, PDF p.108) | §3.10.8 step 3 (PDF p.83) |
| resolution (manual wording; panel label UNCONFIRMED) | `resolution_mm_px` | Size of one depth pixel; LuBan's unit is UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED | §3.10.8 step 3 (PDF p.83) |
| — (ours) | `encoding` | Number format of the saved depth | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: float32 TIFF plus 16-bit PNG) | float32 / uint16 | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `background` | Value for pixels where no surface is hit | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0, black, as in Fig. 147) | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal; Fig. 147 (PDF p.83) |

- **Outputs:** A 2D depth image. It is saved from the image's own window with File → Save "as an FLT file, which is a LuBan-defined file format", storing floating-point values for higher accuracy than BMP, JPG or PNG (§3.10.8, PDF p.83).
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - The depth map opens as its own image, saved from there with File → Save (§3.10.8 steps 3–4, PDF p.83).
  - Workflow stated by the manual: open the model → Mesh → Depth map → set direction and resolution → save as FLT → File → Create → Photo magic, method Puzzle → select the depth map (§3.10.8, PDF p.83). "All these can be done in LuBan" (§3.10.8).
  - Fig. 147 shows the model light on a black background (PDF p.83); whether nearer means brighter is our reading of that figure, UNCONFIRMED.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Standard formats (float TIFF or EXR, 16-bit PNG with millimetre-per-unit metadata) instead of a private FLT format; clean room requires our own formats anyway (CLAUDE.md).
  - The depth map feeds any heightfield generator inside the project, with no save and re-open round trip.
  - Any view direction, set with a rotation gizmo. LuBan's Relief and Contour need the model pre-rotated with Object → Transform for non-axis directions (§5.6.1, PDF p.108; §5.2.2, PDF p.99).
  - Rasterised on all cores with rayon (PLAN §4).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Orthographic z-buffer rasterisation along the chosen axis (research 04 §B.6, Relief: "rasterize a depth map (z-buffer)"); rayon over image rows; three.js depth render for the quick preview.
- **Milestone:** M6 (part 9, first in its row). It is cheap once the M3 mesh import exists, and FORM-RELIEF uses it.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Depth normalisation (relative or absolute millimetres), polarity and background value.
  - No matching video title. "Photo to depth image by Depth Anything V2" (hZpYLAkktgg, title) concerns photos, not meshes.
  - Overlap: the Depth map rows of APP-MESH-TOOLS (part 1) stay as menu facts; this entry owns the feature, and part 3 refers to it (part 7 merge guide).

### TOOL-EXPLODE — Exploded view and part browser (LuBan: Exploded view)
- **LuBan path:** "Object -> Explode" and "Object -> Restore" (blog: exploded-view, 2019-04-03), plus Object → Select (§4.3, PDF p.87–88). Keyboard shortcuts: J for object select and E to explode (video VA67Jm3ijHg @1:00; video F20FZvL0r9g @5:00).
- **What it makes:** "Show multiple objects in a window in an exploded view" (blog). Explode spreads the parts apart, Restore puts them back, and Select highlights one part while "the slider on the toolbar" steps through the parts one by one (§4.3, PDF p.87–88, Fig. 156). Scope note: the manual describes Explode, Restore and Select in a paragraph of §4.3 Grid cut, but gives them no section of their own.
- **Fabrication:** None (a viewing tool). The manual uses Explode and Select to inspect planar-cut parts ("an exploded view of the two parts", §4.2, PDF p.85), grid-cut parts (§4.3), hash contours (§5.4.4, PDF p.105) and lithophane assemblies (Fig. 31, whose caption says "To enable the exploded view, use 'Object → Select'", §2.15.3, PDF p.28), and Select alone to step through nested boxes (§3.2.5, PDF p.51).
- **Inputs:** A scene with several objects (blog).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| slider on the toolbar (manual wording) | `part_index` | Which part is highlighted in Select mode | UNCONFIRMED | one value per part (our reading) | §4.3 (PDF p.88); §3.2.5 (PDF p.51) |
| 删除 [Delete] (2018 Select dialog) | — (ours: `delete_part` action) | Removes the highlighted part. Seen only in the 2018 build's floating Select dialog, titled "选择J", which also showed the current part name ("Part_01") and a slider; the manual never mentions deleting a part | — | button | luban-docs Get started p.24 (via luban-docs notes §2.4) |
| — (none stated) | — | No explode distance or factor is described | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED | blog: exploded-view; §4.3 |
| — (ours) | `explode_factor` | How far parts move apart | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 1.0) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0–3) | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** None (view state only).
- **Behaviour and rules:** Explode and Restore toggle the view; Select plus the slider browses parts; "The highlighted view is useful in figuring out the spacial relationship of the parts" (§4.3, PDF p.88). Select-and-slider browsing "also works for the modular cut method if the number of parts is relatively small, e.g. fewer than 20"; for more parts the manual points to the assembly sequence file instead (§4.5.3, PDF p.90–91). Shortcuts: J = Object → Select, E = explode (video VA67Jm3ijHg @1:00); the 2018 dialog title "选择J" agrees (luban-docs Get started p.24).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - A continuous explode slider with animation, plus a part list with isolate, hide and delete, all undoable. No source shows an explode distance setting in LuBan, and no source says its 2018 Delete button can be undone (luban-docs Get started p.24).
  - Explode along the cut tree to show the assembly order visually. LuBan writes the order to a text file, `* Sequence.txt` (§4.5.3, PDF p.91).
  - Keyboard shortcuts and a command palette (PLAN §4, Modern UX); the view state is saved in the project file.
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Per-part offset = (part centroid − assembly centroid) × factor, or along the cut normals by cut-tree depth; plain three.js transforms. Trivial.
- **Milestone:** M3 (part 9, after TOOL-SEPARATE; needed to inspect cut-to-bed parts); also useful for M2 lithophane assemblies.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Whether LuBan's explode distance can be changed.
  - No matching video title.
  - Overlap: APP-OBJECTS (part 1) keeps the parts list; this entry owns the exploded view, and part 4 refers to it (part 7 merge guide).

- **LuBan path:** UNCONFIRMED (the post gives none; probably a Mesh-menu item, our reading). The post's URL slug is "combine" and its title is "Boolean".

- **Fabrication:** Not applicable (mesh utility).
- **Inputs:** Two or more mesh objects (blog).

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| union, intersection, or subtraction | `operation` | Which boolean to apply | UNCONFIRMED | union / intersection / subtraction | blog: combine |
| — (ours) | `operand_order` | Which object is A in A − B | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: selection order) | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** One mesh (our reading). Format UNCONFIRMED.
- **Behaviour and rules:** Works on two or more objects (blog). Nothing else is stated.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - manifold-backed booleans always return a manifold mesh (research 03 §13), and inputs pass through the mesh doctor first (PLAN §4).
  - Runs on all cores and can be cancelled on large scans (PLAN §4); research 08 §1.4 shows single-threaded booleans on 0.5M triangles already take seconds.

- **Algorithm / building blocks:** manifold through its C API via FFI (PLAN §1; research 03 §13).

- **LuBan path:** UNCONFIRMED for the 2025 tool. The 2018 build's Mesh menu already had 分离 S [Separate] (next to 分割 S [Split / segment]); its function is not described (luban-docs Get started p.3, via luban-docs notes §2.3). Our reading: today's tool is probably still Mesh → Separate, possibly reworked in 2025.
- **What it makes:** "Separate and visualize disconnected components of a model as individual model files" (blog: separate, 2025-04-14).

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — (none stated) | — | The post names no setting | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED | blog: separate |
| — (ours) | `min_part_volume_mm3` (APP-VALIDATE key) | Shells smaller than this are reported as debris and not exported | from APP-VALIDATE (suggest: 50 mm³) | ≥ 0 | AD3D proposal; APP-VALIDATE |
| — (ours) | `keep_voids` | Keep an inner void shell attached to its outer shell | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: yes) | yes / no | AD3D proposal |

| Min thickness / Max thickness (shared lithophane setting; LITH-COMMON) | `thickness_min`, `thickness_max` (LITH-COMMON keys) | Thickness range of the lithophane, mm | UNCONFIRMED for this mode (the shared panel shows 0.8 / 3.2, Fig. 10) | UNCONFIRMED | §2.4 (PDF p.19); Fig. 10 (PDF p.17), general to lithophanes |

- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Depth map of the mesh by z-buffer (research 04 §B.6) → lithophane thickness t = f(depth) on a heightfield (research 04 §B.1) → closed watertight shell.
