### LITH-FRUSTUM — Frustum lithophane (LuBan: Lithophane 14th release "Frustum"; 19th release "Perspective frustum")
- **LuBan path:** UNCONFIRMED (probably File → Create → Lithophane, chosen from the drop-down shape list, §2, PDF p.17; our reading).
- **What it makes:** "Generate a frustum lithophane" (blog: lithophane-14th-release, 2022-12-23) and "Generate a perspective frustum lithophane" (blog: lithophane-19th-release, 2024-11-13). Whether the frustum is a truncated cone or a truncated pyramid is UNCONFIRMED; our reading of "perspective" is a photo pre-distorted for one viewpoint.
- **Fabrication:** 3D print. Our reading: lamp-shade use like the cylinder and cone shapes (§2.16, PDF p.28).
- **Inputs:** Photo(s) (lithophane family; number UNCONFIRMED).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frustum / Perspective frustum | `frustum_mode` | Plain mapping, or perspective-corrected | UNCONFIRMED | plain / perspective | blog: lithophane-14th-release; blog: lithophane-19th-release |
| — (ours) | `faces` | 0 for a round frustum, or the number of flat faces | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0, 3–12) | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `top_diameter_mm`, `bottom_diameter_mm`, `height_mm` | Frustum size | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal (the cone already has top and bottom diameters, §2.16) |
| — (ours) | `eye_distance_mm` | Viewpoint used by the perspective mode | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** UNCONFIRMED.
- **Behaviour and rules:** None stated. Related: on a cone "regional distortion is inevitable", and the fixed mode "only preserves the average aspect ratio and does not deal with the distortion" (§2.16.1, PDF p.29).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Perspective mode projects the photo from a chosen eye point, which removes the distortion the manual says LuBan's cone does not handle (§2.16.1).
  - One parametric generator covers cylinder, cone, frustum and N-sided prisms.
  - Backlight preview seen from the eye point (PLAN §4).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Parametric surface mapping (research 04 §B.1). Notes from the lithophane-shapes section (part 2, ours): a faceted frustum is LITH-POLY with separate top and bottom sizes (tilted planar faces); a round frustum is LITH-REVOLVE's cone, whose developable mapping already places a photo without distortion; a perspective mode can pre-warp each face's photo with a homography so it reads as a rectangle from the eye point (for a round frustum, a pinhole projection from the eye point does the same).
- **Milestone:** M2 (part 9, after LITH-SPIRAL), stretch ("more shapes", PLAN §3). Gated: not started until videos 5KDVcwZzvt0 and 3Oncrnefbtk are transcribed (part 9).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Round or faceted; what exactly "perspective" corrects.
  - Videos 5KDVcwZzvt0 "LuBan Lithophane v14 Frustum" (1:54) and 3Oncrnefbtk "LuBan Lithophane v19 Perspective Frustrum" (8:12; "Frustrum" is the title's spelling), titles.
  - Ownership: part 2 defers to this entry and does not repeat the ID.

### LITH-BOX — Lithophane light box (LuBan: Lithophane 15th release "Box"; 18th release "Double-sided lithophane box")
- **LuBan path:** UNCONFIRMED (numbered as Lithophane releases, so probably File → Create → Lithophane with a Box shape, our reading). The manual's §3.2.9 "Box lithophane" (PDF p.56–58) instead describes an older manual workflow built from Photo magic → Box; that workflow is specified in PHOTO-BOX-LITHO (part 3), which points here for the later generator.
- **What it makes:** "Generate a lithophane box" (blog: lithophane-15th-release, 2023-12-09) and "Generate a double-sided lithophane box" (blog: lithophane-18th-release, 2024-03-03). In the manual's workflow the box's lid is replaced by a lithophane cut to the template's shape, with lights inside (§3.2.9, PDF p.56–58); that the generator builds the same thing is our reading.
- **Fabrication:** 3D print; LEDs, wires and batteries go inside the box (§3.2.9, PDF p.58).
- **Inputs:** A template plus a photo (§3.2.9, PDF p.56). The template can be a bitmap or a vector file in DXF or SHP (blog: vector-image-template, 2024-02-05).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| vector image template in DXF or SHP format | `template` | Outline of the box; a vector template gives "a box with smooth surface" | UNCONFIRMED | bitmap / DXF / SHP | blog: vector-image-template |
| double-sided | `double_sided` | Lithophane on two sides (meaning UNCONFIRMED) | UNCONFIRMED | on / off | blog: lithophane-18th-release |
| CMYK | `color_mode` | Single material or CMYK colour (see LITH-CMYK); same key and values as LITH-STENCIL in part 2 | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: `mono`) | `mono` / `cmyk` | blog: lithophane-17th-release |
| — (ours) | `size_mode`, `base_height_mm`, `wall_mm`, `tolerance_mm` | Box sizing and fit, as in Photo magic Box (inner/outer size §3.2.1, PDF p.47; tolerance §3.2.7, PDF p.53) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: outer size, as the manual's recipe uses, §3.2.9; tolerance −0.2 mm, where the manual says to "start your trials", §3.2.7) | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** UNCONFIRMED. The manual workflow ends with a box base file, a lid file and a resized stencil lithophane STL (§3.2.9).
- **Behaviour and rules:**
  - A bitmap template causes "bumpy artifacts"; a DXF or SHP template avoids them (blog: vector-image-template).
  - Rules of the manual's older recipe (§3.2.9, PDF p.56–58), useful if the generator follows it (UNCONFIRMED): the box is made "with an inlay lid" and "the outer size option so that the box is not expanded"; the lid-shaped lithophane is "thinner" than the original template because "the inlay lid is applied and the letters are shrunk by half of the box thickness"; sizing the lithophane by X alone may still leave "the lid and the lithophane to mismatch in size", so the manual resizes it to the lid's measured X and Y.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - The lithophane lid is cut from the same offset polygon as the lid recess, so the two always match. In LuBan's recipe the user measures lid.stl with Mesh → Statistics and resizes the lithophane by hand because the sizes can mismatch (§3.2.9, PDF p.57–58).
  - One generator builds base, lithophane lid and fit tolerance together. The manual's route takes about fifteen steps, including copying a screenshot of the lid into the 2D window to make a new template and resizing the lithophane by hand with Mesh → Statistics and Object → Transform (§3.2.9, PDF p.56–58).
  - Bitmap templates are traced to smooth vectors automatically (TOOL-VECTORIZE, part 7), and SVG is accepted as well as DXF.
  - Backlight preview with the LED position inside the box (PLAN §4, realistic preview).
  - 3MF with base and lid as named parts (PLAN §4).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Template → polygon (Clipper2) → box walls by offset and extrusion (manifold) → stencil lithophane heightfield clipped to the lid polygon (research 04 §B.1) → tolerance offset.
- **Milestone:** M8 (part 9, after LITH-EGG). It needs the M5 Box and the stencil lithophane. Gated: not started until videos 87n4-Jll8vA and pOBxn7Mc-xw are transcribed (part 9).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - What "double-sided" means; whether walls or only the lid are lithophanes.
  - Videos 87n4-Jll8vA "LuBan lithophane v15 Box" (4:18), Z0HPp89BDXQ "Vector image template for lithophane box" (1:42), jDU-OmR4-fo "LuBan Lithophane v17 CMYK Stencil and Box lithophane" (3:11), pOBxn7Mc-xw "LuBan Lithophane v18 Double-sided lithophane box" (4:43), titles.
  - Merge note: the manual's §3.2.9 "Box lithophane" recipe is a manual section of the same name, specified as PHOTO-BOX-LITHO in part 3, which points here for the later dedicated generator. If the videos show that the generator simply automates that recipe, fold this entry into PHOTO-BOX-LITHO.

### LITH-CMYK — Multi-filament colour lithophane (LuBan: CMYK lithophane)
- **LuBan path:** UNCONFIRMED (Lithophane family, our reading).
- **What it makes:** "Generate CMYK color lithophane" (blog: lithophane-16th-release, 2024-01-04); "Generate CMYK stencil and box lithophane" (blog: lithophane-17th-release, 2024-01-30); "Apply customized filament colors to generate CMYK lithophane" (blog: cmyk-lithophane-filament-color, 2025-02-05). This differs from the manual's colour lithophane, which prints a colour filter photo on paper and attaches it behind a grey lithophane (§2.22, PDF p.42–43).
- **Fabrication:** Multi-colour 3D printing with one filament per colour channel (our reading; UNCONFIRMED). Owner's note: the owner's Creality CR-6 SE (docs/START_HERE.md) is a single-extruder printer (general knowledge, not stated in START_HERE.md; confirm with the owner), so on that printer the colours can only come from filament changes at chosen layer heights (stacked colour layers), not from per-pixel colour (our note).
- **Inputs:** A colour photo; for the stencil and box variants, also a template (blog: lithophane-17th-release).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| customized filament colors | `filament_color` (one per filament) | The real colours of the user's filaments; same key as the backlight preview's filament colour (LITH-BACKLIGHT-PREVIEW, part 2) | UNCONFIRMED (our reading: ideal C, M, Y, K) | one colour per filament | blog: cmyk-lithophane-filament-color |
| CMYK stencil and box (post wording) | `shape` | Which lithophane shape carries the colour | UNCONFIRMED | stencil / box (blog: lithophane-17th-release); which shape the first CMYK release used ("Generate CMYK color lithophane") is UNCONFIRMED (suggest: flat as well) | blog: lithophane-16th-release; blog: lithophane-17th-release |
| Min thickness / Max thickness (shared lithophane setting; LITH-COMMON) | `thickness_min`, `thickness_max` (LITH-COMMON keys) | Thickness range of the light-modulating layer (mm) | UNCONFIRMED for this mode (the shared panel shows 0.8 / 3.2, Fig. 10) | UNCONFIRMED | §2.4 (PDF p.19); Fig. 10 (PDF p.17), general to lithophanes |
| — (ours) | `layer_height_mm` | Printer layer height, which quantises the colour layers | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: from the printer profile) | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `max_color_mm` | Largest thickness of any one colour layer | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 1.2 mm) | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** UNCONFIRMED (our reading: one body per filament colour). Ours: one 3MF with an aligned, coloured part per filament.
- **Behaviour and rules:** Filament colours have been customisable since February 2025 (blog: cmyk-lithophane-filament-color); the earlier releases' colours are UNCONFIRMED. LITH-STENCIL's `color_mode = cmyk` (part 2) points to this entry for the colour behaviour.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - A 3MF with one coloured part per filament and real units, ready for a multi-material printer (PLAN §4: 3MF with multiple parts, which LuBan lacks).
  - Filament transmission is measured from a printed swatch and stored in the material preset (PLAN §4, presets per material).
  - The backlight colour preview uses the same light model as the generator, so what you see matches what is computed.
  - A single-nozzle mode for the owner's CR-6 SE: colours are stacked as whole layers, and the export lists the layer heights at which to pause and swap filament. No source says LuBan targets single-extruder printers.
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Separate the photo into filament channels (C, M, Y plus white) using a Beer–Lambert transmission model per filament; per-pixel thickness per channel, quantised to the layer height. Kromacut (AGPL, colour-layered image prints) is the nearest open-source reference (research 03 §3); AGPL is fine to study or port for personal use (CLAUDE.md).
- **Milestone:** Later / maybe never (part 9).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Whether K or white is used; per-pixel layering or stacked plates; output files.
  - Videos D4Fdf6LFsho "LuBan lithophane v16 CMYK" (4:41), jDU-OmR4-fo "LuBan Lithophane v17 CMYK Stencil and Box lithophane" (3:11), wxtrrqEZDRc "CMYK lithophane filament color" (16:11), titles.

| — (ours) | `tile_mode` | Which reading of "tile" is built: one flat tile showing the model's depth map, or lithophane tiles laid over the model's surface | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: `depth_tile`, the cheaper candidate (a) below) | `depth_tile`, `surface_tiles` | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `view_direction` | Direction the model is seen from for `depth_tile` (as TOOL-DEPTHMAP) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: −Y, front view) | ±X, ±Y, ±Z, or a vector | AD3D proposal; TOOL-DEPTHMAP |
| Model size X / Model size Y (shared lithophane setting) | `size_x`, `size_y` (LITH-COMMON keys) | Overall size of the tile set, mm | UNCONFIRMED for this mode (suggest: 200 × 200) | as LITH-COMMON | §2.3; Fig. 10; LITH-COMMON |
| Min thickness / Max thickness, Resolution (shared lithophane settings) | `thickness_min`, `thickness_max`, `pixel_size` (LITH-COMMON keys) | Thickness range and sampling | UNCONFIRMED for this mode (the shared panel shows 0.8 / 3.2 / 0.12, Fig. 10) | as LITH-COMMON | §2.4–2.5; Fig. 10 (PDF p.17) |
| — (ours) | `tiles_x`, `tiles_z` (PROJ-SQUAMA-TILE keys) | Number of tiles across and up, so each fits the bed | (suggest: auto from the printer profile) | ≥ 1 | AD3D proposal; PROJ-SQUAMA-TILE |

- **Outputs:** UNCONFIRMED.

### PHOTO-STRING-ART — Thread portrait (LuBan: String art)
- **LuBan path:** UNCONFIRMED.
- **What it makes:** "Use many lines to represent a photo" (blog: string-art, 2024-07-15). Our reading: classic string art, a thread wound between pins on a frame.
- **Fabrication:** UNCONFIRMED. Ours: a frame with pin holes, laser cut or CNC-routed from sheet on the owner's 3015 laser or 1325 router; a printed frame must stay under the CR-6 SE's 235 × 235 mm bed or be cut into bed-sized parts (docs/START_HERE.md; our note).
- **Inputs:** A photo (blog).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — (none stated) | — | The post names no setting | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED | blog: string-art |
| — (ours) | `pins` | Number of pins on the frame | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 200) | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `frame_shape`, `frame_size_mm` | Circle or rectangle, and its size | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: circle, 400 mm) | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `lines` | Number of thread lines | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 3000) | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `thread_mm` | Thread width used in the preview and the search | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0.25 mm) | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** UNCONFIRMED. Ours: the pin sequence as text or CSV, a preview image, and the frame with numbered pin holes (SVG for laser, 3MF for print).
- **Behaviour and rules:** None stated.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - The search runs on all cores, shows progress and can be cancelled (PLAN §4); the preview fills in as lines are chosen.
  - Pin numbers are engraved on the frame to make winding practical.
  - The preview draws threads at their physical width, so density looks realistic.
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Greedy line selection: from the current pin, pick the line to another pin that most reduces the remaining darkness (sampled along anti-aliased lines). A well-known approach; not covered in research 03/04.
- **Milestone:** Later / maybe never (part 9).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Video CHHTF4rYRKk "LuBan String Art" (18:52, title; 8.7k views, the most watched video of any blog-only feature).

### PHOTO-HALFTONE-3D — Dot relief (LuBan: Halftone, 2024)
- **LuBan path:** UNCONFIRMED (Photo magic by wording).
- **What it makes:** "Turn a photo into a 3D halftone model" (blog: halftone-2, 2024-07-21). Our reading: dots or cells whose size or height encodes the tone, on a base. The manual's Cell method already turns a photo into a structure of small holes (§3.3, PDF p.59).
- **Fabrication:** 3D print (UNCONFIRMED).
- **Inputs:** A photo (blog).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — (none stated) | — | The post names no setting | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED | blog: halftone-2 |
| — (ours) | `pattern` | Dot shape, or a template image (as TOOL-HALFTONE) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: circle) | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `cell_size_mm`, `max_height_mm`, `base_mm` | Dot pitch, tallest dot, base thickness | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 3, 2, 1.2 mm) | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `polarity` | Bright on dark or dark on bright (as Cell's Bright vs Dark, §3.3.1) | UNCONFIRMED | bright / dark | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** UNCONFIRMED.
- **Behaviour and rules:** None stated.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Shares screening code with TOOL-HALFTONE.
  - A movable directional light in the preview, because raised dots read through their shadows (PLAN §4, realistic preview).
  - A direct heightfield mesher that is watertight by construction instead of unioning thousands of dots; research 08 §1.4 measured batch unions of thousands of cells taking 5–162 s.
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Amplitude-modulated screening → per-cell primitive written straight into one mesh (the same approach as the Squama mesher).
- **Milestone:** M6 (part 9, after LITH-RELIEF-OVERLAY). Reuses the M1 heightfield mesher and the M5 Cell code. Gated: not started until video JwrUiKXbC5M is transcribed (part 9).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Raised dots or holes.
  - Video JwrUiKXbC5M "LuBan Halftone" (10:11, ~2024, title; matched by year).

### FORM-PIPE — Tube-and-node frame (LuBan: Pipe)
- **LuBan path:** UNCONFIRMED (Mesh → LuBan by wording, see conventions).
- **What it makes:** "Convert a 3D model into a structure made of pipes and connectors" (blog: _pipe, 2021-09-08).
- **Fabrication:** UNCONFIRMED. Our reading: printed connectors joined by pipes cut from stock, the approach of Dritsas, Chen and Sass's lattice of dowels ("low cost linear elements") joined by 3D-printed nodes (research 04 §A, item 6, CAADRIA 2017; the paper's "L. Chen" is presumably Lujie Chen, who signs every blog post, our reading).
- **Inputs:** A 3D model (blog).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — (none stated) | — | The post names no setting | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED | blog: _pipe |
| — (ours) | `target_edges` | How far the model is simplified before edges become pipes | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 150 edges) | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `pipe_od_mm` | Outer diameter of the stock pipe or dowel | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 6 mm) | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `socket_depth_mm`, `wall_mm`, `tolerance_mm` | Connector socket depth, wall and fit | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 10, 2, −0.2 mm) | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal (tolerance sign as §3.9.6) |

- **Outputs:** UNCONFIRMED. Ours: connectors as named 3MF parts with engraved IDs, plus a pipe cut list (CSV) with lengths and end labels.
- **Behaviour and rules:** None stated.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - The pipe diameter comes from the real stock in a material preset (PLAN §4, presets per material), with a tolerance calibration coupon.
  - Every connector and pipe is numbered, and a PDF assembly guide is produced (PLAN §4, Better exports).
  - Connector generation runs on all cores and can be cancelled (PLAN §4).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Simplify (meshoptimizer, research 03 §13) → edge graph → each node is the union of sleeves along its incident edges (manifold), the method research 03 §8 describes for wireframe connectors; research 04 §A item 6 for the dowel-and-node idea.
- **Milestone:** Later / maybe never (part 9).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Video xSNW3Z9v0ZI "LuBan Pipe" (19:47, title).

### FORM-VORONOI — Voronoi lattice (LuBan: Voronoi wireframe)
- **LuBan path:** UNCONFIRMED (Mesh → LuBan by wording; the manual's Wireframe is a Mesh → LuBan method, §5.10, PDF p.122).
- **What it makes:** "Generate a Voronoi wireframe model from a 3D model" (blog: voronoi-wireframe, 2025-01-15). The manual's Wireframe builds its wires from Hash-style layers instead (§5.10, PDF p.122).
- **Fabrication:** 3D print (our reading). For the regular 3D wireframe the manual advises printing without support and relying on bridging (§5.10.1, PDF p.122).
- **Inputs:** A 3D model (blog).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — (none stated) | — | The post names no setting | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED | blog: voronoi-wireframe |
| — (ours) | `cell_mm` | Typical Voronoi cell size | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 10 mm) | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `wire_mm` | Wire diameter in millimetres | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 1.6 mm) | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `domain` | Cells on the surface only, or through the volume | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: surface) | surface / volume | AD3D proposal (suggested by part 5) |
| — (ours) | `seed` | Random seed for the point layout | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 1) | any integer | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** UNCONFIRMED.
- **Behaviour and rules:** None stated.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Wire thickness is a real millimetre value checked against the nozzle. LuBan's Wireframe uses a normalised thickness from 1 to 5 (§5.10.2, PDF p.123).
  - The preview shows the real wire thickness. LuBan's 3D wireframe preview does not; "You have to save the model to view the generated 3D wireframe" (§5.10.1, PDF p.122).
  - A seed makes the random layout repeatable and undoable (PLAN §1: deterministic generators).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Poisson-disk samples on the surface → restricted Voronoi diagram on the surface (or in the volume, per `domain`) → edges swept as tubes → union with manifold or an SDF/voxel approach (research 04 §B.8, robust union of thousands of tubes). Reuse FORM-WIREFRAME-3D's tube pipeline (instanced live preview, watertight union, bridge check), as the wireframe section suggests (part 5).
- **Milestone:** Later / maybe never (part 9).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Surface-only or volumetric cells.
  - Video Pt9ssfggSMM "LuBan Voronoi wireframe" (10:16, title).
  - Ownership: part 5 defers to this entry.

- **LuBan path:** UNCONFIRMED (Mesh → LuBan by wording, since the input is a 3D model).
- **What it makes:** "Map a texture photo onto a 3D model" (blog: tiling, 2025-05-01). Our reading: the texture repeated over the surface as relief (displacement), since the outputs are fabrication models. UNCONFIRMED. Related: the tattoo lithophane wraps a photo onto any model around an axis (§2.21, PDF p.40).
- **Fabrication:** UNCONFIRMED (3D print, our reading).
- **Inputs:** A 3D model and a texture photo (blog).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — (none stated) | — | The post names no setting | UNCONFIRMED | UNCONFIRMED | blog: tiling |
| — (ours) | `tile_mm` | Size of one texture repeat on the surface | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 20 mm) | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `depth_mm` | Displacement depth | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0.8 mm) | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `mapping` | How the texture is projected | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: triplanar) | triplanar / cylindrical / spherical / UV | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** UNCONFIRMED.
- **Behaviour and rules:** None stated.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Triplanar mapping avoids choosing an axis and hides seams.
  - The model is remeshed to a uniform density first. LuBan's tattoo lithophane is slow on dense models and asks for "relatively smooth and low density" input (§2.21.2, PDF p.42).
  - Low-resolution preview while dragging, full resolution on release (CLAUDE.md speed rules).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Isotropic remesh (pmp-library, research 03 §13) → texture lookup (triplanar, or UV from xatlas, research 03 §7) → displace along normals → self-intersection check.
- **Milestone:** M12 (part 9, after LITH-TATTOO). Gated: not started until video oVdtZBxa9UM is transcribed (part 9).

  - Displacement or colour; seam handling.

### FORM-MOLD — Casting mold (LuBan: Mold)
- **LuBan path:** UNCONFIRMED. Blog: _mold (2026-05-26), "Generate a mold model from a 3D model." Posts phrased "from a 3D model" are Mesh → LuBan methods where confirmed (Thermal, video F20FZvL0r9g @3:00–4:00), so probably Mesh → LuBan, Method = Mold (our reading). Channel: 3qNtXBbKUfI "LuBan Mold" (21:05, ~2026-06, 2.9k views); oNQARGHis8s "Mold making" (3:18, ~2021).
- **What it makes:** A mold from a 3D model (blog). Our reading: a block containing the model's cavity, split into parts with registration and a pour path. The manual documents three earlier mold routes, cross-referenced below, and LuBan's 2019 introduction deck already lists "mould making and casting formwork for architecture [模具制造 浇筑模板 (建筑)]" among its application areas (luban-docs Introduction p.4, per luban-docs notes §1).
- **Fabrication:**
  - 2026 method: UNCONFIRMED.
  - Cocoon route: generate a cocoon, split it in half with Mesh → Cut's planar cut, "inject some solution to the hollow volume, let it settle, and then open the mold" (§5.1.4, PDF p.98; Fig. 177, PDF p.99, printed two-part molds and casts by a user). Specified in FORM-ENCASE-MOLD.
  - Plate route: finger-jointed plywood plates as formwork, "commonly used in building construction"; Fig. 198 shows cast silicone gel staircases from a plywood mold (§5.5.4, PDF p.107–108). A finger-jointed plate model is watertight and can serve as a casting mold or concrete formwork (papers/CAD16). Specified in FORM-PANELS (part 5).
  - Relief route: a negative relief can be used "as a mold for casting" (§5.6.3, PDF p.109; FORM-RELIEF).
  - Research route: thicken the part with a LuBan feature, subtract the original, then cut recursively until no mold part has an inner-surface overhang: 17 parts, cast in silicone (papers/CAD19, case study 1).
- **History:** mould making and casting formwork for architecture was already one of LuBan's application areas in 2019 (模具制造 浇筑模板, luban-docs Introduction p.4), and the 2018 Plate panel had a 生成模具 [Generate mould] checkbox (luban-docs Get started p.18–19; via luban-docs notes §1, §8). The later Thermal method (blog: thermal, 2026-10-14) also outputs "a positive mold, a negative mold", but for pressing a heated flat piece, not for casting (THERMAL-FORM, part 6).
- **Inputs:** One mesh (blog).
- **Parameters:**

- **Behaviour and rules:** None stated for the 2026 method. The manual's cocoon route leaves the cut to the user and documents no keys, pour hole or vents (§5.1.4, PDF p.98).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - One generator makes keyed, vented parts directly, instead of cocoon plus a manual planar cut (§5.1.4).
  - Undercut analysis with automatic recursive splitting, the method LuBan's own authors demonstrated (papers/CAD19).
  - Undercuts and missing draft are coloured on the model before printing (`draft_check_deg`). The manual's cocoon route documents no undercut or draft check (§5.1.4, PDF p.98).
  - Live preview of parting, keys and sprue; validated watertight parts; 3MF (PLAN §4).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Repair the input first (on the critical path for every mesh feature, research 08 §2.11; APP-MESH-DOCTOR) → box = bounding box + wall → subtract the model (manifold) → split by the parting plane (manifold splitByPlane, decompose) → keys, sprue and vents by booleans → validate. Undercut test: faces whose normal points against their part's pull direction (ours). Recursive segmentation per research 04 §B.12.
- **Milestone:** M11 (part 9, after FORM-ENCASE-MOLD). PLAN §3 lists Mold under Later; part 9 schedules it with the other shells.
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Everything about the 2026 method (the 21:05 video is unwatched): menu path, inputs, settings, number of parts, outputs; whether it replaces the cocoon workflow.

## 8. Features known only from channel videos

This section covers features whose only source is the title of a LuBan YouTube upload: no manual section, no blog post and no transcript in the repo. I checked all 166 videos and 5 Shorts in `docs/research/channel/` against the manual text and table of contents, all 150 blog posts and every other spec section; 15 uploads have no manual section, blog post or transcript behind their title, 13 of them are specified below as short entries grouped by family, and the other 2 already have owners (see "Video-only titles specified in other sections"). Since each video gives only a title, a length, a view count and an approximate date, every LuBan parameter here is UNCONFIRMED: the parameter rows are AD3D proposals, and each entry says what a transcript of its video would settle. Appendix C maps every upload in the catalogue to a feature ID.

**Conventions used in this section**
- `video <id>` = an upload listed in `docs/research/channel/videos_dated.txt` (id, date, title, length, views) or `shorts.txt`. Only the title, length, views and date are known; no frame or caption of these videos is in the repo.
- "catalogued YYYY" = the catalogue's approximate date. It comes from YouTube's relative labels, so for uploads older than a year the real date lies in the 12 months up to the catalogued date (research 01 §4: "LuBan Mac install" was uploaded 2019-12-10 but is catalogued 2020-10-19).
- `§x.y (PDF p.N)` = the manual "Hello LuBan" (PDF page = printed page + 1); `blog: <slug>` = `docs/research/luban-blog/posts-all.txt`; `research NN §x` = `docs/research/NN-*.md`; `zh GS p.N` = "LuBan Get started 快速入门.pdf" (2019) in `docs/reference/luban-docs/`.
- "Our reading" = our interpretation of a title, never a LuBan fact. "— (ours)" in the LuBan label column = a parameter we propose (LuBan's label is unknown); "(suggest: …)" = our proposed default or range.
- "(part N)" after another entry's ID = the part that holds it.
- Clean room: no LuBan binary was run or inspected, and the binary-derived listings in research 02 §2–3 (method lists, file formats read from LuBan's executables) are not used as sources.

The 13 entries fall into five families, in this order: lithophane add-ons (LITH-TEXT, LITH-RELIEF-OVERLAY, LITH-EGG); photo and text preparation (TOOL-PHOTO-TEMPLATE, TOOL-BG-SHAPE, TOOL-TEXT-OUTLINE, TOOL-PHOTO-DEPTH); photo-to-object generators (PHOTO-COIN, PHOTO-DISPLAY-STACK); wearables (PHOTO-NECKLACE, CREATE-RING); and mesh input and print planning (APP-IMPORT-VOXEL, APP-ESTIMATE-PRINT).

### LITH-TEXT — Lithophane caption (LuBan: "Add text to Lithophane", video title only)
- **LuBan path:** UNCONFIRMED. Only source: video SyBoLFeHbV4 "Add text to Lithophane" (3:35, catalogued 2020, 2.4k views). The lithophane chapter (§2, PDF p.17–45) has no text setting, and no blog post mentions text on a lithophane. Whether the text is added in the lithophane panel or painted onto the photo in the 2D window, which "is focused on image processing" (§1.7, PDF p.15), is UNCONFIRMED.
- **What it makes:** A lithophane with words built in: a name, a date or a caption. Our reading: the letters become part of the grey image, so they show dark (thick) or light (thin) when backlit.
- **Fabrication:** 3D print, like the lithophane it belongs to: vertical orientation preferred, low speed "e.g. 30 to 50 mm/second", layer height "usually set to half of the nozzle diameter" (§2.23, PDF p.44–45). The owner's CR-6 SE is a bed-slinger, so an upright plate should stand with its face parallel to Y (START_HERE, owner's machines). The manual also says "A lithophane can be 3D printed or CNC machined as long as light can penetrate the material in use" (§2 intro, PDF p.17), so a captioned lithophane could be milled on the owner's 1325 router (material and tooling UNCONFIRMED).
- **Inputs:** A lithophane job (LITH-COMMON (part 2)) plus text. Elsewhere LuBan takes typed text directly in Cutter, Extrusion and Morphing (§3.4.2, PDF p.62; §3.5, PDF p.65; §3.7.2, PDF p.74: "three text boxes"), and for multi-line or overlapping text it tells users to type in MS Word, take a screenshot and import the image (§3.4.2, PDF p.62; §3.2.8, PDF p.54).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — (ours) | `text` | Caption, multi-line allowed | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: empty) | UTF-8 string | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `font` | Font family and weight | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: a bundled bold sans under the OFL) | system or bundled fonts | AD3D proposal; research 08 §2.13 (font licences) |
| — (ours) | `text_height_mm` | Cap height on the finished part | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 8 mm) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 3–50 mm) | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `text_anchor`, `text_offset_mm` | Where the caption sits on the photo | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: bottom centre, 5 mm margin) | 9 anchors plus x/y offset | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `text_tone` | How the text reads when lit | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: dark) | dark (max thickness) / light (min thickness) / emboss on the border | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `text_halo_mm` | Contrasting outline that keeps letters legible over a busy photo | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0.8 mm) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0–3 mm) | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** The lithophane's normal outputs (LITH-EXPORT (part 2)), with the caption merged into one body. Ours: STL or 3MF; in 3MF the caption can also be a separate named part for a colour change.
- **Behaviour and rules:** None stated for a caption. Related manual rules: text boxes update the model only after Enter (§1.8, PDF p.15–16); the only text-size controls the manual documents are labels on Pillar and Stack, where "To disable the text, set the text size to 0" (Pillar "Text size", §3.9.7, PDF p.80; Stack "Text size", §5.3.3, PDF p.102); the 2019 Chinese deck shows that label control as a 字体大小 [Font size] slider at 16 (zh GS p.6, p.12; 00-luban-docs-notes §6–7). Ours: the text is rasterised into the thickness map at the lithophane's resolution (mm/pixel, §2.5, PDF p.20), so strokes thinner than about two nozzle widths are flagged. An embossed caption on the border must be opaque, which for LuBan's dark border means thicker than the max thickness by 5% (§2.7, PDF p.20).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Text is typed, sized in millimetres and dragged on the live preview. LuBan's documented route for anything past one line is an MS Word screenshot (§3.4.2, §3.2.8), and its text boxes apply only after Enter (§1.8, PDF p.15–16).
  - The backlight preview (LITH-BACKLIGHT-PREVIEW (part 2); PLAN §4, realistic preview) shows the caption lit and unlit before printing.
  - Vector glyphs are rasterised at the lithophane's own resolution, so edges carry no screenshot pixels (ours).
  - The caption is stored in the project and stays editable, with undo (PLAN §4, projects).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Shape and outline the text (suggest: `ttf-parser` + `rustybuzz`), rasterise it anti-aliased into the grey image, then apply the normal mapping t = tmin + (1 − I)(tmax − tmin) (research 04 §B.1). Border emboss: a union on the frame (manifold, research 03 §13). Shares its text engine with TOOL-TEXT-OUTLINE.
- **Milestone:** M8 (part 9, after LITH-DUAL). A small add-on to the M2 lithophanes; it reuses M3's text engine. Gated: not started until video SyBoLFeHbV4 is transcribed (part 9).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Panel option or 2D-window workflow; tonal text or embossed/engraved text; font and size controls. A transcript of SyBoLFeHbV4 would settle all three.

### LITH-RELIEF-OVERLAY — Relief on a lithophane (LuBan: "Relief on Lithophane", video title only)
- **LuBan path:** UNCONFIRMED. Only source: video lIWNKgNKYsU "Relief on Lithophane" (1:38, catalogued 2019, 2.5k views). LuBan's Relief method turns a 3D model into a 2.5D relief (§5.6, PDF p.108; blog: relief, 2019-06-22: "Turn a 3D mesh into a relief that can be fabricated by 3D printing, CNC milling, and laser engraving. Function under "Mesh -> LuBan", Method Relief."); a double-sided option followed (blog: double-sided-relief, 2019-07-09). Both posts fall inside the video's catalogue window (2018-10-20 to 2019-10-19). The lithophane chapter never mentions reliefs.
- **What it makes:** Two readings of the title, both ours: (a) a lithophane carrying raised, opaque relief elements (a logo, an ornament or a model's relief) merged onto its face or frame; (b) a lithophane-style heightfield meant to be seen front-lit as a relief rather than backlit. Which one LuBan shows is UNCONFIRMED.
- **Fabrication:** 3D print, upright like any lithophane (§2.23, PDF p.44). Relief parts thicker than the lithophane's max thickness stop light and read as solid dark when backlit (the same reason a dark border must exceed the max thickness, §2.7, PDF p.20).
- **Inputs:** A lithophane photo (LITH-COMMON (part 2)) plus a relief source: a mesh (as in FORM-RELIEF (part 5)), a depth map (TOOL-PHOTO-DEPTH) or a grey heightmap (ours).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — (ours) | `relief_source` | Where the relief comes from | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: mesh) | mesh / depth map / grey image | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `relief_height_mm` | Height of the relief above the lithophane face | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 2 mm) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0.2–10 mm) | AD3D proposal; cf. FORM-RELIEF "Relief thickness" (§5.6.4, PDF p.110) |
| — (ours) | `relief_region` | Where the relief may sit | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: border) | border / mask image / whole face | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `combine` | How the two height maps merge | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: max) | max / add / replace | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `preview_light` | Preview mode | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: both, side by side) | backlit / front-lit / both | AD3D proposal; PLAN §4 (realistic preview) |

- **Outputs:** One watertight body (STL/3MF).
- **Behaviour and rules:** None stated by any source.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - One model, two previews: backlit (LITH-BACKLIGHT-PREVIEW (part 2)) and front-lit with a movable light (APP-LIGHT (part 1)), so the effect of the relief is visible in both lightings (PLAN §4, realistic preview).
  - The heights merge on one grid before meshing, so the result is a single watertight surface by construction (CLAUDE.md); LuBan sends users to MeshMixer even to add a socket to a balloon lithophane (§2.20, PDF p.36).
  - Relief height updates live while the slider moves (PLAN §4; LuBan: Enter, §1.8).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** H = max(H_lithophane, H_relief) on a common grid, then the lithophane mesher (research 04 §B.1). Mesh reliefs come from a z-buffer depth map (research 04 §B.6; FORM-RELIEF (part 5)).
- **Milestone:** M6 (part 9, after LITH-BRONZE). Gated: not started until video lIWNKgNKYsU is transcribed (part 9).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Reading (a) or (b); whether the video uses the Relief method (§5.6) at all.

### LITH-EGG — Egg lithophane (LuBan: "Easter egg lithophane", video title only)
- **LuBan path:** UNCONFIRMED. Only source: video 9scNC9aa5D0 "Easter egg lithophane" (2:37, catalogued 2020, 1.8k views). No shape named "egg" appears in the manual or blog. Candidate routes: the Vase, whose varying diameters are "controlled by several sliders" (§2.16, PDF p.28) or "control points" (blog: lithophane-6th-release); the Sphere (§2.17, PDF p.31); or a balloon lithophane from an egg-shaped template (§2.20, PDF p.35; part 2 also calls this possible). Which one the video uses is UNCONFIRMED.
- **What it makes:** Our reading: a hollow, egg-shaped lithophane shade with an opening for a light, showing one or more photos when lit from inside.
- **Fabrication:** 3D print. A closed shell with an opening follows the sphere's rule: an exterior lithophane prints opening down and an interior one opening up, so any support touches only the smooth surface (§2.17, PDF p.31; §2.23, PDF p.45). A small sphere may close its top gap without support "with any luck" (§2.23, PDF p.45).
- **Inputs:** One or more photos, mapped around the shape as for revolved lithophanes (§2.16, PDF p.28).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — (ours) | `egg_height_mm` | Overall height | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 80 mm) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 40–200 mm) | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `egg_diameter_mm` | Largest diameter | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 60 mm) | less than the height | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `egg_asymmetry` | How much pointier the top is than the bottom | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0.2) | 0 (ellipsoid) – 0.5 | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `opening_diameter_mm` | Light opening at the base | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 30 mm) | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal. On LuBan's sphere the opening is not set directly: "The sphere angle and diameter can be user specified … based on which the opening diameter is calculated and displayed" (§2.17.2, PDF p.33) |
| Socket diameter (sphere) | `socket_diameter_mm` | Inner diameter of a light socket at the opening; 0 = no socket | UNCONFIRMED for an egg (suggest: 0) | must be less than the opening diameter, "otherwise, you will see a warning" | §2.17.3 (PDF p.34) |
| Fixed vs. Stretch (revolved shapes) | `photo_fit` | Keep the photo's aspect ratio or stretch it over the shell | UNCONFIRMED for an egg (suggest: fixed) | fixed / stretch | §2.16.1 (PDF p.29) |
| (shared lithophane settings) | — | Positive/negative, exterior/interior, min/max thickness, resolution, base and socket | see LITH-COMMON, LITH-BASE-SOCKET (part 2) | — | §2.1–2.12 (PDF p.17–22) |

- **Outputs:** One watertight shell, STL/3MF (LITH-EXPORT (part 2)).
- **Behaviour and rules:** None stated for an egg. Rules from the shapes it would be built on:
  - On the sphere, the photo can be aligned top-to-centre or bottom-to-centre, with "a top and bottom offset to confine the photo to a central band on the sphere … The offset value should be between 0 and 1", which "helps to reduce the photo distortion" (§2.17.1, PDF p.31–32). An egg shares that problem.
  - On a cone or vase "regional distortion is inevitable. The fixed mode only preserves the average aspect ratio", and in both modes "LuBan may duplicate the photos to preserve the original aspect ratio" (§2.16.1, PDF p.29).
  - Sphere socket: "The socket diameter is the inner diameter of the socket and should be less than the opening diameter" (§2.17.3, PDF p.34).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - An explicit egg profile (height, diameter, asymmetry) instead of hand-tuning vase sliders, previewed live while dragging (PLAN §4; LuBan: Enter, §1.8).
  - Backlight preview of the whole shell with a visible seam marker (LITH-BACKLIGHT-PREVIEW (part 2)).
  - A light socket from LITH-BASE-SOCKET (part 2) on every egg route. LuBan's sphere has one (§2.17.3), but if the egg is made as a balloon there is none: "The balloon lithophane does not have a socket option. To insert a light socket, other software, such as MeshMixer, needs to be used" (§2.20, PDF p.36).
  - The opening diameter is a direct input with the profile solved around it, instead of a read-only value derived from sphere angle and diameter (§2.17.2, PDF p.33).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Revolve a closed egg curve (suggest: an ellipse whose half-width shrinks towards the top) and map photo (u,v) onto it with the thickness offset along the normal, as for cylinder, cone and sphere (research 04 §B.1); pole handling as in LITH-SPHERE (part 2).
- **Milestone:** M8 (part 9, after LITH-TEXT). A profile preset on top of the M2 revolved and sphere lithophanes. Gated: not started until video 9scNC9aa5D0 is transcribed (part 9).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Which LuBan shape the video uses; a closed egg or an open half-shell.

### TOOL-PHOTO-TEMPLATE — Photo to template (LuBan: "Photo to Template", video title only)
- **LuBan path:** UNCONFIRMED. Only source: video ue0o2PnOfZU "Photo to Template" (13:08, catalogued 2025, 895 views). No blog post, and no such menu item in the manual.
- **What it makes:** A black-and-white template from an ordinary photo: white = the shape, black = background (our reading of the title, using LuBan's template convention). LuBan's template-driven methods need exactly this: the stencil lithophane ("black pixels indicate background and white pixels indicate regions of the lithohpane", §2.19, PDF p.35), the balloon lithophane (§2.20, PDF p.35), the box lithophane (§3.2.9, PDF p.56–57), the layering arbitrary-shaped frame (§3.6.7, PDF p.71), and Photo magic in general, whose photo "is first manually converted to black and white" (§3, Fig. 63, PDF p.46).
- **Fabrication:** n/a (prepares inputs for print, laser and CNC generators).
- **Inputs:** One photo. Ours: optional hint strokes or a box around the subject.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — (ours) | `method` | How the subject is separated | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: automatic subject) | automatic subject (ML) / threshold / colour key | AD3D proposal; research 04 §C |
| Tool → Threshold → Manual (2D window) | `threshold` | Grey level that separates shape from background | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: Otsu, then adjustable) | 0–255 | §3.6.7 step 6 (PDF p.72); §3.2.9 (PDF p.57) |
| — (Fig. 63: "converted from the blue component") | `channel` | Which channel feeds the threshold | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: luminance) | luminance / R / G / B | Fig. 63 (PDF p.46) |
| Tool → Data → Invert (2D window) | `invert` | Swap shape and background: "Make the letters white and the background black … This step is not needed if the letters are already in white." A black shape on white also works for the balloon, which then inflates the surrounding region | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: off) | on / off | §3.2.9 (PDF p.57); Fig. 45 (PDF p.36) |
| — (ours) | `min_feature_mm` | Drop specks and fill holes smaller than this | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 1 mm) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0–10 mm) | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `smooth_mm` | Outline smoothing | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0.3 mm) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0–3 mm) | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `output_width_mm` | Physical width of the template | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: taken from the receiving generator) | > 0 | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** A B/W PNG with a known mm/pixel and an SVG/DXF outline (ours). A DXF fits LuBan's own convention: "The stencil and box lithophane can accept a vector image template in DXF or SHP format" (blog: vector-image-template, 2024-02-05). Ours: optionally the photo cropped to the template's bounding box, which LuBan users do by hand with Tool → Geometry → Labeling and Tool → Body → Crop (§2.20.4, PDF p.38–39; LITH-TEMPLATE-FIT (part 2)).
- **Behaviour and rules:** From the manual: templates are black and white with white as the region (§2.19, §2.20, PDF p.35); "In general, any black and white image is a template" (§3.2.8, PDF p.54); ready-made templates can be found online, e.g. by searching "star black and white" (§2.20, PDF p.35–36); to make one from a photo the manual says to use "any image processing software, such as Photoshop" (§2.20.4, PDF p.38). The 2D window can vectorise the result: "Tool -> Convert -> Bitmap (binary image) -> Vector" and "Tool -> Convert -> Bitmap (natural image) -> Vector", to "Convert a bitmap to a vector image for the ease of laser cutting" (blog: bitmap-to-vector-conversion, 2019-03-28; APP-VECTORIZE (part 1)).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Subject extraction inside AD3D, drawn as a live overlay on the photo, instead of Photoshop (§2.20.4) or a hand-picked channel and threshold (Fig. 63).
  - Output in millimetres as a clean vector as well as a bitmap, so shapes come out smooth; LuBan reports "bumpy artifacts" from bitmap templates (blog: vector-image-template).
  - One click sends the template and the matching cropped photo into the receiving generator (stencil or balloon lithophane, box, layering) with no file round trip; LITH-TEMPLATE-FIT's crop becomes automatic.
  - `ad3d-cli` can make templates for a whole folder of photos (PLAN §4, Batch / CLI).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Segmentation with BiRefNet (MIT) or a SAM-family model (research 04 §C) run through `ort` (PLAN §1); the classic path is channel select + Otsu threshold; then morphological open/close, hole filling and keeping the largest components; contours traced and simplified (research 04 §C: findContours + Douglas–Peucker; vtracer, MIT, Rust, research 03 §5); clean-up and offsets with Clipper2 (research 03 §13).
- **Milestone:** M5 (part 9, after PHOTO-COMMON; Photo magic needs B/W inputs, §3); the ML path follows in M6 with TOOL-PHOTO-DEPTH, which needs the same `ort` runtime. Gated: not started until video ue0o2PnOfZU is transcribed (part 9).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Whether the video shows a new LuBan function or a 2D-window workflow built from the existing threshold, distance-transform and crop tools; its parameters and output. Related titles: wDikiVpunws (TOOL-BG-SHAPE) and Br-ojEQmZUM "How to prepare template and picture for Balloon lithophane" (LITH-BALLOON (part 2)).

### TOOL-BG-SHAPE — Background shape (LuBan: "Add background shape to an image", video title only)
- **LuBan path:** UNCONFIRMED. Only source: video wDikiVpunws "Add background shape to an image" (3:15, catalogued 2020, 1.1k views). Our reading: a workflow in the 2D window, which "is focused on image processing" (§1.7, PDF p.15).
- **What it makes:** Our reading: an image in which the subject (a photo or a B/W design) sits on a solid shape (circle, rounded rectangle, heart, or an outline that follows the subject), so that outline-based generators receive one connected region (a keychain or cookie cutter whose letters would otherwise fall apart) or a framed photo.
- **Fabrication:** n/a (prepares inputs). Likely consumers: PHOTO-EXTRUSION (part 3), which already has "Base shape, Round corner, Base thickness, and Keychain hole" settings, with a rectangle base or an "original-shaped base" that follows the pattern (§3.5.8 and Fig. 111, PDF p.67); PHOTO-CUTTER (part 3); PHOTO-LAYER-SHAPED (part 3); LITH-STENCIL (part 2).
- **Inputs:** An image plus a shape: a preset or a template image.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — (ours) | `shape` | Background shape | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: offset outline) | circle / ellipse / rounded rectangle / heart / star / offset outline / template image | AD3D proposal |
| Tool → Threshold → Between "0 1000" (documented frame workflow) | `margin_mm` | Width of the band between subject and shape edge | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 3 mm) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0.5–30 mm) | §3.6.7 step 9 (PDF p.72): "0 1000" gives a 10-pixel outline, "0 200" a 2-pixel one |
| Round corner (Extrusion base; not a confirmed label for this tool) | `corner_radius_mm` | Rounding of corners and outline | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 2 mm) | ≥ 0; whether LuBan's round corner is a number or a switch is UNCONFIRMED (part 3) | AD3D proposal; cf. §3.5.8, Fig. 111 (PDF p.67) |
| — (ours) | `shape_tone` | Whether the shape is the solid (white) region or background (black) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: white = solid) | white / black | AD3D proposal; template convention §2.19 (PDF p.35) |
| Keychain hole (Extrusion base; not a confirmed label for this tool) | `hole_mm` | Optional hanging hole in the shape | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0 = none) | ≥ 0; in Extrusion "A keychain hole can be generated by setting a positive hole size" | §3.5.8 (PDF p.67) |

- **Outputs:** A composited B/W image plus a vector outline (ours).
- **Behaviour and rules:** None stated for this title. The closest documented workflow, the arbitrary-shaped frame, builds a frame around a masked photo in the 2D window: Tool → Threshold → Manual, Tool → Data → Set mask value, Tool → Geometry → Distance transform, Tool → Threshold → Between "0 1000", then Tool → Arithmetic → Max (Img1, Img2) (§3.6.7, PDF p.71–73). Related base rules elsewhere: in Extrusion "If you do not want a base, set the base thickness to zero", and the keychain hole "will be automatically placed at one of the corners. If not enough space is found at any of the corners, the keychain hole will not be generated" (§3.5.8, PDF p.67); text morphing's base "is set to rounded rectangle" (blog: morphing-2nd-release, 2020-01-31).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - The hanging hole is placed by dragging, with a warning when it cuts the subject, instead of LuBan's automatic corner placement that silently drops the hole when no corner has room (§3.5.8).
  - One panel with shape presets, a margin in millimetres and a live preview replaces that ten-step recipe, whose outline width is counted in pixels and so changes with image resolution (§3.6.7 steps 8–10).
  - Vector offsets give smooth edges, and the result is checked to be one connected polygon before it reaches a generator (ours).
  - Undoable and saved with the project (PLAN §4).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Offset and union of the subject outline (from TOOL-PHOTO-TEMPLATE or TOOL-VECTORIZE (part 7)) with Clipper2 (research 03 §13); a signed distance transform for the raster preview.
- **Milestone:** Later / maybe never (part 9; after M5; small once the template and vector tools exist).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Whether LuBan has a menu function for this or the video shows a workflow; which shapes it offers.

### TOOL-TEXT-OUTLINE — Text outline (LuBan: "Text outline", video title only)
- **LuBan path:** UNCONFIRMED. Only source: video BWqCCePXOIM "Text outline" (9:04, catalogued 2023, 1.1k views). No blog post.
- **What it makes:** Our reading: a text string turned into outline shapes, i.e. letters plus an offset border that joins them into one piece, for box lights, cookie cutters, extrusions and laser-cut signs. The closest documented workflow is the box light (§3.2.8, PDF p.53–55): letters typed in MS Word ("Verdana Pro Black", condensed spacing "so that S and G overlap"), screenshotted and cropped into a template, then turned into "an outline image of the letters" with Tool → Geometry → Distance transform and Tool → Threshold → Between "-1000 0" (a 10-pixel outline; "-200 0" gives 2 pixels), and exported with File → Export → PNG (Fig. 80, PDF p.55).
- **Fabrication:** 3D print (box light, cutter, extrusion) or laser (cut the outline, engrave the letters) (ours). The owner's 3015 laser makes laser-cut signs worthwhile; whether it cuts wood/acrylic (CO2) or metal sheet (fiber) is UNCONFIRMED (START_HERE), and it sets kerf and minimum stroke width.
- **Inputs:** Text and a font, or a text image.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — (ours) | `text` | String, multi-line allowed | UNCONFIRMED | UTF-8 | AD3D proposal; typed text in Cutter (§3.4.2, PDF p.62) |
| — (Word font in the documented workflow) | `font` | Font family and weight | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: a bundled bold sans under the OFL) | system or bundled fonts | §3.2.8 (PDF p.54) used Verdana Pro Black; research 08 §2.13 |
| — (Word "condensed spacing") | `letter_spacing` | Tracking; negative values overlap letters | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: −50 % to +50 % of the em) | §3.2.8 (PDF p.54) |
| Tool → Threshold → Between "-1000 0" (documented workflow) | `outline_mm` | Width of the outline outside the letters | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 2 mm) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0.4–10 mm) | §3.2.8 (PDF p.55): 10 px for "-1000 0", 2 px for "-200 0" |
| — (ours) | `join_letters` | Merge everything into one connected outline | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: on) | on / off | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `text_height_mm` | Cap height | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 30 mm) | > 0 | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `output` | What is emitted | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: both) | letters / outline / both (two polygons, as in Fig. 80) | Fig. 80 (PDF p.55) |

- **Outputs:** Polygons in millimetres (SVG/DXF, or passed straight to a generator), or a B/W image; with "both", the letters and the outline polygon, like LuBan's two-polygon outline image (§3.2.8, PDF p.55).
- **Behaviour and rules:** From the documented workflow: "The outline image has two polygons; the outer one is an expanded version of the letters and the inner one is directly from the letters", and with the outer-size option "shrinkage of the outer polygon may have unexpected effects on the inner one and cause LuBan to remove the inner pattern completely" (§3.2.8, PDF p.55). Further rules from the same workflow: a box light made from the plain letter template "only works well when the box thickness is small, e.g. 1 to 3 mm; otherwise, light cannot penetrate through the box" (§3.2.8, PDF p.54); the distance transform asks for a threshold, and the manual says "Use the default value" (PDF p.54); with the outline image, "the inner pattern option is set to indent and the pattern depth is set to a value a little bit smaller than the thickness", e.g. 4 mm for a 5 mm thickness, and the inner pattern part is not printed (§3.2.8, PDF p.55). Ours: offsets are computed so the inner letters can never vanish, with a warning when the outline is thinner than two nozzle widths or the laser kerf.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Fonts render inside AD3D: no MS Word, screenshot and crop (§3.2.8, PDF p.54; §3.4.2, PDF p.62).
  - The outline width is a true vector offset in millimetres, independent of image resolution; LuBan's is counted in pixels (§3.2.8).
  - Width and spacing update live while dragging (PLAN §4; LuBan: Enter, §1.8).
  - Laser output keeps cut and engrave on separate layers (PLAN §4, better exports) and applies kerf from the machine profile (research 08 §2.6).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Font parsing and shaping (suggest: `ttf-parser` + `rustybuzz`), Bézier flattening, then polygon union and offset with Clipper2 (research 03 §13). Single-stroke Hershey fonts for engrave-only text, keeping their attribution notice (research 00 §3, Labels row; research 08 §2.13).
- **Milestone:** M5 (part 9, after TOOL-VECTORIZE; text inputs for Cutter, Extrusion and Box; §3.4.2, §3.5, §3.2.8). Gated: not started until video BWqCCePXOIM is transcribed (part 9).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Whether "Text outline" is a new LuBan function or the §3.2.8 workflow; its settings.

### TOOL-PHOTO-DEPTH — Photo to depth map, AI (LuBan: "Photo to depth image by Depth Anything V2", video title only)
- **LuBan path:** UNCONFIRMED. Only source: video hZpYLAkktgg "Photo to depth image by Depth Anything V2" (7:40, catalogued 2025, 1.2k views). No blog post covers photo depth. LuBan's only documented depth map is of a mesh: "Get the depth map of a 3D mesh using "Mesh -> Depth map"" (blog: depth-map-of-a-3d-mesh, 2019-06-13; §3.10.8, PDF p.83; APP-MESH-TOOLS (part 1)), and research 04 §C found no machine learning in the manual. Whether LuBan now runs the model itself or the video uses an outside tool is UNCONFIRMED.
- **What it makes:** A depth image (grey = distance) estimated from one photo by the Depth Anything V2 model, usable wherever a heightmap is accepted.
- **Fabrication:** n/a (input preparation). Consumers: FORM-RELIEF (part 5), which proposes this input; PHOTO-PUZZLE (part 3, "ML depth (Later)"); PHOTO-COIN; LITH-RELIEF-OVERLAY. LuBan's own route from a depth map to an object is the puzzle (§3.10.8, PDF p.83).
- **Inputs:** One photo.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — (ours) | `model` | Which Depth Anything V2 weights | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: Small) | Small (Apache-2.0) / Base / Large (CC-BY-NC-4.0) | research 03 §4; PLAN §1 |
| — (ours) | `near_is_high` | Near surfaces become high | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: on) | on / off | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `depth_range_mm` | Physical height that the depth range maps to | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 5 mm) | > 0 | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `compression` | Tone mapping that tames depth jumps, bas-relief style | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: gamma 0.7) | linear / gamma / gradient-domain | AD3D proposal; research 04 §B.6 |
| — (ours) | `mask` | Limit the depth to the subject | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: none) | none / template (TOOL-PHOTO-TEMPLATE) | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `smooth_px` | Edge-preserving smoothing | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 1 px) | 0–10 px | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** A 16-bit PNG/TIFF or float depth map that carries its millimetre scale (ours; LuBan saves mesh depth maps as FLT, §3.10.8, PDF p.83).
- **Behaviour and rules:** None stated by LuBan. Ours: monocular depth is relative, with no absolute scale, so the user sets the physical depth range.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Runs locally through onnxruntime (CoreML on the Mac) as a cancellable background job (PLAN §1, §4): no Python and no web demo.
  - The depth map is previewed as a lit relief while range and compression are dragged (PLAN §4, realistic preview).
  - It flows straight into the relief, coin and puzzle generators and is cached by photo hash (PLAN §1: pure generators, cached by parameters).
  - Small is the default; the Base/Large weights are CC-BY-NC-4.0 (research 03 §4), which fits this personal, non-commercial app (CLAUDE.md) as an optional download.
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Depth-Anything-V2-Small via `ort` (PLAN §1; research 03 §4); Marigold (Apache-2.0) as an alternative (research 03 §4); Apple Depth Pro has a custom licence to check first (research 04 §C); optional bas-relief compression after Weyrich et al. 2007 (research 04 §A).
- **Milestone:** M6 (part 9, after PHOTO-COIN), last and optional. PLAN §3 lists "Relief (AI depth)" under Later, and PLAN §1 lists "Later: ort … Depth-Anything-V2-Small". Gated: not started until video hZpYLAkktgg is transcribed (part 9).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Whether LuBan integrated the model, its settings and its output format.

### PHOTO-COIN — Photo coin (LuBan: "Make a coin from a photo", video title only)
- **LuBan path:** UNCONFIRMED. Only source: video YOzsrsZzbYc "Make a coin from a photo" (2:50, catalogued 2019, 1.9k views). No blog post or manual section; part 7 lists it as a gap. Within its catalogue window (2018-10-20 to 2019-10-19) the blog had announced these photo and relief tools: Bitmap to vector conversion (2019-03-28), lithophane releases 1–7 (2019-04-25 to 2019-09-28), Mesh → Depth map (2019-06-13), Relief (2019-06-22), Double-sided relief (2019-07-09), Cookie cutter (2019-09-30), Halftone (2019-10-13) and Halftone line (2019-10-15) (blog: posts-all). So the video probably combines existing tools, e.g. a flat lithophane heightmap or a relief (our reading).
  - The manual shows a coin-like round medallion made with Extrusion by a user (Fig. 105 centre, §3.5, PDF p.65), but Extrusion was announced on 2020-01-12 (blog: extrusion), after the end of this video's catalogue window, so the video probably does not use it (part 3 raises the same point).
- **What it makes:** Our reading: a round medallion with the photo as a raised relief on one or both faces, a rim, and optionally text around the edge.
- **Fabrication:** 3D print on the owner's CR-6 SE. Orientation is ours to choose (suggest: face up, which needs no support); the manual's "vertical is sharper" advice is for flat lithophanes (§2.23, PDF p.44), and its layer-height tip ("half of the nozzle diameter", §2.23, PDF p.45) applies. A one-sided coin is a 2.5D heightfield with no undercuts (research 04 §B.6), so it can also be milled on the owner's 1325 router; LuBan says its reliefs "can be fabricated by 3D printing, CNC milling, and laser engraving" (blog: relief, 2019-06-22).
- **Inputs:** A photo for the front, an optional second photo for the back, optional text.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — (ours) | `diameter_mm` | Coin diameter | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 40 mm) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 15–150 mm) | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `thickness_mm` | Base disc thickness | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 3 mm) | > 0 | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `relief_height_mm` | Height of the photo relief | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 1.2 mm) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0.2–5 mm) | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `height_source` | What drives the height | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: brightness) | brightness / AI depth (TOOL-PHOTO-DEPTH) | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `rim_width_mm`, `rim_height_mm` | Raised rim | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 1.5 mm, equal to the relief height) | ≥ 0 | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `two_sided` | Relief on both faces | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: off) | on / off | AD3D proposal; cf. Relief's double-sided option, which "has a model's surface on both sides" (§5.6.2, PDF p.108; blog: double-sided-relief, 2019-07-09) |
| — (ours) | `edge_text` | Text around the rim | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: empty) | string | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours; cf. Extrusion "Keychain hole") | `hole_mm` | Hanging hole for a keychain or pendant | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0 = none) | ≥ 0 | AD3D proposal; cf. §3.5.8 (PDF p.67), where a positive hole size makes a hole that is placed automatically at a corner or not generated if no corner has room |

- **Outputs:** One watertight STL/3MF.
- **Behaviour and rules:** None stated by any source.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Front-lit preview with a movable light (APP-LIGHT (part 1)) that updates while relief height and compression are dragged (PLAN §4).
  - An AI-depth option for portraits (TOOL-PHOTO-DEPTH), with a circular crop positioned on the preview (ours).
  - One watertight part by construction (CLAUDE.md), exported as 3MF with units (PLAN §4).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** A brightness or depth heightfield clipped to a disc, with the rim added on the same grid and meshed directly as a closed heightfield solid (research 04 §B.1, §B.6); depth-to-bas-relief prior art: wingated/digital-bas-relief (MIT, research 03 §4). Edge text from the TOOL-TEXT-OUTLINE engine, joined with a manifold union (research 03 §13).
- **Milestone:** M6 (part 9, after PHOTO-PUZZLE-MESH). Gated: not started until video YOzsrsZzbYc is transcribed (part 9).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Which LuBan tools the video uses; front-lit relief or backlit lithophane coin.
  - Whether the catalogue date is right: if the video is in fact newer, Extrusion (Fig. 105 centre) becomes a candidate route.

### PHOTO-NECKLACE — Necklace (LuBan: "Making a necklace", video title only)
- **LuBan path:** UNCONFIRMED. Only source: video xLe7YThrgwQ "Making a necklace" (7:07, catalogued 2025-11, 399 views). Related blog-only methods: Pendant, "Turn a photo into a pendant." (blog: pendant, 2024-11-23; PHOTO-PENDANT (part 7)), and Block version 2, "Turn a photo into a block chain mail." (blog: block-version-2, 2025-11-03; PHOTO-BLOCK (part 7)); the catalogue dates this video and "LuBan Block v2" to the same month. Our reading: pendants or chain-mail blocks made into a necklace. UNCONFIRMED.
- **What it makes:** Our proposal: a wearable necklace of one or more photo pendants with bails, plus printed chain links or a chain-mail strip and a clasp.
- **Fabrication:** 3D print. Print-in-place links need clearance; LuBan's fit advice is "Since zero tolerance is unlikely to work, you may start your trials from -0.2 mm tolerance" and reuse the value "in all LuBan functions that require a tolerance" (§3.2.7, PDF p.53; research 04 §B.16: negative for FDM). The manual also shows name keychains with rings made with Extrusion (Fig. 105 right, §3.5, PDF p.65), the closest documented wearable-adjacent output.
- **Inputs:** Photo(s) or pendant meshes, and a chain length.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — (ours) | `pendant_source` | What hangs on the chain | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: PHOTO-PENDANT output) | pendant / coin (PHOTO-COIN) / small lithophane / mesh | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `chain_length_mm` | Total chain length | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 450 mm) | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `link_style` | Chain type | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: round links, print-in-place) | round / oval / chain-mail strip (PHOTO-BLOCK) / cord only | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `link_size_mm`, `wire_mm` | Link outer size and wire thickness | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 8 mm, 1.6 mm) | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal |
| Tolerance (LuBan's general fit setting; not a confirmed label for this feature) | `clearance_mm` | Gap between interlocking links (AD3D stores a positive gap; LuBan's FDM tolerance is negative) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0.4 mm; how a LuBan tolerance of −0.2 mm maps to a link gap is UNCONFIRMED) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 0.2–1 mm) | §3.2.7 (PDF p.53): "start your trials from -0.2 mm tolerance" |
| — (ours) | `bail` | Loop on each pendant for the chain | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: on) | on / off | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** Ours: one print-in-place chain (or several segments that fit the bed) plus the pendants, as named parts in one 3MF.
- **Behaviour and rules:** None stated by any source.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - The chain is coiled automatically to fit the bed from the machine profile (PLAN §4, machine profiles; the owner's CR-6 SE bed is 235 × 235 mm, START_HERE).
  - Pendant, chain and clasp travel as separate named parts in one 3MF (PLAN §4: LuBan has no 3MF).
  - Link clearance comes from the calibrated tolerance in the material profile (PLAN §4, presets per material).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Links as swept tori laid along a flat spiral that fits the bed, interlocked with a clearance check (manifold, research 03 §13); pendants from PHOTO-PENDANT (part 7).
- **Milestone:** Later / maybe never (part 9).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Whether the video uses Pendant, Block v2 or something else; whether the chain itself is printed.

### CREATE-RING — Ring (LuBan: "RingTutorial, made by LuBan user Amanda Napthine", video title only)
- **LuBan path:** UNCONFIRMED. Only source: video dZKLQN9SFfA "RingTutorial, made by LuBan user Amanda Napthine" (3:45, catalogued 2020, 520 views), a user's tutorial. The same user made the vase in Fig. 209 of the Spin section (§5.7, PDF p.112), so part 5 suspects Spin (FORM-SPIN (part 5)); Spin's cylinder and vase models have an "Inner diameter" that "determines the size of the inner hole" (§5.7.4, PDF p.113), which a ring would need. UNCONFIRMED. The CREATE- family is our placement: no LuBan "Ring" method is named anywhere.
- **What it makes:** Our reading: a finger ring, a band sized to a ring size and decorated with a repeated motif, text, a relief or a lithophane band.
- **Fabrication:** 3D print, axis vertical so the band needs no support (ours). The owner's printer is the FDM CR-6 SE (START_HERE), so fine decoration is limited by the nozzle; the layer-height tip "half of the nozzle diameter" (§2.23, PDF p.45) applies.
- **Inputs:** A ring size and a decoration source: a mesh motif for Spin-style repetition, text or a photo.
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Inner diameter (Spin) | `inner_diameter_mm` | Finger size | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 17.3 mm, about US 7) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 14–23 mm) | AD3D proposal; cf. §5.7.4 (PDF p.113) |
| — (ours) | `band_width_mm` | Band height along the finger | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 6 mm) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 2–20 mm) | AD3D proposal |
| Model thickness (Spin) | `band_thickness_mm` | Radial wall thickness; Spin's outer diameter is "the inner diameter plus twice of the model thickness" | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 1.8 mm) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 1–4 mm) | AD3D proposal; cf. §5.7.4 (PDF p.113) |
| — (ours) | `decoration` | What the band carries | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: repeated motif) | repeated motif / text / relief / lithophane | AD3D proposal |
| Repeat (Spin) | `repeat` | Motif count around the band | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 8) | ≥ 1 | AD3D proposal; cf. "the number of duplicate models" (§5.7.2, PDF p.113) |
| — (ours) | `comfort_fit` | Rounded inner profile | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: on) | on / off | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** One watertight STL/3MF.
- **Behaviour and rules:** None stated for a ring. If the tutorial uses Spin, these Spin rules apply: "The inner diameter is applicable to the cylinder and vase spin models"; the repeated models "are equally spaced by default and undergo the same type of deformation" (§5.7.2, §5.7.4, PDF p.113); and the source model "should have reasonable vertex density; otherwise, the deformation may produce some defects, such as self-intersections", fixed with "Mesh → Densify" (§5.7, PDF p.112).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - The motif is resampled automatically before it is bent around the band, and the result is checked for self-intersections, instead of leaving users to run Mesh → Densify by hand (§5.7).
  - Sizes picked from standard ring-size tables (US, UK, EU) as well as raw diameters (ours).
  - Live preview, plus a minimum-wall check against the nozzle from the machine profile (PLAN §4).
  - Watertight by construction (CLAUDE.md).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Revolve a band profile, wrap motifs or text around the axis by cylindrical mapping (as the tattoo wrap and Spin do: research 04 §B.1, §B.15), union with manifold (research 03 §13).
- **Milestone:** Later / maybe never (part 9).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - Which LuBan method the tutorial uses (Spin, Morphing, Extrusion or a cylinder lithophane).

- **LuBan path:** UNCONFIRMED. Only source: video eXA3n6sIaes "LuBan Importing and rendering 3D voxel images" (9:36, catalogued 2020, 1.9k views). The manual and blog never mention voxels. Candidate menu items, none of whose functions any source describes:
  - File → Import ▸, a submenu whose items no source shows (video Wd26qsSIRY8 @3:32, frame f_054; zh GS p.2; APP-IMPORT (part 1)).
  - File → "Multi-view sequence" (frame f_054, 2026 build), listed as 多视角图像序列 [Multi-view image sequence] in the 2019 Chinese deck (zh GS p.2; 00-luban-docs-notes §2.2).
  - The 2D window's 三维 [3D] menu (zh GS p.8; 00-luban-docs-notes §2.5).
  - File → Open reads "a 3-D model in OBJ, PLY or STL format" (zh GS p.2), so voxel data needs some other route.
- **What it makes:** Our reading: a 3D volume (a stack of 2D slices such as a CT or MRI scan, or another 3D image) loaded, rendered and turned into a printable surface mesh that every mesh generator can use.
- **Fabrication:** Any downstream mesh route: print, cut to bed, laser slicing (ours).
- **Inputs:** Ours: numbered PNG/TIFF slices or a multi-page TIFF with voxel spacing; raw volumes with given dimensions; DICOM series (suggest; parser and its licence to be checked).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — (ours) | `voxel_size_mm` | Spacing in X, Y and Z | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: read from the file, else 1 mm) | > 0 each | AD3D proposal. Cf. LuBan's "Select unit" dialog on entering Mesh → LuBan (metre, decimetre, centimetre, millimetre, inch; Cancel = last unit) (zh GS p.3–4; APP-UNITS (part 1)) |
| — (ours) | `iso_level` | Value that defines the surface | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: Otsu on the histogram) | data range | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `roi` | Crop box | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: whole volume) | box in mm | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `smoothing` | Pre-smoothing / surface smoothing passes | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 1) | 0–10 | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `keep_largest` | Keep only the largest connected part | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: on) | on / off | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `target_triangles` | Decimation target | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 500 000) | ≥ 1 000 | AD3D proposal |

- **Outputs:** A watertight mesh in the scene (exportable as STL/3MF), plus an optional volume preview (ours).
- **Behaviour and rules:** None stated by any source.
- **How we will do it better:**
  - Slice and 3D previews update while the threshold is dragged, before any meshing (PLAN §4, live preview).
  - Meshing is multi-core and cancellable (PLAN §4); the result passes `validate()` (PLAN §1) and the mesh doctor (APP-MESH-DOCTOR (part 1)).
  - Large volumes stream from disk, and display meshes are decimated while export keeps full resolution (PLAN §1, key design points).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Surface nets or marching cubes over the scalar field (suggest), or manifold's `levelSet` fed by a sampled field (research 08 §2.10 notes it needs an SDF callback); meshoptimizer decimation (research 03 §13); OpenVDB as an option (research 07 §e, licence UNCONFIRMED).
- **Milestone:** Later / maybe never (part 9; after the M3 import and repair work).
