### APP-ESTIMATE-PRINT — Project filament and time estimate (LuBan: "How to get accurate estimate of material and time of a big 3D printing project", video title only)
- **LuBan path:** UNCONFIRMED. Only source: video R0YZ624Z6KU (11:48, catalogued 2025, 619 views). Related documented pieces: the Slicer, "Generate gcode from a 3D model for 3D printing." (blog: slicer, 2023-08-13); Batch slicing, "Slice a batch of models and optionally nest the models." (blog: batch-slicing, 2023-10-23); Modular cut's multi-printer setup with "Relative speed" and "Quantity" per printer (§4.5.1, Fig. 161, PDF p.89–90). Our reading: the video slices all the cut parts of a big model and adds up filament and time. UNCONFIRMED. This entry extends APP-ESTIMATES (part 1) and may be merged into it.
- **What it makes:** A report for a multi-part print job: filament length, mass and cost; print time per part and per printer; plate and spool counts; a schedule.
- **Fabrication:** Planning for 3D printing.
- **Inputs:** Parts (for example CUT-MODULAR (part 4) output) and printer and material profiles (APP-MACHINES (part 1)).
- **Parameters:**

| LuBan label | AD3D key | Meaning | Default | Range / options | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — (ours) | `estimate_mode` | Quick (volume-based) or exact (slicer-backed) | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: quick live, exact on demand) | quick / exact | AD3D proposal |
| — (ours) | `slicer_path` | External slicer used headless for exact numbers | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: auto-detect an installed PrusaSlicer or OrcaSlicer) | path | AD3D proposal; AD3D builds no slicer (APP-GCODE (part 1)) |
| — (ours) | `density_g_cm3`, `filament_diameter_mm`, `cost_per_kg` | Material profile | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: PLA 1.24 g/cm³, 1.75 mm, user value) | > 0 | AD3D proposal; PLAN §4 (presets per material) |
| — (ours) | `infill_percent`, `walls`, `layer_height_mm` | Print settings used by the quick model | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 15 %, 3, 0.2 mm) | UNCONFIRMED | AD3D proposal |
| Relative speed; Quantity | `printers[].speed`, `printers[].quantity` | Printers available, their relative speed and count | UNCONFIRMED (Fig. 161's input fields show 1 and 1) | table of printers (Fig. 161's example rows: Speed 1–2, Quantity 1–3) | §4.5.1, Fig. 161 (PDF p.89–90) |
| — (ours) | `setup_min_per_plate`, `spool_change_min` | Overheads that LuBan "can only roughly estimate" | UNCONFIRMED (suggest: 5 min, 3 min) | ≥ 0 | AD3D proposal; §4.5.1 (PDF p.89) |

- **Outputs:** An on-screen report plus CSV/PDF (ours).
- **Behaviour and rules:** From the manual: LuBan assigns parts so that printers "will finish printing roughly around the same time", but it "can only roughly estimate the time spent in machine set up and filament changes" and cannot account for "print failure and inaccurate speed settings" (§4.5.1, PDF p.89). LuBan's measure section shows "the number of parts of an assembly, estimated machine time and assembly time" only for contour, stack, hash and plate (§5 intro, PDF p.96), and Mesh → Statistics reports bounding-cube sizes, "Cube volume", "Mesh volume" and vertex and triangle counts, with no mass, filament or time (§3.2.9, PDF p.57; Fig. 86, PDF p.58).
  - The 2019 Chinese deck shows that the then Mesh → LuBan method 三维模块 [3-D modules, today's modular cut] did report a print time: 5 parts, 16 h machining, 3 min assembly, 16 h total for a 138 × 163 × 259 mm model on a 200 × 150 × 140 mm bed (zh GS p.24; 00-luban-docs-notes §12). Its measures stay blank until Export parts is pressed (zh GS p.22, p.24; 00-luban-docs-notes §4.4), times are shown in minutes or hours (zh GS p.6, p.24), and "The decks never describe LuBan's time model" (00-luban-docs-notes §12).
- **How we will do it better:**
  - A quick estimate from exact part volumes updates live as parts change; an exact estimate runs the user's own slicer headless on every part in parallel, cancellable (PLAN §4), so the numbers match what the printer will do.
  - Overheads (plate setup, spool changes, a failure allowance) are explicit inputs instead of LuBan's rough internal guess (§4.5.1).
  - Estimates appear before export and show their formula, instead of an opaque hours figure that the old modular cut computed only after "Export parts" (zh GS p.22, p.24; 00-luban-docs-notes §15).
  - Filament mass and cost are reported, which Mesh → Statistics (volume and counts only, Fig. 86) does not give.
  - Real per-part times feed the multi-printer schedule (CUT-MULTIPRINTER (part 4)).
- **Algorithm / building blocks:** Mesh volume and area from `ad3d-core`; quick model = shell volume (area × walls × line width) + infill × the remaining volume (ours); exact = slicer CLI on exported 3MF parts, parsing the reported filament and time (suggest); greedy longest-job-first scheduling across printers, in line with LuBan's load balancing (research 04 §B.12).
- **Milestone:** M3 (part 9, after CUT-SEQUENCE), for the quick estimate alongside cut-to-bed (suggest; PLAN §3's M3 scope does not list estimates, but it includes modular cut, which LuBan pairs with multi-printer time balancing, §4.5.1); Later for the slicer-backed estimate. Gated: not started until video R0YZ624Z6KU is transcribed (part 9).
- **UNCONFIRMED / open questions:**
  - What the video shows; whether LuBan's slicer reports filament and time at all.
  - Whether today's modular cut still reports a print time as the 2019 三维模块 measures did (zh GS p.24); the manual's measure list (§5 intro) covers only Mesh → LuBan methods.

## 9. Recommended build order

**Principles.** This order uses the infrastructure-first proposal as its backbone and grafts in ideas from the owner-value and risk-first proposals.

- **Fixed head.** M1 to M4 follow CLAUDE.md's fixed order: Squama, Lithophanes, Mesh cut-to-bed with connectors, then Laser slicing with nesting. The M0 spike (PLAN §2) gates all of them.
- **Engines are built once.** Each shared engine is a pure function in `ad3d-core` that the CLI can also call. It arrives with the first feature that needs it and lives behind one interface. A feature that would need a second copy of an engine is a design bug. A feature joins the earliest milestone whose engines already cover it.
- **Owner value orders the rest.** After M4, the owner's real machines decide the order (START_HERE): the CR-6 SE printer (235 × 235 × 250 mm, bed-slinger), the 3015 laser and the 1325 router. Features that serve the laser and the router rank above printer-only novelties, and features with short make-and-test loops come first.
- **Risk inside each milestone.** Inside a milestone, the item with the biggest technical unknown goes first.
- **Physical test first.** Every milestone opens with a cheap calibration print or cut on a real machine. Its result goes in `docs/test-log.md` (PLAN §5).
- **The ship gate.** Nothing ships until it passes `validate()` (watertight, consistent winding) under randomised parameters (proptest), has a criterion benchmark at preview and full resolution, and has an export path plus a print/cut checklist (CLAUDE.md; PLAN §5).
- **Gate what is not yet specified.** A feature whose "What it makes" rests only on a blog one-liner or a video title may be placed in a milestone, because its engines land there, but it is not started until its video is transcribed into `docs/research/channel/subs/` and its entry is updated from the transcript. Such IDs carry "(gated on: video <id>)" in the table below. Standard operations that the one-liner fully defines (TOOL-BOOLEAN, TOOL-SEPARATE, TOOL-HALFTONE, TOOL-HALFTONE-LINE) are not gated. A feature known only from a menu item, with no description at all (CREATE-3D-SHAPE), stays in "Later / maybe never".
- **Duplicates.** IDs that duplicate each other across parts are written together as `A = B`. They are built once, and the canonical ID is the first one listed. The second entry has been merged into the first and left as a one-line stub (part 7 merge guide).
- **Effort.** Effort is in developer-weeks for one developer, including test prints (PLAN §3; research 00 §3, 08 §3). Any figure not in those sources is marked UNCONFIRMED.

### Cross-cutting work that rides along

- **Validator and ship gate (every milestone).** `validate()` under proptest, golden tests under `tests/golden/`, and criterion benchmarks at preview and full resolution. A generator is not done until all three pass (CLAUDE.md; PLAN §5). The saddle-pinch and T-junction fixes are gating work in M0/M1, not polish (PLAN §6).
- **Fit-to-bed and fit-to-sheet checks in the shared export path,** never inside individual generators. The CR-6 SE's 235 × 235 × 250 mm volume makes this load-bearing from M1. The 3015 and 1325 sheet limits join it in M4.
- **Hand-over package per feature.** Output path (STL/3MF/SVG/DXF), a print or cut checklist from the M1 template, and a `docs/test-log.md` row (CLAUDE.md; PLAN §5).
- **Thin slices of the APP-* entries.** The APP-* entries grow in slices beside the generators that need them, as their Milestone lines say (part 1). Each is listed once, in the milestone where it starts.

  | APP-HELP | | tooltips | drawer | | | | |
  | APP-UNITS | | mm, 3MF units | | import units | | | |
  | APP-LABELS | | | | part IDs | engraved | | |
  | APP-ESTIMATES | | mesh stats | | | laser metrics | | |
  | APP-MESH-TOOLS | | | | stats, separate, boolean | | | simplify, densify |

- **CLI parity (APP-BATCH).** Every generator gets a CLI entry when it lands (M1 onward). The batch dialog stays Later (part 1).
- **Duplicate-ID merge (done).** The pairs written `A = B` in the table were merged into the first ID, and the second ID is a one-line stub. The same-ID repeats in part 7 (APP-PASSWORD, PHOTO-PAINTING-BOX, CUT-CONIC, CUT-FLEXI, CUT-LAPJOINT, PROJ-PANDORA and five CREATE-* items) were merged into their part 1–6 entries and deleted. LITH-BOX vs PHOTO-BOX-LITHO stays open until the videos are watched (part 7 merge guide).
- **Source-watching backlog.** Before any entry marked "video/blog only" is built, its public video is watched and transcribed into `docs/research/channel/subs/`. Each such entry's UNCONFIRMED list names the video.
- **Performance budgets.** Preview in ≤ 50 ms while dragging, then full resolution on release. Large exports are streamed to disk. Display decimation lands with M3 import (PLAN §6 WebView risk).
- **Shared engine reuse map.**
  - M1's heightfield mesher feeds M2, M5 Cell and M6.
  - M2's Clipper2 outline pipeline feeds M4 and M5.
  - M3's manifold, text and connectors feed M4, M8, M10 and M11.
  - M4's slicer, kerf, nesting and SVG/DXF feed M5 Layer, M7, M9 and M12.

### What would change this order

- **Laser type (fiber vs CO2), the biggest open question** (START_HERE open question 1). Resolve it before M4 design.
  - If CO2, FORM-ETCHED stays in M4 and wood/acrylic engraving, labels and the halftone tools gain value.
  - If fiber, FORM-ETCHED goes to Later, and sheet-wood work goes to the 1325 router. The laser then targets sheet metal (waffles, Cell screens, Fence), and M7's halftone tools become metal marking.
- **The spike fails.** If PLAN §2 criterion 1, 4 or 5 fails, switch the UI to egui + wgpu and keep the core. If manifold or Clipper2 will not build universal, M2's Stencil wave and all of M3 stall. In that case, move LITH-STENCIL, LITH-TEMPLATE-FIT and LITH-BALLOON to just after M4, and ship M1 tiling with simple pin holes.
- **The Squama calibration tile disappoints** (relief too subtle, PLAN §6). Then M1b's shadow-aware optimiser and hex cells matter more, but they still must not delay M2.
- **Owner priorities** (START_HERE open question 2). These moves against PLAN §3 need the owner's confirmation:
  - Relief → M6.
  - Plate → M9.
  - Projection → M8.
  - Pillar → M5.
  - Box/Morph stay in M5, and M8 can jump to just after M2 for more shadow art.
- **The owner's CAM software and tooling for the 1325 router** are not recorded. If the CAM cannot take a heightmap or STL, M6's carving route needs a toolpath step, which is deferred work (research 08 §3: 6–12 wk). That could push Relief back behind M7.
- **Repair is weaker than expected.** M3's import and repair is the critical path for M3, M4, M6 and M10–M12 (PLAN §3, §6). If the corpus shows repair failing often, add voxel-remesh work before cut code, and expect every mesh milestone to slip.
- **A transcript confirms a "Later" feature's geometry.** It is then promoted into the earliest milestone whose engines cover it. FORM-STAR, FORM-VORONOI, FORM-FOLDING and PHOTO-STRING-ART are the most likely, because they suit the laser and router.
- **Hardware changes.** A multi-material printer upgrade makes LITH-CMYK and two-colour Moire/Lenticule worth doing. A second printer makes CUT-MULTIPRINTER worth doing. A larger print bed shrinks the need for M1 tiling and M3 cut-to-bed (it would not remove it).
- **The physical test cycle sets the pace.** Squama (2–3 print cycles), lithophane ramps, connector combs and kerf combs all need the owner's time. If print-and-feedback turnaround is the bottleneck, start the next milestone's coding while the prints are out, but keep the milestone boundaries.
- **The total is large.** M1–M4 alone are about 44–81 dev-weeks (about 50–95 with M1b, labels, radial and the suggested Stencil/Balloon/Spiral estimates), and M5–M12 add roughly 45–90 more, much of it UNCONFIRMED. The tail will likely never be finished solo. That is acceptable as long as every milestone ships usable output.

All 150 posts in `docs/research/luban-blog/posts-all.txt`, in date order, each mapped to the spec entry that covers it. In the ID column, the number in parentheses is the part that holds the entry: "(4)" means part 4 and "(7)" part 7 (legend below the table). Where a part 1 menu row and a separate entry both describe a feature, both are listed; merged IDs are shown by their kept ID (part 7 merge guide). Dates are the publication dates in the posts-all.txt headers, which can differ from a post's byline by one day; six posts also carry a later "Updated" date in their posts-all.txt entry (posts-index.txt has no such dates), noted in the last column. "Facts the post adds" lists only what the manual does not already say, and "nothing beyond §x" means the manual fully covers the post.

The other 69 posts map only to entries in other sections: features the manual documents, plus Projection, Fence, Squama and Thermal, whose primary sources are the video transcripts and the Squama research.

## Appendix C: Channel video → feature map

Every upload in the LuBan YouTube catalogue (166 videos in `docs/research/channel/videos_dated.txt` and 5 Shorts in `shorts.txt`) is mapped below to the AD3D feature ID(s) that cover it and to the source that documents that feature. Most uploads are tutorials for features the manual or a blog post already describes; 15 have no manual section, blog post or transcript behind them, and 13 of those are specified in part 8 while the other 2 are owned by part 4 and part 1. IDs are those of the merged file: merged IDs are shown by their kept ID (part 7 merge guide); the notes after the table list the remaining loose ends.

**How to read the table**
- **Date:** from `videos_dated.txt`, oldest first. "(exact)" marks the eight upload dates confirmed in research 01 §4. All other dates are approximate, because the catalogue converts YouTube's relative labels ("6 years ago") into dates: within the last year the date is the month the label points to; older dates are the end of a 12-month window, so 2020-10-19 means uploaded between 2019-10-20 and 2020-10-19 (research 01 §4: "LuBan Mac install" was uploaded 2019-12-10). Shorts have no date (NA).
- **Video id:** links to the public video (watching LuBan's public videos is allowed by the clean-room rules, CLAUDE.md). **Title** is verbatim, typos included ("Frustrum"). **Length** is m:ss as catalogued; 0:27 and 0:45 are catalogued as "27" and "45".
- **Feature ID(s):** "(N)" = the part that holds the entry: 1 = app shell, 2 = lithophane, 3 = Photo magic, 4 = Mesh → Cut, 5 = Mesh → LuBan forms, 6 = Projection family, Thermal, Mold and Create objects, 7 = blog-only, 8 = video-only. "(likely)" = the mapping rests on the title's wording; "possibly" = a weaker guess. "not built" / "not planned" follow the owner entry. Where a part 1 menu row and a separate entry both describe a feature, both are named with "/", for example "APP-MESH-TOOLS (1), Boolean / TOOL-BOOLEAN (7)".
- **Covered by:** "manual §x (PDF p.N)" = the feature's manual section (PDF page = printed page + 1); "blog: <slug> (date)" = a post in `docs/research/luban-blog/posts-all.txt`; "transcript" = captions in `docs/research/channel/subs/` (the Squama video also has 226 frames, research 01); "video-only (title)" = no other source; "title-only" notes mark what a numbered video adds that no source explains.
- Apart from the four transcripts and the Squama captions and frames, no video content was used: every other row rests on the title, length and date.

### Remaining notes
- **Overlapping owners.** After the duplicate merge, 5 rows name two entries (shown with "/"): a menu row of a part 1 entry (APP-2D, APP-MESH-TOOLS) beside the TOOL-* entry that owns the feature, and Mold making, which is mapped to FORM-ENCASE-MOLD (5) and FORM-MOLD (7) (part 7 merge guide). Same-ID repeats and `A = B` pairs are shown by their kept ID only. LITH-FRUSTUM and FORM-VORONOI are owned by part 7.
- **"Mold making"** (oNQARGHis8s, catalogued 2021) is mapped to FORM-ENCASE-MOLD (5) first because it predates LuBan's separate Mold method (blog: _mold, 2026-05-26); FORM-MOLD (7) also cites it.
- **The Short "Block made by LuBan user Jared Wade"** (G84D_VES5RQ) cannot be assigned to FORM-BLOCK (3D model to blocks, blog: block, 2021) or PHOTO-BLOCK (photo to blocks, blog: block-1, 2024) without watching it.
- **Title-wording mappings,** marked "(likely)": BGaO2QMWJdg → FORM-WAFFLE-RADIAL, OaBs6k90h_o → LITH-TATTOO, 6fwQQ-ucYhg → PHOTO-WHISTLE and the Moon Light Short K98rQvMhx2g → LITH-SPHERE.
- **Version titles** whose changes only the title hints at (Plate 2, Box v3 amendment, Painting v2/v3, string v2, Channel 2, Conic cut 2, Grill base thickness and others) are tabulated in part 8 so the owner entries can cite them.

### Suggested transcription order (ours)
Captions for these public videos can be fetched the way research 01 fetched the Squama captions. Transcribing the videos of the next milestones first would replace UNCONFIRMED defaults with values shown on screen (milestones per part 9):
- **M2 Lithophane:** fKl1rsrthcg "LuBan Lithophane" and ba6xj2IISNU "LuBan Lithophane 2" (13:05, 8.1k views).
- **M3 Cut to bed:** aQl8_1Gl79U "LuBan Mesh Cut" (25:59), CX5Q9yAN0uU "Multi printer modular cut" (7.8k views), EuSTuybHofg, q-opnBCkeZI, PuY5inToqIQ, Li-qz2BHik8 "Assembly Sequence", 2MSuURqw5Yo "Native Connector", ce6XCcfx2DA "Mesh Repair" and nzyQWbjfCCI "Hollow and Cut" (6.2k views).
- **M4 Laser slicing:** Cfz6fh0bLI8 "Stack", FJ6VU2wmcp8 "Hash", BGaO2QMWJdg "Radial", c44s9Hp_I6Y "Contour" and Lx5tmdVsGdk "2D Nesting" (5.9k views).
- **M5 Photo magic:** uL4tD0AGTqg, hAUgk1H4-XY, aUYYmJLh1_k and zNQmO7yB0-A (Box), 08zIxrljivI (Cookie cutter), K2kceUJeMkc (Extrusion), zbALjR4R3BE (Layering), z20h8VsRwHE (Cell) and U4nDFenp8uc (Morphing); plus ue0o2PnOfZU "Photo to Template" and BWqCCePXOIM "Text outline" for the M5 entries in part 8.

### Coverage check (moved from part 8)

- Checked: all 166 videos in `videos_dated.txt` and all 5 Shorts in `shorts.txt`, each against the manual (text and TOC), the 150 blog posts and the other parts. Every upload is mapped in Appendix C.
- 15 uploads rest on a title alone: 13 are specified in part 8, and Hollow and Cut and Mesh Repair are owned by part 4 and part 1.
- The channel catalogue in research 01 §4 lists the same uploads by family; every family there maps to an entry here or in another section.
- Re-checked 2026-10-20: every id in `videos_dated.txt` and `shorts.txt` appears exactly once in Appendix C, with matching title, length and date (the eight "(exact)" dates are those of research 01 §4); a keyword search of the manual text, all blog posts and the luban-docs notes for each title-only subject (text on lithophane, relief on lithophane, egg, template, background shape, text outline, depth image, coin, display stack, necklace, ring, voxel, filament/time estimate) found no source beyond those cited in the entries.
- Facts folded in from LuBan's Chinese decks (luban-docs notes): the File menu's Import ▸ and Multi-view image sequence items and OBJ/PLY/STL Open formats (APP-IMPORT-VOXEL), the "Select unit" dialog (APP-IMPORT-VOXEL), the 字体大小 [Font size] label slider (LITH-TEXT), and the old 三维模块 print-time measures (APP-ESTIMATE-PRINT).
